signature:
Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀_add_le.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

`λ_{i+j}(A + B) ≤ λ_i(A) + λ_j(B)` whenever `i + j < card n`, with the sorted eigenvalues of
`A + B` taken through `hA.add hB`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 4.3.1 (stated there increasingly;
this is the decreasing, zero-indexed form). Atlas `courant-fischer`, `weyl-mirsky`.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

name: Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀_compression_le

**Cauchy interlacing / Poincaré separation, upper bound.** For Hermitian `A` and `Q` with
orthonormal columns, the eigenvalues of the compression `B = QᴴAQ` (Hermitian through
`Matrix.isHermitian_conjTranspose_mul_mul Q hA`) satisfy `λ_i(B) ≤ λ_i(A)`. Horn–Johnson 2013,
Cor 4.3.37 (Poincaré separation theorem; the principal-submatrix case is `eigenvalues₀_submatrix_le`).
The index of `λ(A)` is `Fin.castLE` of `i`, so no side condition `i < card n` is needed
(`card r ≤ card n` is `card_le_card_of_hasOrthonormalCols`). Atlas `cauchy-interlacing`.
atlas: cauchy-interlacing

signature:
Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀_eq_iInf_iSup.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

`card n ≤ dim W + k`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 4.2.6 atlas `courant-fischer`.
atlas: courant-fischer

signature:
Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀_eq_iSup_iInf.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

`λ_k = max_{dim S ≥ k+1} min_{0 ≠ x ∈ S} ρ(x)`, written with `⨆`/`⨅` (both attained) and the

zero-indexed convention) atlas `courant-fischer`.
atlas: courant-fischer

signature:
Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀_last_eq_iInf.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

An integrable real comparison on a conditioning-measurable cut remains true for

Conditional Jensen with a conditioning-measurable parameter for a concave
continuous family whose parameter perturbations satisfy an exponential comparison.
Countable dense fixed parameters and conditional comparison on measurable cuts
prove this from scalar hypotheses, without assuming a conditional Jensen inequality.
Source: Tropp 2011 (matrix Freedman), predictable-offset passage;
atlas `matrix-freedman` (partial).

If the inner integral of a product-integrable function equals a strongly
measurable function `g`, then `g ∘ Prod.fst` is its conditional expectation on
the first coordinate.

A jointly continuous compactly supported fibre integral depends
continuously on a compact parameter set. No regularity of the integrand
outside the actual support is required.

The extended deficit is continuous, including at zero where its value

name: MeasureTheory.differentiableOn_resolventPowerMean
doc: Every actual observable resolvent power mean is holomorphic on the upper half-plane.

actual independently resampled positive squared difference. The hypotheses

2013, Chapter 6.

The bounded measurable independent-copy entropy inequality. All
integrability hypotheses are derived from the actual bound on `f`.

On an interval below a compact support, the actual Stieltjes derivative
and the normalization at negative infinity uniquely determine the actual
logarithmic potential. This is the derivative-and-constant argument needed
in the proof of the block-Wishart variational potential identity.

If a measurable integrable quantity is pointwise a value of a continuous function
on a nonempty connected set times a nonnegative integrable weight, its integral is one
such value times the integral of the weight. No measurable selection of the pointwise
intermediate arguments is required, and a zero total weight is included.
Source: integral mean-value argument in operator derivations, (AQ5)–(AQ6).

name: MeasureTheory.exists_integral_eq_mul_integral_of_pointwise_of_weight_constant_sign
doc:
The weighted integral mean-value theorem also permits a nonpositive weight, by
negating the integrand and weight together. This gives the right-Radau and Lobatto
derivative remainders with their original negative nodal factors.

Actual positive scalar measures for every quadratic probe assemble
to one native positive matrix-valued measure. Each quadratic signed
projection is exactly its original positive scalar measure.

positive matrix measure whenever finite Hermitian coordinates reproduce
the matrix transform. The coordinates are instantiated by polarization

Positive actual sample Stieltjes measures cannot have unbounded
transforms over a real gap of their averaged transform. A local
O(height) estimate suffices: compact tests, almost-everywhere zero
mass, and extension to the true parameter support are all proved.
No measure-valued kernel, pointwise sample gap, or uniform sample
boundary bound is supplied as a hypothesis.

signature:
MeasureTheory.extendedLogIntegral.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (g : α → ℝ) :
  EReal
name: MeasureTheory.extendedLogIntegral
doc:
The total extended logarithmic integral, defined from positive and negative
parts using the native extended logarithm. `ENNReal.ofReal` sends nonpositive
real inputs to zero, whose extended logarithm is `-∞`.

This has the usual unambiguous extended-integral interpretation when at least
one part is finite. In particular, a finite measure and an upper logarithmic
bound make the positive part finite. If both parts are infinite, the definition
only follows native total `EReal` subtraction (`∞ - ∞ = -∞`), without asserting
existence of the corresponding mathematical extended integral.

name: MeasureTheory.extendedLogIntegral_congr_ae
doc:
The genuine extended logarithmic integral is unaffected by almost-everywhere
changes of its argument.

doc:
Consequently the genuine logarithmic integral has the expected ordinary

signature: NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Type u_1

orthonormal Krylov basis. The compression `H = Qᵀ A Q` is `ArnoldiDecomp.H`; for symmetric `A`
the same object is a `LanczosDecomp` with `T = H`. Exists iff `q ≤ krylovGrade A b`
(`arnoldiDecomp`, `IsGradedKrylovBasis.le_krylovGrade`); unique up to column signs
(`ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.3 (Alg. 6.1, Prop. 6.4);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33.

  {q : ℕ} {c x₀ : n → ℝ} (D : NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (q + 1)) (y : Fin q → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q (x₀ + (D.restrict ⋯).Q.mulVec y) ↔
    ∀ (y' : Fin q → ℝ),
      (D.Q.transpose.mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) - D.Hbar.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ
          (D.Q.transpose.mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) - D.Hbar.mulVec y) ≤
        (D.Q.transpose.mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) - D.Hbar.mulVec y') ⬝ᵥ
          (D.Q.transpose.mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) - D.Hbar.mulVec y')
name: NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.isGMRESIterate_add_mulVec_iff
doc:
**GMRES is Arnoldi least squares**: for `D : ArnoldiDecomp A r₀ (q + 1)` (`r₀ = c − A x₀`,
which needs `q < ν(A, r₀)`), `x₀ + Q_q y` is a GMRES iterate iff `y` minimises
`‖Q_{q+1}ᵀ r₀ − H̲_q y‖²`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35, Alg. 35.1;
Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.5.3, Prop. 6.9; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3. Deviation: the
right-hand side is `Q_{q+1}ᵀ r₀` (`= ±‖r₀‖ e₁` for any decomposition,
`transpose_Q_mulVec_eq_smul_single`); the `‖r₀‖ e₁` form is
`isGMRESIterate_add_mulVec_iff_of_pos`. Uses atlas `gmres-def`, `arnoldi-relation`.
atlas: gmres-arnoldi-form

  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {q : ℕ} {c x₀ : n → ℝ} (D : NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (q + 1))
  (hD : 0 < D.Q.col 0 ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)) (y : Fin q → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q (x₀ + (D.restrict ⋯).Q.mulVec y) ↔
    ∀ (y' : Fin q → ℝ),
      (√((c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)) • Pi.single 0 1 - D.Hbar.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ
          (√((c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)) • Pi.single 0 1 - D.Hbar.mulVec y) ≤
        (√((c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)) • Pi.single 0 1 - D.Hbar.mulVec y') ⬝ᵥ
          (√((c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)) • Pi.single 0 1 - D.Hbar.mulVec y')
name: NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.isGMRESIterate_add_mulVec_iff_of_pos
doc:
**GMRES is Arnoldi least squares, `‖r₀‖ e₁` form**: as `isGMRESIterate_add_mulVec_iff` for
a decomposition with `q₁ᵀ r₀ > 0` (e.g. the canonical `arnoldiDecomp`), `x₀ + Q_q y` is a GMRES
iterate iff `y` minimises `‖ ‖r₀‖ e₁ − H̲_q y ‖²`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`],
Lect. 35, Alg. 35.1; Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.9.
atlas: gmres-arnoldi-form

signature:
NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.isLeast_dotProduct_of_isGMRESIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {q : ℕ} {c x₀ : n → ℝ} (D : NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (q + 1)) {x : n → ℝ}
  (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  IsLeast
    (Set.range fun y =>
      (D.Q.transpose.mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) - D.Hbar.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ
        (D.Q.transpose.mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) - D.Hbar.mulVec y))
    ((c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x))
name: NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.isLeast_dotProduct_of_isGMRESIterate
doc:
**The GMRES residual norm is the small least-squares minimum**: for every GMRES iterate `x`,
`‖c − A x‖² = min_y ‖Q_{q+1}ᵀ r₀ − H̲_q y‖²` (as `IsLeast`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 35; Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.9 (the residual norm is computed without
forming `x_q`).
atlas: gmres-arnoldi-form

the last unit vector of `ℝ^q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5, eq. (6.7);

decomposition of size `q + 1`; by the Hessenberg structure `h̲ = h_{q+1,q} e_q`
(`mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_smul`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5, eq. (6.7);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33, eq. (33.13).

signature:

  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Type (max u_1 u_2)
name: NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp
doc:
A **Golub–Kahan decomposition** of `(A, b)` of size `k`: `U : m × (k+1)` is a graded
orthonormal Krylov basis of `(AAᵀ, b)` and `V : n × k` one of `(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`. Then
`A V = U B` with `B = UᵀAV` lower bidiagonal; `V` is the Lanczos basis of `(AᵀA, Aᵀb)` and `U`
that of `(AAᵀ, b)`. Unique up to column signs (`ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign` on each factor);
exists when `k + 1 ≤ krylovGrade (AAᵀ) b` and `k ≤ krylovGrade (AᵀA) (Aᵀb)`
(`golubKahanDecomp`). Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §10.4.1; Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 31.

NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp.range_mul_V_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {k : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp A b k) :
  (A * D.V).mulVecLin.range ≤ D.U.mulVecLin.range
name: NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp.range_mul_V_le
doc:
`range (A V_k) ⊆ range U_{k+1} = K_{k+1}(AAᵀ, b)`. Helper for
`golub-kahan-bidiagonalization`.

signature:
NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp.transpose_B_mul_B_eq_T.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {k : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp A b k) :
  D.B.transpose * D.B = D.lanczosV.T
name: NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp.transpose_B_mul_B_eq_T
doc:
**`BᵀB` is the Lanczos matrix of `AᵀA`**: `B_kᵀ B_k = V_kᵀ (AᵀA) V_k = T_k`, the Jacobi
matrix of the Lanczos process on `(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
§10.4.1; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 31.
atlas: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization

signature:
NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp.transpose_mulVec_U_col_mem_range_V.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {k : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp A b k)
  {j : Fin (k + 1)} (hj : ↑j < k) : A.transpose.mulVec (D.U.col j) ∈ D.V.mulVecLin.range
name: NLAlib.GolubKahanDecomp.transpose_mulVec_U_col_mem_range_V
doc:
**The second Golub–Kahan relation**, column form: for `j < k`, `Aᵀuⱼ ∈ range V_k`, i.e. the
columns `j < k` of `(I − VVᵀ) AᵀU_{k+1}` vanish and `AᵀU_{k+1} = V_k B_kᵀ + r e_{k+1}ᵀ` with
`r = (I − VVᵀ) Aᵀ u_{k+1}` (`= α_{k+1} v_{k+1}`). Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
§10.4.1 (eq. 10.4.5).
atlas: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization

name: NLAlib.GolubKahanState
doc:
The state of the Golub–Kahan recursion: the current `u`, `v`, `α`, `β`. Source:

name: NLAlib.GolubKahanState.beta

NLAlib.GolubKahanState.mk.{u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_3} {n : Type u_4} (u : m → ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) (alpha beta : ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.GolubKahanState.u
doc: The left vector `u_j`.

name: NLAlib.GolubKahanState.v
doc: The right vector `v_j`.

signature:
NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds
doc:
**Success predicate**: no breakdown in the first `k + 1` states, `α_j ≠ 0` and `β_j ≠ 0`.

atlas: golub-kahan-recurrence

An orientation of edge records of an undirected loop-free graph.

name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.adjacent
doc: Every record is an actual edge, so loops are excluded.

name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.complete
doc: Every undirected edge occurs among the edge records.

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.componentKernelEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ) (hw : ∀ (e : E), 0 < w e) :
  (G.ConnectedComponent → ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] ↥(o.weightedIncidence w).mulVecLin.ker
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.componentKernelEquiv
doc:
Componentwise constants are linearly equivalent to the weighted incidence kernel.
This explicit quotient lift identifies all kernel vectors, including isolated vertices.

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.edgeResistance.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V] [Fintype E]

name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.edgeResistance

Effective resistance between the endpoints of an edge. The vector is the
unweighted signed edge incidence, and no resistance across components is defined.

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.eq_of_reachable.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {x : V → ℝ}

name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.eq_of_reachable
doc: Equality along graph edges propagates along every finite walk.

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.incidence.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V}

name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.incidence
doc: The signed incidence matrix of an orientation, with one row per edge.

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.incidence_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (x : V → ℝ) (e : E) :

doc: Incidence multiplication computes oriented endpoint differences.

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.laplacian.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ) : Matrix V V ℝ
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.laplacian
doc: The weighted graph Laplacian, defined as the weighted incidence Gram matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.laplacian_leverage_eq_rangeProjector.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V]
  [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ) :
  o.weightedIncidence w * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (o.laplacian w) * (o.weightedIncidence w).transpose =
    NLAlib.rangeProjector (o.weightedIncidence w)
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.laplacian_leverage_eq_rangeProjector
doc:
The edge leverage matrix is the orthogonal projector onto the weighted
incidence range. No connectedness assumption is imposed.
Source: Spielman–Srivastava.
atlas: laplacian-resistance-leverage (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.mk.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {E : Type u_2} (source target : E → V)
  (adjacent : ∀ (e : E), G.Adj (source e) (target e))
  (complete : ∀ {u v : V}, G.Adj u v → ∃ e, source e = u ∧ target e = v ∨ source e = v ∧ target e = u) :
  NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.mk

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.rank_laplacian.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V] [Fintype E]
  [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ) (hw : ∀ (e : E), 0 < w e) :
  (o.laplacian w).rank = Fintype.card V - Nat.card G.ConnectedComponent
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.rank_laplacian
doc:
The Laplacian rank is `|V| - number of connected components`, including
isolated vertices and all empty dimensions.
Source: Chung, Chapter 1.
atlas: laplacian-resistance-leverage (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.rank_weightedIncidence.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) [Fintype E] (w : E → ℝ) (hw : ∀ (e : E), 0 < w e) :
  (o.weightedIncidence w).rank = Fintype.card V - Nat.card G.ConnectedComponent
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.rank_weightedIncidence
doc:
Rank of a weighted incidence matrix: number of vertices minus number of
connected components. Positive weights and any orientation give the same rank.
Source: Chung, Chapter 1.
atlas: laplacian-resistance-leverage (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.source.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {E : Type u_2}
  (self : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) : E → V
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.source
doc: Initial endpoint of an oriented edge.

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.sum_weight_mul_edgeResistance.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V]
  [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ)
  (hw : ∀ (e : E), 0 < w e) :
  ∑ e, w e * o.edgeResistance w e = ↑(o.laplacian w).rank ∧
    ∑ e, w e * o.edgeResistance w e = ↑(Fintype.card V - Nat.card G.ConnectedComponent)
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.sum_weight_mul_edgeResistance
doc:
Foster's identity: weighted edge resistances sum to the Laplacian rank,
and hence to vertices minus connected components. This includes disconnected
graphs and isolates, and evaluates to zero for an empty edge set.
Source: Spielman–Srivastava.
atlas: laplacian-resistance-leverage (partial)

name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.target
doc: Final endpoint of an oriented edge.

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.weight_mul_edgeResistance_eq_diag.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V]
  [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ)
  (hw : ∀ (e : E), 0 ≤ w e) (e : E) : w e * o.edgeResistance w e = NLAlib.rangeProjector (o.weightedIncidence w) e e
name: NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.weight_mul_edgeResistance_eq_diag
doc:
Weighted effective resistance is exactly the corresponding projector diagonal.
Source: Spielman–Srivastava.
atlas: laplacian-resistance-leverage (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.weight_mul_edgeResistance_mem_Icc.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V]
  [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ)
  (hw : ∀ (e : E), 0 ≤ w e) (e : E) : w e * o.edgeResistance w e ∈ Set.Icc 0 1

doc:
Every edge leverage lies between zero and one.
Source: Spielman–Srivastava.
atlas: laplacian-resistance-leverage (partial)

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.weightedIncidence.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [DecidableEq V]

NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.weightedIncidence_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V]
  [DecidableEq V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (o : NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation G E) (w : E → ℝ) (x : V → ℝ) (e : E) :

signature:
NLAlib.GraphEdgeOrientation.weightedIncidence_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype V]

With strictly positive weights, the weighted incidence kernel imposes

name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev
doc:
A probability measure satisfies the Euclidean logarithmic Sobolev inequality with
constant `c` if `Ent(g²)≤2c∫|∇g|²` for every `C¹` test function whose displayed integrals
are finite. The gradient is the standard coordinate Dirichlet form.
Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.1; atlas `herbst` (general LSI premise).

signature:

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (ι → ℝ)} {c : ℝ} (self : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c) (g : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) :
  ContDiff ℝ 1 g →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2) μ →
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2)) μ →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ g x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2) μ →
          ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2) ∂μ -
              (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
            2 * c * ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ g x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2 ∂μ
name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.inequality

signature:

  (hLSI : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c) (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
  (hf2 : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => f x ^ 2) μ)
  (hdf : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ f x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2) μ) :
  ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), f x ^ 2 * Real.log (f x ^ 2) ∂μ - (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), f x ^ 2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), f x ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
    2 * c * ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ f x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2 ∂μ
name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.inequality_of_integrable
doc:
The Euclidean LSI inequality for every `C¹` function of finite square and Dirichlet
energy, with entropy integrability automatically discharged.
Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.1; atlas `gaussian-log-sobolev`, `herbst`.

signature:
NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.integrable_sq_mul_log_sq.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

Dirichlet energy are integrable. Thus the finite-entropy testing convention in the

truncations and Fatou. Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.1; atlas `gaussian-log-sobolev`, `herbst`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)) (x : n → ℝ) :
  Prop
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer
doc:
`x` minimises the objective `E` over the affine space `x₀ + S`: `x − x₀ ∈ S` and
`E x ≤ E (x₀ + y)` for every `y ∈ S`. Minimising Krylov methods (CG, GMRES, MINRES, LSQR,
sketched GMRES) are instances with `S` a Krylov space. Non-uniqueness is harmless: theorems
quantify over every minimiser. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §5.1 (optimality of projection
methods); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.apply_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}
  {x' : n → ℝ} (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer E x₀ S x) (hx' : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer E x₀ S x') : E x = E x'
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.apply_eq
doc:
Two minimisers over the same affine space have the same value.
Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer E x₀ (NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) x)
  (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  E x ≤ E (xs + ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs))
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_aeval
doc:
**K1, error form.** If `x` minimises any objective `E` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` and
`A x⋆ = c`, then `E x ≤ E (x⋆ + p(A)(x₀ − x⋆))` for every residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`). No hypothesis on `A` or `E`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Thm 6.29 (proof); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (proof); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (consumer: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound`).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_aeval_residual
doc:
**K1, residual form.** If `x` minimises an objective of the projResidual,
`y ↦ F (c − A y)`, over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then `F (c − A x) ≤ F (p(A) r₀)` for every
residual polynomial `p`. No solution `x⋆` is needed (GMRES on singular or inconsistent
systems). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32 (proof); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.3.
Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (consumer: `gmres-def`).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_of_le
doc:
**Monotonicity.** A minimiser over a larger space is at least as good:
`S ≤ S'` gives `E x' ≤ E x`. With `S = K_q`, `S' = K_{q+1}` this is monotonicity of a
minimising Krylov method in the iteration count. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6
(GMRES residuals are nonincreasing).

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_of_sub_mem.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}
  (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer E x₀ S x) {z : n → ℝ} (hz : z - x₀ ∈ S) : E x ≤ E z
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_of_sub_mem
doc:
A minimiser beats every point of the affine space: `z − x₀ ∈ S → E x ≤ E z`.
Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_self.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}
  (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer E x₀ S x) : E x ≤ E x₀
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer.le_self
doc: A minimiser beats the starting point: `E x ≤ E x₀`. Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsBestFrobRankApprox.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (k : ℕ) (Y : Matrix m n 𝕜) : Prop

doc:
`Y` is a **best rank-`k` approximation of `A` in the Frobenius norm**: `rank Y ≤ k` and
`‖A − Y‖_F ≤ ‖A − Z‖_F` for every `Z` of rank at most `k`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.4.8
(Eckart–Young); HMT 2011, §2.1.
atlas: best-rank-approx-def

name: NLAlib.IsBestFrobRankApprox.frobSq_sub_eq_bestRankFrobSq
doc:
Every best Frobenius rank-`k` approximation attains the optimal error `bestRankFrobSq A k`.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.
atlas: eckart-young-frobenius

name: NLAlib.IsBestFrobRankApprox.frobSq_sub_mul_le_bestRankFrobSq_add_frobSq_residual
doc:
Every best rank-`k` approximation of the compressed matrix has lifted
squared error at most the actual global optimum plus projection error.
HMT 2011, §9.2; atlas `truncation-lemma` (ordinary projected component).
This uses arbitrary finite indices, including empty types, and all target ranks.
The full-matrix optimum is attained by the proved Eckart–Young theorem.
atlas: truncation-lemma-projected

name: NLAlib.IsBestFrobRankApprox.frobSq_sub_mul_le_bestRankFrobSq_add_two_mul_frobSq_residual
doc:
The two-residual ordinary projected-truncation bound for a compressed
Frobenius minimizer, on arbitrary finite indices. HMT 2011, §9.2;
atlas `truncation-lemma` (ordinary projected component).
atlas: truncation-lemma-projected

signature:
NLAlib.IsCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsCGIterate
doc:
`x` is a `q`-th conjugate-gradient iterate for `A x = c` from `x₀`: `x − x₀` lies in
`K_q(A, c − A x₀)` and `x` minimises `cgObjective A c` over `x₀ + K_q(A, c − A x₀)`, i.e.
`IsAffineMinimizer (cgObjective A c) x₀ (krylovSpace A (c − A x₀) q) x`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2 (variational form).
Why a predicate: the method is defined by the optimality condition that pins down its iterate
(unique for `A ≻ 0`, `existsUnique_isCGIterate`), not by the recurrence that computes it; the
Hestenes–Stiefel recursion is the witness (`isCGIterate_cgRecurrence`), and every convergence
theorem quantifies over all iterates. Right-hand side convention (all Krylov solvers): the system
is `A x = c`, since `b` names a Krylov starting vector; the rectangular least-squares problem
`min ‖b − A x‖` (`IsCGLSIterate`) keeps the data name `b`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate
doc:
`x` is a `q`-th CGLS (equivalently, in exact arithmetic, LSQR) iterate for
`min ‖b − A x‖` from `x₀`: it minimises `‖b − Ay‖²` over `x₀ + K_q(AᵀA, Aᵀ(b − Ax₀))`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3 (CGNR); Paige–Saunders (1982) [`ps82`]. Deviation: a
predicate, not the Golub–Kahan recurrence.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

name: NLAlib.IsCholesky

doc:
A matrix with a Cholesky factorization is positive definite (`L` invertible, so
`xᵀ A x = ‖Lᵀ x‖² > 0` for `x ≠ 0`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 23.1 (converse direction).

signature: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation (ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ) (F : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation
doc:
An finite positive measure represents `F` by exponentials and is
concentrated on `[a,b]`. This records a representation, not its existence.
Source: Stahl, Theorems 1–2; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (interface).

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.add
doc:
Adding two compactly supported positive exponential measures adds their
represented functions while preserving the common support interval.

NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.ae_mem_Icc {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (self : NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation ν F a b) : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂↑ν, x ∈ Set.Icc a b
name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.ae_mem_Icc
doc:
The representing measure is concentrated on the specified interval.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.analyticAt {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (h : NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation ν F a b) (t : ℝ) : AnalyticAt ℝ F t
name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.analyticAt
doc:
The represented function is real analytic at every real parameter.
Source: compact-support exponential integrability and Mathlib's analytic MGF
theorem; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (consequence).

signature:
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.contDiff {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.contDiff
doc:
Positive compact exponential transforms are smooth, in every finite or
infinite differentiability order.

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.exp_mul_iteratedDeriv_even_zero_le
doc:
For nonnegative time the lower support endpoint bounds every even derivative
from below. Source: Stahl's representation; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl`
(consequence).
atlas: trace-exponential-stahl (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.integrable_exp {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (h : NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation ν F a b) (t : ℝ) : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (t * x)) ↑ν
name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.integrable_exp
doc:
Compact support gives exponential integrability at every real parameter.
Source: boundedness on an interval; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.integrable_pow_mul_exp
doc:
The moment integrands are integrable for every derivative order and real
parameter. Source: compact support; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.integral_exp {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.integral_exp
doc:
The exponential transform is the represented function at every real parameter.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.iteratedDeriv_eq_integral
doc:
Every derivative is the corresponding exponentially tilted moment. No
probability normalization is required. Source: compact-support differentiation
in Stahl's representation; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (consequence).
atlas: trace-exponential-stahl (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.iteratedDeriv_even_le_exp_mul_zero
doc:
For nonnegative time the upper support endpoint bounds every even derivative
from above. Source: Stahl's representation; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl`
(consequence).
atlas: trace-exponential-stahl (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.iteratedDeriv_even_nonneg {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (h : NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation ν F a b) (r : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv (2 * r) F t
name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.iteratedDeriv_even_nonneg
doc:
All even derivatives of a positive exponential representation are nonnegative.
Source: Stahl's representation; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (consequence).

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.le_add_deriv_add_iteratedDeriv_two_mul_coefficient
doc:
An upper support bound controls the exact second-order Taylor remainder.
The coefficient remains defined at a zero upper support endpoint.
Source: Tropp (2026), BMV one-summand replacement argument.

NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.measureReal_univ_eq {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ} {F : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}

Evaluation at zero identifies the total mass, including the zero measure.
Source: Stahl, Theorems 1–2; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (consequence).

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.mem_interior_integrableExpSet
doc:
The full real line lies in the interior of the exponential-integrability set.
Source: compact support; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

name: NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.mk
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.mono
doc:
Widening the support interval preserves an representation.
Source: monotonicity of concentration; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.IsCompactExpRepresentation.two_mul_zero_add_iteratedDeriv_two_le_add {ν : MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure ℝ}

Symmetrizing a positive exponential transform gives its exact quadratic
Taylor lower bound, with all odd terms removed before any expectation.
Source: Tropp (2026), Gaussian one-summand lower comparison.

NLAlib.IsCompleteIrreducibleFamily.{u, v} {G : Type u} [Group G] {P : Type v} {D : P → Type u}

A complete family lists, up to equivalence, every finite-dimensional

NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]

A matrix is diagonalizable if an invertible eigenvector matrix

NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable.finrank_eigenspace_eq_rootMultiplicity.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
A diagonalizable matrix's geometric and algebraic multiplicities agree
at every scalar. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 1.4.10; a scalar
outside the spectrum has both multiplicities zero.

signature:
NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable.isSemisimple.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]

name: NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable.isSemisimple
doc:
A diagonalizable matrix induces a semisimple endomorphism over any field.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Definition 1.4.4 and Theorem 1.4.10; the distinct
linear eigenvalue factors give a squarefree annihilating polynomial.
atlas: diagonalizable-def (partial)

NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable.of_surjective_intertwiner.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]

signature:
NLAlib.IsFullQR.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜) (Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) 𝕜)
  (R : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsFullQR
doc:
**Full QR factorization**: `A = QR` with `Q : m × m` unitary (orthogonal over `ℝ`)
and `R : m × n` upper
trapezoidal. No relation between `m` and `n` is assumed. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7 (full QR);
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.1.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsFullQR.conjTranspose_mul_eq.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜}

name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.conjTranspose_mul_eq
doc: The `R` of a full QR is `Qᴴ A`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsFullQR.eq.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜}
  {Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) 𝕜} {R : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜} (self : NLAlib.IsFullQR A Q R) : A = Q * R
name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.eq
doc: The factorization `A = QR`.

name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.isQR_castLE
doc:
**Thin QR from full QR**: if `n ≤ m`, the first `n` columns of `Q` and the first `n` rows
of `R` form a thin QR. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7 (reduced from full QR); Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Thm 5.2.3 (proof).
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.mk

signature:
NLAlib.IsFullQR.mul_conjTranspose_self.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜}
  {Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) 𝕜} {R : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsFullQR A Q R) : Q * Q.conjTranspose = 1
name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.mul_conjTranspose_self
doc: The `Q` of a full QR is unitary on both sides: `Q Qᴴ = I`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.1.

name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.orth
doc: `Q` is unitary, `Qᴴ Q = I`.

name: NLAlib.IsFullQR.upper
doc: `R` is upper trapezoidal.

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate
doc:
`x` is a GMRES iterate: `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` (`r₀ = c − A x₀`) and `x` minimises
`‖c − A y‖²` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`. MINRES is this predicate for symmetric `A`.
Why a predicate: the method is its least-squares optimality condition (existence
`exists_isGMRESIterate`, uniqueness for invertible `A` `IsGMRESIterate.eq_of_isUnit`); the
Arnoldi realisation is `NLAlib.Krylov.Solvers.GMRESArnoldi`. The system is `A x = c` (see
`IsCGIterate`).
Source: Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §2; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5;
KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eigenvalues_mem_Icc.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eigenvalues_mem_Icc
doc:
**MINRES, definite case (Chebyshev rate).** If `A` is symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`, then `‖r_q‖ ≤ 2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q ‖r₀‖` (squared form).
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Liesen–Strakoš (2013) [`ls13`], §5.6.
atlas: minres-bound (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} {V W : Matrix n n ℝ} {d : n → ℝ} (hVW : V * W = 1)
  (hAd : A = V * Matrix.diagonal d * W) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ (i : n), |Polynomial.eval (d i) p| ≤ M) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤
    (NLAlib.specNorm V * NLAlib.specNorm W * M) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul
doc:
**GMRES bound for real diagonalisable `A`.** If `A = V diag(d) W` with `V W = 1` (so
`W = V⁻¹` and the `dᵢ` are the eigenvalues), then for every residual polynomial `p` with
`|p(dᵢ)| ≤ M`, `‖r_q‖ ≤ ‖V‖₂ ‖V⁻¹‖₂ M ‖r₀‖` (squared form).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 35.2;
Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.4.
Deviation: real eigenvalues and a real eigenvector matrix only (the printed statement allows a
complex diagonalisation, `κ(V) max |p(λᵢ)|` over the complex spectrum, which is the nonnormal
case of interest; it is not available over `ℝ` and enters as a hypothesis on
`A.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)` when a consumer needs it). The constant `‖V‖₂ ‖V⁻¹‖₂` is the source's.
atlas: gmres-diagonalizable (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_sq_mul_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) {M : ℝ}
  (hM : ∀ (i : n), |Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p| ≤ M) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤ M ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_sq_mul_of_isHermitian
doc:
**MINRES spectral bound.** For symmetric `A` and every residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, the GMRES (= MINRES) residual
satisfies `‖r_q‖² ≤ M² ‖r₀‖²`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Paige–Saunders
(1975) [`ps75`].
Deviation: no invertibility of `A` and no solution `x⋆` needed (the bound is on residuals).
atlas: minres-bound (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.eq_of_isUnit
doc:
**The GMRES iterate is unique for invertible `A`.** Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval
doc:
**Polynomial form of the residual**: `c − A x = p(A) r₀` for a residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6; Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 35.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.isLeast_dotProduct_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  IsLeast
    {v |
      ∃ p,
        p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧
          Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧
            v = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)}
    ((c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x))
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.isLeast_dotProduct_aeval
doc:
**`‖r_q‖² = min_{p ∈ 𝒫_q⁰} ‖p(A) r₀‖²`**: the squared GMRES residual is the least value of
`‖p(A) r₀‖²` over residual polynomials. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35 (GMRES as a polynomial approximation problem).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤
    ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_aeval
doc:
**GMRES beats every residual polynomial**: `‖r_q‖² ≤ ‖p(A) r₀‖²` for every `p` with
`deg p ≤ q` and `p(0) = 1`. No hypothesis on `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32
(proof); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 35.2 (proof).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_of_le
doc:
**GMRES residuals are nonincreasing**: for `q ≤ q'`, `‖r_{q'}‖² ≤ ‖r_q‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq
doc:
**The GMRES residual is unique**: two GMRES iterates for the same data have the same
residual `c − A x`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1 (the residual is the orthogonal
projection of `r₀` onto `(A K_q)^⟂`).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : IsUnit A) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x)
  (hq : NLAlib.krylovGrade A (c - A.mulVec x₀) ≤ q) : c - A.mulVec x = 0
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**Finite termination.** For invertible `A`, a GMRES iterate with `q` at least the grade
`ν = krylovGrade A r₀` solves the system: `c − A x = 0`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Prop 6.10 (no breakdown before the solution) and §6.5.6; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature: NLAlib.IsGradedColumnBasis.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A Q : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsGradedColumnBasis
doc:
`Q` is a **graded orthonormal basis of the column flag of `A`**: `Q` has orthonormal columns
and, for each `k`, its first `k + 1` columns span the first `k + 1` columns of `A`. The analogue

doc:
`Q` is a **graded orthonormal Krylov basis** of `(A, b)`: its columns are orthonormal and for
every `i < q` the first `i + 1` columns span `K_{i+1}(A, b)`. Equivalently (`of_mem`), the

doc:
`A = Q H Qᵀ` is a **Hessenberg form** of `A`: `Q` orthogonal and `H` upper Hessenberg.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 26 (`A = Q H Q*`); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.3 (`QᵀAQ = H`).

doc: The similarity `A = Q H Qᵀ`.

name: NLAlib.IsHessenbergForm.eq_arnoldiMatrix
doc:
Under the usual positive-subdiagonal convention, the orthogonal factor
of a Hessenberg reduction is exactly the canonical Arnoldi matrix. Before
normalization the preceding graded-basis theorem identifies its columns up
to signs by `ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign`.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsHessenbergForm.exists_sign {n : ℕ} {A Q₁ H₁ Q₂ H₂ : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ}
  (h₁ : NLAlib.IsHessenbergForm A Q₁ H₁) (h₂ : NLAlib.IsHessenbergForm A Q₂ H₂) (hcol : Q₁.col 0 = Q₂.col 0)
  (hH : NLAlib.IsUnreducedHessenberg H₁) :
  ∃ d,
    (∀ (i : Fin (n + 1)), d i = 1 ∨ d i = -1) ∧
      d 0 = 1 ∧ Q₂ = Q₁ * Matrix.diagonal d ∧ H₂ = Matrix.diagonal d * H₁ * Matrix.diagonal d
name: NLAlib.IsHessenbergForm.exists_sign
doc:
**Implicit Q theorem**: two Hessenberg forms with equal first orthogonal columns and
an unreduced first Hessenberg matrix differ by a diagonal sign matrix, whose first entry is one.
Source: Golub–Van Loan 2013, Theorem 7.4.2; matrix toolkit rederivations, `lem:intertwine`.
The oriented equation `H₂(Q₂ᵀQ₁)=(Q₂ᵀQ₁)H₁` uses precisely the given unreduced matrix.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction (partial)

doc:
**LU factorization**: `A = L U` with `L` unit lower triangular and `U` upper triangular.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2.
atlas: lu-decomposition

signature:
NLAlib.IsLU.det_eq_prod.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A L U : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (h : NLAlib.IsLU A L U) : A.det = ∏ i, U i i
name: NLAlib.IsLU.det_eq_prod
doc: For an LU factorization, `det A = ∏ᵢ uᵢᵢ`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsLU.eq_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A L U : Matrix n n ℝ} (self : NLAlib.IsLU A L U) :
  A = L * U

NLAlib.IsLU.eq_mul_diagonal_mul_transpose.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A L U : Matrix n n ℝ}

name: NLAlib.IsLU.eq_mul_diagonal_mul_transpose
doc:
A symmetric unit-lower LU factorization is the corresponding LDL transpose
factorization, with the actual upper factor's diagonal as pivots.
Source: matrix-toolkit derivations, Lemma “Symmetric LU needs no second elimination
algorithm”; Golub–Van Loan, §8.4.1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsLU.isUnitLowerTriangular.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A L U : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (self : NLAlib.IsLU A L U) : NLAlib.IsUnitLowerTriangular L
name: NLAlib.IsLU.isUnitLowerTriangular
doc: `L` is unit lower triangular.

signature:
NLAlib.IsLU.isUpperTriangular.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A L U : Matrix n n ℝ}

name: NLAlib.IsLU.isUpperTriangular
doc: `U` is upper triangular.

signature:
NLAlib.IsLU.leadingMinor_eq_prod {n : ℕ} {A L U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsLU A L U) (k : ℕ)
  (hk : k ≤ n) : NLAlib.leadingMinor A k = ∏ i, U (Fin.castLE hk i) (Fin.castLE hk i)
name: NLAlib.IsLU.leadingMinor_eq_prod
doc:
For an LU factorization the leading principal minors are the partial products of the
pivots: `det A(1:k,1:k) = ∏_{i<k} uᵢᵢ`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, proof of Thm 3.2.1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsLU.leadingSubmatrix {n : ℕ} {A L U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsLU A L U) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
  NLAlib.IsLU (NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix A k) (NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix L k) (NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix U k)
name: NLAlib.IsLU.leadingSubmatrix
doc:
Leading blocks of an LU factorization form an LU factorization of the leading block:
`A(1:k,1:k) = L(1:k,1:k) U(1:k,1:k)`, since `L` vanishes above and `U` below the diagonal.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, proof of Thm 3.2.1.

name: NLAlib.IsLU.mk

name: NLAlib.IsLU.unique
doc:
**Uniqueness of the LU factorization** of an invertible matrix. Proof: `L'⁻¹ L = U' U⁻¹` is
unit lower and upper triangular, hence the identity. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.2.1;
Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor. 3.5.6; Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20.
atlas: lu-decomposition

signature:
NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution
doc:
`x` is a (linear) least-squares solution of `A x ≈ b`: it minimises the Euclidean residual
`‖b - A y‖₂` over all `y`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11 (problem (11.2)); Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§5.3.1. Every `A` admits one (`isLeastSquaresSolution_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec`).
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations

signature:
NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.norm_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {x : n → ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x) :
  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b)‖ ≤ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖
name: NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.norm_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec_le
doc:
**Minimum-norm solution.** Among all least-squares solutions, `A⁺ b` has the smallest
Euclidean norm: `‖A⁺ b‖ ≤ ‖x‖`, since `x = A⁺ b + z` with `A z = 0` and `A⁺ b ⟂ ker A`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.5.2 (eq. (5.5.6)); Trefethen–Bau 1997, Exercise 11.2.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.norm_sub_mulVec_sq_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {x : n → ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x) :
  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (b - A.mulVec x)‖ ^ 2 = ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖ ^ 2 - ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (A.mulVec x)‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.norm_sub_mulVec_sq_eq
doc:
**Residual identity.** For a least-squares solution, `‖b - A x‖² = ‖b‖² - ‖A x‖²`
(Pythagoras, `b = A x + r` with `r ⟂ A x`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11; Golub–Van Loan
2013, §5.3.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.norm_sub_mulVec_sq_eq_of_eq_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A Q : Matrix m n ℝ} {R : Matrix n n ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hA : A = Q * R) (hR : IsUnit R) {b : m → ℝ} {x : n → ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x) :
  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (b - A.mulVec x)‖ ^ 2 = ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖ ^ 2 - ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (Q.transpose.mulVec b)‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.norm_sub_mulVec_sq_eq_of_eq_mul
doc:
**Residual via thin QR.** If `A = Q R` with `QᵀQ = I` and `R` invertible, the least-squares
residual satisfies `‖b - A x‖² = ‖b‖² - ‖Qᵀ b‖²`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11; Golub–Van Loan
2013, §5.3.3 (eq. (5.3.6)).
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.sub_mulVec_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {x : n → ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x) :
  b - A.mulVec x = (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution.sub_mulVec_eq
doc:
The least-squares residual is `(I - A A⁺) b`, for every least-squares solution.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11 (`r = (I - P) b`).
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

directions where the data and penalty kernels have trivial intersection.

name: NLAlib.IsMonicOrthogonalPolynomial
doc:
A monic degree-`n` polynomial orthogonal to all lower degrees for the bilinear
moment functional. Source: Gautschi (2004), Chapter 1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsMonicOrthogonalPolynomial.eq_of_hankelMomentDet_ne_zero.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜]

Two monic orthogonal polynomials coincide whenever the finite Hankel matrix
at their order is nonsingular. Source: Gautschi (2004), Section 1.3.

Monic orthogonality is unique whenever its lower-degree bilinear pairing is
nondegenerate. This includes complex formal functionals with isotropic vectors.

name: NLAlib.IsMonicOrthogonalPolynomial.eq_of_nonzero_sq
doc:
Two monic orthogonal polynomials of the same degree coincide if all lower-degree
nonzero polynomials have nonzero squared bilinear norm. This applies to positive real
moment functionals and does not require an inner-product-space instance.

signature:
NLAlib.IsMonicOrthogonalPolynomial.functional_mul_X_pow_eq_sq.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜] {L : Polynomial 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜}

Multiplying a monic orthogonal polynomial by its leading monomial gives its
squared bilinear norm, since their difference has lower degree.

same degree gives its squared bilinear norm.

name: NLAlib.IsMonicOrthogonalPolynomial.functional_sq_ne_zero

If the next moment system is nonsingular, the squared bilinear norm of a
monic orthogonal polynomial is nonzero, even for complex formal functionals.

signature:
NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (B : Matrix n m 𝕜) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse
doc:
The four Penrose identities for a matrix and a candidate pseudoinverse, over `ℝ` or `ℂ`:
`A B A = A`, `B A B = B`, and `A B`, `B A` are Hermitian. No rank assumption is imposed.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.
atlas: pseudoinverse

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.conjTranspose
doc:
Conjugate-transposing both matrices preserves the Penrose identities.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.conjTranspose_inv_mul_eq
doc: The row-space projector is Hermitian.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.conjTranspose_mul_eq
doc: The image-space projector is Hermitian.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse of a column Gram matrix is the corresponding
Gram matrix of the inverse: `(AᴴA)⁺ = A⁺A⁺ᴴ`. This identity holds at every rank.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.inv_mul_inv_eq
doc: The second Penrose identity, `B A B = B`.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.inv_mul_isIdempotentElem
doc: `B A` is an idempotent row-space projector.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.kronecker
doc:
Tensoring two matrices and their Moore–Penrose inverses preserves all four
Penrose equations. Horn–Johnson 1991, Section 4.2; rank deficient matrices are allowed.

signature:
NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.mk.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {B : Matrix n m 𝕜} (mul_mul_eq : A * B * A = A) (inv_mul_inv_eq : B * A * B = B)
  (conjTranspose_mul_eq : (A * B).conjTranspose = A * B) (conjTranspose_inv_mul_eq : (B * A).conjTranspose = B * A) :
  NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse A B
name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.mk
NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.mulVec_eq_self_iff
doc:
The fixed vectors of the image-space projector are exactly the image of
the original matrix, including rank-deficient and empty matrices.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.mul_isIdempotentElem
doc:
`A B` is an idempotent image-space projector. Together with the third
Penrose identity this is an orthogonal projector.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.mul_mul_eq
doc: The first Penrose identity, `A B A = A`.

name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.range_mul_eq
doc:
The image of `A B` equals the image of `A`: the Hermitian idempotent
`A B` is the orthogonal projector onto the original column space.

signature:
NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.specNorm_one_sub_inv_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {A' : Matrix n m ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse A A') :
  NLAlib.specNorm (1 - A' * A) ≤ 1
name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.specNorm_one_sub_inv_mul_le
doc: `‖I - A' A‖₂ ≤ 1` for a Moore–Penrose pair: `I - A' A` is a symmetric idempotent.

signature:
NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.specNorm_one_sub_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

NLAlib.IsQR.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

doc:
**Thin QR factorization**: `A = QR` with `Q : m × n` having orthonormal columns and
`R : n × n` upper triangular. The phases of `R_ii` are not fixed (see `IsQR.diagonal_mul`); the
alternative convention `R_ii ≥ 0` is a separate conjunct where it is needed (`exists_isQR`).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7 (reduced QR); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.3 (thin QR).
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

doc:
`Qᴴ A = R`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

NLAlib.IsQR.conjTranspose_mul_self_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]

doc:
`Aᴴ A = Rᴴ R`: `Rᴴ` is a (Cholesky) triangular factor of the Gram matrix `AᴴA`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 11 (normal equations via QR); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.det_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

doc: `det R = ∏ R_ii` (Mathlib's `det_of_isUpperTriangular`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.diagonal_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.IsQR.diagonal_mul
doc:
**Unit-phase change**: multiplying `Q` on the right by a diagonal unitary matrix and
`R` on the left by its adjoint gives another thin QR. Real signs are a special case.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 7.1 (proof, sign choice);
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [LinearOrder n] {A Q : Matrix m n 𝕜} {R : Matrix n n 𝕜} (self : NLAlib.IsQR A Q R) : A = Q * R
name: NLAlib.IsQR.eq
doc: The factorization `A = QR`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.eq_of_diag_pos.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n]
  {A Q₁ Q₂ : Matrix m n ℝ} {R₁ R₂ : Matrix n n ℝ} (h₁ : NLAlib.IsQR A Q₁ R₁) (h₂ : NLAlib.IsQR A Q₂ R₂)
  (hR₁ : ∀ (i : n), 0 < R₁ i i) (hR₂ : ∀ (i : n), 0 < R₂ i i) : Q₁ = Q₂ ∧ R₁ = R₂
name: NLAlib.IsQR.eq_of_diag_pos
doc:
**Uniqueness of the thin QR with positive diagonal**: two thin QR factorizations of the same
`A` whose `R` factors have positive diagonals coincide. (Positivity of the diagonal forces full
column rank, so no separate rank hypothesis is needed.) Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 7.2;
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.3. Proof: `T := Q₂ᵀQ₁` satisfies `T R₁ = R₂` and
`Tᵀ R₂ = R₁` (`IsQR.conjTranspose_mul_eq`), so `T = R₂R₁⁻¹` and `Tᵀ = R₁R₂⁻¹` are both upper
triangular, hence `T` is diagonal, with `T_ii R₁ii = R₂ii`, `T_ii R₂ii = R₁ii`, so `T_ii² = 1`,
`T_ii > 0`; thus `T = I`, `R₂ = R₁` and `Q₂ = A R₂⁻¹ = Q₁`.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsQR.isGradedColumnBasis
doc:
**Every thin QR with invertible `R` is a graded basis of the column flag**: `A = QR` with
`R` upper triangular and `R_ii ≠ 0` gives `span(q_0, …, q_k) = span(a_0, …, a_k)`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (7.1)–(7.2); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.3. Proof: `A = QR` and
`Q = AR⁻¹` with `R⁻¹` upper triangular (`col_mul_mem_span_image_Iic`).
atlas: gram-schmidt

name: NLAlib.IsQR.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff
doc:
**Least squares via `IsQR`.** For a thin QR factorization `IsQR A Q R` with nonzero diagonal
(`R_ii ≠ 0`, i.e. full column rank), the least-squares solution is `x = R⁻¹ Qᵀ b`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11, Algorithm 11.2; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.3.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.isUnit_conjTranspose_mul_self_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]

  IsUnit (A.conjTranspose * A) ↔ ∀ (i : n), R i i ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.IsQR.isUnit_conjTranspose_mul_self_iff
doc:
**Full column rank iff nonzero diagonal**: `AᴴA` is invertible iff every `R_ii ≠ 0`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 7.2 (proof); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsQR.isUnit_det_iff
doc: `R` is invertible iff its diagonal has no zero. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.mk.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

NLAlib.IsQR.mul_conjTranspose_eq
doc:
**`QQᴴ` is the orthogonal projector onto `range A`**: `QQᴴ = AA⁺` under full column rank.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 6–7; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.mul_eq_transpose_mul_mul {n : ℕ} {H Q R : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsQR H Q R) :

doc:
For a square QR, `RQ = QᵀHQ` (`R = QᵀH`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.3.1 (the QR step is an
orthogonal similarity).

**Residual via `IsQR`.** For `IsQR A Q R` with nonzero diagonal and a least-squares solution
`x`, `‖b - A x‖² = ‖b‖² - ‖Qᵀ b‖²`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.3.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.orth.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.IsQR.range_mulVecLin_eq
doc:
`range A = range Q` when `R` is invertible. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7 (the columns of `Q`
span the column flag); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsQR.submatrix_rows
doc:
**Row reindexing**: a thin QR of `A` transports along any bijection of the row index.
Bridge from `Fin` to general `Fintype` row indices.

signature:
NLAlib.IsQR.upper.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

signature: NLAlib.IsRealNormalForm {k : ℕ} (T : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsRealNormalForm
doc:
A real normal form has the real Schur block pattern and opposite
off-diagonal entries. Thus it is a direct sum of real scalar blocks and
blocks `[[a,b],[-b,a]]` with `b≠0`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.5.4.

signature: NLAlib.IsRealSchurForm {k : ℕ} (T : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsRealSchurForm
doc:
A real Schur matrix is upper quasitriangular and each nonscalar block
has shape `[[a,b],[c,a]]` with `bc<0`. The nonzero subdiagonal selects its
two-dimensional blocks. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.3.1;
the corrected form in derivations equation (G1).

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜) (V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsSVD
doc:
`IsSVD A U V` for `A : Matrix m n 𝕜`: `U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜` and `V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜`
are unitary (orthogonal over `ℝ`; so `p = card m`, `q = card n`) and `A = U Σ Vᴴ` with
`Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)` (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1). The `k`-th
columns of `U` and `V` are the left/right singular vectors for `σ_k`. At `m = Fin a`, `n = Fin b`
the factors are square, `U : Matrix (Fin a) (Fin a) 𝕜`. Over `ℝ`, `Uᴴ` is definitionally `Uᵀ`,
so the fields elaborate against the `ᵀ` forms. Atlas `svd`.
atlas: svd-def

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜} {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜}
  (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (i : m) (j : n) :
  A i j = ∑ k, ↑(NLAlib.singularValues A ↑k) * U i (Fin.castLE ⋯ k) * star (V j (Fin.castLE ⋯ k))
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.apply
doc:
Thin-SVD / outer-product expansion, entrywise:
`A i j = ∑_{k < min p q} σ_k U_{ik} conj(V_{jk})`, i.e. `A = ∑_k σ_k u_k v_kᴴ`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.card_left
doc: The left factor of an SVD is square: `p = card m`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.card_right
doc: The right factor of an SVD is square: `q = card n`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜}
  {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) :
  A.conjTranspose = V * NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A) * U.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_eq
doc: `Aᴴ = V Σᴴ Uᴴ`: an SVD of the conjugate transpose. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜}
  {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) :
  U.conjTranspose * A = NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A) * V.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul
doc: `Uᴴ A = Σ Vᴴ`, i.e. `Aᴴ uₖ = σₖ vₖ`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul_left
doc: `U` has orthonormal columns: `UᴴU = I`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

  {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) :
  U.conjTranspose * A * V = NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul_mul
doc: `Uᴴ A V = Σ`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul_right
doc: `V` has orthonormal columns: `VᴴV = I`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜}
  {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) :
  A.conjTranspose * A = (V * Matrix.diagonal fun j => ↑(NLAlib.singularValues A ↑j ^ 2)) * V.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
`AᴴA = V diag(σ₀², …, σ_{q-1}²) Vᴴ`: the right singular vectors diagonalize the Gram matrix
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.coupled_residual_headColumns_left {m n k p : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
  (Uhat : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin p) ℝ) (Vhat : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin p) ℝ) (T : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ) :
  (A - h.truncatedMatrix k) * NLAlib.projResidual (NLAlib.headColumns V hkn) Vhat -
      NLAlib.projResidual (NLAlib.headColumns U hkm) Uhat * T =
    NLAlib.projResidual (NLAlib.headColumns U hkm) (A * Vhat - Uhat * T)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.coupled_residual_headColumns_left
doc:
The first ambient complementary singular residual equation is exact.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; no spectral separation is assumed for the identity.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.coupled_residual_headColumns_right {m n k p : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
  (Uhat : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin p) ℝ) (Vhat : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin p) ℝ) (T : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ) :
  (A - h.truncatedMatrix k).transpose * NLAlib.projResidual (NLAlib.headColumns U hkm) Uhat -
      NLAlib.projResidual (NLAlib.headColumns V hkn) Vhat * T =
    NLAlib.projResidual (NLAlib.headColumns V hkn) (A.transpose * Uhat - Vhat * T)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.coupled_residual_headColumns_right
doc:
The second ambient complementary singular residual equation is exact.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; unmatched rectangular null directions are retained.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.det_gram_mul_submatrix_eq_prod_sq_singularValues {m n k : ℕ} {T : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}

    ∏ i, NLAlib.singularValues T ↑i ^ 2

doc:
The top right singular frame attains the product of the first `k` squared
singular values as its image Gram determinant. Horn's product proof, SVD step.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.eq
doc: The factorization `A = U Σ Vᴴ`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜}
  {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (k : ℕ) :

    (U * NLAlib.rectDiag fun i => if i < k then NLAlib.singularValues A i else 0) * V.conjTranspose +
      (U * NLAlib.rectDiag fun i => if i < k then 0 else NLAlib.singularValues A i) * V.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail
doc:
Block SVD split at index `k` (HMT 2011, §2.1, `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᴴ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᴴ`): the head
`U Σ_{<k} Vᴴ` (the truncated SVD) plus the tail `U Σ_{≥k} Vᴴ`. Atlas `svd`.
atlas: svd

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.frobInner_mul_rectDiag_mul_conjTranspose
doc:
The Frobenius pairing with prescribed coefficients in the same SVD
frames is the singular-value dot product. Bhatia (1997), §IV.2.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.frobSq_sub_truncatedMatrix
doc:
The squared error of the truncated SVD is exactly the singular-value
tail, with no rank/dimension side conditions.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.gram_pow_mul_eq
doc:
An SVD diagonalizes every odd rectangular Gram power.
Source: HMT (2011), §10.4.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.headColumns_left_residual_eq_neg_mul {m n k : ℕ} {A E : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {Uhat : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} {Vhat : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hhat : NLAlib.IsSVD (A + E) Uhat Vhat)
  (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  (A * NLAlib.headColumns Vhat hkn -
      NLAlib.headColumns Uhat hkm * Matrix.diagonal fun i => NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) ↑i) =
    -(E * NLAlib.headColumns Vhat hkn)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.headColumns_left_residual_eq_neg_mul
doc:
The leading right-frame singular residual equals minus perturbation times
that frame. Wedin (1972), Section 3; the frames are from a SVD of `A+E`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.headColumns_projector_mul
doc:
The left leading-frame projector produces the truncation from the same SVD.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; the witness matching matters at singular-value ties.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.headColumns_right_residual_eq_neg_mul {m n k : ℕ} {A E : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {Uhat : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} {Vhat : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hhat : NLAlib.IsSVD (A + E) Uhat Vhat)
  (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  (A.transpose * NLAlib.headColumns Uhat hkm -
      NLAlib.headColumns Vhat hkn * Matrix.diagonal fun i => NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) ↑i) =
    -(E.transpose * NLAlib.headColumns Uhat hkm)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.headColumns_right_residual_eq_neg_mul
doc:
The transpose leading-frame residual is the paired perturbation residual.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; every rectangular null direction remains included.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.inv_eq {k : ℕ} {C U V : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD C U V) (hC : IsUnit C) :
  C⁻¹ = (V * Matrix.diagonal fun i => (NLAlib.singularValues C ↑i)⁻¹) * U.transpose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.inv_eq
doc:
Any SVD computes the ordinary inverse of an invertible square matrix.
Stewart–Sun §I.5; zero-size matrices are included.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.isBestFrobRankApprox_truncatedMatrix
doc:
**Frobenius Eckart–Young minimizer.** Truncating any SVD gives a
best rank-at-most-`k` approximation, rather than assuming a best-approximation
predicate. Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.isMoorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

An SVD `A = U Σ Vᴴ` produces the Moore–Penrose inverse `V Σ⁺ Uᴴ` by reciprocating the

signature:

    Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) U P *
        Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A))

Tensoring two SVD factorizations gives a full orthogonal factorization of the
Kronecker product. Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.15. The rectangular middle
factor need not be sorted in the lexicographic product-coordinate order.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

The leading singular-vector outer product has nuclear norm one and
attains the spectral pairing for every nonzero matrix.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

coordinates. Atlas: `svd`, `norm-lipschitz`.

The leading right singular frame maps to the leading left frame
through its ordered diagonal singular coefficient. Wedin (1972), Section 3.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_headColumns_projector

The right leading-frame projector gives the same matched truncation.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; all rectangular null directions remain in the tail.

The centered overlap Gram is diagonal in the right singular basis.
Stewart–Sun §I.5.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.rank_truncatedMatrix_le

The truncated SVD has rank at most its cutoff, including cutoff zero.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.residual_headColumns_eq_sub_truncatedMatrix

The left leading-frame residual is exactly the matched SVD tail.
Wedin (1972), Section 3.

The right leading-frame residual of the transpose is the transposed tail.
Wedin (1972), Section 3.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.schattenDualCoefficients_attain

In fixed SVD frames, the normalized power coefficients give a unit
conjugate Schatten norm and attain the source matrix norm.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.specNorm_sub_truncatedMatrix

**Spectral Eckart–Young, attainment for a given SVD.** The spectral error of truncating an
SVD after `k` terms is the `(k+1)`-st singular value (zero-indexed `σ_k`):
`‖A − U Σ_{<k} Vᴴ‖₂ = σ_k(A)`. All shapes and cutoffs are allowed (`σ_k = 0` for
`k ≥ min m n`). Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.9.1 (spectral case); HMT 2011, eq. (2.3) atlas `eckart-young`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.sub_truncatedMatrix_mul_headColumns_eq_zero
doc:
The matched SVD tail annihilates the selected right singular frame.
Wedin (1972), Section 3.

doc:
Tail multiplication on the complementary right coordinates is exactly the
left projected original multiplication. Wedin (1972), Section 3; the ambient
form includes every unmatched rectangular null direction.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.sub_truncatedMatrix_transpose_mul_residual_headColumns {m n k p : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.sub_truncatedMatrix_transpose_mul_residual_headColumns
doc:
The transpose tail satisfies the paired complementary-coordinate identity.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; no square-shape or nonempty-complement premise occurs.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.trace_conjTranspose_mul_mul_rectDiag_mul_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]

Pairing with prescribed coefficients in a matrix's own SVD frames gives
the exact full trace, as a real scalar in the coefficient field. In particular
the pairing has zero imaginary part over `ℂ`.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

the interpolation point in the full complex trace pairing. This includes

may exceed either matrix dimension; in that case padding handles the cutoff.

Transpose preserves the truncation matched to a supplied SVD witness.

witnesses are paired also at singular-value ties.

singular directions. Both triplet equations are required for a truncation.

inverse is the test map's adjoint. Both Gramian forms and their product are
balanced in these coordinates. The positive-definite full-state case in the
source is included; the biorthogonality already proves invertibility.

Positive retained singular triplets construct biorthogonal coordinates
and balance both compressed Gramian forms, even when directions are discarded.
Brunton–Kutz (2022), equations (9.29)–(9.35).
atlas: gramian-svd-balancing (partial)

doc:
A thin singular value factorization retains exactly the positive singular
directions. An ordering of the singular directions is unnecessary here.

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.canonicalPartialPolar_eq
doc:
Every thin SVD identifies the same canonical partial polar factor.
Zero singular directions contribute zero automatically.
Source: Horn–Johnson, §7.3.

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.card_le_of_markovParameters_eq
doc:
The dimension recovered by a full-state Hankel SVD is minimal among
all realizations matching those finite Markov data. This is the rank
obstruction, and requires no stability assumption on either realization.
atlas: hankel-svd-era-realization (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.dmdOperator_eq
doc:
With the entire thin SVD, the exact-mode factorization equals full
Moore–Penrose DMD. This bridge does not assert that an arbitrary truncation
equals full DMD. Tu et al. (2014), §2.
atlas: dmd-reduced-eigenpair-lifting (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.eq
doc: The factorization contains the entire matrix.

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.era_markovParameter
doc:
Exact full-state ERA preserves every Markov parameter, not only the
finite parameters used to construct its Hankel matrix.
atlas: hankel-svd-era-realization (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.era_similarity
doc:
The exact full-state ERA formulas give an invertible state-coordinate
change and preserve the realization by similarity. The SVD is of the actual
block Hankel matrix; no pre-assumed realization certificate is used.
Brunton–Kutz (2022), §9.3.
atlas: hankel-svd-era-realization (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.isSingularTripletFamily
doc: A full thin SVD is, in particular, a positive singular-triplet family.

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.landweberIterate_zero_eq
doc:
With zero initialization, the actual iteration is precisely the finite
Landweber spectral filter, including rank-deficient matrices.
atlas: landweber-spectral-filter (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.landweberStepMatrix_mul
doc:
Positive singular directions diagonalize the Landweber error multiplier,
and its complementary nullspace projection is fixed.

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.landweberStepMatrix_pow
doc:
Exact powers of the Landweber step: a fixed nullspace component and
the scalar powers `(1-ησ²)^t` in the positive singular subspace.
atlas: landweber-spectral-filter (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.left_orth
doc: The left singular directions are orthonormal.

NLAlib.IsThinSVD.moorePenroseInverse_eq

Reciprocating a thin singular factorization gives the full Moore–Penrose
inverse, at any matrix rank. Horn–Johnson, §7.3.

doc: The row-space projector from a thin SVD.

name: NLAlib.IsThinSVD.mul_moorePenroseInverse_eq

signature: NLAlib.IsUpperQuasiTriangular.{u_1} {k : ℕ} {K : Type u_1} [Zero K] (T : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) K) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsUpperQuasiTriangular
doc:
Upper quasitriangular means zeros below the first subdiagonal and no
two adjacent nonzero subdiagonal entries, giving consecutive diagonal blocks
of size at most two. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §2.3 and Theorem 2.6.2.
The predicate records the block zero pattern; any spectral restrictions on
the two-dimensional blocks are stated separately.

  {R T : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) K} (hT : NLAlib.IsUpperQuasiTriangular T) (hR : R.IsUpperTriangular) :
  NLAlib.IsUpperQuasiTriangular (R * T)
name: NLAlib.IsUpperQuasiTriangular.upperTriangular_mul
doc:
Left multiplication by an upper triangular matrix preserves upper
quasitriangularity and its block boundaries. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Theorem 2.6.2; this is the final real QR step for the second pencil factor.

A rectangular matrix is **upper trapezoidal** (upper triangular in the rectangular sense):
`R i j = 0` whenever `j < i`. For square matrices this is Mathlib's `IsUpperTriangular`
(`isUpperTrapezoidal_iff_isUpperTriangular`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2 (the `R` of a full QR).
