doc:
Assembly-shaped grade-preserving light estimate, with exactly the
`3*bTerm` right-hand side consumed by `ConcreteBandAssembly`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.offDiagonal_sum_le {ell : ℕ} (hell : 1 ≤ ell) (energy : Fin ell → ℝ)
  (cross : Fin ell → Fin ell → ℝ) (hcross : ∀ (i j : Fin ell), i ≠ j → cross i j ≤ (energy i + energy j) / 2) :
  ∑ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, cross i j ≤ (↑ell - 1) * ∑ i, energy i
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.offDiagonal_sum_le
doc:
Pairwise arithmetic behind the block-Gram estimate.

`cross i j` is the scalar contribution of the `(i,j)` block to one fixed
quadratic form, while `energy i` is the squared norm of the `i`th input block.
The premise is exactly the operator Cauchy--Schwarz estimate after
`2ab ≤ a²+b²`; no operator fact is hidden here.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorAbstract`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.BlockPattern T ell)
  (z : { z // NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.OrbitCompatible T ell out inp z }) :
  { z // NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.LegalLightMove (↑out) (↑inp) z }
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove
doc:
Forget labels from one compatible omitted-slot configuration, retaining
the target and source columns of the induced Pattern move.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove_injective {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.BlockPattern T ell) :
  Function.Injective (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove T ell out inp)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove_injective
doc:
Forgetting the labels of a compatible move is injective.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove_surjective {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.BlockPattern T ell) :
  Function.Surjective (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove T ell out inp)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbitToLegalMove_surjective
doc:
Every legal physical light move is represented by a compatible labelled move.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbit_legal_weighted_sum {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.BlockPattern T ell) (a b : Fin n → ℝ) :
  (∑ k,
      ∑ tau,
        if NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.OrbitCompatible T ell out inp (k, tau) then
          a (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.canonicalLightWord T ell out k).2 *
            b (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.permutedLightWord T ell inp tau k).2
        else 0) =
    ∑ r, ∑ i, ∑ j, if NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.LegalLightMove ↑out ↑inp (r, i, j) then a i * b j else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbit_legal_weighted_sum
doc:
Weighted finite-sum form of the exact orbit/legal-move bijection.  The
weights depend only on the target and source columns, as in the frame Gram
entry.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbit_sum_labelledG_eq_ghatBlock {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ) (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.BlockIndex d T ell) :
  ∑ tau,
      NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.labelledG F ell (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.blockLabel T ell out (Equiv.refl (Fin ell)))
        (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.blockLabel T ell inp tau) =
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.ghatBlock F T ell out inp
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.orbit_sum_labelledG_eq_ghatBlock
doc:
The labelled orbit sum is exactly the physical shared-leg block entry.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n) : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FockOp m n
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt
doc:
The annihilation operator `P_(r,i)` on the literal pattern basis.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt_apply_characterization {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt r i out inp =
    if inp (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.one ∧ out = Function.update inp (r, i) NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.zero then
      1
    else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt_apply_characterization
doc:
An annihilation entry is one exactly for its legal occupied-to-empty transition.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt_mul_pDagAt_of_ne {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) :

    NLAlib.SparseSketch.wordKernel (r, i) (r, j) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Leg.pDown, NLAlib.SparseSketch.Leg.pUp)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt_mul_pDagAt_of_ne
doc:
Light annihilation and creation at distinct sites form the corresponding word kernel.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt_ne_zero_input_one {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) (h : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt r i out inp ≠ 0) :
  inp (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.one
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt_ne_zero_input_one
doc:
A nonzero annihilation entry requires an occupied input site.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n) : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FockOp m n
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt
doc:
The creation operator `P†_(r,i)` on the literal pattern basis.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_apply {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n) (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i out inp =
    if
        out (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.one ∧
          inp = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Heavy.setSite out (r, i) NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.zero then
      1
    else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_apply
doc:
One-site light creation has coefficient one precisely at the matching marked transition.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_apply_characterization {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i out inp =
    if inp (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.zero ∧ out = Function.update inp (r, i) NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.one then
      1
    else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_apply_characterization
doc:
A creation entry is one exactly for its legal empty-to-occupied transition.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_column_inner {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n)
  (a b : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  ∑ p, NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i p a * NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i p b =
    if a = b ∧ a (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.zero then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_column_inner
doc:
The same-site creation column has exactly the fresh-site projection as
its scalar Gram.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_mul_pAt_apply {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i j : Fin n)
  (out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i * NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt r j) out inp =
    if
        inp (r, j) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.one ∧
          ((r, i) = (r, j) ∨ inp (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Level.zero) ∧
            out = NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.lightMove inp (r, j) (r, i) then
      1
    else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_mul_pAt_apply
doc:
A creation-after-annihilation entry is the indicator of a legal light move.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_mul_pAt_of_ne {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i * NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pAt r j =
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.wordKernel (r, i) (r, j) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Leg.pUp, NLAlib.SparseSketch.Leg.pDown)

doc:

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_mul_pDagAt_of_ne
doc:

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_row_inner {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n) (a b : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  ∑ p, NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i a p * NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt r i b p =

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_row_inner
doc:
The scalar row kernel `P†P` is exactly the indicator of a light site.

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.pDagAt_sq_zero {m n : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n) :

NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.permutedLightWord_eq_iff {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ)

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.permutedLightWord_permutationOfLightWord {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n))
  (ell : ℕ) (p : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.BlockPattern T ell) (w : Fin ell → NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n)

The permutation recovered from an injective light enumeration reconstructs that enumeration.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.rowProjection_CreateAnalysisStack_gradeProjection {d m n : ℕ}

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedLegGramQuadratic
doc:
The literal quadratic form of the dependent block matrix whose diagonal
blocks are `V_kᵀV_k=dI` and whose off-diagonal blocks are the proved concrete
cross matrices.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedLegGramQuadratic_le {d m n ell : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (z : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.DomainFamily m n ell) (hell : 1 ≤ ell) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedLegGramQuadratic F z ≤
    (↑d + ↑ell - 1) * ∑ k, NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.componentEnergy z k

doc:
Concrete finite-coordinate block-Gram bound.  There is no assumed
cross-map estimate: every cross term invokes `crossMatrix_energy_le`, already
proved from Parseval above.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedQ {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) :
  Matrix (Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n) (Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedQ
doc:
The literal one-particle positive matrix `Q = Σ_r |w_r><w_r|`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedQ_apply {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (out inp : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedQ F out inp =
    if out.2.1 = inp.2.1 then (F.u out.2.2).ofLp out.1 * (F.u inp.2.2).ofLp inp.1 else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedQ_apply
doc:
The one-particle operator has entries given by the frame outer product in each row register.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedRankOne {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (r : Fin m) :

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.Light.sharedRankOne

One literal rank-one matrix `|w_r><w_r|`.

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

  (z : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n) :

The shared vector entry is a frame coordinate when row registers match.

`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

  (operatorFailure :

            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯).prob

            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯).prob

  (exactColumnSparsity :

          (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n)
      (i : Fin n),
      Fintype.card { r // NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample r i ≠ 0 } =
        NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)

      ↑(NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps))

  (rowsStrict :

  (bAtLeastTwo : 2 ≤ NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.UniformExactSMainConclusions.exactColumnSparsity {n d : ℕ} {delta eps : ℝ}
  {F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d} {heps0 : 0 < eps} {heps1 : eps ≤ 1}
  (self : NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.UniformExactSMainConclusions delta eps F heps0 heps1)
  (X :
    NLAlib.UniformSparseSample
      (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps *
        NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
      (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n)
  (i : Fin n) :
  Fintype.card { r // NLAlib.uniformSparseMatrix X r i ≠ 0 } =
    NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.UniformExactSMainConclusions.exactColumnSparsity

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.UniformExactSMainConclusions.mk {n d : ℕ} {delta eps : ℝ}
  {F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d} {heps0 : 0 < eps} {heps1 : eps ≤ 1}
  (operatorFailure :
    (NLAlib.uniformSparseSampleLaw ⋯).prob
        {X | eps < ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.uniformSparseMatrix X)‖} ≤
      delta)
  (oseSuccess :
    1 - delta ≤
      (NLAlib.uniformSparseSampleLaw ⋯).prob
        {X | NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.uniformSparseMatrix X) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix F.u) eps})
  (exactColumnSparsity :
    ∀
      (X :
        NLAlib.UniformSparseSample
          (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps *
            NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
          (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n)
      (i : Fin n),
      Fintype.card { r // NLAlib.uniformSparseMatrix X r i ≠ 0 } =
        NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
  (qAtLeastOne : 1 ≤ NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta)
  (sparsityStrict :
    ↑(NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) <
      1356 * ↑(NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) / eps)
  (rowsStrict :
    ↑(NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) <
      306456 * (↑d + ↑(NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta)) / eps ^ 2)
  (bAtLeastTwo : 2 ≤ NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
  (rowsFactor :
    NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps =
      NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps *
        NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.UniformExactSMainConclusions delta eps F heps0 heps1

doc:
The hollow iid Gram error with the genuine exact-`s` coupling scale on
each whole column.  It is expressed through the existing block-first error so
the already-proved iid/Fock bridge can be reused literally.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.UniformExactSTransfer`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.exactScaledIIDError_apply_grouped {b s n d : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b)
  (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (Y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.IidColumnSample b s n) (a c : Fin d) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.exactScaledIIDError hb F Y a c =
    1 / ↑s *
      ∑ i,
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
          (∑ g,
                NLAlib.SparseSketch.UniformSparse.exactScale hb ^ 2 *
                  inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseSketch.unscaledYVector (Y i g)) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.unscaledYVector (Y j g))) *
              (F.u i).ofLp a *
            (F.u j).ofLp c

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.blockGram_finite_row_bound
doc:
A finite scalar row-majorization version of the block-Gram estimate.

One distinguished diagonal entry is bounded by `d * energy`; each of the other
`ell - 1` entries is bounded by `energy`. No operator-norm statement is hidden
in this lemma.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ScalarBounds`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:

  (hdiag : diagonal ≤ d * energy) (hcross : cross ≤ (ell - 1) * energy) : diagonal + cross ≤ (d + ell - 1) * energy
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.blockGram_row_bound
doc:
The algebraic last step in the block-Gram estimate `d + ℓ - 1`.

The operator-specific hypotheses (diagonal block at most `d`, each off-diagonal
block at most `1`) are deliberately represented as scalar premises here.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ScalarBounds`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:

  ∑ a, NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix Z (g, a) i * NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix Z (g, a) j =
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.invSqrt s ^ 2 *
      inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g i) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g j)

NLAlib.SparseSketch.conditionalMixtureLaw_expect_eq_iidArrayLaw_expect {b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (s n : ℕ)

NLAlib.SparseSketch.conditionalMixtureLaw_expect_eq_iterated {b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (s n : ℕ)

first over the selector array, then over its conditional ternary array.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.conditionalMixtureLaw_weight {b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (s n : ℕ) (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) :

      (NLAlib.SparseSketch.selectorArrayLaw hb s n).weight x * (NLAlib.SparseSketch.conditionalArrayLaw hb x).weight y

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.conditionalMixtureLaw_weight_eq_iidArrayLaw_weight {b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (s n : ℕ)
  (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseSketch.conditionalMixtureLaw hb s n).weight y = (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw hb s n).weight y

mass.  This is the full finite-array marginal identity, not merely equality of

  {z z' : NLAlib.SparseSketch.ArraySite s n} (hzz : z ≠ z') :

      inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseSketch.scaledYVector (y z)) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.scaledYVector (y z'))) =

signature:

  {delta eps : ℝ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdelta0 : 0 < delta) (hdelta1 : delta ≤ 1) (heps0 : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1)
  (frameLaw : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw Omega) (frames : Omega → NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) :
  1 - delta ≤
    (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix outcome.2.toSample)
          (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix (frames outcome.1).u) eps}

NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_entry_hasLocalDegree_two {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)

doc:
Every scalar entry of the pointwise SparseStack Gram error has local
interaction degree at most two.  The proof uses the exact hollow identity,
so no independence is involved.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_eq_block_first {s b n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (Z : NLAlib.SparseStackSample s b n) (hs : 0 < s) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix Z) = fun a c =>
    1 / ↑s *
      ∑ g,
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g i) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g j) * (F.u i).ofLp a *
              (F.u j).ofLp c

doc:
The exact hollow identity (paper (2.2)): the Parseval diagonal cancels from
`UᵀΠᵀΠU-I`, leaving only ordered pairs `i ≠ j`.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError_apply {m n d : ℕ} (b : ℕ) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)

  (frameLaw : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw Omega) (frames : Omega → NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)

    ∀ (omega : Omega) (shift : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift),
      ∀ nu ≤ 2 * NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta,
        ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand (NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) (frames omega)
                (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) shift *
              NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandEnvelope d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)) :
  (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        eps < ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError (frames outcome.1) (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix outcome.2.toSample)‖} ≤
    delta

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.independent_frame_ose_success_of_band_bounds.{u_1} {Omega : Type u_1} [Fintype Omega] {n d : ℕ}
  {delta eps : ℝ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdelta0 : 0 < delta) (hdelta1 : delta ≤ 1) (heps0 : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1)
  (frameLaw : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw Omega) (frames : Omega → NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (hband :
    ∀ (omega : Omega) (shift : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift),
      ∀ nu ≤ 2 * NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta,
        ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand (NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) (frames omega)
                (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) shift *
              NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandEnvelope d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)) :
  1 - delta ≤
    (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix outcome.2.toSample)
          (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix (frames outcome.1).u) eps}

signature:

    ‖((1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Lminus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      a + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m)
  (hmixed :
    ‖(1 / ↑m) •
            √(↑b - 1) •
              ((NLAlib.SparseSketch.XplusAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                NLAlib.SparseSketch.YplusAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + 3 / 2 * c)
  (hheavy :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • √(↑b - 1) ^ 2 • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Hminus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      c)
  (hbTerm : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) :
  ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand m F b NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift.minus * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandConstant * (a + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + c)

NLAlib.SparseSketch.parameter_envelope {rootTerm linearTerm sparseTerm ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1)

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.plus_band_envelope_of_components {d m n b : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (nu : ℕ)
  {a c : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (hlight :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Lplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      a + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m)
  (hmixed :
    ‖(1 / ↑m) •
            √(↑b - 1) •
              ((NLAlib.SparseSketch.Xplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                NLAlib.SparseSketch.Yplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + 3 / 2 * c)
  (hheavy :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • √(↑b - 1) ^ 2 • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Hplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      c)
  (hbTerm : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) :
  ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand m F b NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift.plus * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandConstant * (a + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + c)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.plus_band_envelope_of_components
doc:
Exact operator-level assembly for the positive band.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ConcreteBandAssembly`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.plus_row_envelope {a b c : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hc : 0 ≤ c) :

NLAlib.SparseSketch.productBasis_orthonormal {m n b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (p q : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :

NLAlib.SparseSketch.productBasis_reconstruction {m n b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (f : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Configuration m n → ℝ)

  f x =

Completeness of the product polynomial family, proved explicitly rather

        (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) ^ (2 * q)).trace) /
      ε ^ (2 * q)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseStack_ose_failure_tail
doc:
Failure of the vector OSE property is contained in the concrete norm-tail
event, so it obeys the same trace-moment bound.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.MatrixTail`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseStack_ose_success_probability {s b n d : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (δ : ℝ)
  (hmoment :
    ((NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).expect fun z =>
          (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) ^ (2 * q)).trace) /
        ε ^ (2 * q) ≤
      δ) :
  1 - δ ≤
    (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).prob
      {z | NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix F.u) ε}

doc:
The squared Euclidean norm `∑ i, x i ^ 2` of a finitely indexed real vector.

This is the single sum-of-squares spelling of the sparse-sketch proof: it replaces the
former copies `LightSectorConcrete.energy`, `LightSectorConcrete.coordinateEnergy`,
`HeavyBandsConcrete.coordNormSq` and `HeavyBandsConcrete.fockNormSq`. It is an interim
definition (decision D9 of `docs/SPARSE_INTEGRATION.md`): it equals `x ⬝ᵥ x`
(`sumSq_eq_dotProduct`) and is to be replaced by that expression.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.sumSq_eq_dotProduct
doc:
The interim sum of squares is the self dot product.

symmetric matrices.  The only analytic premise is the displayed convexity of

      (NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseVectorError F x ^ (2 * q)).trace) ≤

      (NLAlib.SparseSketch.scaledIIDVectorError F y ^ (2 * q)).trace

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.zero_band_envelope_of_components {d m n b : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (nu : ℕ) {c : ℝ}
  (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (hlight :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Lzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      3 * NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m)
  (hmixed :
    ‖(1 / ↑m) •
            √(↑b - 1) •
              ((((NLAlib.SparseSketch.Xzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                    NLAlib.SparseSketch.XzeroAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Yzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                NLAlib.SparseSketch.YzeroAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + (1 + √2) * c)
  (hheavy :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • √(↑b - 1) ^ 2 • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Hzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      2 * c)
  (hbTerm : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) (ha : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.aTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) :
  ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand m F b NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift.zero * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandConstant * (NLAlib.SparseSketch.aTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + c)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.zero_band_envelope_of_components
doc:
Exact operator-level assembly for the grade-preserving band.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ConcreteBandAssembly`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [RCLike 𝕜] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] : Type (max (max u_1 u_2) u_3)
name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm
doc:
A unitarily invariant matrix norm on `Matrix m n 𝕜` (`𝕜 = ℝ` or `ℂ`) in Mathlib's bundled
real-seminorm vocabulary, with an explicit separating zero criterion: a real seminorm `ν` with
`ν (U A V) = ν A` for unitary `U`, `V` (`HasOrthonormalCols`). At `𝕜 = ℝ` this is an
orthogonally invariant norm. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.7; Bhatia 1997, §IV.2.
atlas: unitarily-invariant-norm-def

name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.eq_zero_of_map_eq_zero
doc: The seminorm separates zero and is therefore a norm.

signature:
NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.exists_symmetricGauge_representation.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (ν : NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm ℝ m n) :
  ∃ Φ, ∀ (A : Matrix m n ℝ), ν.seminorm A = Φ.matrixValue A
name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.exists_symmetricGauge_representation
doc:
Every invariant norm has a fixed symmetric gauge representation,
valid simultaneously for every matrix of that shape.
Bhatia (1997), Theorem IV.2.1.
atlas: unitarily-invariant-norm-def

name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.left_invariant
doc: Unitary multiplication on the left preserves the norm.

signature:
NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.mk.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (seminorm : Seminorm ℝ (Matrix m n 𝕜))
  (eq_zero_of_map_eq_zero : ∀ (A : Matrix m n 𝕜), seminorm A = 0 → A = 0)
  (left_invariant :
    ∀ (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (U : Matrix m m 𝕜), NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U → seminorm (U * A) = seminorm A)
  (right_invariant :
    ∀ (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (V : Matrix n n 𝕜), NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V → seminorm (A * V) = seminorm A) :
  NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm 𝕜 m n
name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.mk
NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.reindex
doc:
Relabel a bundled invariant norm, pulling it back through the exact matrix
linear equivalence. This preserves all norm properties and orthogonal symmetries.

signature:
NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.reindex_seminorm_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}

  [DecidableEq q] (ν : NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm ℝ m n) (em : m ≃ p) (en : n ≃ q) (A : Matrix p q ℝ) :

doc: The reindexed norm is the original norm of the inverse-reindexed matrix.

name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.right_invariant

name: NLAlib.UnitarilyInvariantNorm.seminorm

Every nonnegative coordinate pairing of a weakly majorized vector is

signature:
NLAlib.X_mul_orthonormalMomentPolynomial (L : Polynomial ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (n : ℕ)
  (hL : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, NLAlib.hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0) (hH : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, 0 < NLAlib.orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k) :
  Polynomial.X * NLAlib.orthonormalMomentPolynomial L n =
    Polynomial.C √(NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L n) * NLAlib.orthonormalMomentPolynomial L (n - 1) +
        Polynomial.C (NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha L n) * NLAlib.orthonormalMomentPolynomial L n +
      Polynomial.C √(NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L (n + 1)) * NLAlib.orthonormalMomentPolynomial L (n + 1)
name: NLAlib.X_mul_orthonormalMomentPolynomial
doc:
Positive monic norms normalize the actual three-term recurrence, with square-root
off-diagonal coefficients and the zero boundary coefficient at order zero. The top
polynomial is normalized only under its explicit positive norm hypothesis.
Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 1.27; operator derivations (OF8).
atlas: monic-orthogonal-recurrence (partial), jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.X_sub_C_mul_christoffelPolynomial.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜] (L : Polynomial 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (n : ℕ) {z : 𝕜}
  (hz : Polynomial.eval z (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n) ≠ 0) :
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C z) * NLAlib.christoffelPolynomial L z n =
    NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1) -
      Polynomial.C
          (Polynomial.eval z (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1)) /
            Polynomial.eval z (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n)) *
        NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n
name: NLAlib.X_sub_C_mul_christoffelPolynomial
doc:
The linear modification quotient is exact: multiplying it by `X-z` recovers
the numerator, without an analytic division operation.
Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 1.33.
atlas: kernel-polynomials-christoffel (partial), christoffel-uvarov-modification (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.X_sub_C_mul_monicOrthogonalKernelPolynomial.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜] {L : Polynomial 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜} (n : ℕ)
  (hL : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, NLAlib.hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0) (y : 𝕜) :
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C y) * NLAlib.monicOrthogonalKernelPolynomial L (n + 1) y =
    Polynomial.C (Polynomial.eval y (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n) / NLAlib.orthogonalPolynomialNorm L n) *
        NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1) -
      Polynomial.C
          (Polynomial.eval y (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1)) / NLAlib.orthogonalPolynomialNorm L n) *
        NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n
name: NLAlib.X_sub_C_mul_monicOrthogonalKernelPolynomial
doc:
Multiplying by the argument difference gives the Christoffel–Darboux
identity, with no distinct-argument hypothesis. Source: Gautschi (2004),
Theorem 1.28.
atlas: monic-orthogonal-recurrence (partial)

name: NLAlib.abs_compressionQuadratureEstimate_inv_sub_hutchinsonEstimate_le
doc:
**SLQ quadrature error for `f(x) = 1/x`.** If `A` is symmetric with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, each `Q_k` has orthonormal columns with `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`, then
`|SLQ(1/x) − tr_m(f(A))| ≤ 2 (2/a) ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^{2q} · tr_m(I)` with `f(A) = cfc (1/x) A`
(`= A⁻¹`). Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], Thm 4.1 and §4.2 (inverse); the rate is the
CG/Chebyshev rate of `inverse-polynomial-approx`. Atlas: `slq-error`; uses
`lanczos-gauss-quadrature`, `inverse-polynomial-approx`.
atlas: slq-error (partial)

name: NLAlib.abs_compressionQuadratureEstimate_sub_hutchinsonEstimate_le
doc:
**SLQ quadrature error, deterministic.** If `A` is symmetric with spectrum in `[a, c]`,
each `Q_k` has orthonormal columns with `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`, and `|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`
for a polynomial `p` of degree `< 2q`, then `|SLQ − tr_m f(A)| ≤ 2E · tr_m(I)`, where `tr_m` is
the Hutchinson estimator with the same test vectors and `tr_m(I) = (1/m) ∑ₖ ‖g_k‖²`.
Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], proof of Thm 4.1 (Lemma 4.2). Atlas: `slq-error`;
uses `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`.
atlas: slq-error (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_cfc_exp_neg_mulVec_sub_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {b δ : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc 0 b) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (v : n → ℝ)

  |v ⬝ᵥ (cfc (fun x => Real.exp (-x)) A).mulVec v -
        Q.transpose.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ (cfc (fun x => Real.exp (-x)) (Q.transpose * A * Q)).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec v)| ≤
    2 * δ * ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ ^ 2

doc:
**Gauss quadrature error for `exp(−x)`**: for a symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[0, b]` and
`2q` above the approximation degree `exponentialApproxDegree b δ`,
`|vᵀ exp(−A) v − (Qᵀv)ᵀ exp(−QᵀAQ) (Qᵀv)| ≤ 2δ ‖v‖²`.
Source: Sachdeva–Vishnoi (2014) [`sv14`], Thm 4.1; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], §6.2.
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (exponential rate).

name: NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_le
doc:
A function bounded by `E` on the eigenvalues gives a quadratic form bounded by `E ‖v‖²`:
`|vᵀ g(A) v| ≤ E (v ⬝ v)`. Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper; the `cfc` form of
`polynomial-spectral-bound`).

signature:
NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_degree_lt_two_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * ↑q) {a c E : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c)
  (hfp : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c, |f x - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ E) :
  |b ⬝ᵥ (cfc f A).mulVec b - Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ (cfc f (Q.transpose * A * Q)).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)| ≤
    2 * E * ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_degree_lt_two_mul
doc:
**Error of Gauss (Lanczos) quadrature.** Let `A` be symmetric with spectrum in `[a, c]`, `Q`
with orthonormal columns, `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, and `p` a polynomial of degree `< 2q` with
`|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`. Then `|bᵀ f(A) b − (Qᵀb)ᵀ f(QᵀAQ) (Qᵀb)| ≤ 2 E ‖b‖²`. Valid for
every `q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], §6.2 (error of Gauss quadrature via best approximation);
Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`], Lem. 2.2; Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], proof of Thm 4.1.
Deviation: stated with an arbitrary approximant `p` (the source takes the best uniform
approximation, `E = E_{2q−1}(f)`); any orthonormal `Q` with `K_q ⊆ range Q`.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

**Gauss quadrature error for a Lipschitz function**: if `f` is `L`-Lipschitz on `[a, c]`,
an interval containing the spectrum of the symmetric `A`, `Q` has orthonormal columns and

Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], §6.2, with Jackson's theorem (Cheney (1966), §4.6).
atlas: lanczos-quadrature-lipschitz-error

atlas: chebyshev-minimax

The derivative of `T_q` is bounded by `q²` on `[-1, 1]`: `|x| ≤ 1 → |T_q'(x)| ≤ q²`.

`chebyshev-second-kind`.

      Real.sin ((↑↑j + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / ↑N) =

doc:
The derivative modulus at a Chebyshev zero times its root-angle sine is `N`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : |x| < 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q * M / √(1 - x ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Bernstein's inequality** for algebraic polynomials. If `p` has degree at most `q` and
`|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q M / √(1 − x²)` for `|x| < 1`.

Source: Bernstein (1912); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7; Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
Proof (algebraic form of the trigonometric argument): with `a = x = cos θ₀`, `b = √(1 − x²)`, the
odd part of `θ ↦ p(cos(θ₀ + θ))` is `sin θ · r(cos θ)` for a polynomial `r` of degree `< q` (built
from Hasse derivatives of `p`), `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, and `r(1) = −b p'(x)`; Schur's
inequality `abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` at `y = 1` gives
`b |p'(x)| ≤ q M`.
atlas: bernstein-polynomial-inequality

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q ^ 2 * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality** (the first Markov inequality, sharp constant). If `p` has
degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q² M` for all `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), Thm 2.24 / §2.7;
Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
Proof: Bernstein's inequality `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le` gives
`√(1 − y²) |p'(y)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`, and Schur's inequality
`abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` applied to `p'` (degree `< q`) gives
`|p'(x)| ≤ q · q M`. The equality case (`p = ±M T_q`, `x = ±1`) is not formalised.
atlas: markov-brothers

name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality on an interval.** If `p` has degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on
`[a, b]` (`a < b`), then `|p'(x)| ≤ 2 q² / (b − a) · M` for all `x ∈ [a, b]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (affine
rescaling of `abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`). Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
atlas: markov-brothers

  (hb : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ M) (hx : 1 ≤ |x|) :

Scaled form of Chebyshev's extremal growth bound: if `P` has degree at most `q` and

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {r : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q)
  (hr : r.degree < ↑q) (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, √(1 - y ^ 2) * |Polynomial.eval y r| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x r| ≤ ↑q * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Schur's inequality.** If `r` has degree `< q` and `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then
`|r(x)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`.

Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (Schur's lemma); Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Proof: for `|x| ≤ cos(π/(2q))` directly from
`√(1 − x²) ≥ sin(π/(2q)) ≥ 1/q`; for `x ≥ cos(π/(2q))` by Lagrange interpolation at the zeros
`ξ_k` of `T_q`, where all partial nodal products are nonnegative and the weights satisfy
`|r(ξ_k)| / |T_q'(ξ_k)| ≤ M/q`, so `|r(x)| ≤ (M/q) T_q'(x) ≤ q M`; the case `x ≤ −cos(π/(2q))` by
reflection. Atlas: auxiliary for `markov-brothers` and `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
atlas: schur-polynomial-inequality

signature:
NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_inverseIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≠ μ) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ}
  (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u) (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {d D : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d)
  (hdJ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → d ≤ |hA.eigenvalues₀ i - μ|)
  (hD : ∀ (i : n), |hA.eigenvalues i - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤ D) {x₀ : n → ℝ} (hx₀ : u ⬝ᵥ x₀ ≠ 0) (k : ℕ) :
  |NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A (NLAlib.inverseIterate A μ x₀ k) - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤
    D * ((|hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ - μ| / d) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀)
name: NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_inverseIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Inverse iteration, Rayleigh quotient.** Under the hypotheses of
`overlapTangentSq_inverseIterate_le`, with `|λᵢ − λ_{i₀}| ≤ D` for all `i` and `u ⬝ x₀ ≠ 0`:
`|ρ(x_k) − λ_{i₀}| ≤ D (|λ_{i₀} − μ|/d)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Thm 27.2 (second bound).
atlas: inverse-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_powerIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u)
  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) (hl : hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ ≠ 0) {ρ D : ℝ}
  (hρ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → |hA.eigenvalues₀ i| ≤ ρ)
  (hD : ∀ (i : n), |hA.eigenvalues i - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤ D) {x₀ : n → ℝ} (hx₀ : u ⬝ᵥ x₀ ≠ 0) (k : ℕ) :
  |NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A (NLAlib.powerIterate A x₀ k) - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤
    D * ((ρ / |hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀|) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀)
name: NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_powerIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Power iteration, Rayleigh quotient.** For real symmetric `A`, a unit eigenvector `u` of
`λ₁ = λ_{i₀} ≠ 0`, `|λᵢ| ≤ ρ` at the other sorted positions, `|λᵢ − λ₁| ≤ D` for all `i`, and
`u ⬝ x₀ ≠ 0`: `|ρ(A^k x₀) − λ₁| ≤ D (ρ/|λ₁|)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`, the squared rate of the
angle. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.1; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
Thm 8.2.1. Deviation: explicit constant `D` (T&B: `O(|λ₂/λ₁|^{2k})`).
atlas: power-iteration

name: NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_sub_le_mul_overlapTangentSq
doc:
**Rayleigh quotient error from the angle.** For real symmetric `A`, a unit eigenvector `u`
for the eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀`, `D` with `|λᵢ − λ₁| ≤ D` for every
`i` (e.g. `D = λ_max − λ_min`), and `x` with `u ⬝ x ≠ 0`: `|ρ(x) − λ₁| ≤ D tan² ∠(u, x)`.
Proof: split `x = (u ⬝ x) u + w` with `w ⟂ u`; then
`ρ(x) − λ₁ = (wᵀAw − λ₁ ‖w‖²)/‖x‖²` and `|wᵀAw − λ₁ ‖w‖²| ≤ D ‖w‖²`. Source:
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.1 (second bound) and Lect. 27 (`ρ(x) − λ = O(‖x − u‖²)`);
Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §4.1. Deviation: explicit constant `D` instead of `O(·)`; two-sided.
atlas: power-iteration

2013, Cor 7.3.5; Bhatia 1997, §III.2. Atlas `weyl-mirsky`.

proof of Cor. 5.35).

  (hMean : μ[X | m] =ᵐ[μ] 0) {L θ : ℝ} (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθL : θ * L < 3)
  (hBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, X ω ≤ (algebraMap ℝ (Matrix n n ℂ)) L) :

        NLAlib.matrixLog (μ[fun ω => NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) | m] ω) ≤

doc:
The native Chebyshev polynomial of a concrete field sends the actual
vacuum to its repeated-letter unit basis vector.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_conjGram_mul_eq_mul_aeval_conjGram.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.aeval_conjGram_mul_eq_mul_aeval_conjGram
doc:
Complex rectangular Gram polynomials intertwine through the original matrix.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, its complex `A A*`/`A* A` identity. The polynomial
has real coefficients, as in the manuscript.

name: NLAlib.aeval_conjGram_mul_mul_eq_of_block_decomposition
doc:
A polynomially filtered block SVD has the corresponding filtered diagonal blocks.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, the intertwining step before `sa:filter-theorem`.
The blocks need not be diagonal, so their squared singular blocks are written as Grams.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (d : n → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
  (Polynomial.aeval (Matrix.diagonal d)) p = Matrix.diagonal fun i => Polynomial.eval (d i) p
name: NLAlib.aeval_diagonal
doc:
A polynomial of a diagonal matrix is the diagonal matrix of the polynomial values:
`p(diag d) = diag(p ∘ d)`. Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_diagonal_ofReal.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ι → ℝ)

  (Polynomial.aeval (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(d i))) p = Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(Polynomial.eval (d i) p)
name: NLAlib.aeval_diagonal_ofReal
doc:
A real polynomial of a real diagonal matrix cast to `𝕜` is the diagonal of the values:
`p(diag (d : 𝕜)) = diag (p(d) : 𝕜)`.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_entries_mem_wordWickDegreeSpan.{u_1, u_2} {D : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype D] [DecidableEq D]

name: NLAlib.aeval_entries_mem_wordWickDegreeSpan
doc:
Native real polynomial evaluation multiplies the actual entry degree
by at most its polynomial degree. Constants and empty dimensions are included.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_eq_mul_diagonal_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_gram_diagonal_mul_diagonal_inv_eq_one.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]

    1
name: NLAlib.aeval_gram_diagonal_mul_diagonal_inv_eq_one
doc:
The polynomial filter of the Gram matrix of a square diagonal is invertible by the diagonal
of reciprocals: `p(Sᴴ S) · diag (p(s i²)⁻¹) = 1` when `p` does not vanish on the squared
entries. Halko–Martinsson–Tropp 2011, §10.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_gram_mul_eq_mul_aeval_gram.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.aeval_gram_mul_eq_mul_aeval_gram
doc:
The two rectangular Gram polynomials intertwine through the original matrix.
Source: the manuscript `sa:filter`, its displayed polynomial-intertwining identity.

name: NLAlib.aeval_gram_mul_mul_eq_of_block_decomposition
doc:
A polynomially filtered block SVD has the corresponding filtered diagonal blocks.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, the intertwining step before `sa:filter-theorem`.
The blocks need not be diagonal, so their squared singular blocks are written as Grams.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_moment_eq_wordField_of_semicircular.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [Ring A] [Algebra ℂ A]
  (φ : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ) (X : ι → A) (hLaw : ∀ (i : ι) (n : ℕ), φ (X i ^ n) = if Even n then ↑(catalan (n / 2)) else 0) (i : ι)

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v =
    ∑ i, (Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p * (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) • (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp
name: NLAlib.aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
**Polynomial calculus, vector form.** `p(A) v = ∑ᵢ p(λᵢ) ⟨uᵢ, v⟩ uᵢ` for real symmetric `A`
with orthonormal eigenvectors `uᵢ = hA.eigenvectorBasis i`. Standard (Saad 2003, §6.11);
audit G3 C1; atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_mulVec_eq_zero_iff_vectorMinpoly_dvd.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K) (b : n → K) (p : Polynomial K) :
  ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b = 0 ↔ NLAlib.vectorMinpoly A b ∣ p
name: NLAlib.aeval_mulVec_eq_zero_iff_vectorMinpoly_dvd
doc:
A polynomial annihilates the vector exactly when the vector-relative minimal
polynomial divides it. This is the full annihilator interface, with no nonzero
vector or positive dimension assumption. Source: operator derivations, (S1).
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_mul_eq_mul_aeval_of_mul_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {R : Type u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_4} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring 𝕜] [Algebra R 𝕜]
  {B : Matrix m m 𝕜} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {C : Matrix n n 𝕜} (h : B * A = A * C) (p : Polynomial R) :
  (Polynomial.aeval B) p * A = A * (Polynomial.aeval C) p
name: NLAlib.aeval_mul_eq_mul_aeval_of_mul_eq
doc:
Polynomial calculus preserves rectangular intertwining: `BA = AC` implies
`p(B) A = A p(C)` for every polynomial `p`. Source: the manuscript `sa:filter`; Horn–Johnson
(2013), Lemma 2.4.4.0; standard polynomial functional calculus.
atlas: sylvester-equation

name: NLAlib.aeval_prod_eq_qrAlgorithmQ_mul_qrAlgorithmR
doc:
**Shifted simultaneous iteration**: `∏_{j<k} (A − μ_j I) = Q^{(k)} R^{(k)}` (the product of
the shifted matrices, written as the polynomial `∏_{j<k} (X − μ_j)` evaluated at `A`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 28.3 and Lect. 29 (shifted form); Golub–Van Loan
(2013) [`gvl13`], §7.5.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_upperBlockThree.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {o : Type u_4}
  [CommRing 𝕜] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype o] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq o] (p : Polynomial 𝕜)
  (A : Matrix m m 𝕜) (G : Matrix m n 𝕜) (B : Matrix n n 𝕜) (H : Matrix n o 𝕜) (C : Matrix o o 𝕜) :
  (Polynomial.aeval (NLAlib.upperBlockThree A G B H C)) p =
    Matrix.fromBlocks
      (Matrix.fromBlocks ((Polynomial.aeval A) p) (NLAlib.polynomialBlockDifference p A B G) 0 ((Polynomial.aeval B) p))
      ((NLAlib.polynomialSecondBlockDifference p A B C G H).fromRows (NLAlib.polynomialBlockDifference p B C H)) 0
      ((Polynomial.aeval C) p)
name: NLAlib.aeval_upperBlockThree
doc:
The ordered second difference is the actual first-to-third block of the
polynomial of a three-block triangular matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_upperBlockTwo.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [CommRing 𝕜] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (p : Polynomial 𝕜) (A : Matrix m m 𝕜) (H : Matrix m n 𝕜)
  (B : Matrix n n 𝕜) :
  (Polynomial.aeval (NLAlib.upperBlockTwo A H B)) p =
    Matrix.fromBlocks ((Polynomial.aeval A) p) (NLAlib.polynomialBlockDifference p A B H) 0 ((Polynomial.aeval B) p)
name: NLAlib.aeval_upperBlockTwo
doc: Polynomial evaluation on an actual triangular matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_vectorMinpoly_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

The vector-relative minimal polynomial annihilates its vector.
Source: Saad (2003), Props. 6.1–6.3.
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

The scalar affine evaluation at actual real coordinates is exactly
the ordinary Gaussian matrix series, with its original coefficients.

NLAlib.analyticAt_inversePencilUpperRootSum
doc:
The actual upper-root sum of a Hermitian pencil is analytic throughout
both nonreal half-planes. The proof localizes the upper cluster by a fixed
circle and permits arbitrary collisions within the selected cluster.
Source: planar root-sum reorganization of Stahl's contour argument.
atlas: trace-exponential-stahl (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.analyticAt_orderedMatrixExp.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (H : List (Matrix n n ℂ)) (z : ℂ) :
  AnalyticAt ℂ (NLAlib.orderedMatrixExp H) z
name: NLAlib.analyticAt_orderedMatrixExp
doc:
Ordered exponential products are entire, without commutativity of the
generators or a choice of logarithmic branches.

signature:
NLAlib.analyticAt_simpleEigenvalueSchurFunction.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (μ a : ℂ)

doc:
The scalar Schur equation is analytic near the origin when the trailing
block excludes the leading eigenvalue. The matrix inverse in the definition
is the Banach-algebra inverse on a neighborhood of the base point.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

name: NLAlib.analyticOnNhd_wordNativeDysonResolvent
doc: The actual native compressed free resolvent is holomorphic off the real axis.

A locally integrable density satisfying the weak derivative sign has antitone
smooth regularizations on every interior half-line. Source: Edelman 1988; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).

`x cot x` decreases on the positive half quadrant, including its right endpoint.
Source: the sharp Lobatto-kernel comparison in equation `eq:cotpair`.

signature:
NLAlib.antitone_density_le_of_mellin_endpoint (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ) (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (h : ℝ → ℝ)
  (hh : Measurable h) (hnn : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioi 0, 0 ≤ h x) (hanti : AntitoneOn h (Set.Ioi 0))
  (hdens :
    μ.restrict (Set.Ioi 0) =
      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioi 0)).withDensity fun x =>

  (M : ℝ → ℝ) (C : ℝ)

Subcritical Mellin bounds with a finite endpoint residue bound an antitone
Gamma-weighted density uniformly. Source: operator rederivations, Section 5;

NLAlib.antitone_sub_prefix_gap {N k : ℕ} (a : Fin N → ℝ) (ha : Antitone a) (hk0 : 0 < k) (hkN : k < N) :

The boundary-gap-shifted decreasing list is still decreasing.
This makes the ordinary finite weight budget yield a quantitative deficit.

signature:
NLAlib.apply_eq_sum_mul_single.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : (ι → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (x : ι → ℝ) :

A real linear functional on a finite coordinate space is its coordinate
pairing with the values on standard basis vectors. HLP support helper.

signature:
NLAlib.apply_eq_zero_of_posSemidef_of_apply_self_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]

NLAlib.apply_eq_zero_of_posSemidef_of_apply_self_eq_zero'.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}

name: NLAlib.apply_zero_ne_zero_of_mulVec_eq_smul
doc:
Every nonzero eigenvector of an unreduced Hessenberg transpose has nonzero
first coordinate. Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 1.19.

signature:
NLAlib.apply_zero_of_mem_hessenbergReflectors {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (u : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) :

doc:
Every reflector vector of the reduction has first entry `0` (so every reflector fixes
`e₀`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 26.

signature: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis
doc:
The **Arnoldi basis** `q_0, q_1, …`: Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation of `b, A b, A² b, …`
(`gramSchmidtNormed` over `ℕ`); `q_j = 0` from the grade on (breakdown). Column `j` does not
depend on how many columns are taken. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 6.1;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33. Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_dotProduct
doc: Orthonormality of the Arnoldi vectors below the grade: `q_i ⬝ q_j = δ_ij`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_dotProduct_of_ne.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≠ j) : NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b i ⬝ᵥ NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b j = 0
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_dotProduct_of_ne
doc:
Distinct Arnoldi vectors are orthogonal, `q_iᵀ q_j = 0` for `i ≠ j`, with no grade hypothesis
(past the grade the vectors are `0`). Helper for `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (b : n → ℝ) {j : ℕ} (hj : NLAlib.krylovGrade A b ≤ j) : NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b j = 0
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
The Arnoldi vectors vanish from the grade on: `arnoldiBasis A b j = 0` for
`krylovGrade A b ≤ j` (breakdown). Helper for `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.6.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  (j : ℕ) : NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b j ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (j + 1)
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_mem_krylovSpace
doc: The Arnoldi vector `q_j` lies in `K_{j+1}(A, b)`. Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_zero_dotProduct_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)

The first canonical Arnoldi vector is `b/‖b‖`: `q_1 ⬝ b = ‖b‖ > 0` (for `b ≠ 0`, i.e.
`0 < krylovGrade A b`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 6.1. Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

signature:

The **canonical Arnoldi decomposition** (Gram–Schmidt, positive subdiagonal) of size
`q ≤ krylovGrade A b`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 6.1 and Prop. 6.4.
atlas: arnoldi-def

doc:

Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp_H_subdiag_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  {q : ℕ} (h : q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b) {j : ℕ} (hj : j + 1 < q) :
  0 < (NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp A b q h).H ⟨j + 1, hj⟩ ⟨j, ⋯⟩
name: NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp_H_subdiag_pos
doc:
**The canonical decomposition has positive subdiagonal**: `h_{j+1,j} = ‖g_{j+1}‖/‖g_j‖ > 0`
with `g_j` the unnormalised Gram–Schmidt vectors. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 6.1
(`h_{j+1,j} = ‖w_j‖`).
atlas: arnoldi-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp_Q.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ}
  (h : q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b) : (NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp A b q h).Q = NLAlib.arnoldiMatrix A b q
name: NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp_Q
doc: The basis of the canonical decomposition is `arnoldiMatrix`. Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ

doc:
The Arnoldi Hessenberg matrix `H_q = Q_qᵀ A Q_q`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg_apply_eq_zero_of_add_one_lt.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} {i j : Fin q} (hij : ↑j + 1 < ↑i) : NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg A b q i j = 0
name: NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg_apply_eq_zero_of_add_one_lt
doc:
**The Arnoldi Hessenberg matrix is upper Hessenberg**, `h_ij = 0` for `i > j + 1`, for every
`A` and every `q` (no symmetry, no non-breakdown hypothesis).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33.
atlas: arnoldi-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg_apply_eq_zero_of_add_one_lt_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} {i j : Fin q} (hij : ↑i + 1 < ↑j) :
  NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg A b q i j = 0
name: NLAlib.arnoldiHessenberg_apply_eq_zero_of_add_one_lt_of_isHermitian
doc:
**For symmetric `A` the Arnoldi Hessenberg matrix is tridiagonal**: also `h_ij = 0` for
`j > i + 1` (the Lanczos case). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36.

name: NLAlib.bernsteinTail
doc:
The matrix Bernstein tail `d · exp (-(t²/2)/(v + L t/3))`, defined piecewise in the degenerate
case `v + L t/3 = 0` (`d` at `t = 0`, `0` otherwise). Tropp 2015, Thm 6.1.1.
atlas: matrix-bernstein

signature:
NLAlib.bernstein_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L θ : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
  (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθL : θ < 3 / L) (hMeas : Measurable X) (hHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian)
  (hL2 : MeasureTheory.MemLp X 2 μ) (hMean : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (X ω) ≤ L) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ ≤ NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ^ 2 ∂μ) ∧
    NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ) ≤ (θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ^ 2 ∂μ
name: NLAlib.bernstein_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a centered Hermitian random matrix with `λmax X ≤ L` and `0 < θ < 3/L`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼
matrixExp (c • 𝔼 X²)` and `matrixLog 𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ c • 𝔼 X²`, where `c = (θ²/2)/(1 -
θL/3)`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 6.6.2. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

signature:
NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (K : ι → ℝ)
  (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (hK : ∀ (i : ι), 0 < K i)
  (hmean : ∀ (i : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|X i ω| / K i)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B)
  (hKB : ∀ (i : ι), K i ≤ B) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  μ.real {ω | t ≤ |∑ i, X i ω|} ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-(1 / 64) * min (t ^ 2 / ∑ i, K i ^ 2) (t / B))
name: NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two
doc:
**Scalar Bernstein inequality from `ψ₁` exponential bounds.** For mutually
independent centered real coordinates with positive scales satisfying
`E exp(|Xᵢ|/Kᵢ)≤2`, and any positive `B` dominating those scales,
`P(|ΣXᵢ|≥t)≤2exp(-min(t²/ΣKᵢ²,t/B)/64)` for `t≥0`.
The family may be empty; all moment and exponential-integrability conditions are derived.
Vershynin 2018, Theorem 2.8.4; atlas `bernstein-scalar`.
atlas: bernstein-scalar

signature:
NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two_uniform.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (K : ℝ)
  (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (hK : 0 < K)
  (hmean : ∀ (i : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|X i ω| / K)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  μ.real {ω | t ≤ |∑ i, X i ω|} ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-(1 / 64) * min (t ^ 2 / (↑(Fintype.card ι) * K ^ 2)) (t / K))
name: NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two_uniform
doc:
Uniform-scale scalar Bernstein bound from `ψ₁` exponential moments:
`P(|ΣXᵢ|≥t)≤2exp(-min(t²/(N K²),t/K)/64)` for independent centered coordinates.
The bound also covers the empty family. Vershynin 2018, Theorem 2.8.4 (common-scale
corollary of `bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two`).

signature:
NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

doc:

singular-value tail `∑_{k ≤ i < card m} σ_i²` (Eckart–Young; the infimum form is
`bestRankFrobSq_eq_sInf`, attained by `truncatedSVD A k`). Padding includes rectangular null
directions and zero dimensions. Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.
atlas: best-rank-approx-def

name: NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq_eq_sInf
doc:
The optimal rank-`k` squared Frobenius error is the infimum over all matrices of rank at
most `k` (attained by `truncatedSVD A k`). Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.
atlas: eckart-young-frobenius

signature:

signature:

signature:

Hermitian linearization is at most four times the original energy. The

doc:
A literal uniform unit-sphere coefficient budget bounds the attained
closed-ball bilinear energy. Zero probes and empty shapes are included.

NLAlib.bilinearSquareMass_le_specNorm_coefficientCovariance.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]

series variance for Hermitian coefficients, including empty dimensions.

Euclidean unit balls. It is finite for square-integrable matrix laws.
Source: arXiv:2201.05142v3, the sigma-star parameter.

NLAlib.bilinearWeakVariance_eq_sSup_unitSphere.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]

      ((fun q => ∫ (A : Matrix n n ℂ), ‖star q.1.ofLp ⬝ᵥ (A - ∫ (B : Matrix n n ℂ), B ∂μ).mulVec q.2.ofLp‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ''
        {q | ‖q.1‖ = 1 ∧ ‖q.2‖ = 1})

The defined centered bilinear weak variance equals the literal source
unit-sphere supremum in nonempty dimension. Genuine vector normalization
proves the reverse inequality; no maximizing probe is assumed.

signature: NLAlib.bisectionInterval (f : ℝ → ℝ) (v lo hi : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ × ℝ
name: NLAlib.bisectionInterval
doc:
Midpoint bisection for the equation `f x = v`, with the lower half retained
when the midpoint value is at least `v`.

signature:
NLAlib.bisectionInterval_contains_root {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a v lo hi root : ℝ} (hf : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Ioi a))
  (hroot : f root = v) (ha : a ≤ lo) (hlo : lo < root) (hhi : root ≤ hi) (n : ℕ) :
  a ≤ (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).1 ∧
    (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).1 < root ∧ root ≤ (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).2
name: NLAlib.bisectionInterval_contains_root
doc:
Bisection preserves a root of a strictly increasing function on `(a,∞)`.
The initial lower endpoint is allowed to be exactly `a`; every midpoint lies
strictly above `a`, so the recursion never queries a singular endpoint.

name: NLAlib.bisectionInterval_screeThreshold
doc:
Midpoint bisection of the actual threshold equation retains the threshold
and has the exact width `(sqrt 3 - 1) * b / 2^j`. The singular edge is never
evaluated. Source: ScreeNOT, Supplement Appendix A.
atlas: scree-threshold-root (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.bisectionInterval_sub (f : ℝ → ℝ) (v lo hi : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).2 - (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).1 = (hi - lo) / 2 ^ n
name: NLAlib.bisectionInterval_sub
doc:
Each bisection step halves the interval width, independently of the
comparison oracle and without any regularity assumptions on `f`.

signature:
NLAlib.bisectionInterval_upper_sub_root_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a v lo hi root : ℝ} (hf : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Ioi a))
  (hroot : f root = v) (ha : a ≤ lo) (hlo : lo < root) (hhi : root ≤ hi) (n : ℕ) :
  0 ≤ (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).2 - root ∧
    (NLAlib.bisectionInterval f v lo hi n).2 - root ≤ (hi - lo) / 2 ^ n
name: NLAlib.bisectionInterval_upper_sub_root_le
doc:
The computed upper endpoint is within the exact bisection width of the
root. This statement covers a root at the initial upper endpoint.

signature:
NLAlib.card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_sign_changes {m : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {x : ℝ}
  (hp : ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ m → NLAlib.leadingMinor (A - x • 1) k ≠ 0) :
  {i | hA.eigenvalues i < x}.card =
    {k | NLAlib.leadingMinor (A - x • 1) ↑k * NLAlib.leadingMinor (A - x • 1) (↑k + 1) < 0}.card
name: NLAlib.card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_sign_changes
doc:
**Eigenvalue count from the leading principal minors (Sturm / Jacobi).** Let `A : Fin m × Fin m`
be real symmetric and `p_k = det (A − xI)_{1:k, 1:k}` (`p_0 = 1`). If every `p_k` (`1 ≤ k ≤ m`)
is nonzero, then the number of eigenvalues of `A` below `x` equals the number of sign changes
in `p_0, p_1, …, p_m`, i.e. `#{k < m : p_k p_{k+1} < 0}`. For an unreduced symmetric
tridiagonal `A` the `p_k` obey the Sturm three-term recurrence
`p_{k+1} = (a_{k+1} − x) p_k − b_k² p_{k−1}`, and this count drives bisection.
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 8.5.1 and §8.4.1; Parlett (1998) [`parlett98`], Ch. 3;
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5. Nonzero leading minors give `LU` of `A − xI`
(`luSucceeds_iff_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero`), symmetric so
`A − xI = L D Lᵀ` with `d_{k+1} = p_{k+1}/p_k` (`IsLU.leadingMinor_eq_prod`); then
`card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_neg_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul` and `p_{k+1}/p_k < 0 ↔ p_k p_{k+1} < 0`.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:

`f(A)` is `p(A)` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the (distinct) eigenvalues of the

doc:
A matrix function of a symmetric `A` equals the polynomial calculus of any polynomial that
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues: `f(A) = p(A)` when `p(λᵢ) = f(λᵢ)` for all `i`.
Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4 and Thm 1.12). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper).

The Hermitian functional calculus in eigenbasis coordinates: `f(A) = U diag(f(λᵢ)) Uᴴ`
(Mathlib's `IsHermitian.cfc`, unfolded). Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.5.6.

signature:

Every scalar function on a finite Hermitian spectrum uses the same

signature:

A block-diagonal matrix of Hermitian blocks is Hermitian, its spectrum is the union of the block
spectra, and the functional calculus acts blockwise.

Tropp 2015, proof of Thm 8.5.2. Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from the Prove2me
mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

Auxiliary; not a numbered result in the source.

Every real function on a Hermitian matrix's finite spectrum commutes with
unitary conjugation. No global continuity premise is needed. Source: Mathlib's
CFC transport and Tropp 2015, Theorem 8.5.2; atlas `golden-thompson`,

signature: NLAlib.cgInit.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.CGState n
name: NLAlib.cgInit
doc:
The initial state `(x₀, r₀, r₀)` with `r₀ = c − A x₀`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Alg. 38.1. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

signature: NLAlib.cgObjective.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.cgObjective
doc:
The conjugate-gradient objective `φ(x) = ½ xᵀ A x − cᵀ x`. Its minimiser over `ℝⁿ` (for
positive definite `A`) solves `A x = c`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.6).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (c u d : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (u + d) = NLAlib.cgObjective A c u + d ⬝ᵥ (A.mulVec u - c) + NLAlib.quadForm A d / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_add
doc:
Expansion of the CG objective along a direction: for symmetric `A`,
`φ(u + d) = φ(u) + dᵀ (A u − c) + ½ dᵀ A d`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of
Thm 38.2. Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c z = NLAlib.cgObjective A c xs + NLAlib.quadForm A (z - xs) / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub
doc:
The CG objective measures the `A`-norm error: if `A x⋆ = c` then
`φ(z) = φ(x⋆) + ½ ‖z − x⋆‖_A²`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.7).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A W : Matrix n n ℝ) (c y : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (W.mulVec y) = NLAlib.cgObjective (W.transpose * A * W) (W.transpose.mulVec c) y
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec
doc:
The CG objective under a change of variables: `φ_{A,c}(Wy) = φ_{WᵀAW, Wᵀc}(y)`.
Helper for `preconditioned-cg`.

signature: NLAlib.cgRecurrence.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.CGState n
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence
doc:
The **conjugate-gradient recursion**: the state after `k` Hestenes–Stiefel steps from
`(x₀, r₀, r₀)`, as `Nat.iterate`. `(cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).x` is the CG iterate `x_k`
(`isCGIterate_cgRecurrence`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 38.1; Hestenes–Stiefel
(1952). Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_add_of_r_eq_zero
doc:
After a zero residual the recursion is constant: if `r_k = 0` then for every `m ≥ 1` the
state `k + m` is `(x_k, 0, 0)`. Atlas: `cg-recurrence` (totality).

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) k ∧
    (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (k + 1) ∧
      (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).p ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (k + 1)
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
**Krylov memberships**, for every `A` (no hypothesis): `x_k − x₀ ∈ K_k(A, r₀)` and
`r_k, p_k ∈ K_{k+1}(A, r₀)`. Induction on `k` with `mulVec_mem_krylovSpace_succ`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (the inclusion half).
Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_p_eq_zero_of_r_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {k : ℕ}
  (hk : (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r = 0) : (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).p = 0
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_p_eq_zero_of_r_eq_zero
doc:
A zero residual forces a zero search direction: `r_k = 0 → p_k = 0` (for `k = 0`, `p_0 = r_0`;
otherwise `β_{k−1} = 0`). No hypothesis on `A`. Atlas: `cg-recurrence` (totality).

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r = c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).x
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_eq
doc:
**The residual identity** `r_k = c − A x_k`, for every `A` and every `k` (no hypothesis).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 38.1 (the update of `r` is the update of
`c − A x`). Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**The residual vanishes from the grade on**: for `A ≻ 0`, `r_k = 0` when
`k ≥ ν(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1. Proof:
`cgRecurrence_x_eq_of_krylovGrade_le` with `x⋆ = A⁻¹ c` and `cgRecurrence_r_eq`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_ne_zero_of_lt_krylovGrade.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k < NLAlib.krylovGrade A (c - A.mulVec x₀)) : (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_ne_zero_of_lt_krylovGrade
doc:
**No breakdown before the grade**: `r_k ≠ 0` for `k < ν(A, r₀)`, for every `A` (no
definiteness needed). With `cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le` this says that for `A ≻ 0`
the recursion stops (`r_k = 0`, the only case in which a denominator vanishes, since
`pᵀAp = 0 ↔ p = 0`) exactly at the grade. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (the
hypothesis "`r_{k−1} ≠ 0`" is automatic below the grade); Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.3.
Proof: if `r_k = 0` then `r₀ = A (x_k − x₀) ∈ A K_k`, so `K_{k+1} ≤ A K_k` and
`min (k+1) ν ≤ min k ν` (`finrank_krylovSpace`), forcing `ν ≤ k`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_succ.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ (k + 1) = NLAlib.cgStep A (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k)
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_succ
doc: One more step of the recursion. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_x_eq_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**Finite termination of the recursion**: for `A ≻ 0` and `A x⋆ = c`, `x_k = x⋆` once
`k ≥ ν(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (CG converges in at most `n`
steps); Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.7. Proof: `isCGIterate_cgRecurrence` and
`eq_of_isCGIterate_of_krylovGrade_le` (atlas `cg-finite-termination`).
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ 0 = NLAlib.cgInit A c x₀
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_zero
doc: The recursion starts at `(x₀, r₀, r₀)`. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

signature: NLAlib.cgStep.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (s : NLAlib.CGState n) : NLAlib.CGState n
name: NLAlib.cgStep
doc:
One Hestenes–Stiefel step: `α = rᵀr / pᵀAp`, `x' = x + α p`, `r' = r − α A p`,
`β = r'ᵀr' / rᵀr`, `p' = r' + β p`. Total: with `x / 0 = 0` a zero residual gives `α = β = 0`
(`cgStep_of_r_eq_zero`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 38.1; Saad (2011)
[`saad11`], Alg. 6.18. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgStep_of_r_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {s : NLAlib.CGState n} (hs : s.r = 0) :
  NLAlib.cgStep A s = { x := s.x, r := 0, p := 0 }
name: NLAlib.cgStep_of_r_eq_zero
doc:
**A zero residual freezes the state**: if `r = 0` then `cgStep A s = (x, 0, 0)` (`α = 0`
and `β = 0/0 = 0`). Atlas: `cg-recurrence` (totality).

signature:
NLAlib.cgf_const_mul.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Y : Ω → ℝ} (a θ : ℝ) :
