signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_eq_of_preconnected.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [TopologicalSpace Ω] [PreconnectedSpace Ω] (A : Ω → Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : Continuous A) (K L : Set ℂ) (hK : IsCompact K)
  (hL : IsCompact L) (hdisj : Disjoint K L) (hspec : ∀ (t : Ω), spectrum ℂ (A t) ⊆ K ∪ L) (s t : Ω) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn (A s) K = NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn (A t) K
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_eq_of_preconnected
doc:
Along a continuous family over a preconnected parameter space, the
number of characteristic roots in either of two disjoint compact spectral
sets is constant, including algebraic multiplicities.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.1.1; the finite closed root-count fibers are
clopen, so no root tracking or analytic projector is required.

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinColumnUnion_eq_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

  (hdisj : Disjoint (NLAlib.gershgorinColumnUnion A I) (NLAlib.gershgorinColumnUnion A Iᶜ)) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn A (NLAlib.gershgorinColumnUnion A I) = I.card
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinColumnUnion_eq_card
doc:
A union of selected closed column discs, disjoint from the remaining
closed column discs, contains exactly as many algebraic eigenvalues as
selected columns. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 6.1.3; all degenerate
and repeated-root cases are retained by transpose and the root multiset.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinRowUnion_eq_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

  (hdisj : Disjoint (NLAlib.gershgorinRowUnion A I) (NLAlib.gershgorinRowUnion A Iᶜ)) :

name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinRowUnion_eq_card
doc:
A union of `|I|` closed row discs, disjoint from the remaining closed
row discs, contains exactly `|I|` eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.1.1; internal overlaps, repeated roots,
zero-radius discs, empty selections and empty matrices are included.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_le_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (K : Set ℂ) :

name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_le_card
doc:
A characteristic-root count is at most the matrix dimension, including
empty shapes. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.1.1.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_add_vecMulVec_mul_X_sub_C.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [Infinite K] {A : Matrix n n K} {x : n → K} {μ : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hAx : A.mulVec x = μ • x) (y : n → K) :
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C μ) * (A + Matrix.vecMulVec x y).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (μ + y ⬝ᵥ x)) * A.charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_add_vecMulVec_mul_X_sub_C
doc:
The rank-one eigenvalue update satisfies a polynomial cross-product
identity, including every value of the polynomial variable.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.4.10.1; the infinite-field proof extends the
determinant-lemma computation across the finite old spectrum.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_bordered_diagonal_insertNth {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (p : Fin (n + 1)) (v : Fin n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) (p.insertNth 0 v))
        (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) (p.insertNth 0 v)) (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d p)) *
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ p.succAbove)) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) v)
          (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) v) (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_bordered_diagonal_insertNth
doc:
Inserting a zero coupling in a bordered diagonal matrix restores an
uncoupled scalar characteristic factor. The border scalar is preserved.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.21; repeated-root restoration helper.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_colleagueMatrix (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
  (NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp).charpoly = p * Polynomial.C p.leadingCoeff⁻¹
name: NLAlib.charpoly_colleagueMatrix
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of the colleague matrix is the monic normalization
of its polynomial, with root multiplicities preserved. Source: Trefethen, ATAP,
Theorem 18.1; proved by quotient multiplication and basis invariance.
atlas: colleague-matrix (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_colleagueMatrix_of_chebyshev_expansion (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (a : ℕ → ℝ)
  (ha : p = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (p.natDegree + 1), a j • Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑j) :
  (NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp).charpoly = Polynomial.C (1 / (2 ^ (p.natDegree - 1) * a p.natDegree)) * p
name: NLAlib.charpoly_colleagueMatrix_of_chebyshev_expansion
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of a colleague matrix for a Chebyshev expansion
is `p/(2^(n−1)a_n)`. Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 18.1. This identity preserves
multiplicities; the explicit recurrence rows are supplied by the adjacent lemmas.
atlas: colleague-matrix

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_companionMatrix.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {p : Polynomial K} (hp : p.Monic) :
  (NLAlib.companionMatrix p).charpoly = p
name: NLAlib.charpoly_companionMatrix
doc:
A monic polynomial is exactly the characteristic polynomial of its companion matrix,
including the constant monic polynomial one and the empty companion matrix.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 3.2.4.2.
atlas: companion-matrix (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field K]
  [Infinite K] (d v : n → K) :
  (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly =
    ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i)) -
      ∑ i, Polynomial.C (v i ^ 2) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d j))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of a diagonal matrix plus `v vᵀ` is its
diagonal product minus the sum of squared couplings times products with
one factor erased. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), converse interlacing;
no distinctness, nonzero-entry or invertibility assumption is required,
and the empty matrix has characteristic polynomial one.
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_insertNth {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (p : Fin (n + 1)) (v : Fin n → ℝ) :
  (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec (p.insertNth 0 v) (p.insertNth 0 v)).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d p)) * (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ p.succAbove) + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_insertNth

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (e : n ≃ m) (d v : n → ℝ) :
  (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ ⇑e.symm) + Matrix.vecMulVec (v ∘ ⇑e.symm) (v ∘ ⇑e.symm)).charpoly =
    (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_reindex
doc:
Relabeling a diagonal rank-one update leaves its characteristic
polynomial unchanged. Source: permutation similarity; helper for converse
interlacing on arbitrary finite matrix labels.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_arrowhead_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (e : n ≃ m) (d v : n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ ⇑e.symm)) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) (v ∘ ⇑e.symm))
        (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) (v ∘ ⇑e.symm)) (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
    (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) v) (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) v)
        (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_arrowhead_reindex

signature: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_one_neg_one_eq : (Matrix.diagonal ![1, -1]).charpoly = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - 1
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_one_neg_one_eq
doc:
The diagonal matrix with entries one and minus one has characteristic
polynomial `X²-1`. This is the gap-coefficient counterexample in frontier
equation `herm:coefficient-correct`, correcting `sylvester-criterion`.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_orthogonal_compression.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {k : ℕ} (f : Module.End 𝕜 E) {u : E}
  (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) {μ : 𝕜} (hfu : f u = μ • u) (hk : Module.finrank 𝕜 E = k + 1) :
  LinearMap.charpoly f =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C μ) * (↑(𝕜 ∙ u)ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘ₗ f ∘ₗ (𝕜 ∙ u)ᗮ.subtype).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_orthogonal_compression
doc:
Compressing away a unit eigenvector removes exactly its characteristic
linear factor. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 2.3.1; no
normality or simplicity assumption is needed.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_submatrix_of_isolated_coordinate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [CommRing K] (M : Matrix n n K) (i : n) (μ : K) (hcol : ∀ (j : n), M j i = if j = i then μ else 0)
  (hrow : ∀ (j : n), M i j = if j = i then μ else 0) :
  M.charpoly = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C μ) * (M.submatrix (fun j => ↑j) fun j => ↑j).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_submatrix_of_isolated_coordinate
doc:
An isolated coordinate contributes exactly one characteristic linear
factor. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 1.4.7; the remaining block is
the principal submatrix on all other coordinates, including an empty block.
The special case of `charpoly_eq_mul_of_isolated_equiv` for the equivalence
`Fin 1 ⊕ {j // j ≠ i} ≃ n` (over any commutative ring).

name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_succ_submatrix
doc:
A first-column eigenvalue factors out of the characteristic polynomial.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §1.4; first-column Laplace expansion.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_mul_of_isolated_equiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [CommRing K] (A : Matrix m m K) (e : Fin 1 ⊕ n ≃ m)
  (h : ∀ (j : n), A (e (Sum.inl 0)) (e (Sum.inr j)) = 0 ∧ A (e (Sum.inr j)) (e (Sum.inl 0)) = 0) :
  A.charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (A (e (Sum.inl 0)) (e (Sum.inl 0)))) *
      (A.submatrix (fun j => e (Sum.inr j)) fun j => e (Sum.inr j)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_mul_of_isolated_equiv
doc:
An uncoupled scalar coordinate contributes one linear characteristic
factor, with the other coordinates in any specified order. Horn–Johnson
2013, Section 1.2; converse-interlacing restoration helper.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_prod_of_eval_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (d : n → ℂ)
  (h : ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card n + 1)), Polynomial.eval (↑↑j) A.charpoly = ∏ i, (↑↑j - d i)) :
  A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_prod_of_eval_eq

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_fromBlocks_diagonal_replicate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Field K] [Infinite K] {l : Type u_3} [Unique l] [Fintype l] [DecidableEq l] (d v : n → K) (a : K) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol l v) (Matrix.replicateRow l v)
        (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) * ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i)) -
      ∑ i, Polynomial.C (v i ^ 2) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d j))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_fromBlocks_diagonal_replicate
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of a real or infinite-field diagonal
arrowhead is the diagonal product times its last linear factor, minus the
sum of squared couplings times the products with one factor erased.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), converse interlacing; the formula is
unconditional, including repeated diagonal entries and empty leading blocks.
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_gramian_product_mul_X.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} {a : Type u_3}
  {b : Type u_4} [Fintype n] [Fintype a] [Fintype b] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq a] [DecidableEq b] (R : Matrix n a 𝕜)
  (O : Matrix b n 𝕜) :
  Polynomial.X ^ Fintype.card a * (R * R.conjTranspose * (O.conjTranspose * O)).charpoly =
    Polynomial.X ^ Fintype.card n * ((O * R).conjTranspose * (O * R)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_gramian_product_mul_X
doc:
The Gramian product and `HᴴH`, `H=OR`, have identical nonzero
characteristic roots, with multiplicities certified before cancellation.
Thus its positive eigenvalues are precisely positive squared singular values
of `OR`, including the rectangular and singular cases.
atlas: gramian-svd-balancing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_inverse_mul_eq_prod_of_congruence.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B S : Matrix n n ℝ} {d : n → ℝ} (hS : IsUnit S) (hA : A = S * S.transpose)
  (hB : B = S * Matrix.diagonal d * S.transpose) : (A⁻¹ * B).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_inverse_mul_eq_prod_of_congruence
doc:
The diagonal of a definite-pair congruence enumerates the relative
operator's eigenvalues with full characteristic multiplicity.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.6.1;
helper for `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence`.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_jacobiMatrix_eq_jacobiContinuant.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜] [Infinite 𝕜] (a β : ℕ → 𝕜) (n : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.jacobiMatrix a β n).charpoly = NLAlib.jacobiContinuant a β n
name: NLAlib.charpoly_jacobiMatrix_eq_jacobiContinuant
doc:
The finite Jacobi continued-fraction denominator is the actual monic matrix
characteristic polynomial. Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 1.34; (OF26).
atlas: monic-orthogonal-recurrence (partial), jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_mul_conjTranspose_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} {r : Type u_4} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq r] (B U : Matrix n r 𝕜) (hr : Fintype.card r ≤ Fintype.card n) :
  (B * U.conjTranspose).charpoly = Polynomial.X ^ (Fintype.card n - Fintype.card r) * (U.conjTranspose * B).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_mul_conjTranspose_eq
doc:
Ambient and reduced DMD have the same nonzero characteristic roots with
their algebraic multiplicities. This is the rectangular product identity and
therefore also applies to any retained positive SVD block.
atlas: dmd-reduced-eigenpair-lifting (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_mul_mul_transpose_of_hasOrthonormalCols.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (Q A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) : (Q * A * Q.transpose).charpoly = A.charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_mul_mul_transpose_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Orthogonal conjugation preserves the characteristic polynomial.
Source: similarity invariance, used by the converse-interlacing transports.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_neg_eq_prod_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (d : n → ℝ) (hd : A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))) :
  (-A).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (-d i))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_neg_eq_prod_of_isHermitian
doc:
Negating a real symmetric matrix negates every entry of any complete
characteristic-root list, including multiplicities. Source: the spectral
theorem; helper for the negative rank-one converse-interlacing construction.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_nonsing_inv_mul_mul_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]
  (A S : Matrix n n K) (hS : IsUnit S) : (S⁻¹ * A * S).charpoly = A.charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_nonsing_inv_mul_mul_eq
doc:
Nonsingular similarity preserves the characteristic polynomial.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §1.3; this is the cyclic characteristic identity.

name: NLAlib.charpoly_orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of the actual moment Jacobi matrix is the
canonical monic orthogonal polynomial. Its simple Hermitian spectrum therefore
constructs every real Gauss node.
Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorems 1.19 and 1.27.
atlas: orthogonal-polynomial-zeros (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_symmetricBorder_single_last {q : ℕ} (J : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) (b d : ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.symmetricBorder J (Pi.single (Fin.last q) b) d).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C d) * J.charpoly -
      Polynomial.C (b ^ 2) * (J.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_symmetricBorder_single_last
doc:
The actual symmetric last-coordinate border has the classical monic
characteristic-polynomial recurrence. No tridiagonal shape is needed; the off-spectrum
Schur calculation is extended to a polynomial identity at every point.
Source: focused mathematical reroutes, Section 3 (BL6), after (BL10).
atlas: gauss-radau-lobatto (partial)

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex (N k : ℕ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex
doc:
Frequency folding into the degree range of the canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_eq_self_of_le {n k : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hk : k ≤ n) : NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex n k = k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_eq_self_of_le
doc:
Interpolation leaves low Chebyshev frequencies unchanged.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1; helper for `chebyshev-aliasing`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_le {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex N k ≤ N
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_le
doc:
Every folded frequency has degree at most the grid cutoff.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_two_mul_add_mul {n : ℕ} (_hn : 0 < n) (l r : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex n (2 * (l * n + r)) = NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex n (2 * r)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_two_mul_add_mul
doc:
Folding an even frequency depends only on its index modulo the grid size.
Source: the finite-block proof in the focused quadrature reroute.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier
doc:
The gap-amplifying polynomial `chebyshevAmplifier α γ q = T_q(X/α) / T_q(1 + γ)`: equal to
`1` at `α(1 + γ)`, increasing beyond it, and exponentially small on `[−α, α]`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5; Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.
atlas: chebyshev-amplifier

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + γ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C (1 / α) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff
doc:
The real Chebyshev coefficients are the real parts of the standard contour coefficients.
For a function real on `[-1,1]` these are the usual real Chebyshev expansion coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_eq_chebyshevCoeff {F : ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k = NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_eq_chebyshevCoeff
doc:
A continuous real restriction identifies the real contour coefficient with the
weighted real Chebyshev coefficient. No holomorphic extension is needed for this equality.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant (F : ℂ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant
doc:
The Lagrange interpolant on the `(N+1)`-point canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Mathlib totalizes the `N=0` grid at the point `1`; this convention is made explicit.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 2 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, definition).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc (F : ℂ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc
doc:
The degree-`N` truncation of the canonical real Chebyshev coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, definition).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAngleMeasure : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAngleMeasure
doc: Lebesgue angle measure used by the Chebyshev change of variables.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction
doc:
Pull back a complex function on the Bernstein ellipse to the additive circle.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_coe_eq_cos (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F ↑θ = F ↑(Real.cos θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_coe_eq_cos
doc:
The circle pullback evaluated at a real angle is exactly `F(cos θ)`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_neg (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F (-θ) = NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F θ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_neg
doc:
The circle pullback is even, by the inversion symmetry of the Joukowski transform.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff
doc:
Real Chebyshev coefficient with zeroth normalization `1/π` and positive normalization
`2/π`, using the arcsine weight. Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3.
atlas: chebyshev-coefficients-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_eq_half_integral (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => |x|) k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) / Real.pi * (1 + (-1) ^ k) * ∫ (θ : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi / 2, Real.cos θ * Real.cos (↑k * θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_eq_half_integral
doc:
Reflecting the absolute-cosine coefficient integral reduces it to half a period.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6; helper for `chebyshev-series-abs-sign`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_even {j : ℕ} (hj : 0 < j) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => |x|) (2 * j) = 4 / Real.pi * (-1) ^ (j + 1) / (4 * ↑j ^ 2 - 1)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_even
doc:
The positive even Chebyshev coefficients of absolute value are the exact classical fractions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6.
atlas: chebyshev-series-abs-sign (partial)

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_odd (j : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => |x|) (2 * j + 1) = 0
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_odd
doc:
Every odd Chebyshev coefficient of absolute value vanishes.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6.
atlas: chebyshev-series-abs-sign (partial)

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_zero : NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => |x|) 0 = 2 / Real.pi
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_abs_zero
doc:
The constant Chebyshev coefficient of absolute value is `2/π`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6.
atlas: chebyshev-series-abs-sign (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_add {f g : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => f x + g x) k = NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k + NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff g k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_add
doc:
Chebyshev coefficient functionals preserve addition of continuous functions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3.
atlas: chebyshev-coefficients-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_congr {f g : ℝ → ℝ} (hfg : Set.EqOn f g (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k = NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff g k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_congr
doc:
Chebyshev coefficients depend only on the unit-interval restriction.
Source: the actual cosine integral; helper for `chebyshev-projection-lebesgue-constant`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_const_mul (f : ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => c * f x) k = c * NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_const_mul
doc:
Chebyshev coefficient functionals preserve scalar multiplication.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3.
atlas: chebyshev-coefficients-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_cosine_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) / Real.pi * ∫ (θ : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi, f (Real.cos θ) * Real.cos (↑k * θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_cosine_integral
doc:
The weighted coefficient is the usual cosine coefficient, including the zeroth
normalization. Source: the cosine substitution for the Chebyshev weight.
atlas: chebyshev-coefficients-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_integral_derivative {u v : ℝ → ℝ} (hu : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval u (-1) 1)
  (huv : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ), x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1 → deriv u x = v x) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff u k = 2 / (Real.pi * ↑k) * ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, v x * Real.sin (↑k * Real.arccos x)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_integral_derivative
doc:
AC integration by parts expresses a positive Chebyshev coefficient using its derivative.
Source: focused reroutes, Lemma `lem:ip`; helper for `chebyshev-coeff-bv-decay`.
The derivative representative is specified almost everywhere on the interval.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_re_fourierCoeff {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) * (fourierCoeff (fun t => ↑(NLAlib.realChebyshevCircleFunction f t)) ↑k).re
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_re_fourierCoeff
doc:
The actual Chebyshev coefficient is the real Fourier coefficient, doubled except at zero.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 3.1; helper for `chebyshev-series-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_sub_derivative {u v : ℝ → ℝ} (hu : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval u (-1) 1)
  (huv : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ), x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1 → deriv u x = v x) (hv : BoundedVariationOn v (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) {k : ℕ}
  (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff u k = (NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff v (k - 1) - NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff v (k + 1)) / (2 * ↑k)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_sub_derivative
doc:
A derivative representative shifts a positive Chebyshev coefficient by one in each direction.
Source: focused reroutes, equation `eq:rec`; helper for `chebyshev-coeff-bv-decay`.
The `k=1` normalization is handled in `chebyshevCoeff_one_eq_derivative`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_weighted_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) / Real.pi *
      ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, f x * Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k) * √(1 - x ^ 2)⁻¹
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_weighted_integral
doc:
The arcsine-measure coefficient is the classical weighted integral on `[-1,1]`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3.
atlas: chebyshev-coefficients-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eval_T (j k : ℕ) :

The coefficient of a Chebyshev basis polynomial is its Kronecker delta.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eval_eq_zero_of_degree_lt {p : Polynomial ℝ} {n k : ℕ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑n) (hnk : n < k) :

Coefficients above the degree of a polynomial vanish.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eval_interpolant_eq_foldCoeff {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))

name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eval_interpolant_eq_foldCoeff
doc:
The interpolant's genuine Chebyshev coefficient is exactly its folded frequency fiber.
This is the aliasing coefficient formula for every index, including both endpoint fibers.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eval_sum_smul_T (c : ℕ → ℝ) (n k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => Polynomial.eval x (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), c j • Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑j)) k =

name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eval_sum_smul_T
doc:
The Chebyshev coefficient of a finite Chebyshev expansion is its corresponding entry.
Source: finite orthogonal projection, Trefethen ATAP, Chapter 3.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_exp_eq_modifiedBesselCoeff (a : ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => Real.exp (a * x)) k = (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) * NLAlib.modifiedBesselCoeff a k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_exp_eq_modifiedBesselCoeff
doc:
The exponential's Chebyshev coefficients are the modified Bessel coefficients,
with the constant coefficient undoubled.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.15.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_one_eq_derivative {u v : ℝ → ℝ} (hu : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval u (-1) 1)
  (huv : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ), x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1 → deriv u x = v x) (hv : BoundedVariationOn v (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff u 1 = NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff v 0 - NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff v 2 / 2
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_one_eq_derivative
doc:
The first Chebyshev coefficient has the special undoubled zeroth derivative coefficient.
Source: focused reroutes, equation `eq:rec1`; helper for `chebyshev-coeff-bv-decay`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sign_eq_half_integral (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff Real.sign k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) / Real.pi * (1 - (-1) ^ k) * ∫ (θ : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi / 2, Real.cos (↑k * θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sign_eq_half_integral
doc:
Reflection reduces the sign-function coefficient integral to the positive half period.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6; helper for `chebyshev-series-abs-sign`.
Endpoint values and the value at the central jump do not affect the integral.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sign_even (j : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff Real.sign (2 * j) = 0
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sign_even
doc:
Every even Chebyshev coefficient of the real sign function vanishes.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6.
atlas: chebyshev-series-abs-sign (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sign_odd (j : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff Real.sign (2 * j + 1) = 4 * (-1) ^ j / (Real.pi * (2 * ↑j + 1))
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sign_odd
doc:
The exact odd sign coefficients have the corrected alternating sign `(-1)^j`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 3.6; the coefficient at frequency `2j+1` is `4(-1)^j/(π(2j+1))`.
atlas: chebyshev-series-abs-sign (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sub {f g : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (fun x => f x - g x) k = NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k - NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff g k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_sub
doc:
Chebyshev coefficient functionals preserve subtraction of continuous functions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3; helper for `chebyshev-series-convergence`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff
doc:
Complex Chebyshev coefficients in their Joukowski contour form. The zeroth coefficient
has normalization `1/(2πi)`; positive coefficients have normalization `1/(πi)`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k = (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) * fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) ↑k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff
doc:
The contour definition agrees exactly with the standard Fourier definition of the
Chebyshev coefficients, including the distinct zeroth normalization.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_ofReal_chebyshevCoeff {F : ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k = ↑(NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_ofReal_chebyshevCoeff
doc:
The complex contour coefficient itself is the real weighted coefficient when the
restriction is real and continuous. Source: even-real Fourier symmetry and the contour bridge.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCube.{u_1} (ι : Type u_1) [Fintype ι] : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevExtrema (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)) : ↑(Set.Icc (-1) 1)

The canonical Chebyshev extrema, bundled in `[-1,1]` with finite indexing.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevFoldCoeff (a : ℕ → ℝ) (n j : ℕ) : ℝ

doc:
Folding an absolutely summable coefficient sequence adds each frequency fiber once.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.2; operator rederivations `polyseries:aliasing`.
The fiber formulation includes the distinct endpoint coefficients without double counting.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevFoldPolynomial (a : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevFoldPolynomial
doc:
The finite Chebyshev polynomial formed by folded coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.2; helper for `chebyshev-aliasing`.

The actual Lagrange interpolant on the canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 4.1 and 4.2.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevInterpolant_eq_foldPolynomial {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))

The actual interpolant of a continuous function with absolute Chebyshev coefficients

Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 4.1 and 4.2.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a b : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate for spectrum in `[a, b]`: the polynomial method whose residual
polynomial is `chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`,
i.e. iteration polynomial `(1 − chebyshevResidual a b q) /ₘ X`. Source: Saad (2003)
[`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: defined by its polynomial; the
recurrence of Saad Alg. 12.1 is the theorem `chebyshevIterate_add_two`.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_add_two.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ (q + 2) =
    (Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑(q + 2)))⁻¹ •
      ((4 / (b - a) * Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑(q + 1))) •
          (((b + a) / 2) • NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ (q + 1) +
            (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ (q + 1)))) -
        Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) • NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_add_two
doc:
**The Chebyshev three-term recurrence** (Saad Alg. 12.1 in three-term form): for `0 < a < b`,
with `τ_k = T_k(σ)`, `σ = (b + a)/(b − a)`, `θ = (b + a)/2`, `δ = (b − a)/2` and
`r_k = c − A x_k`,
`τ_{q+2} x_{q+2} = (2τ_{q+1}/δ)(θ x_{q+1} + r_{q+1}) − τ_q x_q`, i.e.
`x_{q+2} = τ_{q+2}⁻¹ ((4τ_{q+1}/(b − a)) (θ x_{q+1} + r_{q+1}) − τ_q x_q)`.
No hypothesis on `A` and no solution is needed (a polynomial identity applied to `r₀`).
Saad's two-term form with `ρ_k = τ_k/τ_{k+1}` and `d_k = x_{k+1} − x_k`
(`d_k = ρ_kρ_{k−1} d_{k−1} + (2ρ_k/δ) r_k`) is a rearrangement of this identity together with
`τ_{q+2} = 2σ τ_{q+1} − τ_q`. Proof: `Polynomial.funext` after cancelling `X`, using
`Chebyshev.T_add_two` at `σ − 2t/(b − a)` and at `σ`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3, Alg. 12.1; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`].
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ 1 = x₀ + (2 / (b + a)) • (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_one
doc:
**First Chebyshev step**: `x_1 = x₀ + r₀/θ`, `θ = (b + a)/2`, for `0 < a < b`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 12.1 (`d_0 = r_0/θ`).
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
  (hab : a < b) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate lies in `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` (its iteration polynomial has degree
`< q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a b : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ 0 = x₀
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_zero
doc:
`chebyshevIterate` at `q = 0` is the starting point. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Alg. 12.1. Atlas: `chebyshev-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel_coe_eq_sum (M : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel M ↑t =
    1 + 2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M, NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M (j + 1) * Real.cos (↑(j + 1) * t)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel_coe_eq_sum
doc: Evaluating the circle kernel at a real angle gives its ordinary cosine expansion.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel_eq_sum (M : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel M t =
    1 + 2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M, NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M (j + 1) * ((fourier ↑(j + 1)) t).re
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel_eq_sum
doc: Autocorrelation gives the exact finite cosine expansion of the circle kernel.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel_nonneg (M : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  0 ≤ NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel M t
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel_nonneg
doc: The circle kernel is nonnegative by its actual squared-norm construction.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping (M j : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping
doc: The explicit Jackson damping coefficient, with its continuous trigonometric formula.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_eq_autocorrelation (M j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ M + 1) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M j =
    2 / (↑M + 2) *
      ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (M + 1 - j),
        NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonSineWeight M l * NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonSineWeight M (l + j)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_eq_autocorrelation
doc: The displayed closed damping formula is its normalized sine autocorrelation.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_le_one {M j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ M + 1) : NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M j ≤ 1
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_le_one
doc:
Every retained damping coefficient lies below one; positivity and normalization
of the actual kernel prove this bound, including its first zero frequency.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_mem_Icc {M j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ M + 1) : NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M j ∈ Set.Icc 0 1
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_mem_Icc
doc: The explicit Jackson multipliers are genuine coefficient contractions.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_nonneg {M j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ M + 1) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M j
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_nonneg
doc: The exact Jackson damping coefficients are nonnegative, including the next zero mode.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_one (M : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M 1 = Real.cos (NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonAngle M)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_one
doc: The first damping coefficient is the cosine of the Jackson angle.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_succ (M : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M (M + 1) = 0
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_succ
doc: The next frequency after the cutoff has zero sine autocorrelation.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_two (M : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M 2 = ((↑M + 1) * Real.cos (2 * NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonAngle M) + 1) / (↑M + 2)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_two
doc:
The second coefficient has a simple formula also valid at the first cutoff,
where the second frequency is zero.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_zero (M : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M 0 = 1
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping_zero
doc: The zeroth Jackson damping coefficient preserves constants exactly.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel (M : ℕ) (x r : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel
doc: The actual finite normalized Chebyshev Jackson kernel.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_cos_eq_circle (M : ℕ) (a b : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel M (Real.cos a) (Real.cos b) =
    (NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel M ↑(a - b) + NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonCircleKernel M ↑(a + b)) / (2 * Real.pi)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_cos_eq_circle
doc:
The Chebyshev kernel is the sum of two translates of the positive circle
kernel. This is an equality of the actual finite kernels.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_cos_eq_sum (M : ℕ) (a b : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel M (Real.cos a) (Real.cos b) =
    1 / Real.pi +
      2 / Real.pi *
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.range M,
          NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonDamping M (j + 1) * Real.cos (↑(j + 1) * a) * Real.cos (↑(j + 1) * b)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_cos_eq_sum
doc: The normalized polynomial kernel has the usual finite cosine-product expansion.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_nonneg (M : ℕ) {x r : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) (hr : r ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :

doc: The explicit finite Jackson kernel is nonnegative on the entire closed square.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_symm (M : ℕ) (x r : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel M x r = NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel M r x
name: NLAlib.chebyshevJacksonKernel_symm
doc: The explicit Jackson kernel is symmetric.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevMoment_two_mul_add_one (j : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevMoment (2 * j + 1) = 0

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevProjectionLinearMap (n : ℕ) : C(↑(Set.Icc (-1) 1), ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] C(↑(Set.Icc (-1) 1), ℝ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevProjectionLinearMap
doc:
Chebyshev projection on continuous unit-interval functions is the restriction
of their genuine coefficient truncation. Clamping provides a canonical extension
whose values outside the interval do not affect any coefficient.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 15.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevProjectionLinearMap_eq_self (n : ℕ) (p : C(↑(Set.Icc (-1) 1), ℝ))

The bounded Chebyshev projection is the genuine algebraic coefficient projection.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) : Module.Basis (Fin p.natDegree) ℝ (AdjoinRoot p)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis
doc:
The first `deg p` Chebyshev polynomials form a basis of the quotient by any
nonzero real polynomial `p`. Source: triangular Chebyshev change of basis and
polynomial division; the finite-basis ingredient of ATAP Theorem 18.1.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis_apply (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (i : Fin p.natDegree) :
  (NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis p hp) i = (Polynomial.aeval (AdjoinRoot.root p)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑↑i)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis_apply
doc:
Each quotient Chebyshev basis vector is the residue of its Chebyshev polynomial.
Source: the basis construction for ATAP Theorem 18.1.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual
doc:
The shifted, scaled Chebyshev polynomial normalised to `1` at `0`:
`chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2 X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`. For `0 < a < b`
it has the smallest maximum modulus on `[a, b]` among polynomials of degree at most `q` with
value `1` at `0` (the residual polynomial of Chebyshev iteration and the model for CG).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: chebyshev-minimax

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C ((b + a) / (b - a)) - Polynomial.C (2 / (b - a)) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def

name: NLAlib.chebyshevTrunc

The degree-`n` partial sum of the Chebyshev expansion.

NLAlib.chebyshevTrunc_congr {f g : ℝ → ℝ} (hfg : Set.EqOn f g (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (n : ℕ) :

The Chebyshev zeros `chebyshevZero q k = cos((2k + 1)π/(2q))`, `k < q`: the `q` roots of

of the first kind"); Mathlib `Polynomial.Chebyshev.roots_T_real`.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.

name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_eq_cos_half_index
doc:
The actual Chebyshev zero uses the half-index root angle.
Source: the equivalent forms of the standard Chebyshev root formula.

name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_mem_Icc

signature: NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient (L θ : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient
doc:
The Chernoff cgf coefficient `(e^{θL} - 1)/L`, equal to `θ` when `L = 0`. Tropp 2015, Lemma 5.4.1.
Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail (dimension : ℕ) (a L ε : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail
doc:
The matrix Chernoff lower tail `d · (e^{-ε}/(1-ε)^{1-ε})^{a/L}`, equal to `d` when `L = 0`. Tropp
2015, eq. (5.1.5). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail (dimension : ℕ) (a L ε : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail
doc:
The matrix Chernoff upper tail `d · (e^{ε}/(1+ε)^{1+ε})^{a/L}`, equal to `d` when `L = 0`. Tropp
2015, eq. (5.1.6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature:
NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
  (hMeas : Measurable X) (hHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X ω) ≤ L) (θ : ℝ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ ≤ NLAlib.matrixExp (NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient L θ • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ) ∧
    NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ) ≤ NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient L θ • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ
name: NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a random positive semidefinite `X` with `λmax X ≤ L`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ matrixExp (g(θ) •
𝔼 X)` and `matrixLog 𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ g(θ) • 𝔼 X`, where `g = chernoffCgfCoefficient L`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 5.4.1. Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

Stated for all real `θ`; `L = 0` is handled by the piecewise definition of
`chernoffCgfCoefficient`.

signature: NLAlib.cholesky {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.cholesky
doc:
**The Cholesky recursion** on the leading pivot: for `A = [[a, cᵀ], [c, C]]`,
`L = [[√a, 0], [c/√a, L']]` with `L' = cholesky (C − c cᵀ/a)` (`pivotSchur`; for a symmetric
`A` the first row and column agree). Total: a nonpositive pivot gives `√a = 0` and junk, never
an error. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 23.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.5 (outer-product form).
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (t : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace
doc:
Expected residual trace is the finite weighted sum over adaptive pivot histories.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, `u_t = E tr R_t`.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_antitone.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) : Antitone (NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A)
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_antitone
doc:
The expected trace is nonincreasing along the actual finite-history process.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, bounded finite moments and monotonicity.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_rank_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {t : ℕ} (ht : A.rank ≤ t) : NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t = 0
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc:
The expected trace is exactly zero after at most the input rank positive pivots.
Source: manuscript `sa:rp-rank` and `sa:rp-theorem`, zero-tail branch.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_spectralTraceTail_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (ht : NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r = 0) (hk : r ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k = 0
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_spectralTraceTail_eq_zero
doc:
A zero optimal trace tail yields exact RPCholesky expected trace after at most
the target rank pivots, including a rank-zero input. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hτ : 0 < NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) (hbudget : ↑r / ε + ↑r * Real.log (A.trace / (ε * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r)) ≤ ↑k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k ≤ (1 + ε) * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail
doc:
The actual RPCholesky expected trace reaches the precise relative-error target
under the manuscript's logarithmic pivot budget. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`;
CETW (2025). This is the positive-tail real-matrix branch, with all positive tolerances.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hτ : 0 < NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r) {ε h : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) (hh : 0 < h)
  (hbudget :
    ↑r * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r / (ε * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r + h) +
        ↑r * Real.log (A.trace / (ε * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r + h)) ≤
      ↑k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k ≤ (1 + ε) * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r + h
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail_add
doc:
An additive tolerance has its own scale-correct pivot budget, distinct from the
relative optimal tail parameter. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`, additive corollary.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_of_relativeSpectralTraceTail.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hτ : 0 < NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r)
  {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hbudget : ↑r / ε + ↑r * Real.log (1 / (ε * NLAlib.relativeSpectralTraceTail A ⋯ r)) ≤ ↑k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k ≤ (1 + ε) * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_of_relativeSpectralTraceTail
doc:
The relative parameter is exactly `eta = tau_*/tr A`, with the source's budget
`r/epsilon + r log(1/(epsilon eta))`. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`; CETW (2025).
It is not interpreted as an additive error tolerance.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (t : ℕ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_nonneg
doc:
Every expected Cholesky residual trace is nonnegative.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, bounded finite moments.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (t : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A (t + 1) =
    ∑ h,
      NLAlib.choleskyHistoryWeight A t h *
        ((NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h).trace -
          (NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h * NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h).trace /
            (NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h).trace)
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_eq
doc:
The actual adaptive expected trace obeys the exact finite one-step averaging
formula before applying the scalar tail drift. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-recursion`.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_le_traceExcessDrift.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (t : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A (t + 1) ≤
    NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t -
      NLAlib.traceExcessDrift (NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r) (NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t) / ↑r
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_le_traceExcessDrift
doc:
The actual adaptive expected trace obeys the source's nonlinear relative-tail
recursion. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-recursion`; CETW (2025).
All matrix and probability inequalities are derived from the input PSD matrix.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :

The expected trace starts at the original input trace.

NLAlib.choleskyHistoryLaw.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] [MeasurableSpace n]

The measure of adaptive pivot histories, including absorbed zero residuals.

The probability mass function of the adaptive pivot history.
Source: CETW (2025), RPCholesky pivot rule.

name: NLAlib.choleskyHistoryWeight

The probability weight of a finite adaptive pivot history is the product of its
transition probabilities. Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, finite-history law.

NLAlib.choleskyHistoryWeight_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

Finite adaptive-history weights are nonnegative for positive semidefinite input.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, finite probability law.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyPivotProbability.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (R : Matrix n n 𝕜)
  (i : n) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivotProbability
doc:
The **RPCholesky pivot law** `Re rᵢᵢ / Re (tr R)`, uniform when `Re (tr R) = 0` (so it sums
to one for every `R`; for a PSD `R` the trace is real and vanishes only at `R = 0`).
CETW 2023, Alg. 1.

NLAlib.choleskyPivotProbability_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  {R : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hR : R.PosSemidef) (i : n) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.choleskyPivotProbability R i
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivotProbability_nonneg
doc: A PSD residual gives a nonnegative pivot law. CETW 2023, Alg. 1.

signature: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Equiv.Perm (Fin n) × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted
doc:
**Cholesky with diagonal pivoting** as a total recursion: swap the largest diagonal entry
to the front (`diagPivotSwap`), take one Cholesky step, recurse on the Schur complement and
permute the computed column by the later pivots. Returns the pivot order `σ` and `L`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 4.2.4 (outer-product form with symmetric pivoting); Higham 2002,
§10.3. For PSD `A` a zero pivot means the remaining matrix is zero, and the recursion then
produces zero columns (`x / 0 = 0`), so it never fails.
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_eq_zero_of_rank_le {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) (i j : Fin n)
  (hj : A.rank ≤ ↑j) : (NLAlib.choleskyPivoted A).2 i j = 0
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc:
**Pivoted Cholesky terminates at the rank**: all columns with index at least `rank A`
vanish for every positive semidefinite input.
Source: Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9; Higham 2002, §10.3; matrix toolkit rederivations, `lem:rankL`.
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_self_pos_iff_lt_rank {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef)
  (i : Fin n) : 0 < (NLAlib.choleskyPivoted A).2 i i ↔ ↑i < A.rank
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_self_pos_iff_lt_rank
doc:
**Pivoted Cholesky stops at the rank**: its diagonal is positive exactly in the first
`rank A` positions for every positive semidefinite input.
Source: Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9; Higham 2002, §10.3; matrix toolkit rederivations, `lem:prefix`.
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.choleskySucceeds_iff_forall_cholesky_apply_self_pos {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.CholeskySucceeds A ↔ ∀ (i : Fin n), 0 < NLAlib.cholesky A i i
name: NLAlib.choleskySucceeds_iff_forall_cholesky_apply_self_pos
doc:
The pivots are the squares of the diagonal: the recursion succeeds iff the diagonal of
`cholesky A` is positive.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskySucceeds_iff_posDef {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  NLAlib.CholeskySucceeds A ↔ A.PosDef
name: NLAlib.choleskySucceeds_iff_posDef
doc:
**Breakdown of the Cholesky recursion**: for symmetric `A`, the recursion succeeds iff `A`
is positive definite (Cholesky is the test for positive definiteness). Proof: induction on `n`
with `posDef_iff_pivotSchur`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 23.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.5;

doc:

modification interpretation requires a nonsingular original moment system and
nonvanishing original degree-`n` evaluation at `z`.

signature:
NLAlib.christoffelPolynomial_eq_C_mul_monicOrthogonalKernelPolynomial.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜]
  (L : Polynomial 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (n : ℕ) (hL : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, NLAlib.hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0) {z : 𝕜}

    Polynomial.C (NLAlib.orthogonalPolynomialNorm L n / Polynomial.eval z (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n)) *
      NLAlib.monicOrthogonalKernelPolynomial L (n + 1) z

doc:
The Christoffel quotient is the monic reproducing kernel scaled by

signature:

The actual rule integrates every polynomial through its degree cutoff exactly.

signature:
NLAlib.clenshawCurtisWeight_eq_cosine_sum {n j : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hj : j ≤ n) :

    NLAlib.lobattoEndpointWeight n j / ↑n *

formula for every actual Clenshaw–Curtis weight.
Source: finite DCT cardinal formula; focused rederivations `thm:lobatto`.

NLAlib.coefficientBlockKappa_eq_variance_of_commute.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype d]

Pairwise commuting Hermitian coefficients give exactly `kappa = sigma`.
Source: Bandeira et al. (2026), Proposition 1.3.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientBlockKappa_kronecker_one.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype ι]
  [Fintype d] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq d] [DecidableEq r] [Nonempty r] (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ)

  (NLAlib.coefficientBlockKappa fun i => Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) 1) =
    NLAlib.coefficientBlockKappa A
name: NLAlib.coefficientBlockKappa_kronecker_one
doc:
Tensoring the actual coefficients with any nonempty finite identity leaves
the source parameter unchanged. The proof preserves the largest eigenvalue,
rather than replacing it by the spectral norm of an indefinite block.
Source: Bandeira et al. (2026), §1.1, amplification invariance.
atlas: coefficient-block-partial-transpose (partial)

name: NLAlib.coefficientBlockKappa_le_sqrt_variance_covariance
doc:
The coefficient-block correction scale is bounded by the geometric mean
of the usual variance scale and the unnormalized entry-covariance scale.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientCovariance_gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3}

        NLAlib.coefficientCovariance fun ia =>
          Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A ia.1) (Matrix.single ia.2 ia.2 1)) +
      (1 - q) •

          Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A ik.1) (NLAlib.gueCoefficientMatrix ik.2)

diagonal tensor covariance and the actual GUE tensor covariance.

NLAlib.coefficientCrossingBlock_eq_covariance_compression.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3}

NLAlib.coefficientCrossingSum_eq_stack_compression.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3}

  Matrix d d ℂ
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance
doc: The usual matrix-series variance matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVarianceLift.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [DecidableEq ι] (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) :
  Matrix (ι × ι × d) (ι × d) ℂ
name: NLAlib.coefficientVarianceLift
doc: The variance lift applies every coefficient to every input block.

signature: NLAlib.coefficientVarianceSwap.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} : Equiv.Perm (ι × ι × d)
name: NLAlib.coefficientVarianceSwap
doc: Exchange the two coefficient labels and retain the vector coordinate.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVariance_diagonal_single.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] :
  (NLAlib.coefficientVariance fun a => Matrix.single a a 1) = 1
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance_diagonal_single
doc: The actual diagonal coordinate coefficient variance is the identity.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVariance_gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3}
  [Fintype ι] [Fintype n] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq d] (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 ≤ q)
  (hq1 : q ≤ 1) :
  NLAlib.coefficientVariance (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient A q) =
    Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (NLAlib.coefficientVariance A) 1
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance_gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient
doc:
The actual variance of the true finite-N interpolation is exactly the
original variance tensor the ensemble identity, throughout the closed unit
interval. No Hermitian or positive-dimension hypothesis is required.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVariance_gramCoefficientDilation.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype d]
  (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) :
  NLAlib.coefficientVariance (NLAlib.gramCoefficientDilation A) =
    Matrix.fromBlocks (∑ i, A i * (A i).conjTranspose) 0 0 (Matrix.fromBlocks (∑ i, (A i).conjTranspose * A i) 0 0 0)
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance_gramCoefficientDilation
doc:
Its literal variance consists of the two original row/column variance
blocks and one zero block.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVariance_gueCoefficientMatrix.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] :
  NLAlib.coefficientVariance NLAlib.gueCoefficientMatrix = 1
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance_gueCoefficientMatrix
doc:
The actual GUE coefficient variance is the identity, with the true
normalization of the native Gaussian ensemble.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVariance_kronecker.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} {n : Type u_4}
  [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype d] [Fintype n] (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (B : κ → Matrix n n ℂ) :
  (NLAlib.coefficientVariance fun ik => Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A ik.1) (B ik.2)) =
    Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (NLAlib.coefficientVariance A) (NLAlib.coefficientVariance B)
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance_kronecker
doc:
The variance of an actual product-indexed Kronecker coefficient family
is the Kronecker product of the two actual variance matrices.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVariance_realCoefficientDilation.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype ι] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (B : ι → Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.coefficientVariance (NLAlib.realCoefficientDilation B) =
    Matrix.fromBlocks ((∑ i, B i * (B i).conjTranspose).map Complex.ofReal) 0 0
      ((∑ i, (B i).conjTranspose * B i).map Complex.ofReal)
name: NLAlib.coefficientVariance_realCoefficientDilation
doc:
The actual variance of the dilated family is the block diagonal matrix of
the original row and column variances.

signature: NLAlib.coefficientVectorization.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) : Matrix (d × d) ι ℂ
name: NLAlib.coefficientVectorization
doc: Ordinary column labels for the vectorized coefficient entries.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVectorization_gram_gramCoefficientDilation.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d]
  (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) :
  (NLAlib.coefficientVectorization (NLAlib.gramCoefficientDilation A)).conjTranspose *
      NLAlib.coefficientVectorization (NLAlib.gramCoefficientDilation A) =
    (NLAlib.coefficientVectorization A).conjTranspose * NLAlib.coefficientVectorization A +
      ((NLAlib.coefficientVectorization A).conjTranspose * NLAlib.coefficientVectorization A).map star
name: NLAlib.coefficientVectorization_gram_gramCoefficientDilation
doc:
The true vectorized Gram is the original Gram plus its entrywise
conjugate. This retains the conjugation required for complex coefficients.

signature:
NLAlib.coefficientVectorization_gram_realCoefficientDilation.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2}
  {n : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
  (B : ι → Matrix m n ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.coefficientVectorization (NLAlib.realCoefficientDilation B)).conjTranspose *
      NLAlib.coefficientVectorization (NLAlib.realCoefficientDilation B) =
    2 • (NLAlib.coefficientEntryRows B * (NLAlib.coefficientEntryRows B).conjTranspose).map Complex.ofReal
name: NLAlib.coefficientVectorization_gram_realCoefficientDilation
doc:
The Gram matrix of the vectorized dilations is twice the original real
coefficient-row Gram matrix after scalar extension. The real hypothesis is
essential: complex dilation is only real-linear.

name: NLAlib.col_mem_krylovSpace_of_hessenberg_intertwines
doc:
An unreduced Hessenberg intertwining forces column `j` into the first
`j+1` Krylov space. This is the converse direction to Arnoldi's Hessenberg
relation and uses only nonzero subdiagonal entries.

signature:
NLAlib.col_mem_span_gramSchmidtCol.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) (j : Fin n) :
  A.col j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A '' Set.Iic j)
name: NLAlib.col_mem_span_gramSchmidtCol
doc: `a_j ∈ span(q_0, …, q_j)` (every `A`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (7.2).

name: NLAlib.col_mul_eq_mulVec_col
doc:
Column `j` of a product is the matrix applied to column `j`: `(M N) e_j = M (N e_j)`.
Stated over any non-unital non-associative semiring (covers `ℝ` and `ℂ`). Helper for
`block-krylov-subspace` and `arnoldi-relation`.

signature:
NLAlib.col_mul_mem_span_image_Iic.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} {Q : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ} {T : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  (hT : T.IsUpperTriangular) (j : Fin n) : (Q * T).col j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Q.col '' Set.Iic j)
name: NLAlib.col_mul_mem_span_image_Iic
doc:
If `T` is upper triangular, column `j` of `Q T` lies in the span of the first `j + 1` columns
of `Q`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2 (column flags under triangular maps).

signature: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) : Matrix (Fin p.natDegree) (Fin p.natDegree) ℝ
name: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix
doc:
The colleague matrix is the evaluation-recurrence transpose of multiplication
by `X` modulo `p`, in the first-kind Chebyshev basis. Source: Trefethen, ATAP,
Theorem 18.1. A nonzero constant polynomial has the empty colleague matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_apply (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (j k : Fin p.natDegree) :
  NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp j k =
    ((NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis p hp).repr (AdjoinRoot.root p * (NLAlib.chebyshevQuotientBasis p hp) j)) k
name: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_apply
doc:
Entries of the evaluation-recurrence colleague matrix are Chebyshev coordinates
of multiplication by the residue of `X`. Source: ATAP Theorem 18.1.

signature:
NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_degree_one (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (a : ℕ → ℝ)
  (ha : p = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (p.natDegree + 1), a j • Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑j) (han : a p.natDegree ≠ 0)
  (hn : p.natDegree = 1) (j k : Fin p.natDegree) : NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp j k = -a 0 / a 1
name: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_degree_one
doc:
For a degree-one polynomial `a₀+a₁X`, the colleague matrix is the single entry
`−a₀/a₁`. Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 18.1. This degree-one branch is distinct
from the half-scaled last-row recurrence, which requires degree at least two.
atlas: colleague-matrix

signature:
NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_interior_row (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (j k : Fin p.natDegree) (hj0 : 0 < ↑j)
  (hjn : ↑j + 1 < p.natDegree) :
  NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp j k = 1 / 2 * ((if ↑j - 1 = ↑k then 1 else 0) + if ↑j + 1 = ↑k then 1 else 0)
name: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_interior_row
doc:
Every interior colleague row has one-half in its two neighboring columns.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP (18.1), from the first-kind Chebyshev recurrence.

signature:
NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_last_row (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (a : ℕ → ℝ)
  (ha : p = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (p.natDegree + 1), a j • Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑j) (han : a p.natDegree ≠ 0)
  (hn : 2 ≤ p.natDegree) (k : Fin p.natDegree) :
  NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp ⟨p.natDegree - 1, ⋯⟩ k =
    (if p.natDegree - 2 = ↑k then 1 / 2 else 0) - a ↑k / (2 * a p.natDegree)
name: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_last_row
doc:
In degree at least two, the last colleague row is the half-scaled penultimate
basis coordinate minus `a_k/(2a_n)`. Source: Trefethen, ATAP (18.1).
atlas: colleague-matrix (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_zero_row (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (hn : 2 ≤ p.natDegree) (k : Fin p.natDegree) :
  NLAlib.colleagueMatrix p hp ⟨0, ⋯⟩ k = if ↑k = 1 then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.colleagueMatrix_zero_row
doc:
In degrees at least two, the first colleague row has its single entry `1`
in column one. Source: ATAP (18.1); the special first-kind Chebyshev recurrence.

signature:
NLAlib.coloredMatrixChaos.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {τ : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {m : Type u_3} {n : Type u_4} [Fintype τ]

signature:
NLAlib.columnRowProbabilities.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {t : Type u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_4}

The normalized column/row weights as nonnegative real probabilities.
The accompanying sum-to-one theorem applies when the total weight is positive.

signature:
NLAlib.columnRowSample.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {t : Type u_3} (A : Matrix m n ℂ)

One inverse-probability rescaled column/row product.
Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm`. Zero probability uses totalized inverse.

signature:
NLAlib.columnRowWeight.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {t : Type u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_4} [Fintype m]

doc:
The product of a column's Euclidean norm and its corresponding row norm,
which specifies the variance-minimizing finite sampling law.
Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm-theorem`.

name: NLAlib.columnRowWeight_nonneg
doc:
Column/row weights are nonnegative.
Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm-theorem`.

signature:
NLAlib.columnRowWeight_sq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {t : Type u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_4} [Fintype m]

The square of a column/row weight is the outer product's squared Frobenius
norm. Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm-variance`.

NLAlib.columnSpace.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

NLAlib.columnSpace_eq_span_columns.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

NLAlib.columnSpace_mul_eq_of_right_inverse.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]

Actual complex column spaces decrease under right multiplication.

name: NLAlib.columnSpace_orthonormalBasisMatrixOfEuclideanSubspace
doc: The Hilbert-subspace basis matrix spans precisely the input subspace.

signature:
NLAlib.commute_blockDiagonal'_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ι → Type u_2}
  [(i : ι) → Fintype (m i)] [(i : ι) → DecidableEq (m i)] {K : Type u_4} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
  (A : (i : ι) → Matrix (m i) (m i) K) (hdisj : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (spectrum K (A i)) (spectrum K (A j)))
  (X : Matrix ((i : ι) × m i) ((i : ι) × m i) K) :
  Commute (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A) X ↔ ∃ Y, X = Matrix.blockDiagonal' Y ∧ ∀ (i : ι), Commute (A i) (Y i)
name: NLAlib.commute_blockDiagonal'_iff
doc:
The commutant of a block diagonal matrix with pairwise disjoint block
spectra consists exactly of block diagonal matrices whose diagonal blocks
commute with the corresponding primary blocks. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Corollary 2.4.4.2; the diagonal commutation conditions are essential.
atlas: sylvester-equation (partial)

name: NLAlib.commute_cyclicShift_iff_exists_circulant
doc:
A matrix commutes with the cyclic shift exactly when it is a circulant.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.7.
atlas: structured-matrices-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.commute_nonsing_inv_mul_mul_iff.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]

doc:
Simultaneous nonsingular conjugation preserves commutation.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §1.3; matrix similarity algebra.

signature:
NLAlib.commute_of_posSemidef_add_eq_diagonal_projection.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
Two PSD summands of a diagonal orthogonal projection commute.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.6; helper for singular simultaneous congruence.

name: NLAlib.commute_of_posSemidef_add_eq_diagonal_projection_ofReal
doc: PSD summands of a real diagonal projection commute, over either field.

Simultaneously diagonalized matrices commute. Source: Horn–Johnson
(2013), Theorem 1.3.12; repeated diagonal values require no exception.

NLAlib.commute_orthogonal_compressions_of_invariant.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]

Compressing two commuting operators onto the orthogonal complement
of a common invariant subspace preserves their commutation. Quotient-space
identity; helper for `simultaneous-diagonalization`.

NLAlib.commute_signNewtonIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A S : Matrix n n ℂ} (h : Commute S A)

signature:
NLAlib.commute_similarity_blockDiagonal'_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {m : ι → Type u_2} [(i : ι) → Fintype (m i)] [(i : ι) → DecidableEq (m i)] {K : Type u_3} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
  (A : (i : ι) → Matrix (m i) (m i) K) (hdisj : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (spectrum K (A i)) (spectrum K (A j)))
  (S X : Matrix ((i : ι) × m i) ((i : ι) × m i) K) (hS : IsUnit S) :

A conjugated block diagonal matrix with pairwise disjoint block spectra

name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = projResidual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.
Conclusion: `eq:completion`,
`E‖A − Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA‖_F² = (1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (helper; uses `sketched-regression`, `orthonormal-completion`).
atlas: gn-expected-error

    U.toBlocks₁₂.rank = U.toBlocks₂₁.rank ∧
      U.toBlocks₂₂.rank = U.toBlocks₁₁.rank + Fintype.card q - Fintype.card p ∧
        (∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
            ∃ t,

                Antitone t ∧

                    ∃ H,

                        H * H.conjTranspose = 1 ∧

                                ∀ i < g, t i = √(NLAlib.singularValues P i ^ 2 - 1)) ∧

                    (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Q).range = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin P).range ∧
                      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin W).range = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin P).kerᗮ ∧
                        have θ := NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype W Q ⟨P.rank - 1, ⋯⟩;
                        (∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin P.rank))), NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype W Q i ≤ θ) ∧

            (0 < P.rank → P.rank < Fintype.card n → ‖1 - P‖ = ‖P‖) ∧

name: NLAlib.complex_cs_decomposition_properties
doc:
The complete complex unitary CS and complex oblique-projection
theorem. Four unitary factors have block sizes `p,p,q,q`; their cosines
are actual singular values. Every complex idempotent has its actual canonical
singular coefficients, range/kernel principal-angle secant at positive rank,
equal complementary norms at proper positive rank, and exact norm endpoints.
Together with `cs_decomposition_properties`, this supplies both the real
orthogonal and advertised complex unitary contracts without narrowing either.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Lemma 2.1.10, Theorem 2.7.1 and Corollary 3.4.3.3;
derivations Section alg:cs. Empty spaces and zero/pi/2 CS angles are included.
