  [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] (A : Matrix m n R) : Matrix (NLAlib.SizedSubset m r) (NLAlib.SizedSubset n r) R
name: NLAlib.compoundMatrix
doc:
A compound matrix consists of all minors of a fixed size. Each finite
subset receives a fixed coordinate order; every product uses that same order
on its shared middle subsets. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.7.
atlas: cauchy-binet

name: NLAlib.compoundMatrix_conjTranspose
doc:
Compounds commute with conjugate transpose over every commutative star
ring, using exactly the same fixed row and column enumerations.
Source: Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 0.8.7.
atlas: cauchy-binet (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.compoundMatrix_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {r : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [Fintype r] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq r] [DecidableEq k] [CommRing R] {m : Type u_4} {n : Type u_5} (A : Matrix m k R) (B : Matrix k n R) :
  NLAlib.compoundMatrix r (A * B) = NLAlib.compoundMatrix r A * NLAlib.compoundMatrix r B
name: NLAlib.compoundMatrix_mul
doc:
Compounds are multiplicative in every size, with the shared subset
orientation occurring twice and hence cancelling. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.7.
atlas: cauchy-binet (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.compoundMatrix_one.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {r : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype r]
  [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq r] [CommRing R] : NLAlib.compoundMatrix r 1 = 1
name: NLAlib.compoundMatrix_one
doc:
The compound of the identity is the identity at every minor size,
including the unique empty minor and impossible-size empty compounds.
Source: Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 0.8.7.
atlas: cauchy-binet (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.compressionQuadratureEstimate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype κ]
  {r : Type u_3} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (G : Matrix n κ ℝ) (Q : κ → Matrix n r ℝ) :
  ℝ
name: NLAlib.compressionQuadratureEstimate
doc:
The stochastic Lanczos quadrature estimate
`(1/m) ∑ₖ (Q_kᵀ g_k)ᵀ f(Q_kᵀ A Q_k) (Q_kᵀ g_k)` with test vectors `g_k` the columns of `G` and
bases `Q_k`. With the Lanczos basis, `Q_kᵀ g_k = ‖g_k‖ e₁` and the summand is `‖g_k‖² f(T_k)₁₁`.
Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], eq. (5).
This is the supplied-frame compression kernel; error theorems require orthonormality and
`K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`. Their `q` controls exactness order; it does not constrain
`card r` or the cost of constructing `Q`. The average is zero for an empty probe family.
atlas: trace-estimators-def

signature:
NLAlib.compression_complementaryEigenframe_eq_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card n) :
  (NLAlib.complementaryEigenframe hA hk).transpose * A * NLAlib.complementaryEigenframe hA hk =
    Matrix.diagonal fun i => hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨↑i + k, ⋯⟩
name: NLAlib.compression_complementaryEigenframe_eq_diagonal
doc:
The complementary compression is diagonal with exactly the eigenvalues
following the top `k`; no zero or simple-spectrum assumption is imposed.

name: NLAlib.compression_sortedEigenframe_eq_diagonal
doc: The sorted spectral frame diagonalizes the matrix with decreasing eigenvalues.

signature:
NLAlib.compression_submatrix_cols_eq_diagonal.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {r : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype r]
  [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq r] {A P : Matrix n n ℝ} (hP : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P) (d : n → ℝ)
  (hA : A = P * Matrix.diagonal d * P.transpose) (e : r ↪ n) :
  (P.submatrix id ⇑e).transpose * A * P.submatrix id ⇑e = Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ ⇑e)
name: NLAlib.compression_submatrix_cols_eq_diagonal
doc:
In spectral coordinates, selecting orthogonal columns of a diagonalizing
matrix compresses a matrix to the selected diagonal entries. Ky Fan helper.

signature:
NLAlib.compression_topEigenframe_eq_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card n) :
  (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA hk).transpose * A * NLAlib.topEigenframe hA hk =
    Matrix.diagonal fun i => hA.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.castLE hk i)
name: NLAlib.compression_topEigenframe_eq_diagonal
doc: The top-frame compression is diagonal with exactly the first `k` eigenvalues.

NLAlib.concaveOn_cfc_rpow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r : ℝ} (hr : r ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) :

Operator concavity of every real power between zero and one on the real
positive-semidefinite cone. Bhatia, Theorem V.1.9.

Cotangent minus the reciprocal is concave, including its removable value zero.

signature:
NLAlib.concaveOn_det_rpow_inv_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (hN : 0 < Fintype.card n) :

doc:
The positive determinant root is concave on the positive definite cone
in every positive dimension. Both endpoint weights are included.

signature:
NLAlib.condExp_independentResampling_originals.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  [Nonempty ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E] (ν : ι → MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  [∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (ν i)] (hν : ∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.Integrable id (ν i)) :
  (NLAlib.independentResamplingMeasure ν)[NLAlib.independentResamplingOriginal - NLAlib.independentResamplingPartner |
      MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.fst inferInstance] =ᵐ[NLAlib.independentResamplingMeasure ν]
    fun p => (↑(Fintype.card ι))⁻¹ • (NLAlib.independentResamplingOriginal p - ∑ j, ∫ (t : E), t ∂ν j)
name: NLAlib.condExp_independentResampling_originals
doc:
Conditioning on all original summands gives the exact uniform resampling
regression. This is a genuine conditional expectation, with no assumption that
the summands have equal laws. Source: Tropp (2026), §6.3; atlas
`exchangeable-matrix-covariance`.
atlas: exchangeable-matrix-covariance (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.condExp_independentResampling_sum.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  [Nonempty ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E] (ν : ι → MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  [∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (ν i)] (hν : ∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.Integrable id (ν i)) :
  (NLAlib.independentResamplingMeasure ν)[NLAlib.independentResamplingOriginal - NLAlib.independentResamplingPartner |
      MeasurableSpace.comap NLAlib.independentResamplingOriginal
        inferInstance] =ᵐ[NLAlib.independentResamplingMeasure ν]
    fun p =>
    (↑(Fintype.card ι))⁻¹ •
      (NLAlib.independentResamplingOriginal p -
        ∫ (t : (ι → E) × ι × (ι → E)), NLAlib.independentResamplingOriginal t ∂NLAlib.independentResamplingMeasure ν)
name: NLAlib.condExp_independentResampling_sum
doc:
Conditioning only on the original sum gives the Stein regression with
`α = 1 / card ι`. Combined with the proved exchangeability and second moments,
this verifies every hypothesis of the covariance identities for independent
nonidentical summands. Source: Tropp (2026), §6.3; atlas
`exchangeable-matrix-covariance`.
atlas: exchangeable-matrix-covariance (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.condExp_traceExp_add_le_traceExp_add_matrixLog_of_ae_posDef_condExp.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2}
  {m mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} (hm : m ≤ mΩ)
  [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (H : Matrix n n ℂ) (hH : H.IsHermitian) (X : Ω → Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian) (hExp : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => NLAlib.matrixExp (X ω)) μ)
  (hTrace : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => NLAlib.traceExp (H + X ω)) μ)
  (hmean : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (μ[fun ω => NLAlib.matrixExp (X ω) | m] ω).PosDef) :
  μ[fun ω => NLAlib.traceExp (H + X ω) | m] ≤ᵐ[μ] fun ω =>
    NLAlib.traceExp (H + NLAlib.matrixLog (μ[fun ω => NLAlib.matrixExp (X ω) | m] ω))
name: NLAlib.condExp_traceExp_add_le_traceExp_add_matrixLog_of_ae_posDef_condExp
doc:
Conditional Lieb for a fixed Hermitian offset, using the actual conditional mean of
the matrix exponential. This is a genuine conditional Jensen theorem, not the existing
unconditional inequality or an assumed conditional-mgf certificate. Its conditional-mean
positivity and trace integrability premises are supplied by the subsequent martingale bounds.
Source: Tropp 2011, Freedman's inequality; operator rederivations `eq:condlieb`.
atlas: matrix-freedman (partial)

name: NLAlib.condExp_traceExp_add_le_traceExp_add_matrixLog_of_predictable
doc:
Conditional Lieb with an actual conditioning-measurable Hermitian random offset.
The underlying probability space is arbitrary. Upper-only spectral bounds derive every
integrability premise; positivity of the actual conditional exponential mean is the
explicit remaining prerequisite, supplied by conditional centering in the martingale use.
Source: Tropp 2011, Freedman's inequality; operator rederivations `eq:condlieb`.
atlas: matrix-freedman (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.condExp_traceExp_variance_update_le.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {m mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hm : m ≤ mΩ) {X Y W : Ω → Matrix n n ℂ} (hXMeas : Measurable X) (hYMeas : Measurable Y) (hWMeas : Measurable W)
  (hX : MeasureTheory.Integrable X μ) (hX2 : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => X ω ^ 2) μ)
  (hXHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian) (hYHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (Y ω).IsHermitian)
  (hW : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (W ω).PosSemidef) (hMean : μ[X | m] =ᵐ[μ] 0) {L θ b : ℝ} (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθL : θ * L < 3)
  (hXBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, X ω ≤ (algebraMap ℝ (Matrix n n ℂ)) L)
  (hYBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, Y ω ≤ (algebraMap ℝ (Matrix n n ℂ)) b) :
  μ[fun ω => NLAlib.traceExp (θ • (Y ω + X ω) - (θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • (W ω + μ[fun ω => X ω ^ 2 | m] ω)) |
      m] ≤ᵐ[μ]
    fun ω => NLAlib.traceExp (θ • Y ω - (θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • W ω)
name: NLAlib.condExp_traceExp_variance_update_le
doc:
The actual trace-exponential potential decreases conditionally after one centered
Hermitian increment. Its variance update is the actual conditional second moment.
The predictable previous sum has only an upper spectral bound and the previous variance
is PSD; no conditional-mgf or supermartingale conclusion is assumed.
Source: Tropp 2011, Freedman's inequality; operator rederivations Section 3.3.
atlas: matrix-freedman (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) : ENNReal
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber
doc:
The spectral condition number `κ₂(A) = ‖A‖₂ ‖A⁻¹‖₂` of a square matrix, `⊤` when `A` is
singular. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2; Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.13).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_circulant_of_dft_ne_zero {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (c : ZMod n → ℂ)
  (hc : ∀ (i : ZMod n), ZMod.dft c i ≠ 0) :
  NLAlib.conditionNumber (Matrix.circulant c) = ENNReal.ofReal (‖ZMod.dft c‖ * ‖fun i => (ZMod.dft c i)⁻¹‖)
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_circulant_of_dft_ne_zero
doc:
The finite spectral condition number is the largest Fourier modulus times
the largest reciprocal modulus; equivalently, the maximum-to-minimum ratio.
Source: Meyer §5.5.
atlas: circulant-fourier-diagonalization (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) : NLAlib.conditionNumber A.conjTranspose = NLAlib.conditionNumber A
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_conjTranspose
doc:
Conjugate transposition preserves the condition number. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio.{u_3} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio
doc:
For a positive-definite `A` on a nonempty index type, `κ₂(A) = λ_max/λ_min`, the ratio of the
first and last sorted eigenvalues. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_ofReal_moorePenroseConditionNumber
doc:
The condition number of an invertible matrix is the pseudoinverse quantity
`moorePenroseConditionNumber A` (cast to `ℝ≥0∞`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

doc:
`κ₂(A) = σ₁/σ_n` for an invertible `A` (zero-indexed: `σ 0 / σ (card n - 1)`).
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and §5.5.2; Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.14).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_top_iff.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_top_iff
doc:
The condition number is `⊤` exactly on singular matrices. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_inv.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

Inversion preserves the condition number: `κ₂(A⁻¹) = κ₂(A)` (both `⊤` when `A` is singular,

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_ne_top_iff
doc: The condition number is finite exactly on invertible matrices.

rank-one samples. Source: operator re-derivation `sa:leverage`.

`generalized-schur-complement-psd`.

including scalar matrices and degenerate ellipses. The Bloch sphere is an

doc:
The core noise `E_core = (ΨᵀQ)† Ψᵀ A⊥` with `A⊥ = (I - QQᵀ)A` (Chen–Persson,

signature:
NLAlib.coreNoise_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} {r : Type u_4} {s : Type u_5}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [Fintype r] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq q] [DecidableEq m] (Q : Matrix m q ℝ) (Qp : Matrix m r ℝ)

  NLAlib.coreNoise Q Ψ A =
    NLAlib.pinvL (Ψ.transpose * Q) * (Ψ.transpose * Qp) * (Qp.transpose * NLAlib.projResidual Q A)
name: NLAlib.coreNoise_eq
doc:
Deterministic core of `lem:tGN-core` and `eq:tGN-fitted-core` (Chen–Persson): the noise
term `E_core = (ΨᵀQ)† Ψᵀ A⊥` equals `G₁† G₂ B` with `G₁ = ΨᵀQ`, `G₂ = ΨᵀQ⊥`, `B = Q⊥ᵀ A⊥`, where

Atlas `sketched-regression`.

signature:
NLAlib.cs_decomposition_properties.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {p : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype p] [Fintype q]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq p] [DecidableEq q] [DecidableEq n] (U : Matrix (p ⊕ q) (p ⊕ q) ℝ)
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (hCard : Fintype.card p ≤ Fintype.card q) (P : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  (∃ e,
      have c := fun i => NLAlib.singularValues U.toBlocks₁₁ ↑((Fintype.equivFin p) i);
      (∀ (i : p), c i ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
        ∃ V₁ W₁ V₂ W₂,
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
            NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W₁ ∧
              NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧
                NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W₂ ∧
                  (Matrix.fromBlocks V₁ 0 0 V₂).transpose * U * Matrix.fromBlocks W₁ 0 0 W₂ =
                    NLAlib.csCanonicalMatrix c (Matrix.submatrix 1 id ⇑e)) ∧
    U.toBlocks₁₂.rank = U.toBlocks₂₁.rank ∧
      U.toBlocks₂₂.rank = U.toBlocks₁₁.rank + Fintype.card q - Fintype.card p ∧
        (∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
            ∃ t,
              (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
                Antitone t ∧
                  (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
                    ∃ H,
                      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols H ∧
                        H * H.transpose = 1 ∧
                          H.transpose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (NLAlib.rectDiag t) 0 0 ∧
                            (∀ (i : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues P i = if i < P.rank then √(1 + t i ^ 2) else 0) ∧
                              (∀ (i : ℕ), 1 < NLAlib.singularValues P i ↔ i < g) ∧
                                ∀ i < g, t i = √(NLAlib.singularValues P i ^ 2 - 1)) ∧
          (∀ (hr : 0 < P.rank),
              ∃ Q W,
                NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧
                  NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W ∧
                    (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Q).range = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin P).range ∧
                      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin W).range = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin P).kerᗮ ∧
                        have θ := NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype W Q ⟨P.rank - 1, ⋯⟩;
                        (∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin P.rank))), NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype W Q i ≤ θ) ∧
                          θ < Real.pi / 2 ∧ NLAlib.specNorm P = 1 / Real.cos θ) ∧
            (0 < P.rank → P.rank < Fintype.card n → NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = NLAlib.specNorm P) ∧
              (P.rank = 0 → NLAlib.specNorm P = 0 ∧ NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = if Fintype.card n = 0 then 0 else 1) ∧
                (P.rank = Fintype.card n →
                  (NLAlib.specNorm P = if Fintype.card n = 0 then 0 else 1) ∧ NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = 0)
name: NLAlib.cs_decomposition_properties
doc:
The complete real CS and oblique-projection theorem. The CS factors have
one `p` and one `q` block on each side, with actual singular-value cosines and
literal coordinate inclusion. The oblique canonical coefficients have their
full actual singular-spectrum identities. The secant is asserted at positive
rank for the actual range and kernel-complement subspaces; complementary norm
equality requires proper positive rank and both rank endpoints are explicit.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Lemma 2.1.10, Theorem 2.7.1 and Corollary 3.4.3.3;
derivations §alg:cs. Empty spaces and zero/pi/2 CS angles are included.

NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix_mul_diagonal_mul_transpose_apply.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [CommRing 𝕜] {n : ℕ} (d e : ℕ → 𝕜)

  ((NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix n e * Matrix.diagonal fun k => d ↑k) * (NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix n e).transpose) i j =
    if ↑i = ↑j then d ↑i + if ↑i = 0 then 0 else e (↑i - 1) ^ 2 * d (↑i - 1)
    else if ↑i + 1 = ↑j then e ↑i * d ↑i else if ↑j + 1 = ↑i then e ↑j * d ↑j else 0
name: NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix_mul_diagonal_mul_transpose_apply
doc: The entry formula for a unit lower bidiagonal LDL transpose product.

signature: NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [CommRing 𝕜] (n : ℕ) (q : ℕ → 𝕜) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) 𝕜
name: NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix
doc:
The upper bidiagonal factor with diagonal `q_j` and unit superdiagonal.
Source: finite monic Darboux factorization, OP24.

signature:
NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix_mul_darbouxLowerMatrix.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [CommRing 𝕜] (n : ℕ) (q e : ℕ → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix n q * NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix n e =

name: NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix_mul_darbouxLowerMatrix
doc:

signature:
NLAlib.davis_kahan_bounds.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype k]
  [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (hE : E.IsHermitian) {Q Qhat : Matrix n k ℝ} {R : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQhat : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qhat) (hR : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols R)
  (hcomp : Qhat * Qhat.transpose + R * R.transpose = 1) {L : Matrix k k ℝ} {M : Matrix r r ℝ} (hAQ : A * Q = Q * L)
  (hAR : (A + E) * R = R * M) :
  (∀ (a b δ : ℝ),
      0 < δ →
        (∀ (j : k), a ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues j ∧ ⋯.eigenvalues j ≤ b) →
          (∀ (i : r), ⋯.eigenvalues i ≤ a - δ ∨ b + δ ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues i) →
            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles Q Qhat) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
                NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
                  NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles Q Qhat) ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
                    NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
                      NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm E / δ ∧
                        NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ √↑(Fintype.card k) * NLAlib.specNorm E / δ) ∧
    (∀ (j : ℕ) (hj0 : 0 < j) (hjN : j < Fintype.card n),
        0 < hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩ →
          have S := NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA ⋯) (NLAlib.topEigenframe ⋯ ⋯);
          have δ := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
          NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
            NLAlib.frobNorm S ≤ min (√↑j * NLAlib.specNorm E) (NLAlib.frobNorm E) / δ) ∧
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (hj0 : 0 < j) (hjN : j < Fintype.card n),
          0 < hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩ →
            have S := NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA ⋯) (NLAlib.topEigenframe ⋯ ⋯);
            have g := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
            NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / g ∧
              NLAlib.frobNorm S ≤ 2 * min (√↑j * NLAlib.specNorm E) (NLAlib.frobNorm E) / g) ∧
        ∀ (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ Fintype.card n),
          j = 0 ∨ j = Fintype.card n →
            NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA hj) (NLAlib.topEigenframe ⋯ hj) = 0
name: NLAlib.davis_kahan_bounds
doc:
All requested Davis–Kahan bounds for invariant frames and sorted spectral subspaces. Davis–Kahan §6 and Yu–Wang–Samworth (2015),
Theorems 1–2. The generic interval theorem includes empty selected or
complementary frames and needs no endpoint-order assumption. The population
Frobenius minimum is unconditional and is proved by the finite trace deficit;
zero and full top-frame widths have zero sine matrices.
atlas: davis-kahan-sin-theta

signature:
NLAlib.davis_kahan_top_frame_bounds.{u_1, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n]
  [DecidableEq r] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hE : E.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ} (hj0 : 0 < j)
  (hjN : j < Fintype.card n) {Q Qhat : Matrix n (Fin j) ℝ} {R : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQhat : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qhat) (hR : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols R)
  (hcomp : Qhat * Qhat.transpose + R * R.transpose = 1) {L : Matrix (Fin j) (Fin j) ℝ} {M : Matrix r r ℝ}
  (hAQ : A * Q = Q * L) (hAR : (A + E) * R = R * M) (hmin : ∀ (t : Fin j), hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues t)
  (hmax : ∀ (t : r), ⋯.eigenvalues t ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩) :
  have S := NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles Q Qhat;
  have δ := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
  have g := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
  (0 < δ →
      NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
          NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
            NLAlib.frobNorm S ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
              NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
                NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ min (√↑j * NLAlib.specNorm E) (NLAlib.frobNorm E) / δ) ∧
    (0 < g → NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / g) ∧ (E = 0 → 0 < g → S = 0)
name: NLAlib.davis_kahan_top_frame_bounds
doc:
Supplied top invariant frames satisfy the exact mixed-gap residual
bounds and unconditional population spectral bound, including tied perturbed
choices and zero perturbations; Davis--Kahan, Section 6, and Yu--Wang--Samworth,
Theorem 2. The spectral hypotheses describe the selected/complementary cluster
and contain no angle or desired norm inequality.

signature:
NLAlib.decoupledMatrixChaos_reindexModes.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3}

Relabeling coefficient modes and coordinate groups together leaves the

signature:
NLAlib.decoupledMatrixChaos_sum_recursion.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {τ : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {m : Type u_3}
  {n : Type u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_5} [Fintype τ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq τ] [DecidableEq ι] [RCLike 𝕜]

The actual decoupled polynomial is a linear series in its final coordinate

signature:
NLAlib.definite_pair_congruence_characterizations.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
  (∃ S d,
      IsUnit S ∧
        A = S * S.transpose ∧
          B = S * Matrix.diagonal d * S.transpose ∧
            (A⁻¹ * B).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i)) ∧
              spectrum ℝ (A⁻¹ * B) = Set.range d ∧
                NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable (A⁻¹ * B) ∧
                  NLAlib.inertiaPos (Matrix.diagonal d) = NLAlib.inertiaPos B ∧
                    NLAlib.inertiaNeg (Matrix.diagonal d) = NLAlib.inertiaNeg B ∧ (B.PosSemidef → ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ d i)) ∧
    NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable (A * B) ∧ (B.PosSemidef → spectrum ℝ (A * B) ⊆ Set.Ici 0)
name: NLAlib.definite_pair_congruence_characterizations
doc:
The full definite-pair congruence clause gives the exact relative
eigenvalue list, its inertia and PSD signs, and real diagonalizability of
both relative and ordinary products. The general indefinite and PSD-pair
variants are separate parts of the atlas bundle.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.6.1 and Corollary 7.6.2.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence

signature:
NLAlib.deflatedTraceEstimate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r]
  {κ : Type u_3} [Fintype κ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (Q : Matrix n r ℝ) (Z : Matrix n κ ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.deflatedTraceEstimate
doc:
The deflated trace kernel with a supplied basis `Q` and Hutchinson test matrix `Z`:
`tr(QᵀAQ) + tr_m((I − QQᵀ)A(I − QQᵀ))`. Source: Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021) [`mmmw21`],
Alg. 1. Atlas: `hutchpp`, `hutchpp-unbiased`. `Q` is arbitrary here; unbiasedness requires orthonormality. The sketch-based
`hutchPlusPlusEstimate` below constructs its basis from `range (A S)`. An empty test family
has a zero residual average, leaving the compressed trace.
atlas: trace-estimators-def

signature:
NLAlib.deflated_spectralRadius_lt_one_of_simple_unique_peripheral.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  [Nonempty ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) {p q : ι → ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hp : p ≠ 0) (hpair : q ⬝ᵥ p ≠ 0)

  (hperipheral : ∀ μ ∈ spectrum ℂ A, ‖μ‖ = r → μ = ↑r) :

signature:
NLAlib.degree_fixed_denominator_partial_fractions_lt_iff.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [Fintype ι]

signature:
NLAlib.degree_le_and_abs_sub_chebyshev_approximations_le_of_open_ellipse {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (hmatch : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (N : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc F N).degree ≤ ↑N ∧
    (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N).degree ≤ ↑N ∧
      ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1,
        |f x - Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc F N)| ≤ 2 * M / ρ ^ N / (ρ - 1) ∧
          |f x - Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N)| ≤ 4 * M / ρ ^ N / (ρ - 1)

Both canonical analytic Chebyshev approximations satisfy their exact source constants:
the coefficient truncation has error `2Mρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)`, and the `(N+1)`-point grid
interpolant has error `4Mρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)`. Both polynomials have degree at most `N`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 8.2; original open-ellipse assumptions, with the `N=0`
grid convention inherited explicitly from Mathlib's `node`.

  (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix x y).det = (Matrix.vandermonde x).det * (Matrix.vandermonde y).det / ∏ i, ∏ j, (x i + y j)
name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_eq_vandermonde
doc:
Cauchy's determinant is the product of the two Vandermonde determinants
divided by all denominators. Repeated parameters and the empty determinant
are included. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.
atlas: structured-matrices-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_eq_vandermonde_fintype.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (x y : n → ℝ)
  (hDen : ∀ (i j : n), x i + y j ≠ 0) :
  (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix x y).det =
    (Matrix.vandermonde (x ∘ ⇑(Fintype.equivFin n).symm)).det *
        (Matrix.vandermonde (y ∘ ⇑(Fintype.equivFin n).symm)).det /
      ∏ i, ∏ j, (x i + y j)
name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_eq_vandermonde_fintype
doc:
Cauchy's determinant formula on arbitrary finite labels, with the two
Vandermonde factors in the same finite coordinate ordering. The denominator
product is intrinsic. Empty labels and repeated parameters are included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.
atlas: structured-matrices-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_pos_of_strictMono {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → ℝ) (hx : StrictMono x) (hy : StrictMono y)

name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_pos_of_strictMono
doc:
Ordered Cauchy parameters with positive denominators have positive
determinant, including the empty matrix. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.

signature:
NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_succ {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (hDen : ∀ (i j : Fin (n + 1)), x i + y j ≠ 0) :
  (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix x y).det =
    ((1 / (x 0 + y 0) * ∏ i, (x i.succ - x 0) / (x i.succ + y 0)) * ∏ j, (y j.succ - y 0) / (x 0 + y j.succ)) *
      (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix (fun i => x i.succ) fun j => y j.succ).det
name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_succ
doc:
One Schur elimination step gives the Cauchy determinant recurrence. The
only divisions are by the assumed nonzero denominators, so repeated x or y
values require no separate branch. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.

signature:

NLAlib.det_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_sum_norm_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {r : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype r]

The complex column-Gram determinant is the sum of squared absolute
values of all full-column minors. Too few rows, singular matrices and

Equality in positive definite Hadamard holds exactly for a diagonal

NLAlib.det_eq_prod_diag_iff_of_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

PSD Hadamard equality holds exactly for a diagonal matrix or a zero

Fischer's determinant inequality for arbitrary PSD real blocks, including

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobSq_sub_projector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq k] (B : Matrix m k ℝ) (v : Matrix m (Fin 1) ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobSq_sub_projector
doc:
Appending one column multiplies the Gram determinant by its squared distance
from the existing column range. Source: manuscript `sa:volume-column`;
Deshpande--Rademacher--Vempala--Wang (2006), determinant-weighted projection identity.
The Moore--Penrose projector includes dependent starting columns and empty shapes.

Appending a genuine complex column multiplies its Gram determinant by
the squared Frobenius projection residual. Dependent starting columns and
empty shapes are included. Source: `sa:volume-column`.

A singular column Gram matrix stays singular after left multiplication.
Horn product proof, singular intermediate-image case; all finite shapes are allowed.

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_mul_le_det_gram_mul_prod_sq_singularValues {m p k : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin p) ℝ)

name: NLAlib.det_gram_mul_le_det_gram_mul_prod_sq_singularValues
doc:
A left image's Gram determinant is bounded by the original Gram determinant
times the product of the top squared singular values of the left multiplier.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 3.3.4, polar-compression step; singular inputs included.

doc:
The Gram determinant of the image of an orthonormal frame is bounded by the
product of the squared top singular values. Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 3.3.4,
compression-determinant step; all empty and rank deficient cases are included.

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_updateCol_eq_det_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq p] (C : Matrix m p ℝ) (hC : IsUnit (C.transpose * C).det) (i : p) (t : p → ℝ) (d : m → ℝ)
  (hd : C.transpose.mulVec d = 0) :
  ((C.updateCol i (C.mulVec t + d)).transpose * C.updateCol i (C.mulVec t + d)).det =
    (C.transpose * C).det * (t i ^ 2 + ‖WithLp.toLp 2 d‖ ^ 2 * (C.transpose * C)⁻¹ i i)
name: NLAlib.det_gram_updateCol_eq_det_mul
doc:
The exact one-column Gram-volume exchange identity. Here `C t` is the
component in the selected column range and `d` is perpendicular to that range.
The inverse-Gram diagonal is the squared norm of the corresponding inverse
triangular-factor row in QR coordinates. No approximation or relaxed constant
is used. Gu–Eisenstat 1996, Theorem 3.2. Supports `rank-revealing-qr`.

NLAlib.det_inverse_complement_minor_eq_sign_mul_div.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3}

increasing-coordinate convention. No selected minor is assumed invertible.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.4.

signature:

    ((A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ J) fun x => x ∈ K) -

      0

doc:

Three pairwise disjoint principal index sets satisfy the overlapping determinant inequality. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.8.9.

signature:
NLAlib.det_principal_union_mul_inter_eq_iff_of_posDef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

doc:

atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

Minkowski's determinant-root inequality extends continuously to positive
semidefinite real matrices in positive dimension, including singular inputs.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 7.6.8; supports Fan's accretive determinant bound.

the inverse pencil. This retains algebraic multiplicities when used through

regularity these pairs define the complete projective eigenvalue list,

name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap
doc:
The directed gap from the source subspace `range X` to the target subspace
`range Q`, represented by orthonormal frames: `‖(I − QQᴴ) X‖₂`. For arbitrary
blocks this definition is the residual norm. With orthonormal source and target
it lies in `[0, 1]` and depends only on their ranges. It is generally asymmetric
for unequal widths: a source contained in its target has gap zero, while the
reverse gap can be one. For equal widths it is the sine of the largest
principal angle (`directedSubspaceGap_eq_sin_principalAngles`).
Source: Stewart–Sun (1990), §I.5; Golub–Van Loan (2013), §2.5.3.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_comm.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {𝕜 : Type u_4} [RCLike 𝕜] {Q X : Matrix n k 𝕜} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hX : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols X) : NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q X = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap X Q
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_comm
doc:
Equal-width orthonormal frames have symmetric directed gaps, equal to the
sine of their largest principal angle. This statement does not extend to
unequal-dimensional subspaces. Source: Stewart–Sun (1990), §I.5.

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_congr_left.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k'] {k₂ : Type u_4} [Fintype k₂]

  (hP : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P) (h : Q.mulVecLin.range = P.mulVecLin.range) (X : Matrix n k' ℝ) :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q X = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap P X
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_congr_left
doc:
The directed gap depends only on the target range `range Q`. Source: Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`], §I.5.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_congr_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k'] {k₂ : Type u_4} [Fintype k₂] [DecidableEq k₂]
  (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) {Q' : Matrix n k' ℝ} {Q'' : Matrix n k₂ ℝ} (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q')
  (hQ'' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q'') (h : Q'.mulVecLin.range = Q''.mulVecLin.range) :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q''
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_congr_right
doc:
The directed gap depends only on the source range `range Q'` among orthonormal frames: if `Q'`, `Q''` have
orthonormal columns and the same range then `‖(I − QQᵀ)Q'‖₂ = ‖(I − QQᵀ)Q''‖₂`. Proof:
`Q'' = Q' (Q'ᵀQ'')` with `‖Q'ᵀQ''‖₂ ≤ 1`, and symmetrically. Source: Stewart–Sun (1990)
[`ss90`], §I.5.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sin_principalAngles.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {Q Q' : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') (hk : 0 < Fintype.card k) :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' = Real.sin (NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype Q Q' ⟨Fintype.card k - 1, ⋯⟩)
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sin_principalAngles
doc:
`sin θ_max` is the sine of the largest principal angle: for frames `Q`, `Q'` of the same
positive width, `‖(I − QQᵀ)Q'‖₂ = sin θ_last`, `θ` the ordered principal angles
`principalAnglesFintype Q Q'`. (For unequal widths `0 < r' ≤ r` use
`directedSubspaceGap_eq_sqrt_one_sub_sq_singularValues`.) Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
§6.4.3; Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`], Def I.5.3 and Thm I.5.5.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k'] {r : Type u_4} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r]
  (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) {Qp : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQp : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qp)
  (hc : Q * Q.transpose + Qp * Qp.transpose = 1) (X : Matrix n k' ℝ) :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q X = NLAlib.specNorm (Qp.transpose * X)
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul
doc:
With an orthonormal complement `Q⊥` (`Q⊥ᵀQ⊥ = I`, `QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`):
`sin θ_max = ‖Q⊥ᵀ X‖₂`. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 2.5.1; Stewart–Sun (1990)
[`ss90`], Thm I.5.5.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sqrt_one_sub_sq_singularValues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r r' : ℕ}
  {Q : Matrix n (Fin r) ℝ} {Q' : Matrix n (Fin r') ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') (hr' : 0 < r') (hrr : r' ≤ r) :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' = √(1 - NLAlib.singularValues (Q.transpose * Q') (r' - 1) ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sqrt_one_sub_sq_singularValues
doc:
**Principal angles from the SVD.** For `Q : n × r`, `Q' : n × r'` with orthonormal columns and
`0 < r' ≤ r`: `sin θ_max = √(1 − σ_{r'−1}(QᵀQ')²)`, `σ` the zero-indexed singular values.
Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §6.4.3 and Thm 2.5.1; Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`],
Def I.5.3. Proof: `specNorm_residual_sq_eq_one_sub_singularValues_last_sq` and
`σ_min(M) = σ_{r'−1}(M)` for `M : r × r'` with `r' ≤ r` (Courant–Fischer for `MᵀM`, the bridge
`singularValues` = `√` eigenvalues of `MᵀM`, `NLAlib.Matrix.Spectral.SVD`).
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

doc:
Containment of the source range in the target range makes the directed gap

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_le_of_range_le.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] {a : Type u_4} {b : Type u_5} [Fintype a] [DecidableEq a] [Fintype b] [DecidableEq b] (Q : Matrix n k ℝ)
  {Y : Matrix n a ℝ} {Z : Matrix n b ℝ} (hY : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Y) (hZ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Z)
  (hle : Z.mulVecLin.range ≤ Y.mulVecLin.range) : NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Z ≤ NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Y
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_le_of_range_le
doc:
Monotonicity behind `directedSubspaceGap_congr_right`: if `Y`, `Z` have orthonormal columns and
`range Z ⊆ range Y`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)Z‖₂ ≤ ‖(I − QQᵀ)Y‖₂`, since `Z = Y (YᵀZ)` with
`‖YᵀZ‖₂ ≤ 1`. Helper for `principal-angles-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_le_one.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k'] {𝕜 : Type u_4} [RCLike 𝕜] {Q : Matrix n k 𝕜}
  {Q' : Matrix n k' 𝕜} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' ≤ 1
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_le_one
doc:
The directed gap is at most one for `Q`, `Q'` with orthonormal columns. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013)
[`gvl13`], §2.5.3. Atlas `principal-angles-def` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_lt_one_iff_isUnit.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {Q Q' : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') : NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' < 1 ↔ IsUnit (Q.transpose * Q')
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_lt_one_iff_isUnit
doc:
**`QᵀQ'` is invertible iff `θ_max < π/2`.** For `Q`, `Q'` with orthonormal columns indexed by
the same `k`: `sin θ_max < 1 ↔ IsUnit (QᵀQ')`. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
§2.5.3. Proof: by `specNorm_residual_sq_eq_one_sub_singularValues_last_sq` (`k` nonempty; the empty case
is trivial), `sin θ_max < 1 ↔ σ_min(QᵀQ') > 0 ↔` `QᵀQ'` injective `↔` invertible (square).
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

contains. Any real `A`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.

monic polynomials of its degree, when `K_{card k}(A, b) ⊆ range Q`. Any real `A`. Source: Saad
(2011) [`saad11`], §6.6 (the Lanczos polynomial as the least-residual monic polynomial).

signature:

orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, then for every polynomial `p` with
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = (Qᵀb)ᵀ p(QᵀAQ) (Qᵀb)`. Valid for every `q` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).

`Qᵀb = ‖b‖e₁` and the right side is `‖b‖² (p(T_q))₁₁`.

[`saad11`], §6.6.

Eigen-expansion of a quadratic form of a matrix function: for symmetric `A`,
`vᵀ f(A) v = ∑ᵢ f(λᵢ) (uᵢ ⬝ v)²` with `(λᵢ, uᵢ)` the eigenpairs of `A`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 7, eq. (7.1). Atlas: `spectral-measure`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_self_eq_sum

Squared length after finite matrix functional calculus, in eigenbasis
coordinates. Parlett §4.5; bare functions are continuous on the finite spectrum.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_self_le
doc:
**Spectral bound, `cfc` form.** If every eigenvalue of the symmetric `A` lies in `S` and
`|g| ≤ M` on `S`, then `‖g(A) v‖² ≤ M² ‖v‖²`. The `cfc` form of
`dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_le` (Saad 2003, §6.11). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper; the
`cfc` form of `polynomial-spectral-bound`).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error bound.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in `[a, c]`, `Q` with
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, and `p` a polynomial with `deg p < q` and
`|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`. Then `‖f(A) b − Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b‖² ≤ (2E)² ‖b‖²`, i.e.
`‖f(A) b − Q f(T) Qᵀ b‖ ≤ 2E ‖b‖`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4 (with Lemma 3.1);
Druskin–Knizhnerman (1989) [`dk89`]; Higham (2008) [`higham08`], §13.2.
Deviation: an arbitrary approximant `p` in place of the best one (minimise over `p` to get the
printed form); squared norms; no `q ≥ 1` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
atlas: lanczos-fa-error

`abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_open_bernsteinEllipse`,
`‖f(A) v − Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ v‖² ≤ (4M ρ^{1−q}/(ρ − 1))² ‖v‖²`.
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4; Trefethen (2019) [`atap`], Thm 8.2.
Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (analytic rate).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cgRecurrence_p_mulVec_eq_zero
doc:
SCAFFOLD: cg-recurrence
**Search directions are `A`-conjugate**: for `A ≻ 0`, `p_iᵀ A p_j = 0` for `i ≠ j`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (conjugacy of the search directions); Saad
(2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.20. Proof sketch: the joint induction of
`dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero` (the two invariants are proved together; for `j < k`,
`p_{k+1}ᵀ A p_j = r_{k+1}ᵀ A p_j + β_k p_kᵀ A p_j`, the first term is
`r_{k+1}ᵀ (r_j − r_{j+1}) / α_j = 0`, and for `j = k` the choice of `β_k` cancels the two terms).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero
doc:
SCAFFOLD: cg-recurrence
**Residuals are mutually orthogonal**: for `A ≻ 0`, `r_iᵀ r_j = 0` for `i ≠ j` (all `i, j`; after
the grade the residuals are `0`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (orthogonality
of the residuals); Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.19. Proof sketch: joint strong induction on
`k` for `∀ j < k, r_kᵀ r_j = 0 ∧ p_kᵀ A p_j = 0`, using `r_j ∈ span p_{≤j}` and
`p_j ∈ span r_{≤j}` (from the recurrence), the symmetry `uᵀ A v = vᵀ A u`, the identities
`r_kᵀ p_k = r_kᵀ r_k` and `p_kᵀ A p_k = r_kᵀ A p_k`, and `A p_j = (r_j − r_{j+1}) / α_j` when
`α_j ≠ 0`. Degenerate steps: `pᵀAp = 0 → p = 0` (`Matrix.PosDef.dotProduct_mulVec_pos`) and then
`r = 0` (from `r_kᵀ p_k = r_kᵀ r_k`), after which the state freezes
(`cgRecurrence_add_of_r_eq_zero`). Deferred: a long case analysis, not hard mathematics.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_mem
doc:
**Galerkin orthogonality of the recursion**: for `A ≻ 0`, `r_k ⟂ K_k(A, r₀)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1; Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.19.
Proof: `K_k = span r_{<k}` (`span_cgRecurrence_r`) and `r_k ⟂ r_j` for `j < k`
(`dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero`). Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_fromBlocks_eq_generalizedSchurComplement_square.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m m 𝕜) (B : Matrix m n 𝕜) (C : Matrix n n 𝕜)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hRange : A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * B = B) (y : m → 𝕜) (x : n → 𝕜) :
  star (Sum.elim y x) ⬝ᵥ (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.conjTranspose C).mulVec (Sum.elim y x) =
    star (y + (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec (B.mulVec x)) ⬝ᵥ
        A.mulVec (y + (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec (B.mulVec x)) +
      star x ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.generalizedSchurComplement A B C).mulVec x

doc:
**Square completion** with the Moore–Penrose inverse: for Hermitian `A` with
`A A⁺ B = B`,
`(y, x)ᴴ M (y, x) = (y + A⁺Bx)ᴴ A (y + A⁺Bx) + xᴴ (M / A) x`. Albert 1969, Theorem 1; supports
`generalized-schur-complement-psd`.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_generalizedSchurComplement_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Variational characterisation, attainment**: for `M = [[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]] ⪰ 0` the minimum
over `y` of `(y, x)ᴴ M (y, x)` is attained at `y = −A⁺Bx` and equals `xᴴ (M / A) x`.
Albert 1969, Thm 1; cf. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.7.
Proof: the square completion `dotProduct_fromBlocks_eq_generalizedSchurComplement_square` with
`y + A⁺Bx = 0`.
atlas: generalized-schur-complement-psd (partial)

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_generalizedSchurComplement_mulVec_le
doc:
**Variational characterisation, lower bound**: for `M = [[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]] ⪰ 0`,
`xᴴ (M / A) x ≤ (y, x)ᴴ M (y, x)` for every `y`. Albert 1969, Thm 1; cf. Horn–Johnson 2013,
§7.7. The lower-bound half of `isLeast_generalizedSchurComplement_quadratic`.
atlas: generalized-schur-complement-psd (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_golubKahan_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {k : ℕ} (h : NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds A b k) :
  (∀ j ≤ k,
      (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).u ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).v =
        (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).alpha) ∧
    ∀ j < k,
      (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b (j + 1)).u ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).v =
        (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b (j + 1)).beta
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_golubKahan_eq
doc:
SCAFFOLD: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization
**The entries of `B` are the recursion's `α, β`.** Without breakdown through state `k`:
`u_{j+1}ᵀ A v_{j+1} = α_{j+1}` for `j ≤ k` and `u_{j+2}ᵀ A v_{j+1} = β_{j+2}` for `j < k`, so the
`B` of the realised decomposition has diagonal `α` and subdiagonal `β` (all positive). Source:
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Alg. 10.4.1 and eq. (10.4.4). Proof sketch: from the
recursion, `Aᵀu_{j+1} = α_{j+1}v_{j+1} + β_{j+1}v_j` and
`Av_{j+1} = α_{j+1}u_{j+1} + β_{j+2}u_{j+2}`, then orthonormality
(`isGradedKrylovBasis_golubKahanU_V`). Difficulty 2 given the realisation.
atlas: golub-kahan-recurrence

signature:

doc:
Splitting off the first mode turns a tensor contraction into a linear
form in its first vector factor.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_moorePenroseInverse_mul_mulVec_le_dotProduct_self.{u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

signature:

A symmetric quadratic form is bounded above by its largest eigenvalue.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_mul_dotProduct_of_eigenvalues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
Upper Rayleigh bound from an eigenvalue enclosure: `xᵀ A x ≤ c ‖x‖²` if every eigenvalue is
at most `c`. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Thm 4.2.2. Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_mem_range
doc:
Rayleigh quotients over `range Q` are bounded by any upper bound `θ` on the eigenvalues of
`QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), for `Q` with orthonormal columns: `yᵀAy ≤ θ ‖y‖²` for `y ∈ range Q`.
Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1 (Rayleigh–Ritz). Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
  {M : Matrix m m ℝ} (hM : M.PosSemidef) {y : m → ℝ} (hy : y ⬝ᵥ y ≤ 1) {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) :
  (y ⬝ᵥ M.mulVec y) ^ s ≤ y ⬝ᵥ (M ^ s).mulVec y
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec
doc:
**Jensen for a positive semidefinite quadratic form.** For `M ⪰ 0`, a vector `y` with
`y ⬝ y ≤ 1` and `s ≥ 1`, `(yᵀMy)^s ≤ yᵀM^s y`. With `y = Σᵢ cᵢuᵢ` in an eigenbasis this is
`(Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ)^s ≤ Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ^s`, convexity of `t ↦ t^s` on `t ≥ 0` with total weight `Σᵢ cᵢ² ≤ 1`.
HMT 2011, proof of Prop 8.6. Atlas `power-iteration-deterministic` (helper; belongs in
`Matrix/PolynomialCalculus.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {σlo σhi : ℝ} (hlo : 0 < σlo) (hlohi : σlo ≤ σhi)
  (hlow : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σlo ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)
  (hup : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v ≤ σhi ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v) {b : m → ℝ} {x₀ xs x : n → ℝ}
  (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate A b x₀ q x) :
  A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((σhi - σlo) / (σhi + σlo)) ^ q) ^ 2 * A.mulVec (x₀ - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate
doc:
**CGLS/LSQR convergence, `κ(A)` rate.** Let `A : ℝ^{m×n}` have all singular values in
`[σ_lo, σ_hi]`, `0 < σ_lo ≤ σ_hi`, stated as `σ_lo² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖² ≤ σ_hi² ‖v‖²` for all `v` (so `A`
has full column rank), let `x⋆` solve the normal equations `AᵀA x⋆ = Aᵀb`, and `x` be a `q`-th
CGLS iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖A(x − x⋆)‖² ≤ (2((σ_hi − σ_lo)/(σ_hi + σ_lo))^q)² ‖A(x₀ − x⋆)‖²`.
Proof: CG on `AᵀA` with spectrum in `[σ_lo², σ_hi²]` (`quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3; Paige–Saunders (1982) [`ps82`].
Deviation: squared norms; the singular-value hypothesis in Rayleigh form.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

signature:

The quadratic form of a matrix on `Fin (n + 1)` at `(x₀, y)`, expanded over the bordered
splitting.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_moorePenroseInverse_mul_mulVec.{u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (M : Matrix m n ℝ) (d : n → ℝ) :

doc:
The Moore–Penrose row projector `Z = M⁺M` satisfies `(d − Zd)ᵀ(d − Zd) = dᵀd − dᵀZd`
(Pythagoras for the orthogonal projector onto `range Mᵀ`). Horn–Johnson §7.3; helper for
`sketch-and-project` (Gower–Richtárik 2015).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_chebyshevIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_chebyshevIterate_le
doc:
**Chebyshev iteration, residual rate.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, `‖c − A x_q‖² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖r₀‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3. Deviation: squared norms.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_polyIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {s : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hM : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x (1 - Polynomial.X * s)| ≤ M) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) :
  (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.polyIterate A c x₀ s)) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.polyIterate A c x₀ s)) ≤
    M ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_polyIterate_le
doc:
**Residual bound for a polynomial method.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `S` and
`|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`, `‖c − A x‖² ≤ M² ‖r₀‖²`. No solution is needed.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_richardsonIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b ω : ℝ} (hω : 0 ≤ ω) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.richardsonIterate ω A c x₀ q)) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.richardsonIterate ω A c x₀ q)) ≤
    (max |1 - ω * a| |1 - ω * b| ^ q) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_richardsonIterate_le
doc:
**Richardson contraction, residual norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]` and
step `ω ≥ 0`, `‖c − A x_q‖² ≤ ρ^{2q} ‖r₀‖²`, `ρ = max(|1 − ωa|, |1 − ωb|)`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2. Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

NLAlib.dotProduct_shift_pow_mulVec_of_left_eigenvector.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

Pairing with a left eigenvector turns shifted matrix powers into scalar
powers. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), proof of Lemma 1.4.11.

signature:

Pythagoras separates the optimal Rayleigh residual and the shift error.

The shifted residual squared length is the weighted squared spectral
distance. Parlett §4.5; weights are squared eigenbasis coordinates.

  (hlow : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σlo ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)
  (hup : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v ≤ σhi ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v) {b : m → ℝ} {x₀ xs x : n → ℝ}
  (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate A b x₀ q x) :
  (b - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec x) ≤
    (b - A.mulVec xs) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xs) +
      (2 * ((σhi - σlo) / (σhi + σlo)) ^ q) ^ 2 * A.mulVec (x₀ - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_le_of_isCGLSIterate
doc:
**CGLS/LSQR residual bound.** Under the hypotheses of
`dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate`,
`‖b − Ax‖² ≤ ‖b − Ax⋆‖² + (2((σ_hi − σ_lo)/(σ_hi + σ_lo))^q)² ‖A(x₀ − x⋆)‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (y : n → ℝ) :
  (b - A.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec y) = 2 * NLAlib.cgObjective (A.transpose * A) (A.transpose.mulVec b) y + b ⬝ᵥ b
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq
doc:
The least-squares objective is twice the CG objective of the normal equations plus a
constant: `‖b − Ay‖² = 2 φ_{AᵀA, Aᵀb}(y) + ‖b‖²`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3.
Helper for `cgls-lsqr-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq_add.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b)
  (x : n → ℝ) :
  (b - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec x) = (b - A.mulVec xs) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xs) + A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_le_mul_overlapTangentSq
doc:
**Rayleigh–Ritz step of Kaniel–Paige–Saad.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every
eigenvalue `≥ a`, `u` a unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue `λ` at sorted position `i₀`, `Q`
with orthonormal columns, `θ₁ = θ_{j₁}` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`, and `x ∈ range Q`
with `u ⬝ x ≠ 0`. Then `λ − θ₁ ≤ (λ − a) tan² ∠(u, x)` (from
`λ − xᵀAx/xᵀx ≤ (λ − a) sin² ∠(u, x)`). Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4.
Helper for `kaniel-paige-saad`.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {u : n → ℝ}
  (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 • u) (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c)
  (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues₀ 0) (hspec : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ 0 → hA.eigenvalues₀ i ∈ Set.Icc a c)
  {b : n → ℝ} (hb : u ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0) (q : ℕ) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {j₁ : k}
  (hj₁ : ∀ (j : k), ⋯.eigenvalues j ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues j₁) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - ⋯.eigenvalues j₁ ≤
    (hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - a) *
      (NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u b /
        Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound for the largest Ritz value.** Let `A` be real symmetric with top
eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ₀(A)` and unit eigenvector `u`, every other eigenvalue (sorted position `≠ 0`)
in `[a, c]` with `a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`), `u ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q` with orthonormal
columns and `K_{q+1}(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (e.g. a Lanczos basis after `q` matvecs), and `θ₁` the
largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`. Then
`λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) tan² ∠(u, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`; the lower bound
`0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` is `eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`); Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4.
Deviation: Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`, so `T_{m−1} = T_q`); `[a, c]` any enclosure
of the other eigenvalues (Saad: `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`, factor `λ₁ − λₙ`); any orthonormal `Q`
whose range contains the Krylov space.
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le_of_poly
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad, polynomial form.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every eigenvalue
`≥ a`, `u` a unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue `λ` at sorted position `i₀`, `u ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q`
with orthonormal columns and `K_q(A, b) ⊆ range Q`, and `θ₁` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`.
For every polynomial `p` with `deg p < q`, `p(λ) ≠ 0` and `|p| ≤ M` at every other sorted
position: `λ − θ₁ ≤ (λ − a) (M/p(λ))² tan² ∠(u, b)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_mul_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {u : n → ℝ} {L : ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = L • u) (i : n) :
  (hA.eigenvalues i - L) * (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ u = 0
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_mul_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq_zero
doc:
Eigen-coordinates of an eigenvector: `(λᵢ − L)(uᵢ ⬝ u) = 0` when `A u = L u`. Helper for
`krylov-eigenvector-angle`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
The Ritz values are at most the top eigenvalue: `θⱼ ≤ λ₀(A)` for every eigenvalue `θⱼ` of
`Qᵀ A Q`, `Q` with orthonormal columns. This is the lower half `0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` of the
Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (left inequality; Cauchy
interlacing).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_mem_Icc
doc:
The eigenvalues of the compression `Qᵀ A Q` (`Q` with orthonormal columns) lie in any
interval `[a, c]` containing the eigenvalues of `A` (the Ritz values stay inside the spectral
interval). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4; Parlett (1998), Thm 10.1.1 (weak form).
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper; Matrix-level, to move to `Matrix/Basic/QuadForm`).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le_add_eigenvalues₀_zero
doc:
Weyl's signed eigenvalue perturbation bound, upper side.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.1. Indices are decreasing and zero-indexed.
atlas: eigenvalue-perturbation-symmetric

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le_of_card_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n))
  (hi : ↑i + {j | 0 < hB.eigenvalues₀ j}.card < Fintype.card n) :
  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨↑i + {j | 0 < hB.eigenvalues₀ j}.card, hi⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ i
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le_of_card_pos
doc:
An update with `π` positive eigenvalues shifts the upper bound by
exactly `π` places in decreasing order. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.3.
atlas: low-rank-update-interlacing (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le_of_rank_le
doc:
A symmetric update of rank at most `r` shifts the upper eigenvalue
bound by at most `r` indices. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.5.
atlas: low-rank-update-interlacing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_cfc_of_antitone.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hf : Antitone fun i => f (hA.eigenvalues₀ i))
  (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) : ⋯.eigenvalues₀ i = f (hA.eigenvalues₀ i)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_cfc_of_antitone

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_congruence_bounds_of_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (S : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (hk : 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ k) :
  NLAlib.singularValues S (Fintype.card n - 1) ^ 2 * hA.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ k ∧
    ⋯.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ NLAlib.specNorm S ^ 2 * hA.eigenvalues₀ k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_congruence_bounds_of_nonneg
doc:
At a nonnegative original eigenvalue, congruence scales between the
squared smallest and largest singular values. Singular transformations
are included. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.5.9.
atlas: ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_congruence_bounds_of_nonpos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (S : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (hk : hA.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ 0) :
  NLAlib.specNorm S ^ 2 * hA.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ k ∧
    ⋯.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ NLAlib.singularValues S (Fintype.card n - 1) ^ 2 * hA.eigenvalues₀ k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_congruence_bounds_of_nonpos
doc:
At a nonpositive original eigenvalue, congruence reverses the two
extreme-singular-value scaling bounds. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.5.9.
atlas: ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_dilation {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : Fin (m + n)) :
  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ k) = NLAlib.realDilationSpectrum A k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_dilation
doc:
Every sorted eigenvalue of the real dilation equals the corresponding
explicit paired singular value. Bhatia 1997, Section III.4; all rectangular
shapes, multiplicities and zero padding are included.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_dilation_bottom {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (i : Fin (min m n)) :
  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ (Fin.castLE ⋯ i).rev) = -NLAlib.singularValues A ↑i
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_dilation_bottom
doc:
The reversed bottom thin slots of real dilation are the negative singular values.
Bhatia 1997, Section III.4; all empty and rank-deficient cases are included.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_dilation_top {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (i : Fin (min m n)) :
  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ (Fin.castLE ⋯ i)) = NLAlib.singularValues A ↑i
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_dilation_top
doc:
The top thin slots of real dilation are the ordered singular values.
Bhatia 1997, Section III.4; singular zeros cause no exceptions.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_charpoly_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [RCLike 𝕜]
  {A B : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h : A.charpoly = B.charpoly) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ = hB.eigenvalues₀
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_charpoly_eq
doc:
Hermitian matrices (over `ℝ` or `ℂ`) with equal characteristic polynomials have the same
sorted eigenvalue list. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 4.1.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {q : ℕ} {S : Matrix n n 𝕜} {W : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (hS : S.IsHermitian) {μ : Fin q → ℝ}
  (hμ : Antitone μ) (hW : W.conjTranspose * W = 1) (hq : Fintype.card n = q)
  (hSW : S = (W * Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(μ i)) * W.conjTranspose) (k : Fin q) : hS.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ k) = μ k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul
doc:
For a Hermitian `S = W diag(μ) Wᴴ` with `W : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜`, `WᴴW = 1`, `q = card n`
and `μ` real and non-increasing, `μ` is Mathlib's sorted eigenvalue list `eigenvalues₀` of `S`
(uniqueness of the sorted spectrum, via the characteristic polynomial). Atlas `svd` (helper;
belongs with the spectral API).

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_matrix_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [RCLike 𝕜]
  {A B : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h : A = B) : hA.eigenvalues₀ = hB.eigenvalues₀
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_matrix_eq
doc:
Equal Hermitian matrices have equal sorted eigenvalue lists.
Mathlib's spectral definition and proof irrelevance; helper for
`singular-value-interlacing` and congruence spectrum comparisons.

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_last_mul_le_dotProduct_mulVec
doc:
A symmetric quadratic form is bounded below by its smallest eigenvalue.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.2.2; no sign condition on the matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_add_of_card_neg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n))
  (hi : ↑i + {j | hB.eigenvalues₀ j < 0}.card < Fintype.card n) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨↑i + {j | hB.eigenvalues₀ j < 0}.card, hi⟩ ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ i
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_add_of_card_neg
doc:
An update with `ν` negative eigenvalues gives the matching lower
bound, shifted by `ν` places in decreasing order.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.3.
atlas: low-rank-update-interlacing (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_add_of_rank_le
doc:
A rank-`r` symmetric update has the matching lower eigenvalue bound.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.5.
atlas: low-rank-update-interlacing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_zero_of_card_pos_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hB : B.IsHermitian) (j : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (hj : {i | 0 < hB.eigenvalues₀ i}.card ≤ ↑j) : hB.eigenvalues₀ j ≤ 0
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_zero_of_card_pos_le

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_lt_of_forall_mem.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (W : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ))

  hA.eigenvalues₀ k < c
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_lt_of_forall_mem
doc:
A strict upper Rayleigh bound on a subspace of codimension at most
`k` implies a strict bound for the `k`-th largest eigenvalue.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.2.10.
atlas: eigenvalue-order-and-counting (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_map_ofReal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (hC : (A.map Complex.ofReal).IsHermitian) : hC.eigenvalues₀ = hA.eigenvalues₀
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_map_ofReal
doc:
Complexification preserves the full ordered spectrum of a real
symmetric matrix. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 4.1; eigenvalues have exactly
their original multiplicities.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_neg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_neg
doc:
Negation reverses and negates sorted eigenvalues, including repeated
eigenvalues. Horn--Johnson (2013), Observation 4.2.5.
atlas: eigenvalue-order-and-counting (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_nonneg_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_nonneg_of_posSemidef
doc: Sorted eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix_strict_interlacing (L : Polynomial ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) {n : ℕ}
  (hL : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, NLAlib.hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0) (hH : ∀ k < n + 1, 0 < NLAlib.orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k)

  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ i.succ) < ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ i) ∧

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix_strict_interlacing
doc:
Eigenvalues of consecutive moment Jacobi matrices strictly interlace.
Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 1.19.
atlas: orthogonal-polynomial-zeros (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_pencil_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (t h : ℝ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) : ⋯.eigenvalues₀ i = ⋯.eigenvalues₀ i
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_pencil_add
doc:
Successive increments of a symmetric affine pencil agree with their summed
parameter. The exact matrix identity; supports the shifted Lidskii variation.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_rank_one_add_interlacing.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (z : n → ℝ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_rank_one_add_interlacing
doc:
A PSD rank-one update has one-step decreasing-order interlacing.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.7.
atlas: low-rank-update-interlacing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_rank_one_sub_interlacing.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (z : n → ℝ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :
  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ i ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ i ∧

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_rank_one_sub_interlacing
doc:
A PSD rank-one downdate has the corresponding reversed one-step
interlacing. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.9.
atlas: low-rank-update-interlacing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_reindex.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype p]

  (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) : ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ i) = hA.eigenvalues₀ i
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_reindex

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_aeval_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) (i : n) :
  (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v =
    Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p * (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v
name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_aeval_mulVec
doc:
Eigen-coordinates of `p(A) v`: `uᵢ ⬝ p(A) v = p(λᵢ) (uᵢ ⬝ v)` for real symmetric `A`.
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eigenvectorBasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (i j : n) : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ (hA.eigenvectorBasis j).ofLp = if i = j then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eigenvectorBasis
doc:
The eigenvector basis is orthonormal in dot-product form: `uᵢ ⬝ uⱼ = δᵢⱼ`.
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_inv_sub_mulVec
doc:
The resolvent shares the eigenvectors of `A`: if `μ` is not an eigenvalue,
`uᵢ ⬝ ((A − μI)⁻¹ v) = (λᵢ − μ)⁻¹ (uᵢ ⬝ v)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 27.
Helper for `inverse-iteration`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_mul_eq
doc:
For an eigenvector `u` with `A u = L u`, `uᵢ ⬝ u` vanishes unless `λᵢ = L`, so any `g` acts
as `g(L)` on these coordinates: `(uᵢ ⬝ u) g(λᵢ) = (uᵢ ⬝ u) g(L)`. Helper.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_pow_mulVec_eq
doc:
Eigen-coordinates of powers of a spectral multiplier: if `uᵢ ⬝ (B y) = fᵢ (uᵢ ⬝ y)` for all
`y`, then `uᵢ ⬝ (B^k v) = fᵢ^k (uᵢ ⬝ v)`. Helper for `power-iteration`, `inverse-iteration`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_sub_smul_mulVec
doc:
The shifted matrix in eigen-coordinates: `uᵢ ⬝ ((A − μI) y) = (λᵢ − μ)(uᵢ ⬝ y)`. Helper for
`inverse-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvectorProjector.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
  {A : Matrix d d 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (i : d) : Matrix d d 𝕜
name: NLAlib.eigenvectorProjector
doc:
The **rank-one eigenvector projector** `U eᵢ eᵢᴴ Uᴴ = uᵢ uᵢᴴ` of a Hermitian matrix `A`
onto its `i`-th eigenvector `uᵢ`, where `U = hA.eigenvectorUnitary` is Mathlib's chosen
eigenvector basis (so the projector depends on that choice; it is a proof device, and the
basis-free object is the eigenspace projector `eigenspaceProjector hA ℓ` of
`Matrix/Perturbation/EigenspaceProjector.lean`). Tropp 2015, §2.1.6.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvectorUnitary_mul_transpose_self.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) : ↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary * (↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary).transpose = 1
name: NLAlib.eigenvectorUnitary_mul_transpose_self
doc:
The eigenvector matrix of a real symmetric matrix is orthogonal: `UUᵀ = I`.
Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature: NLAlib.eliminationStep.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} (A : Matrix n n K) (t : n) : Matrix n n K
name: NLAlib.eliminationStep
doc:
**One elimination step** on pivot `t`: `A − A(:,t) A(t,:) / A(t,t)`, the Schur complement of
`A(t,t)` padded with a zero row and column at `t`. Total: for `A(t,t) = 0` it returns `A`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2.1, §4.2.9; CETW 2023, §2.

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} (A : Matrix n n K) (t i j : n) :
  NLAlib.eliminationStep A t i j = A i j - (A t t)⁻¹ * (A i t * A t j)
name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply
doc: Entrywise form of an elimination step: `aᵢⱼ − aᵢₜ aₜⱼ / aₜₜ`.

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_eq_zero_of_col.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {A : Matrix n n K}

name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_eq_zero_of_col
doc: An elimination step keeps zero columns zero.

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_eq_zero_of_row.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {A : Matrix n n K}
  {u : n} (hu : ∀ (j : n), A u j = 0) (t j : n) : NLAlib.eliminationStep A t u j = 0
name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_eq_zero_of_row
doc: An elimination step keeps zero rows zero.

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_left.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.PosSemidef) (t j : n) : NLAlib.eliminationStep A t t j = 0
name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_left
doc:
After an elimination step on a PSD matrix the pivot row vanishes (also at a zero pivot,
whose row is already zero).

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_left_of_ne_zero.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {A : Matrix n n K}

name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_left_of_ne_zero

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_right.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_right
doc: After an elimination step on a PSD matrix the pivot column vanishes.

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_right_of_ne_zero.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2}
  {A : Matrix n n K} {t : n} (ht : A t t ≠ 0) (i : n) : NLAlib.eliminationStep A t i t = 0
name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_apply_pivot_right_of_ne_zero
doc: A nonzero pivot eliminates its entire column (no positivity needed).

signature:
NLAlib.eliminationStep_eq_self_of_apply_self_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2}
  {A : Matrix n n K} {t : n} (ht : A t t = 0) : NLAlib.eliminationStep A t = A
name: NLAlib.eliminationStep_eq_self_of_apply_self_eq_zero

`Ent_ν(F) = ∫ F log F dν - (∫ F dν) log ∫ F dν`.
Source: Ledoux, *The Concentration of Measure Phenomenon*, Prop 5.6; Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart
2013, Thm 4.10. Atlas: `entropy-tensorization`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.entropy_tensorization`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_T_real_eq_of_one_le {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (q : ℕ) :

signature:

signature:

The actual absolute-value Chebyshev truncation has a cancellation-preserving
finite expression in a complex sine coordinate.

name: NLAlib.eval_christoffelPolynomial_ne_zero_of_outside_support_interval

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.eval_div_linearPoleProduct_eq_partial_fractions.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [Fintype ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] (v : ι → 𝕜) (s : ι → ℕ) (q : Polynomial 𝕜) (c : (i : ι) → Fin (s i) → 𝕜) {t : 𝕜}

  Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) ((Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.image hA.eigenvalues Finset.univ) id) f) =

signature:
NLAlib.eval_interpolate_eq_circleIntegral.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → ℂ)
  (hv : Set.InjOn v ↑s) {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c x : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (Metric.ball c R))
  (hvR : ∀ i ∈ s, v i ∈ Metric.ball c R) (hx : x ∈ Metric.ball c R) :
  Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate s v) (f ∘ v)) =
    (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I)⁻¹ *
      ∮ (t : ℂ) in C(c, R),
        f t *
          ((Polynomial.eval t (Lagrange.nodal s v) - Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal s v)) /
            (Polynomial.eval t (Lagrange.nodal s v) * (t - x)))
name: NLAlib.eval_interpolate_eq_circleIntegral
doc:
Hermite's formula writes the Lagrange interpolant as one circle integral.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 11.1. It suffices that `f` is holomorphic in the
open disc and continuous on its closure; all nodes and the evaluation point are interior.
The empty set of nodes is included.
atlas: hermite-integral-formula

signature:
NLAlib.eval_interpolate_node_succ_eq_barycentric (k : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) {x : ℝ}
  (hx : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 2), x ≠ Polynomial.Chebyshev.node (k + 1) j) :
  Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.range (k + 2)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.node (k + 1))) f) =
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 2),
        ((-1) ^ j * if j = 0 ∨ j = k + 1 then 1 / 2 else 1) * (x - Polynomial.Chebyshev.node (k + 1) j)⁻¹ * f j) /
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 2),
        ((-1) ^ j * if j = 0 ∨ j = k + 1 then 1 / 2 else 1) * (x - Polynomial.Chebyshev.node (k + 1) j)⁻¹

doc:
The Chebyshev endpoint-grid interpolant has the barycentric formula with
alternating endpoint-halved weights. Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 5.2.
At grid nodes the interpolant is instead evaluated by its interpolation property.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_map_secondKindPolynomial_div_eq_mass_mul_jacobiFraction {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  (hμ : NLAlib.HasPolynomialMoments μ) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n) (hn : ↑n ≤ μ.support.encard) {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) :
  Polynomial.eval z
        (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.secondKindPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) /
      Polynomial.eval z
        (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) =
    ↑(∫ (x : ℝ), 1 ∂μ) *
      NLAlib.jacobiFraction (⇑Complex.ofRealHom ∘ NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ))
        (⇑Complex.ofRealHom ∘ fun i => √(NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceBeta (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) i)) z n 0

doc:
The actual second-kind rational approximant is its original mass times the
ordinary complex Jacobi fraction away from the real axis. Source: operator
derivations (OF25), (OF27), (AQ18).
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial), jacobi-fraction-second-kind (partial)

signature:

    ↑(∫ (x : ℝ), 1 ∂μ) *
      (z • 1 - (NLAlib.orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map ⇑Complex.ofRealHom)⁻¹

doc:

  (hinverseSpec :
