  [DecidableEq p] [DecidableEq q] (U : Matrix (p ⊕ q) (p ⊕ q) ℝ) (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (e : p ↪ q) :
  have c := fun i => NLAlib.singularValues U.toBlocks₁₁ ↑((Fintype.equivFin p) i);
  (∀ (i : p), c i ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
    ∃ V₁ W₁ V₂ W₂,
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧
            NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W₂ ∧
              (Matrix.fromBlocks V₁ 0 0 V₂).transpose * U * Matrix.fromBlocks W₁ 0 0 W₂ =
                NLAlib.csCanonicalMatrix c (Matrix.submatrix 1 id ⇑e)
name: NLAlib.exists_cs_decomposition_of_embedding
doc:
The full CS factorization with a literal coordinate inclusion into the
larger block. The four basis factors have the required sizes `p,p,q,q`.
Any injective coordinate placement works; a placement exists exactly when
`card p ≤ card q`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.7.1.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_definite_pair_congruence_diagonal.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {𝕜 : Type u_2}
  [RCLike 𝕜] {A B : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
  ∃ S d,
    IsUnit S ∧
      A = S * S.conjTranspose ∧
        B = (S * Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(d i)) * S.conjTranspose ∧ (B.PosSemidef → ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ d i)
name: NLAlib.exists_definite_pair_congruence_diagonal
doc:
A positive definite and Hermitian pair over real or complex scalars is
simultaneously congruent to the identity and a real diagonal in factor form.
The diagonal entries are nonnegative whenever the second matrix is PSD.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.6.1; extends the real form to `RCLike`.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence (partial)

signature:

name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_eval_le_on_two_intervals
doc:
A Chebyshev residual composed with quadratic folding has degree at most `2k`,
equals one at zero, and is exponentially small on two equal-length intervals.
Source: Greenbaum (1997), §3.1; Liesen–Strakoš (2013), §5.6;
operator derivations §3. No optimality assertion is added.
atlas: two-interval-minimax

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_exp_neg_sub_eval_le {b δ : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1) :

Exponential approximation in the existential polynomial interface, with the exact source
degree `ceil(sqrt(2t log(4/δ)))` and `t=ceil(max(e²b/2,log(2/δ)))`.
Source: Sachdeva–Vishnoi, Theorem 4.1.
atlas: exp-polynomial-approx

Monomial approximation in the existential polynomial interface used by Krylov proofs.

Principal real powers have the stated enclosure bound on a right-half-plane ellipse.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_jackson_interval {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a c : ℝ} {L : NNReal} (hac : a < c)
  (hf : LipschitzOnWith L f (Set.Icc a c)) (n : ℕ) :
  ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑n ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c, |f x - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ Real.pi * ↑L * (c - a) / (4 * (↑n + 1))
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_jackson_interval
doc:
Every Lipschitz function on a nondegenerate interval has an degree-`n` real
polynomial with the sharp error `πL(c-a)/(4(n+1))`, for every `n ≥ 0`.
Source: Arnold, *Numerical Analysis* lecture notes, §1.2 (Jackson's theorem).
The sawtooth interpolation, sharp norm, periodic error, cosine-polynomial representation,
and affine rescaling are all proved without an approximation certificate.
atlas: jackson-lipschitz

name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_jackson_unit
doc:
The required sharp Jackson theorem on the unit interval: a degree-`n` algebraic
polynomial approximates every `L`-Lipschitz function with error at most `πL/(2(n+1))`.
Source: Arnold, *Numerical Analysis* lecture notes, §1.2 (Jackson's theorem).
Atlas `jackson-lipschitz` (unit-interval form).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_of_open_bernsteinEllipse {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)

doc:
A bounded holomorphic extension on the open Bernstein ellipse supplies a real polynomial
of degree at most `N` with the exact error `2M ρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)` on `[-1,1]`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 8.2.
No boundary continuity or coefficient/approximation conclusion is assumed.
atlas: bernstein-ellipse-approx

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_of_open_bernsteinEllipse_interval {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} {a c ρ M : ℝ}

doc:
Affine transplantation of the Bernstein-ellipse polynomial rate to any real interval.
The analytic extension is of `t ↦ f(((c-a)t+c+a)/2)` on the original open ellipse.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 8.2.
atlas: bernstein-ellipse-approx

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_of_rightHalfPlane {a b ρ M : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} (ha : 0 < a)

A function holomorphic in the right half-plane, bounded on the explicit ellipse

signature:

An actual degree-bounded polynomial attains the absolute-value approximation
error, and thus supplies its pointwise uniform bound.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_approx_of_bv {ν n : ℕ} {F : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ} {V : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hn : ν < n)
  (hAC : ∀ j < ν, AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval (F j) (-1) 1)
  (hderiv : ∀ j < ν, ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ), x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1 → deriv (F j) x = F (j + 1) x)
  (hBV : BoundedVariationOn (F ν) (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (hV : (eVariationOn (F ν) (Set.Icc (-1) 1)).toReal ≤ V) :
  ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑n ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |F 0 x - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ 2 * V / (Real.pi * ↑ν * (↑n - ↑ν) ^ ν)
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_approx_of_bv
doc:
The differentiable bound is attained by an explicit degree-bounded polynomial.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Thm 7.2; the existential approximation interface.
atlas: chebyshev-approx-differentiable

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_eval_eq_one_abs_eval_le {a c L : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hcL : c < L) (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ p,
    p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧
      Polynomial.eval L p = 1 ∧
        ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c,
          |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ 1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((L - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_eval_eq_one_abs_eval_le
doc:
**The shifted Chebyshev amplifier.** For `a < c < L` and every `q` there is a polynomial
`p` of degree at most `q` with `p(L) = 1` and `|p| ≤ 1/T_q(1 + 2γ)` on `[a, c]`,
`γ = (L − c)/(c − a)`: namely `p(x) = T_q((2x − c − a)/(c − a))/T_q(1 + 2γ)`, the
`chebyshevAmplifier` with `α = (c − a)/2`, `γ' = 2γ`, shifted by `(c + a)/2`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1. Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (belongs in
`NLAlib.Polynomial.FunctionApproximation.Approximation` next to `chebyshev-amplifier`).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_mul_sub_mul_eq_of_isCoprime {m n : ℕ} {p q H : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p ≠ 0) (hq : q ≠ 0)
  (hcop : IsCoprime p q) (hpdeg : p.degree ≤ ↑m) (hqdeg : q.degree ≤ ↑n)
  (hH : H.degree ≤ ↑(max (m + q.natDegree) (n + p.natDegree))) :
  ∃ P Q, P.degree ≤ ↑m ∧ Q.degree ≤ ↑n ∧ P * q - p * Q = H
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_mul_sub_mul_eq_of_isCoprime
doc:
The full polynomial tangent-numerator map of a reduced nonzero rational function is
surjective, with the exact defect-adjusted degree bound.
Source: operator rederivations, `polybest:rational-linear-map`; the constructive proof
uses Bézout remainders on the larger side of the degree maximum.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_norm_sub_eq_minimaxError {s : Set ℝ} [CompactSpace ↑s] (n : ℕ) (f : C(↑s, ℝ)) :

name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_norm_sub_eq_minimaxError
doc:
A polynomial of degree at most `n` attains the best uniform approximation error.
Source: Cheney (1966), Chapter 2; ATAP, Chapter 10. The compact set may be any compact
subset of the real line, including empty sets.
atlas: minimax-error-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_resolvent_modulus_approximation {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (M : ℝ) (hM : 0 ≤ M) (r : ℕ)
  (hr : 0 < r) :
  ∃ Q, Q.degree ≤ ↑r ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-M) M, |‖(z - ↑x)⁻¹‖ - Polynomial.eval x Q| ≤ 6 * M / (↑r * z.im ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_resolvent_modulus_approximation
doc:
The actual degree-`r` Jackson approximant has the source's simpler
`6M/(rη²)` bound when `r` is positive.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_resolvent_modulus_jackson {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (M : ℝ) (hM : 0 ≤ M) (r : ℕ) :
  ∃ Q,
    Q.degree ≤ ↑r ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-M) M, |‖(z - ↑x)⁻¹‖ - Polynomial.eval x Q| ≤ Real.pi * M / (2 * (↑r + 1) * z.im ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_resolvent_modulus_jackson

On every centered compact interval, the scalar nonreal resolvent
modulus has an actual degree-`r` polynomial approximant with the sharp

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_weighted_norm_sub_minimal {s : Set ℝ} [CompactSpace ↑s] (n : ℕ) (f w : C(↑s, ℝ)) :
  ∃ p,
    p.degree ≤ ↑n ∧
      ∀ (q : Polynomial ℝ), q.degree ≤ ↑n → ‖w * (f - p.toContinuousMapOn s)‖ ≤ ‖w * (f - q.toContinuousMapOn s)‖
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_weighted_norm_sub_minimal
doc:
A weighted polynomial minimizer exists on every compact real set, even for
a weight that vanishes. Source: finite-dimensional minimax attainment, RC10.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le {a b : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) :
  ∃ p, p.degree < ↑q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, |Polynomial.eval x p - 1 / x| ≤ 2 / a * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le
doc:
Polynomial approximation of `1/x` on `[a, b]`: for `0 < a < b` there is a polynomial `p` of
degree `< q` with `|p(x) − 1/x| ≤ (2/a)((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q` on `[a, b]`. The polynomial is
`p = (1 − r)/X` for the Chebyshev residual `r = chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the CG error bound). Atlas:
`inverse-polynomial-approx`.
atlas: inverse-polynomial-approx

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul_of_eval_zero_eq_one {p : Polynomial ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) : ∃ s, s.degree < ↑q ∧ 1 - p = Polynomial.X * s
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul_of_eval_zero_eq_one
doc:
**Residual-polynomial factorisation.** If `deg p ≤ q` and `p(0) = 1`, then `1 − p = X s` for
some `s` with `deg s < q`. This is the algebra behind every residual-polynomial Krylov argument:
`x₀ + s(A) r₀ ∈ x₀ + K_q` has error `p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11
(the set `P_q^0`); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35. Promoted from the private CG lemma
`exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul` (atlas `residual-polynomial`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_denominator_ne_zero_of_cross_error_le {a b E : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f)
  (p q : Polynomial ℝ) (hq : q ≠ 0)
  (herror : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, |f x * Polynomial.eval x q - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ E * |Polynomial.eval x q|) :
  ∃ P Q,
    P.degree ≤ p.degree ∧
      Q.degree ≤ q.degree ∧
        q * P = p * Q ∧
          ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b,
            Polynomial.eval x Q ≠ 0 ∧ |f x * Polynomial.eval x Q - Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ E * |Polynomial.eval x Q|
name: NLAlib.exists_denominator_ne_zero_of_cross_error_le
doc:
A uniformly bounded rational limit has an equivalent representation whose denominator
has no zeros in the interval, with degrees no larger and the same cross-multiplied error
bound. Source: operator rederivations, `polybest:rational-limit`; iterative linear-factor
cancellation replaces the multiplicity/unboundedness argument and includes interval endpoints.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_det_add_I_smul_factors.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {H K : Matrix n n ℂ}
  (hH : H.PosDef) (hK : K.IsHermitian) :

name: NLAlib.exists_det_add_I_smul_factors
doc:
Positive Hermitian and arbitrary Hermitian parts admit exact determinant
product formulas after simultaneous congruence. The diagonal parameters also
detect whether the imaginary Hermitian part vanishes. Empty dimension is included.
Source: operator derivations, (S13).
atlas: psd-hermitian-part (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_charpoly {n : ℕ} (d b : Fin n → ℝ) (hd : Monotone d) (hb : Monotone b)
  (hlo : ∀ (i : Fin n), d i ≤ b i) (hhi : ∀ (i j : Fin n), ↑i + 1 = ↑j → b i ≤ d j) :

name: NLAlib.exists_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_charpoly
doc:
Every pair of weakly increasing real lists with positive rank-one
interlacing is realized by a real diagonal matrix plus `vvᵀ`. The target
characteristic polynomial records every multiplicity, including repeated
original and target roots and the empty list. Horn–Johnson 2013,
Theorem 4.3.26; derivations Section herm:converse.
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_charpoly_of_strictMono {n : ℕ} (d b : Fin n → ℝ) (hd : StrictMono d)
  (hb : Monotone b) (hlo : ∀ (i : Fin n), d i ≤ b i) (hhi : ∀ (i j : Fin n), ↑i + 1 = ↑j → b i ≤ d j) :
  ∃ v, (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly = ∏ j, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (b j))
name: NLAlib.exists_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_charpoly_of_strictMono
doc:
Any weakly interlacing target list above a strictly ordered original
list is the exact characteristic spectrum of a positive rank-one update.
Target repetitions and zero updates are allowed, including dimension zero.
Source: Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 4.3;
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_charpoly_with_sum_sq {n : ℕ} (d b : Fin n → ℝ) (hd : Monotone d) (hb : Monotone b)
  (hlo : ∀ (i : Fin n), d i ≤ b i) (hhi : ∀ (i j : Fin n), ↑i + 1 = ↑j → b i ≤ d j) :

name: NLAlib.exists_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_charpoly_with_sum_sq
doc:
The positive rank-one converse realizes the entire weak target spectrum
with the exact squared Euclidean coupling norm equal to the target sum
minus the original sum. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.26;
includes zero coupling, repeated roots and empty dimension.
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_diagonal_congruence_iff_isDiagonalizable_inverse_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAu : IsUnit A) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :

doc:
Two real symmetric matrices with nonsingular first matrix are
simultaneously diagonal under real congruence exactly when their relative

the real-spectrum requirement in real diagonalizability itself.

atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence

signature:
NLAlib.exists_diagonal_congruence_of_isDiagonalizable_inverse_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAu : IsUnit A) (hB : B.IsHermitian)
  (hT : NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable (A⁻¹ * B)) :
  ∃ X a b, IsUnit X ∧ X.transpose * A * X = Matrix.diagonal a ∧ X.transpose * B * X = Matrix.diagonal b
name: NLAlib.exists_diagonal_congruence_of_isDiagonalizable_inverse_mul
doc:

(1992) [`kw92`] for the random-start analysis. The gap-dependent bound of Saad (2011), Thm 6.4,
is `eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le` (`kaniel-paige-saad`).

inverse family on an open slit-plane domain. The global bound includes the

doc:

Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

atlas: cholesky-decomposition

Limits of functions with positive exponential representations on a common
compact interval have a positive representation on that interval. Mass bounds
follow from convergence at zero, rather than being added as hypotheses.
Source: Stahl's compactness reduction; atlas `trace-exponential-stahl` (partial).

Every finite Hermitian pencil has a finite positive representing measure
supported on the direction's exact spectral interval, with the trace-exponential
identity valid for every real parameter. No commutation, simple-spectrum, or
positive-definiteness hypothesis is required. Empty dimension gives the zero
measure through the commuting specialization.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorems 1 and 2, via the planar root-sum proof.
atlas: trace-exponential-stahl

A Hermitian pencil with distinct real diagonal slopes has a positive finite
exponential representing measure on every closed interval containing those
slopes. Density positivity is proved by the planar root-sum argument, and the
atoms and density give the actual measure.

atlas: trace-exponential-stahl (partial)

The real atom-plus-density identity and almost everywhere nonnegativity
of its exact circle density construct a finite positive representing measure.
The underlying measure is displayed explicitly, so no measure-existence or
Laplace-transform conclusion is assumed. Positive exponential parameters here
are equivalent to the Laplace convention by substituting `-t`.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (measure assembly).

doc:

matrix `A : Matrix m n 𝕜` over `ℝ` or `ℂ`, with `m`, `n` arbitrary finite types, is

vectors `A vⱼ / σⱼ` with `σⱼ ≠ 0` are orthonormal and are completed to an orthonormal basis of
`𝕜ᵐ` (atlas `orthonormal-completion`) giving `U`.

`[a, b]` (hypotheses as in `exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono`), then `f^{(q+1)}`
vanishes somewhere in `(a, b)`.

atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:

doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem.** If `f` vanishes at `q + 2` points `v 0 < ⋯ < v (q+1)` of
`[a, b]`, `f` is continuous on `[a, b]` and the derivatives `f', …, f^{(q)}` are continuous on
`(a, b)`, then `f^{(q+1)}(ξ) = 0` for some `ξ ∈ (a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, proof of Thm 6.2; Atkinson,
*An Introduction to Numerical Analysis* (2nd ed.), proof of Thm 3.2.
Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
Deviation: stated with `q + 2` zeros and the `(q + 1)`-st derivative (so the conclusion is in the
open interval without a side condition); only continuity of `f^{(k)}`, `1 ≤ k ≤ q`, on `(a, b)`
is assumed — no differentiability, because `iteratedDeriv` is Mathlib's global derivative and
Rolle (`exists_deriv_eq_zero`) needs only continuity.

signature:

  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues₀ 0)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ 0 → hA.eigenvalues₀ i ∈ Set.Icc a c) {b : n → ℝ} (hb : u ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0)
  (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1),
    u ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x ≤
        NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u b /
          Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_overlapTangentSq_le
doc:
**Angle between the top eigenvector and the Krylov space (Chebyshev bound).** Let `A` be
real symmetric with top eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ₀(A)` and unit eigenvector `u`, and suppose every other
eigenvalue (every sorted position `≠ 0`) lies in `[a, c]` with `a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`,
`c = λ₂`). If `u ⬝ b ≠ 0` then `K_{q+1}(A, b)` contains `x` with `u ⬝ x ≠ 0` and
`tan² ∠(u, x) ≤ tan² ∠(u, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`.
The witness is `x = T_q((2A − (c + a)I)/(c − a)) b`, written through `chebyshevAmplifier`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1 (case `i = 1`); Saad (2003), §6.11.
Deviation: squared tangents; Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`) so that the degree is `q`;
an arbitrary enclosure `[a, c]` of the other eigenvalues instead of `[λₙ, λ₂]`.
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle

    u ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x ≤

                  2 * √((hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - c) / (c - a) + ((hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - c) / (c - a)) ^ 2)) ^
                q) ^

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthogonal_idempotent_canonical.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  ∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
    ∃ t,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
        Antitone t ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
            ∃ H,
              NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols H ∧
                H * H.transpose = 1 ∧ H.transpose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (NLAlib.rectDiag t) 0 0
name: NLAlib.exists_orthogonal_idempotent_canonical
doc:
Every real idempotent is orthogonally similar to `[I diag(t); 0 0]`,
where `t` is nonnegative, decreasing and positive exactly before `g`.
Pairing these `g` range/kernel coordinates displays the direct sum of
`[1 tᵢ; 0 0]`, an identity of size `rank P - g`, and a zero block of size
`card n - rank P - g`. Zero and full rank are included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; derivations §alg:cs.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthogonal_idempotent_canonical_spectrum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

    ∃ t,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
        Antitone t ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
            ∃ H,
              NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols H ∧
                H * H.transpose = 1 ∧
                  H.transpose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (NLAlib.rectDiag t) 0 0 ∧
                    (∀ (i : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues P i = if i < P.rank then √(1 + t i ^ 2) else 0) ∧
                      (∀ (i : ℕ), 1 < NLAlib.singularValues P i ↔ i < g) ∧
                        ∀ i < g, t i = √(NLAlib.singularValues P i ^ 2 - 1)

doc:
The complete orthogonal oblique-projector canonical form, together with
the actual singular spectrum at every natural index. Exactly the first `g`
singular values exceed one, and their blocks have coefficient
`sqrt(σᵢ(P)²-1)`; all other range values are one and all kernel values are zero.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; derivations §alg:cs.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:

Finite-conjugate Schatten duality is attained on arbitrary finite matrix indices:
the witness is the explicit singular-power formula in SVD frames (transported from `Fin`),
and the zero matrix uses the zero witness, covering empty shapes.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

Finite Schatten duality is attained in the full trace pairing over both
real and complex scalars, on every finite rectangular matrix space.

Schatten duality in the left-test orientation used by analytic matrix
interpolation. The tester is an actual matrix with conjugate unit norm bound.

signature:

The elementary radius `1+γ` gives a sign polynomial with error

signature:
NLAlib.exists_similarity_primary_upperTriangular.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
  ∃ d e S T,
    IsUnit S ∧
      (S⁻¹ * A * S).submatrix ⇑e ⇑e = Matrix.blockDiagonal' T ∧
        (∀ (μ : ℂ), (T μ).IsUpperTriangular) ∧ ∀ (μ : ℂ) (i : Fin (d μ)), T μ i i = μ
name: NLAlib.exists_similarity_primary_upperTriangular
doc:
Every complex matrix is similar to the direct sum of single-eigenvalue
upper triangular primary blocks. The block index is the scalar itself;
zero-size blocks are permitted, and the equivalence with the original index
type certifies that only finitely many nonempty blocks occur.
Horn–Johnson (2013), §2.4; empty matrices are included.
atlas: sylvester-equation

signature:
NLAlib.exists_similarity_small_entries_of_triangular_similarity.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

  (htri : ∀ (i j : n), e.symm j < e.symm i → (S⁻¹ * A * S) i j = 0) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ R,
    IsUnit R ∧
      (∀ (i j : n), e.symm j < e.symm i → (R⁻¹ * A * R) i j = 0) ∧
        ∀ (i j : n), e.symm i < e.symm j → ‖(R⁻¹ * A * R) i j‖ < ε
name: NLAlib.exists_similarity_small_entries_of_triangular_similarity
doc:
Any real or complex triangularizing similarity can be refined to make
its strict upper entries arbitrarily small over the same field.
Horn–Johnson (2013), §2.3; this supplies the real small-entry clause whenever
a real triangular form exists.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_similarity_upper_triangular_small_entries.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (e : Fin (Fintype.card n) ≃ n) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ S,
    IsUnit S ∧
      (∀ (i j : n), e.symm j < e.symm i → (S⁻¹ * A * S) i j = 0) ∧

name: NLAlib.exists_similarity_upper_triangular_small_entries
doc:
Every complex matrix has an upper triangular similar matrix whose
strictly upper entries are smaller than any prescribed positive epsilon.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §2.3; arbitrary finite labels are ordered by
the supplied enumeration, and zero-dimensional matrices are included.
atlas: schur-triangularization

signature:
NLAlib.exists_simpleEigenvalueSchurFunction_branch.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (μ a : ℂ)
  (B F : Matrix n n ℂ) (b c : n → ℂ) (hμ : μ ∉ spectrum ℂ B) :
  ∃ ψ,
    ψ 0 = 0 ∧
      ContinuousAt ψ 0 ∧
        HasDerivAt ψ a 0 ∧
          (∀ᶠ (t : ℂ) in nhds 0, NLAlib.simpleEigenvalueSchurFunction μ a B F b c (t, ψ t) = 0) ∧
            ∀ᶠ (p : ℂ × ℂ) in nhds 0, NLAlib.simpleEigenvalueSchurFunction μ a B F b c p = 0 ↔ ψ p.1 = p.2
name: NLAlib.exists_simpleEigenvalueSchurFunction_branch
doc:
The separated scalar Schur equation has a locally unique continuous
differentiable shift branch with derivative equal to its leading perturbation
entry. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.3.12; the parameter may be complex,
which is stronger than the real-parameter conclusion of the source.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_simple_eigenvalue_isolated_similarity.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2}
  [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] {A : Matrix n n K} {x y : n → K} {μ : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0)
  (hAx : A.mulVec x = μ • x) (hyA : Matrix.vecMul y A = μ • y) (hμ : Polynomial.rootMultiplicity μ A.charpoly = 1) :
  ∃ S i,
    IsUnit S ∧
      S.col i = x ∧
        (∀ (j : n), S⁻¹ i j = y j / y ⬝ᵥ x) ∧
          (∀ (j : n), (S⁻¹ * A * S) j i = if j = i then μ else 0) ∧
            (∀ (j : n), (S⁻¹ * A * S) i j = if j = i then μ else 0) ∧
              μ ∉ spectrum K ((S⁻¹ * A * S).submatrix (fun j => ↑j) fun j => ↑j)
name: NLAlib.exists_simple_eigenvalue_isolated_similarity
doc:
A simple eigenvalue admits a left–right normalized isolated similarity,
and the remaining principal block excludes that eigenvalue.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Lemmas 1.4.11 and 6.3.10; the distinguished coordinate
can be relabeled as the first coordinate of the scalar/direct-sum split.
atlas: left-right-eigenvectors (partial), simple-eigenvalue-perturbation (partial)

A common invertible eigenvector basis can put one selected member's

An arbitrary commuting family of real symmetric matrices has one common

signature:
NLAlib.exists_simultaneous_triangular_similarity_iff_unitary.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.exists_simultaneous_triangular_similarity_iff_unitary
doc:
A family is simultaneously triangularizable by an invertible similarity
if and only if it is simultaneously triangularizable by a unitary matrix.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.3.3; arbitrary families are allowed
and no commutation assumption is imposed.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization (partial)

doc:
The equivalence of similarity and unitary simultaneous triangularization
over arbitrary finite labels, with their order supplied by an enumeration.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.3.3; no commutation assumption is used.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization

A commuting normal family's common unitary eigenbasis can put one

signature:
NLAlib.exists_simultaneous_unitary_schur_triangularization.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

doc:
A commuting complex family has a common unitary Schur basis, with each
diagonal giving that member's characteristic roots with multiplicity.

arbitrary finite and empty matrix shapes, and the family may be infinite.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization

signature:
NLAlib.exists_simultaneous_unitary_schur_triangularization_with_charpoly.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : ι → Matrix n n ℂ) (hcomm : Pairwise fun a b => Commute (A a) (A b))
  (order : Fin (Fintype.card n) ≃ n) (a₀ : ι) (d : n → ℂ)
  (hchar : (A a₀).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))) :

    (∀ (a : ι),
        A a = ↑U * T a * (↑U).conjTranspose ∧

doc:
Any complete ordering of a designated member's characteristic roots
can be realized within one simultaneous unitary upper triangularization of
an arbitrary commuting complex family. The same unitary works for every
family member, including an infinite family; every member's diagonal lists
its characteristic roots with multiplicity. Repetitions and empty matrix
dimension are allowed, without normality or diagonalizability assumptions.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.3.3; prescribed-order strengthening in
derivations Section.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_small_real_schur_subspace.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [Nontrivial E] (T : Module.End ℝ E) :
  ∃ p,
    0 < p ∧
      p ≤ 2 ∧
        ∃ P,
          ∃ (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, T x ∈ P),
            ∃ b,
              ∀ (i j : Fin p),

                          (LinearMap.toMatrix b.toBasis b.toBasis) (LinearMap.restrict T hP) i j <
                        0

doc:
Every real endomorphism in positive dimension has an invariant
orthonormal scalar or canonical nonreal Schur block of size at most two.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.3.1; real Schur induction step.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_strong_rank_revealing_qr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ A.rank) (f : ℝ) (hf : 1 ≤ f) :
  ∃ π Q R₁₁ R₁₂ R₂₂,
    NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧
      Q * Q.transpose = 1 ∧
        IsUnit R₁₁ ∧
          R₁₁.IsUpperTriangular ∧
            NLAlib.IsUpperTrapezoidal R₂₂ ∧
              A.submatrix id ⇑π = Q * Matrix.fromBlocks R₁₁ R₁₂ 0 R₂₂ ∧
                (∀ i < k,
                    NLAlib.singularValues A i / √(1 + f ^ 2 * ↑k * (↑(Fintype.card n) - ↑k)) ≤
                      NLAlib.singularValues R₁₁ i) ∧
                  (∀ (j : ℕ),
                      NLAlib.singularValues R₂₂ j ≤
                        NLAlib.singularValues A (k + j) * √(1 + f ^ 2 * ↑k * (↑(Fintype.card n) - ↑k))) ∧
                    (∀ (i : Fin k) (j : Fin (Fintype.card n - k)), |(R₁₁⁻¹ * R₁₂) i j| ≤ f) ∧ (k = A.rank → R₂₂ = 0)
name: NLAlib.exists_strong_rank_revealing_qr
doc:
Strong rank-revealing QR exists with the exact constants
`sqrt(1 + f² k(n-k))` and interpolation bound `f`, for every `f ≥ 1`.
The column equivalence is a reordering of all input columns; the
full orthogonal factor has both Gram identities; the leading block is
invertible and upper triangular and the trailing block is upper trapezoidal.
Every leading and every zero-padded trailing singular value is controlled.

The necessary source repair is `k ≤ rank A`, since an ordinary leading
inverse is required. This theorem allows all such `k`, so applying it with
`k = rank A` proves the rank-adapted replacement when a requested rank is
too large; its last clause gives an exactly zero residual. At rank zero the
leading inverse is the valid empty inverse and the factorization reconstructs
the zero matrix. Gu–Eisenstat 1996, Theorem 3.2; Martinsson–Tropp 2020,
Section 13.2; derivations §alg:rrqr, maximum-volume proof.
atlas: rank-revealing-qr

Source: finite multiplicity Rolle argument in operator derivations (AQ4), (AQ9)–(AQ11).
The evaluation point is assumed off the nodal roots; node values are exact separately.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b x : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ} (hab : a < b)
  (hv : Function.Injective v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 1)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo a b)) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b,
    f x - Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ v) (f ∘ v)) =
      iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ / ↑(q + 1).factorial * Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ v)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq
doc:
**Interpolation remainder formula.** Let `v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ` be distinct nodes in
`[a, b]`, `f` continuous on `[a, b]` with `f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(a, b)`, and
`x ∈ [a, b]`. Then for the interpolating polynomial `L = Lagrange.interpolate univ v (f ∘ v)`
and the nodal polynomial `ω = ∏ (X − v i)` there is `ξ ∈ (a, b)` with
`f x − L(x) = f^{(q+1)}(ξ) / (q + 1)! · ω(x)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, Thm 6.2; Atkinson (2nd ed.),
Thm 3.2; Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas:
`interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: `ξ` is in the open interval `(a, b)` (stronger than `[a, b]`), at the cost of the
hypothesis `a < b` (used only when `x` is a node).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

[`tb97`], Lect. 35. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial: forward direction).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  ∃ r U₁ U₂ V₁ V₂ S₂,
    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧ V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0 ∧ NLAlib.frobSq S₂ = NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq A k
name: NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks
doc:
Every real matrix has an SVD-derived right-space block split whose
tail is the optimal squared rank-`k` error. The head singular values
are absorbed into `U₁=A V₁`, as permitted by HMT's structural lemma.
Only `k≤n` is needed; `k>m` is handled by the padded zero singular values.
HMT 2011, Theorem 9.1; atlas `rsvd-expected-error`, `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks_specNorm {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  ∃ r U₁ U₂ V₁ V₂ S₂,
    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧
            V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0 ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm S₂ = NLAlib.singularValues A k ∧ NLAlib.frobSq S₂ = NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq A k
name: NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks_specNorm
doc:
**SVD right blocks with spectral tail.** For `k ≤ n` every real `A` splits as
`A = U₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ` with `U₂`, `V₁`, `V₂` orthonormal, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`, `‖Σ₂‖ = σ_{k+1}` and
`‖Σ₂‖_F² = ∑_{j>k} σ_j²` (zero-indexed `singularValues A k`, `bestRankFrobSq A k`). The
blocks are those of `exists_svd_right_blocks` (`U₁ = AV₁`, `U₂ = U`), with the spectral tail
identified through `IsSVD.specNorm_sub_truncatedMatrix`. HMT 2011, §2.1 and Thm 9.1.
Atlas `rsvd-spectral-expected` (helper; uses `svd`, `eckart-young`; belongs in
`Matrix/SvdBlocks.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_tail_mem_of_mem_powersetCard_succ {n k : ℕ} {T : Finset (Fin n)}

name: NLAlib.exists_tail_mem_of_mem_powersetCard_succ
doc:
Every size-`k+1` subset of zero-indexed finite labels contains a label at least
`k`. Source: manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`, the finite tail-index argument.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_tendsto_sum_sin_odd_div (φ : ℝ) (hφ : Real.sin φ ≠ 0) :

doc:
The odd sine harmonic series converges in its ordinary partial-sum order away from zero.
Source: Dirichlet's test; helper for `chebyshev-series-abs-sign`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_threshold_of_weight_order.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (a p : ι → ℝ) (hp0 : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ p i)

A scalar threshold separates occupied and vacant weights whenever every
occupied/vacant pair is weakly ordered. Schur–Horn variational rederivation,

Every positive-dimensional circulant is an ordinary Toeplitz matrix;

signature:

The bottom eigenvectors attain the bottom eigenvalue sum. Fan (1949), the

**Ky Fan maximum principle, attainment.** The top `k` eigenvectors form an orthonormal
frame whose compression trace is the sum of the `k` largest eigenvalues, for every

atlas: ky-fan-maximum-principle

signature:

doc:
A word containing a marked factor has the same trace as a nonempty
cyclic product of powers followed by marked factors. The exponents sum
to its number of unmarked factors.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_trace_twoSided_compression_eq_kyFanNorm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

doc:
Top singular frames attain the Ky Fan singular-value sum on arbitrary finite
row and column types, for every admissible prefix including zero and full prefixes.
Fan (1949), Theorem 1; Horn–Johnson (1991), Theorem 3.4.1.
atlas: ky-fan-maximum-principle (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_transpose_mul_apply_succ_zero_eq_zero {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.exists_transpose_mul_apply_succ_zero_eq_zero
doc:
For every `A : (m+1) × (n+1)` there is an orthogonal `W` with `WᵀA` zero below the pivot in
its first column: `W` completes `a₀ / ‖a₀‖` to an orthonormal basis
(`exists_unitary_completion`), or `W = I` when `a₀ = 0`. The reflector-free form of one
Householder step. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.2.

signature:

doc:
The actual arc and its actual first derivative admit global uniform
bounds. The constants are constructed from the native coefficient maps and

signature:
NLAlib.exists_uniform_matrixKResolvent_defect_bound_below_trace_support.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

Below the actual normalized-trace law, every sample in the true

positive test and supportwise bound are constructed from the original

assumed.
Source: Montanari--Saeed (2026), Theorem 3, real-gap converse.
atlas: block-wishart-variational-edges (partial)

Every continuous real function has a unique best pole-free rational approximant of

A smallest singular vector attains the unit-sphere minimum, including
singular matrices.

A singular second pencil map gives unit domain and image vectors with
its image zero and the first map's image on the chosen image line.

If the leading principal blocks of orders one through the rank are

signature:

Every square complex contraction is an average of two unitary matrices,
with no invertibility assumption. Tropp (2022), Proposition 12.24.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_congruence_diagonal_of_commute.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

A commuting Hermitian pair has one orthonormal eigenvector matrix,
and both diagonal lists are real. Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.5.5.

Every complex normal matrix is unitarily diagonalizable.

NLAlib.exists_unitary_diagonalization_of_normal_with_charpoly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
A normal matrix can be unitarily diagonalized in any prescribed complete
characteristic eigenvalue order. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.5.3;

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  ∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
    ∃ t,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
        Antitone t ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
            ∃ H,
              H.conjTranspose * H = 1 ∧
                H * H.conjTranspose = 1 ∧
                  H.conjTranspose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 ((NLAlib.rectDiag t).map Complex.ofReal) 0 0
name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical
doc:
Every complex idempotent is unitarily similar to the complexification
of `[I diag(t);0 0]`, where `t` is nonnegative, decreasing, and positive
exactly on the first `g` coordinates. These are the actual canonical
oblique planes `[1 tᵢ;0 0]`, with all remaining ones and zeros included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; zero and full rank are allowed.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical_spectrum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  ∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
    ∃ t,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
        Antitone t ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
            ∃ H,
              H.conjTranspose * H = 1 ∧
                H * H.conjTranspose = 1 ∧
                  H.conjTranspose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 ((NLAlib.rectDiag t).map ⇑Complex.ofRealHom) 0 0 ∧
                    (∀ (i : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues P i = if i < P.rank then √(1 + t i ^ 2) else 0) ∧
                      (∀ (i : ℕ), 1 < NLAlib.singularValues P i ↔ i < g) ∧
                        ∀ i < g, t i = √(NLAlib.singularValues P i ^ 2 - 1)
name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical_spectrum
doc:
Every complex idempotent has its full unitary oblique canonical form,
and the actual singular values are `sqrt(1+tᵢ²)` on the range and zero
after the rank. Exactly the first `g` values exceed one, with canonical
coefficient `sqrt(σᵢ²-1)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3;
all rank endpoints and the empty matrix are included.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_range_blocks.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :

name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_range_blocks
doc:
Complex orthonormal coordinates adapted to an idempotent's actual
range give the exact block form `[I T; 0 0]`, with identity size equal to
its actual rank. Both coordinate Gram identities are supplied.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; includes rank zero, full rank and
empty dimension.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_mul_eq_of_gram_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_mul_eq_of_gram_eq
doc:
Two complex matrices of the same shape and with equal Gram matrices
differ by an ambient left unitary factor. Singular and empty matrices are
included. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.1; complex CS completion helper.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_qz_triangularization.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix n n ℂ)

doc:
Every complex square pencil admits a simultaneous two-sided unitary
upper triangular form. The common row and column order may be any enumeration
of the finite labels. Singular and identically singular pencils, common zero
images and the empty pencil are included. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.6.1, Theorem.
atlas: schur-triangularization

Complex QZ in the usual finite-coordinate upper triangular notation,
including empty and singular pencils. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.6.1.
atlas: schur-triangularization (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_right_block_of_first_columns_eq.{u_1, u_2} {p : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} [Fintype p] [Fintype q]

atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

NLAlib.exists_unitary_similarity_iff_charpoly_eq_of_normal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_sum_completion.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}

oblique-projector part of `cs-decomposition`.

NLAlib.expErr_le_frobConditionNumber.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

The Kaczmarz recurrence has the advertised condition-number contraction
under the necessary full-column-rank hypothesis.

signature: NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient (r : ℝ) : ℝ

remainder. Its definition includes the zero parameter without division.

the integral definition supplies its removable value at zero.

signature:
NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient_le_div {r : ℝ} (hr : r < 3) :

Bernstein's scalar exponential bound controls the exact integral
remainder coefficient up to the pole at three, including the zero parameter.
Source: Tropp (2015), Lemma 6.6.2; Tropp (2026), Section 4.9.

signature: NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient_nonneg (r : ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient r
name: NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient_nonneg

signature: NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient_zero : NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient 0 = 1 / 2
name: NLAlib.expSecondRemainderCoefficient_zero
doc:
At the zero parameter the continuous exponential remainder coefficient
is one half.

recover the quadratic MGF behavior of a centered variable from an Orlicz exponential moment.
Atlas `subgaussian-def`, `bernstein-scalar` (analytic helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exp_mul_lambdaMax_lambdaMin_le_traceExp_smul.{u_2} {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] [Nonempty d]
  (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (θ : ℝ) :

    (0 < θ → Real.exp (θ * NLAlib.lambdaMax A) ≤ NLAlib.traceExp (θ • A)) ∧
      (θ < 0 → Real.exp (θ * NLAlib.lambdaMin A) ≤ NLAlib.traceExp (θ • A))
name: NLAlib.exp_mul_lambdaMax_lambdaMin_le_traceExp_smul
doc:
`traceExp (θ • A)` is nonnegative and dominates `exp (θ λmax A)` for `θ > 0` and `exp (θ λmin A)`
for `θ < 0`.

Tropp 2015, §3.2, eq. (3.2.3). Atlas: `matrix-laplace`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 3*.

signature:
NLAlib.exp_mul_le_one_add_mul_add_sq_mul_of_le {L θ x : ℝ} (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθL : θ * L < 3) (hx : x ≤ L) :

doc:
The scalar one-sided Bernstein exponential bound, permitting arbitrarily negative
`x ≤ L`: `exp(θx) ≤ 1+θx+((θ²/2)/(1-θL/3))x²`.
Source: Tropp 2015, Lemma 6.6.2; scalar Taylor comparison in operator rederivations
`eq:scalarbernstein`. Reused by `matrix-bernstein` and `matrix-freedman` (partial).

A global quadratic upper bound for the negative exponential on the nonnegative half-line:

Atlas `hanson-wright` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exp_neg_mul_tsum_pow_div_factorial_nat_add_le {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ) (t : ℕ) (ht : Real.exp 2 * ℓ ≤ ↑t) :

The exact value error of the explicit denominator is its smoothing-kernel
integral of the finite Laguerre residual. Source: the focused reciprocal reroute.

signature:

NLAlib.fderiv_eval_interpolationGapPolynomial_node_apply {n : ℕ} {t : Fin n → ℝ} (ht : t ∈ NLAlib.interiorNodeSimplex n)
  (i : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 2)) (h : Fin n → ℝ) :

        t)
      h =
    -Polynomial.eval (NLAlib.canonicalIntervalNodes n t j)
          (Polynomial.derivative (NLAlib.interpolationGapPolynomial n t i)) *

name: NLAlib.fderiv_eval_interpolationGapPolynomial_node_apply
doc:
Differentiating the actual fixed nodal equations gives the corresponding
node functional derivative of the gap polynomial.
Source: the chain rule applied to the nodal interpolation equations;
focused reroutes, peak Jacobian.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_fderiv_normalizedTrace_mixed_resolvent_coordinate_cyclic_apply.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d]
  [DecidableEq d] (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (ζ ω : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0) (hω : ω.im ≠ 0) (a b : ℕ)
  (y h k : d × d ⊕ d × d → ℝ) :
  ((fderiv ℝ
          (fderiv ℝ fun x =>
            NLAlib.normalizedTrace
              (resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates x) ζ ^ a *
                resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates x) ω ^ b))
          y)
        k)
      h =
    ↑a •
        NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y)
          (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates h) (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates k) ζ ω (a + 1) b +
      ↑b •
        NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y)
          (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates h) (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates k) ζ ω a (b + 1)
name: NLAlib.fderiv_fderiv_normalizedTrace_mixed_resolvent_coordinate_cyclic_apply
doc:
The true second coordinate derivative is the cyclic two-arc Hessian.
The formula is obtained by differentiating the actual first gradient, so it
does not assume any Hessian or twice-insertion identity.
Source: arXiv:2108.06312v2, Lemma 6.2.
atlas: gaussian-free-spectrum-two-sided (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_fderiv_rationalMatrixEval_apply.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (P Q : Polynomial 𝕜) (A G H : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hA : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval A) Q)) :
  ((fderiv 𝕜 (fun B => fderiv 𝕜 (NLAlib.rationalMatrixEval P Q) B) A) G) H =
    NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference P Q A A A G H + NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference P Q A A A H G
name: NLAlib.fderiv_fderiv_rationalMatrixEval_apply
doc:
The actual second Fréchet derivative is the sum of the two ordered
second block differences. Source: F19.
atlas: matrix-function-block-divided-differences (partial)

name: NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFiniteMixedArc_apply
doc:
Exact positive-arc insertion formula for the genuine native mixed arc's
coordinate derivative. Inserted coefficients need not commute with the
resolvents; zero arc exponents simply contribute empty sums.
Source: arXiv:2108.06312v2, Lemma 6.3.
atlas: gaussian-free-spectrum-two-sided (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFiniteMixedArc_single_eq_sum_split.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2}
  {d : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [Fintype n] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq d] (A₀ : Matrix d d ℂ)
  (hA₀ : A₀.IsHermitian) (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : ∀ (i : ι), (A i).IsHermitian) (q : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0)
  (a b : ℕ) (x : NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n → ℝ) (k : NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n) :
  (fderiv ℝ (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteMixedArc A₀ A q ζ a b) x) (Pi.single k 1) =
    ∑ j,
      NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteMixedArc A₀ A q ζ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitLeft a b j).1
            (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitLeft a b j).2 x *
          NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient A q k *
        NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteMixedArc A₀ A q ζ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitRight a b j).1
          (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitRight a b j).2 x
name: NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFiniteMixedArc_single_eq_sum_split
doc:
A genuine native mixed arc's single-coordinate derivative is the exact
finite sum of two positive native arcs with the actual coefficient between
them. No direction commutation or derivative identity is assumed.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFinitePartialTraceResolventEntry_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2}
  {d : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [Fintype n] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq d] (A₀ : Matrix d d ℂ)
  (hA₀ : A₀.IsHermitian) (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : ∀ (i : ι), (A i).IsHermitian) (q : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0)
  (a b : d) (x h : NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n → ℝ) :
  (fderiv ℝ (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFinitePartialTraceResolventEntry A₀ A q ζ a b) x) h =
    NLAlib.normalizedPartialTrace
      ((resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x) ζ *
          ∑ k, h k • NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient A q k) *
        resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x) ζ)
      a b
name: NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFinitePartialTraceResolventEntry_apply
doc:
The genuine partial-trace resolvent derivative is the actual native
single-insertion resolvent sandwich. Every coordinate direction uses the
true finite-N coefficient matrices of the existing Gaussian realization.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFiniteResolvent_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype ι]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq d] (A₀ : Matrix d d ℂ) (hA₀ : A₀.IsHermitian)
  (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : ∀ (i : ι), (A i).IsHermitian) (q : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0)
  (x h : NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n → ℝ) :
  (fderiv ℝ (fun y => resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q y) ζ) x) h =
    (resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x) ζ *
        ∑ k, h k • NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient A q k) *
      resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x) ζ
name: NLAlib.fderiv_gaussianFreeFiniteResolvent_apply
doc:
The actual coordinate derivative of the genuine affine finite-N
resolvent is the literal native single-insertion sandwich.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_hermitianCoordinateResolventWord_apply.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : ℕ}
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (w : Fin m → ℂ × Matrix n n ℂ) (hw : ∀ (i : Fin m), (w i).1.im ≠ 0)
  (y h : n × n ⊕ n × n → ℝ) :
  (fderiv ℝ (NLAlib.hermitianCoordinateResolventWord A w) y) h =
    ∑ i,
      NLAlib.hermitianCoordinateResolventWord A
        (NLAlib.resolventWordInsert w i (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates h)) y
name: NLAlib.fderiv_hermitianCoordinateResolventWord_apply
doc:
The real derivative of an actual inverse word is the sum of its genuine
ordered insertions. No derivative identity is assumed as a hypothesis.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_matrixExp_apply.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A E : Matrix n n 𝕜) :
  (fderiv 𝕜 NLAlib.matrixExp A) E = ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..1, NLAlib.matrixExp ((1 - s) • A) * E * NLAlib.matrixExp (s • A)
name: NLAlib.fderiv_matrixExp_apply
doc:
The full Fréchet derivative of the matrix exponential is the
noncommutative insertion integral. Both real and complex matrices and
empty dimensions are covered.
atlas: matrix-exponential-frechet-integral

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_normalizedTrace_mixed_resolvent_coordinate_cyclic_apply.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
  (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (ζ ω : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0) (hω : ω.im ≠ 0) (a b : ℕ)
  (y h : d × d ⊕ d × d → ℝ) :
  (fderiv ℝ
        (fun x =>
          NLAlib.normalizedTrace
            (resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates x) ζ ^ a *
              resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates x) ω ^ b))
        y)
      h =
    ↑a •
        NLAlib.normalizedTrace
          (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates h *
              resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) ζ ^ (a + 1) *
            resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) ω ^ b) +
      ↑b •
        NLAlib.normalizedTrace
          (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates h *
              resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) ζ ^ a *
            resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) ω ^ (b + 1))
name: NLAlib.fderiv_normalizedTrace_mixed_resolvent_coordinate_cyclic_apply
doc:
The actual directional first derivative in Hermitian coordinates is the
two-term cyclic formula, with no commutation assumption on the direction.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_rationalMatrixEval_apply.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (P Q : Polynomial 𝕜) (A H : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hA : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval A) Q)) :
  (fderiv 𝕜 (NLAlib.rationalMatrixEval P Q) A) H = NLAlib.rationalBlockDifference P Q A A H

doc:
Applying the actual first Fréchet derivative gives the triangular block
difference. Source: F19.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_resolvent_sq_apply.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (ζ : ℂ) (A H : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0) :
  (fderiv ℂ (fun B => resolvent B ζ ^ 2) A) H = NLAlib.resolventSquareDifference ζ A A H

Applying the squared resolvent derivative gives exactly the two ordered

name: NLAlib.fderiv_sineTruncation_comp
doc:
The derivative multiplier of the smooth truncation has absolute value
at most one. Source: Mathlib's `HasFDerivAt.sin`.
Atlas: `gaussian-log-sobolev`.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_sub_sub_smul_iteratedFDeriv_two_normalizedTrace_mixed_eq_kernel.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (ζ : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0) (p : ℕ) (x D V : n × n ⊕ n × n → ℝ)
  (a : ℝ) :
  have Φ := fun y =>
    NLAlib.normalizedTrace
      (resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) ζ ^ p *
        resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) (star ζ) ^ p);
  (fderiv ℝ Φ (x + a • D) - fderiv ℝ Φ x) D - a • (iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 Φ (x - a • V)) ![D, D] =
    a ^ 2 • NLAlib.resolventMomentTaylorKernel A ζ p a x D V
name: NLAlib.fderiv_sub_sub_smul_iteratedFDeriv_two_normalizedTrace_mixed_eq_kernel
doc: Exact actual gradient/Hessian cancellation in terms of its native kernel.

signature:
NLAlib.fderiv_sub_sub_smul_iteratedFDeriv_two_normalizedTrace_mixed_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (ζ : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0) (p : ℕ) (x D V : n × n ⊕ n × n → ℝ)
  (a : ℝ) :
  have Φ := fun y =>
    NLAlib.normalizedTrace
      (resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) ζ ^ p *
        resolvent (A + NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates y) (star ζ) ^ p);
  (fderiv ℝ Φ (x + a • D) - fderiv ℝ Φ x) D - a • (iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 Φ (x - a • V)) ![D, D] =
    a ^ 2 •
      ∫ (u : ℝ) (v : ℝ) in 0..1,
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j,
            ∑ k,
              NLAlib.normalizedTrace
                (NLAlib.hermitianCoordinateResolventWord A
                  (NLAlib.resolventWordInsert
                    (NLAlib.resolventWordInsert
                      (NLAlib.resolventWordInsert (NLAlib.mixedResolventWord ζ p) i
                        (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates D))
                      j (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates D))
                    k (NLAlib.hermitianMatrixFromRealCoordinates (V + u • D)))
                  (x - a • V + v • a • (V + u • D)))
name: NLAlib.fderiv_sub_sub_smul_iteratedFDeriv_two_normalizedTrace_mixed_eq_sum
doc:
The actual primitive's Taylor cancellation is the exact finite sum of
literal ordered inverse words, with the unnormalized a² coefficient.

signature: NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean
doc:
The Cesàro mean of the first `n+1` genuine Chebyshev truncations.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 6.6.

signature: NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean_const (c : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean (fun x => c) n = Polynomial.C c
name: NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean_const
doc:
Fejér means preserve every constant function, so the contraction bound has norm exactly one.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 6.6.
atlas: fejer-chebyshev-means (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean_eq_sum_smul_T (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean f n =
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      (1 - ↑k / (↑n + 1)) • (Polynomial.C (NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k) * Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k)
name: NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean_eq_sum_smul_T
doc:
The genuine Cesàro mean has the triangular Chebyshev coefficient weights
`1-k/(n+1)`, including the constant coefficient with weight one.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Exercise 6.6; the finite Cesàro sum.
atlas: fejer-chebyshev-means (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean_sub {f g : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (n : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean (fun x => f x - g x) n = NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean f n - NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean g n
name: NLAlib.fejerChebyshevMean_sub
doc:
Fejér means preserve subtraction of continuous functions.
Source: finite Chebyshev coefficient linearity; helper for `fejer-chebyshev-means`.

signature: NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel (n : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel
doc:
The normalized nonnegative Fejér kernel is the squared finite character sum.
Source: Fejér's finite kernel identity, ATAP Exercise 6.6.

signature:
NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel_eq_avg_dirichlet (n : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel n t = (↑n + 1)⁻¹ * ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), NLAlib.dirichletCircleKernel m t
name: NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel_eq_avg_dirichlet
doc:
The positive Fejér kernel is the average of the finite Dirichlet kernels.
Source: Fejér's finite kernel identity, ATAP Exercise 6.6.

signature: NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel_nonneg (n : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel n t
name: NLAlib.fejerCircleKernel_nonneg
doc:
The Fejér kernel is nonnegative at every circle argument.
Source: Fejér's squared-norm formula, ATAP Exercise 6.6.

signature: NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse (ρ : ℝ) : Set ℂ
name: NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse
doc:
The filled Bernstein ellipse is the Joukowski image of the closed annulus
`1≤|w|≤ρ`. For `ρ>1` this has semiaxes `(ρ+ρ⁻¹)/2` and `(ρ-ρ⁻¹)/2`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8; used by `bernstein-ellipse-approx` and
`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`.

signature:
NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse_subset_openBernsteinEllipse {r ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ) (hrρ : r < ρ) :
  NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse r ⊆ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ
name: NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse_subset_openBernsteinEllipse
doc:
Every strictly smaller closed Bernstein ellipse lies inside the larger open ellipse.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, radius-limit proof of Theorem 8.1
(`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs {κ : ℕ} [Nonempty (Fin κ)] (s : Fin κ → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs

The smallest absolute leading polynomial value. Source: manuscript `sa:filter`,
its `c_phi`. A positive-dimensional leading block makes the minimum nonempty.

NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs_le {κ : ℕ} [Nonempty (Fin κ)] (s : Fin κ → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (i : Fin κ) :

The leading filter minimum bounds each leading filter value from below.

The largest absolute filtered singular tail entry, with value zero for an empty
tail. Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, its `t_phi`; zero-padded singular values are allowed.

name: NLAlib.finLobattoSchurBorder_bounds_and_endpoints

The actual finite indexed Lobatto Schur border lies in the endpoint interval and
has both designated endpoint eigenvalues. Source: focused reroutes, Section 3 (BL9).

Isolate a chosen finite coordinate as the first singleton summand,
with every remaining coordinate in its original increasing order.

The singled-out coordinate of `finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv` is the chosen

The remaining coordinates of `finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv` are exactly

signature:
NLAlib.finRadauSchurBorders_bounds_and_endpoints {q : ℕ} (J : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ) (v : Fin q → ℝ) (d a c : ℝ)
  (hJa : (J - a • 1).PosDef) (hJc : (c • 1 - J).PosDef) (hMa : (NLAlib.symmetricBorder J v d - a • 1).PosSemidef)

The actual finite indexed Radau matrices retain the endpoint spectrum and

NLAlib.finSymmetricBorder_last_castSucc {q : ℕ} (J : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ) (v : Fin q → ℝ) (d : ℝ) (i : Fin q) :

  NLAlib.finiteMomentUpdate ν R u p ≤ 2 * ↑p * x ^ (2 * p - 1) * (↑q * ν / (x - 2 * ↑q * R))

NLAlib.forall_exists_mem_spectrum_dist_le_of_resolvent_error_bounds.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

  (ξ : ℝ) : ξ ∈ spectrum ℝ A → ∃ β ∈ spectrum ℝ B, dist ξ β ≤ 2 * C * η

name: NLAlib.forwardSubst
doc:
**Forward substitution** for `L x = b`, as a total recursion on the leading pivot:
`x₀ = b₀ / L₀₀`, then solve the trailing system with right-hand side `b_{1:} − L_{1:,0} x₀`.
For a lower triangular `L` with nonzero diagonal this is the textbook loop
`xᵢ = (bᵢ − ∑_{j<i} Lᵢⱼ xⱼ) / Lᵢᵢ`; a zero pivot gives junk (`x / 0 = 0`), never an error.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.1.1 (column-oriented form); Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 17.
atlas: triangular-matrices-def

signature:

  NLAlib.frobInner A P ≤ NLAlib.kyFanNorm A k

A spectral contraction of rank at most `k` pairs with a matrix at most its Ky Fan `k`

NLAlib.frobInner_le_nuclearNorm_of_specNorm_le_one.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

signature:
NLAlib.frobInner_le_sqrt_mul_frobNorm_mul_specNorm_of_rank_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {r : ℕ} (X E : Matrix m n ℝ) (hX : X.rank ≤ r) :
  NLAlib.frobInner X E ≤ √↑r * NLAlib.frobNorm X * NLAlib.specNorm E
name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_sqrt_mul_frobNorm_mul_specNorm_of_rank_le
doc:
**Rank corollary of the von Neumann trace inequality.** If `rank X ≤ r` then
`⟨X, E⟩_F ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`. Proof: with the orthogonal projector `P = X X⁺` onto `range X`,
`⟨X, E⟩_F = ⟨X, P E⟩_F ≤ ‖X‖_F ‖P E‖_F ≤ ‖X‖_F √(rank P E) ‖P E‖₂ ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`.
It follows from Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.1.1 (von Neumann) and Cauchy–Schwarz over the top
`r` singular values; this is the `VonNeumannRankBound` hypothesis of the Chen–Persson LRA
formalization. Atlas `von-neumann-trace` (rank corollary); arbitrary finite index types, no
full-rank or nonemptiness condition.
atlas: von-neumann-rank-bound

signature:
NLAlib.frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (X E : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.frobInner X E ≤
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min (Fintype.card m) (Fintype.card n)), NLAlib.singularValues X k * NLAlib.singularValues E k
name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul
doc:
**Von Neumann trace inequality.** For real matrices,
`⟨X, E⟩_F = tr(XᵀE) ≤ ∑_{k < min (card m) (card n)} σ_k(X) σ_k(E)`. Horn–Johnson 2013,
Thm 7.4.1.1 (real case, `Re tr(X E*) = frobInner X E`); Mirsky 1975. Proof: Ky Fan's maximum
principle for the diagonal of `UᵀEV` (through the weighted top-`k` inequality
`sum_mul_le_sum_ite_lt_of_antitone`) and Abel summation over `σ(X)`; no Birkhoff theorem is
needed. Stated over `ℝ` because the singular-value invariances `singularValues_isometry_mul`,
`singularValues_mul_unitary` are real.
atlas: von-neumann-trace

    NLAlib.frobSq (Q * Z * P) + NLAlib.frobSq (Q * Z * (1 - P)) + NLAlib.frobSq ((1 - Q) * Z * P) +
      NLAlib.frobSq ((1 - Q) * Z * (1 - P))

doc:

§III.3; no rank or nonempty-dimension condition is needed.

Atlas `projection-facts`.

doc:
`Q(QᴴA)` is the best Frobenius approximation of `A` with columns in `range Q`:
`‖(I − QQᴴ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖A − QB‖_F²` for every `B`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_of_eq_mul

Monotonicity of the residual under range inclusion (HMT 2011, Prop. 8.5, Frobenius case):
if `range Q₁ ⊆ range Q₂`, written `Q₁ = Q₂ C`, then `‖(I − Q₂Q₂ᴴ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖(I − Q₁Q₁ᴴ)A‖_F²`.
Deviation: only `Q₂` needs orthonormal columns; `Q₁` is arbitrary (with `residual` defined
by the formula `A − Q₁Q₁ᴴA`). Atlas `projection-facts`.
atlas: projection-facts

name: NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset
doc:
**Deterministic range-finder bound, Frobenius form** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.1, squared Frobenius
case): if `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖Σ₂‖_F² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²`.
Chen–Persson, Prop. `prop:hmt-struct`, second inequality (LRA `hmt_second_frob`).

Deviations from the printed statement: the SVD is a block decomposition with only the
hypotheses the proof uses (`U₂ᵀU₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality,
no conditions on `U₁`); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`
(HMT take `range Q = range(AΩ)`); index types are arbitrary `Fintype`s. Atlas
`hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

signature:

doc:
**Gamma-ratio estimate.** For `1 ≤ r ≤ k`,
`2^{(k-r-1)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(r/2) Γ(k-r+1)) ≤ ((k+r)/2)^{(k-r+1)/2} / (2 Γ(k-r+1))`,
i.e. the constant of the density bound (B.5) is at most the constant of (B.6).

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.6). Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper). Proof: iterated Gautschi
inequality (log-convexity of `Γ`, Bohr–Mollerup) and AM–GM (`prod_range_add_le_pow`). Ported
from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.tw_gamma_ratio_bound`.
atlas: wishart-lambda-min-tail

signature:

name: NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le
doc:
The endpoint quadratic-probe constant for an `r × k` Gaussian matrix
is bounded by the strengthened inverse spectral moment constant.
Source: direct quadratic-probe proof, endpoint moment calculation; the
arithmetic-progression mean retains `k+r-1`. Atlas:
`inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gauss_lebesgue_quadrature_of_orthogonal_nodal.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {n : ℕ}
  (hcard : Fintype.card ι = n + 1) (v : ι → ℝ) (hv : Function.Injective v) (hvI : ∀ (i : ι), v i ∈ Set.Ioo (-1) 1)
  (horth :
    ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      p.degree < ↑(Fintype.card ι) →
        ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ v) * Polynomial.eval x p = 0) :
  (∀ (i : ι), 0 < ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ v i)) ∧
    ∑ i, ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ v i) = 2 ∧
      (∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
          p.degree ≤ ↑(2 * n + 1) →
            ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x p =
              ∑ i, (∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ v i)) * Polynomial.eval (v i) p) ∧
        ∃ σ,
          (∀ (i : ι), v (σ i) = -v i) ∧
            ∀ (i : ι),
              ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ v (σ i)) =
                ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ v i)

doc:
The actual integrated cardinal rule at `(n+1)` interior orthogonal nodes has
positive weights, mass two, exact degree `2n+1`, and paired equal weights.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 19.1 and 19.4.

signature:
NLAlib.gauss_quadrature_of_orthogonal_nodal.{u_1} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {a b : ℝ} (hμ : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂μ, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty)
  (v : ι → ℝ) (hv : Set.InjOn v ↑s)
  (horth :
    ∀ (q : Polynomial ℝ),
      q.degree < ↑s.card → ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal s v) * Polynomial.eval x q ∂μ = 0)
  (hsupport : ∃ u, Set.InjOn u ↑s ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, u i ∈ μ.support) :
  (∀ i ∈ s, 0 < ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis s v i) ∂μ) ∧
    ∑ i ∈ s, ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis s v i) ∂μ = (μ Set.univ).toReal ∧
      ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
        p.degree < ↑(2 * s.card) →
          ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x p ∂μ =

mass, and exactness through degree `2N−1`. The supplied distinct nodes are defined
by their monic nodal polynomial's orthogonality to all degrees below `N`. The measure

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation_eq_diagonal_add_gue.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3}
  [Fintype ι] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A₀ : Matrix d d ℂ) (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (q : ℝ)
  (x : NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x =
    Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) A₀ 1 +
        √q • ∑ i, Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) (Matrix.diagonal fun a => ↑(x (Sum.inl (i, a)))) +
      √(1 - q) •
        ∑ i, Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) (NLAlib.gueMatrix (fun k => x (Sum.inr (i, k))) ())
name: NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation_eq_diagonal_add_gue
doc:
The canonical coordinate-series realization is literally the source
diagonal-Gaussian/GUE interpolation formula. The GUE families use disjoint
coordinate blocks for different coefficient indices.

`3/(k-r+1)` (`integrable_and_integral_rpow_inv_sum_sq_gaussianReal_lt`, atlas
`chi-square-neg-moment`); Minkowski's inequality bounds `‖tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_{L^q}` and Markov's
inequality gives the tail. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.pinv_frobenius_tail`.

name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_one_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_eq

`G` (`k ≥ 1`) and `t ≥ 0`, `σ_min(Gᵀ)² = ‖G‖² ∼ χ²_k`, and
`P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] = ∫₀ᵗ c(1,k) x^{(k-2)/2} e^{-x/2} dx` with
`c(1,k) = 2^{(k-2)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(1/2) Γ(k))` (`= 1/(2^{k/2} Γ(k/2))` by Legendre
duplication): the `χ²_k` CDF written in the shape of Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5).

Gaussian vector and the substitution `y = √x`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.wishart_lambda_min_cdf_rank_one`.

complete pairing. Source: Isserlis 1918; Janson 1997, *Gaussian Hilbert Spaces*, Thm 1.28.

re-derivation `pg:wick`; the construction includes odd and empty lengths.

  have s := √(NLAlib.bilinearSquareMass A Finset.univ);
  have E := ξ * Real.log ↑(Fintype.card d) ^ (3 / 4);
  have H := fun x =>
    Metric.hausdorffDist (spectrum ℝ (A₀ + ∑ i, x i • A i))
      (spectrum ℝ (NLAlib.wordNativeMatrixLinearCombination A₀ A));
  ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), H x ∂NLAlib.gaussianVector ι ≤ 100000000000000000000 * E ∧
    ∀ (t : ℝ),
      0 ≤ t →
        (NLAlib.gaussianVector ι).real {x | 100000000000000000000 * E + 100000000000000000000 * s * t < H x} ≤
          Real.exp (-t ^ 2)

NLAlib.generalizedSchurComplement.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

doc:

`M = [[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]]`, with the Moore–Penrose inverse `A⁺` (`moorePenroseInverse`), so no
invertibility is needed. Albert 1969, §1; Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.7. For invertible `A` this is
the classical Schur complement `C − Bᴴ A⁻¹ B` (`moorePenroseInverse` of an invertible matrix is
its inverse).

name: NLAlib.givens

The **Givens rotation** `G(i, j, θ)` in the `(i, j)` plane with `c = cos θ`, `s = sin θ`:
`planeRotation eᵢ eⱼ c s`, the identity except for `G i i = c`, `G i j = s`, `G j i = −s`,

`a = b = 0` (so that the rotation is always orthogonal). Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 5.1.3.

`(AAᵀ, b)` (size `k + 1`) and of `(AᵀA, Aᵀb)` (size `k`), the canonical witnesses with positive

signature:
NLAlib.golubKahanInit.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.GolubKahanState m n
name: NLAlib.golubKahanInit
doc:
The first state: `β₁ = ‖b‖`, `u₁ = b/β₁`, `α₁ = ‖Aᵀu₁‖`, `v₁ = Aᵀu₁/α₁` (junk `0` on

**The Golub–Kahan recursion**, zero-indexed: state `j` holds `u_{j+1}, v_{j+1}, α_{j+1},
β_{j+1}` in Golub–Van Loan's one-based notation. Total (`x/0 = 0`). Source: Golub–Van Loan
(2013) [`gvl13`], Alg. 10.4.1; Paige–Saunders (1982), §3.
atlas: golub-kahan-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.golubKahanStep.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (s : NLAlib.GolubKahanState m n) : NLAlib.GolubKahanState m n
name: NLAlib.golubKahanStep
doc:
One Golub–Kahan step: `β' u' = A v − α u`, `α' v' = Aᵀ u' − β' v`, with `α', β' ≥ 0` the
norms (junk `0` on breakdown). Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Alg. 10.4.1. Helper for
`golub-kahan-bidiagonalization`.

signature:
NLAlib.golubKahanSucceeds_iff.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds A b k ↔
    k + 1 ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade (A * A.transpose) b ∧ k + 1 ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade (A.transpose * A) (A.transpose.mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.golubKahanSucceeds_iff
doc:
SCAFFOLD: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization
**Breakdown.** The recursion runs without breakdown through state `k` iff both Krylov grades
are at least `k + 1`: `GolubKahanSucceeds A b k ↔ k + 1 ≤ grade(AAᵀ, b) ∧
k + 1 ≤ grade(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`. (In particular `b = 0` or `Aᵀb = 0` fails at once.) Source:
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §10.4.1; Paige–Saunders (1982), §3. Proof sketch: the
interleaved sequence `u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂, …` is the Lanczos basis of `[[0, A], [Aᵀ, 0]]` from
`(b, 0)`, whose Krylov space of dimension `2j` (resp. `2j + 1`) is
`K_j(AAᵀ, b) ⊕ K_j(AᵀA, Aᵀb)` (resp. `K_{j+1}(AAᵀ, b) ⊕ K_j(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`); Lanczos breaks down
exactly at the grade (`krylovGrade`, `finrank_krylovSpace`), and the norms `α, β` are the
Lanczos `β`'s. Difficulty 3.
atlas: golub-kahan-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.gordon_extreme_singular_values {N n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun A => NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card (Fin n) - 1))
      (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n)) ∧
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun A => NLAlib.specNorm A) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n)) ∧
      √↑N - √↑n ≤
          ∫ (A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ),
            NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card (Fin n) - 1) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ∧
        ∫ (A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ),
              NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card (Fin n) - 1) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ≤
            ∫ (A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ), NLAlib.specNorm A ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ∧
          ∫ (A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ), NLAlib.specNorm A ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ≤ √↑N + √↑n

doc:
**Gordon's theorem for Gaussian matrices.** For an `N × n` standard Gaussian matrix `G`
with `n ≥ 1`, `σ_min(G)` and `‖G‖₂` are integrable and
`√N - √n ≤ 𝔼 σ_min(G) ≤ 𝔼 ‖G‖₂ ≤ √N + √n`. Source: Vershynin 2012, Thm 5.32; Gordon 1985;
Davidson–Szarek 2001, Thm II.13. Atlas: `gordon`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gordon`.
atlas: gordon

  [Fintype U] [Fintype T] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}

  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω p => Y p.1 p.2 ω) Q)
  (hX0 : ∀ (u : U) (t : T), ∫ (ω : Ω), X u t ω ∂P = 0) (hY0 : ∀ (u : U) (t : T), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y u t ω ∂Q = 0)
  (hsame : ∀ (u : U) (t s : T), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X u t ω - X u s ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y u t ω - Y u s ω) ^ 2 ∂Q)

doc:
**Gordon's minimax inequality** (expectation form). Let `X` (on `(Ω, P)`) and `Y` (on
`(Ω', Q)`) be centred Gaussian processes indexed by `U × T` (finite) such that
`𝔼 (X_{u,t} - X_{u,s})² ≤ 𝔼 (Y_{u,t} - Y_{u,s})²` for all `u, t, s` and
`𝔼 (Y_{u,t} - Y_{v,s})² ≤ 𝔼 (X_{u,t} - X_{v,s})²` for `u ≠ v`. Then
`𝔼 minᵤ maxₜ X_{u,t} ≤ 𝔼 minᵤ maxₜ Y_{u,t}`. No equal-variance assumption is needed in the
expectation form. Source: Gordon 1985; Vershynin 2018, Exercise 7.2.14. Atlas: `gordon-minimax`.

signature: NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) (j : Fin n) : m → ℝ
name: NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol
doc:
The `j`-th **Gram–Schmidt vector** `q_j = v_j / ‖v_j‖` with
`v_j = a_j − ∑_{i<j} (q_iᵀ a_j) q_i` (well-founded recursion on `j`). When `v_j = 0` (breakdown)
`q_j = 0` and the process continues. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 7.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Alg. 5.2.5.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature:
NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol_dotProduct_of_lt.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) {i j : Fin n}
  (hij : i < j) : NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A i ⬝ᵥ NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A j = 0
name: NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol_dotProduct_of_lt
doc:
**The Gram–Schmidt columns are pairwise orthogonal**, for every `A` (breakdowns included):
`q_iᵀ q_j = 0` for `i < j`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.7.
Proof: induction on `j`; `q_iᵀ v_j = q_iᵀ a_j (1 − q_iᵀ q_i) = 0` since `q_iᵀ q_i ∈ {0, 1}` and
`q_i = 0` when it is `0`.

  [DecidableEq κ] (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian
doc:
The coordinate Laplacian represented by the explicit Gram Hessian.
Source: operator tail proof; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).
atlas: inverse-power-gram-def

signature:
NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq ι]
  [DecidableEq κ] (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hpd : (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G).PosDef) :
  have R := (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G)⁻¹;
  have T := (R ^ n).trace;
  NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian n ε G =
    2 * ↑(Fintype.card κ) * (NLAlib.inversePowerSoftMinWeight n (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G)).trace +
        4 * (↑n + 1) * T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 2) * (R ^ (2 * n + 2) * (G * G.transpose)).trace -
      T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 1) *
        ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          (2 * (R ^ (n + 2) * (G * G.transpose)).trace +
              (R ^ (n - a + 1)).trace * (R ^ (a + 1) * (G * G.transpose)).trace +
            (R ^ (a + 1)).trace * (R ^ (n - a + 1) * (G * G.transpose)).trace)
name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq
doc:
The exact finite resolvent Gram Laplacian in trace-power form. This
identity exposes the cancellations needed for the sharper limiting
Laplacian bound. Source: operator tail proof; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).

name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_normalized
doc:
Factoring any positive reference inverse eigenvalue normalizes the
resolvent Gram Laplacian into power sums and a geometric kernel. Source:
operator tail proof; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_spectral.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq ι]
  [DecidableEq κ] (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hpd : (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G).PosDef) :
  have b := ⋯.eigenvalues;
  have l := fun i => (b i)⁻¹ - ε;
  have T := ∑ i, b i ^ n;
  NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian n ε G =
    2 * ↑(Fintype.card κ) * T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 1) * ∑ i, b i ^ (n + 1) +
        4 * (↑n + 1) * T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 2) * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (2 * n + 2) -
      T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 1) *
        ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          (2 * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (n + 2) + (∑ i, b i ^ (n - a + 1)) * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (a + 1) +
            (∑ i, b i ^ (a + 1)) * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (n - a + 1))
name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_spectral
doc:
The Gram resolvent Laplacian is exactly a finite scalar expression
in the inverse eigenvalues and the corresponding Gram eigenvalues.
Source: spectral form of the operator tail proof; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).

name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_spectral_offDiag
NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_unshifted_eq
