NLAlib.lpNorm_two_mul_le_sqrt_of_hasSubgaussianMGF.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Ω → ℝ} {c : NNReal}
  (h : ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF X c μ) {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) :
  MeasureTheory.lpNorm X (2 * ↑p) μ ≤ √(4 * ↑c * ↑p)
name: NLAlib.lpNorm_two_mul_le_sqrt_of_hasSubgaussianMGF
doc:
An actual sub-Gaussian fluctuation has even Lp norm at most
`sqrt (4*c*p)`. Integrability follows from its MGF, including when `c=0`.

name: NLAlib.lt_eigenvalues₀_of_forall_mem
doc:
A strict lower Rayleigh bound on a subspace of dimension at least
`k+1` implies a strict bound for the `k`-th largest eigenvalue.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.2.10.
atlas: eigenvalue-order-and-counting (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lt_lambdaMax_complexification_one_sub_of_not_smul_one_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {ε : ℝ} (hfail : ¬(1 - ε) • 1 ≤ A) :
  ε < NLAlib.lambdaMax (NLAlib.realMatrixComplexification (1 - A))
name: NLAlib.lt_lambdaMax_complexification_one_sub_of_not_smul_one_le
doc:
Failure of a real symmetric lower Loewner bound is detected by the
largest eigenvalue of its complexified identity defect. This is the event
bridge used for relative sample-covariance lower bounds.

signature:
NLAlib.lt_lambdaMax_one_sub_of_not_smul_one_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℂ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {ε : ℝ} (hfail : ¬(1 - ε) • 1 ≤ A) : ε < NLAlib.lambdaMax (1 - A)
name: NLAlib.lt_lambdaMax_one_sub_of_not_smul_one_le
doc:
Failure of the lower Loewner bound is detected by a strict largest
eigenvalue deviation of the identity defect. No positivity assumption or
restriction on the real threshold is necessary.

signature: NLAlib.lu {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.lu
doc:
**Gaussian elimination without pivoting** (Doolittle LU) as a total recursion on the
leading pivot: with `A = [[a, rᵀ], [c, C]]`, `L = [[1, 0], [c/a, L']]`,
`U = [[a, rᵀ], [0, U']]` where `(L', U') = lu (C − c rᵀ/a)`. A zero pivot gives junk through
`x / 0 = 0`. For `n = 0` the output is `(1, A)` (both are the empty matrix).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 20.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.2.1 (outer-product form).
atlas: lu-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.luPartialPivot {n : ℕ} :
  Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Equiv.Perm (Fin n) × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.luPartialPivot
doc:
**Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting** as a total recursion. With
`B = partialPivotSwap A = [[a, rᵀ], [c, C]]` and `(σ', L', U') = luPartialPivot (C − c rᵀ/a)`,
the output is `σ = decomposeFin⁻¹ (p, σ')` (row `p` first, then the rows of `B` in the order
`σ'`), `L = [[1, 0], [σ'(c/a), L']]` (multipliers permuted by the later swaps, as in the
textbook's "swap the rows of `L` too"), `U = [[a, rᵀ], [0, U']]`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 21.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.4.1.
atlas: lu-partial-pivoting

signature:
NLAlib.luPartialPivotSucceeds_iff_isUnit_det {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LUPartialPivotSucceeds A ↔ IsUnit A.det
name: NLAlib.luPartialPivotSucceeds_iff_isUnit_det
doc:
Partial pivoting succeeds iff `A` is invertible. Proof: `det A = ± ∏ᵢ uᵢᵢ` from
`isPLU_luPartialPivot` (`Matrix.det_permute`), and the pivots are the diagonal of `U`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 21; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.4.1.
atlas: lu-partial-pivoting

signature:
NLAlib.luPartialPivot_wilkinsonMatrix_last (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.luPartialPivot (NLAlib.wilkinsonMatrix n t)).2.2 (Fin.last n) (Fin.last n) = 2 ^ n * t
name: NLAlib.luPartialPivot_wilkinsonMatrix_last
doc:
The actual partial-pivoting recursion attains Wilkinson's exponential
growth, with its implemented tie rule. The last pivot in dimension `n+1`
is `2^n t`. Trefethen–Bau, Lecture 22.
atlas: lu-growth-factor (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LUSucceeds A ↔ ∀ k ≤ n, NLAlib.leadingMinor A k ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero
doc:
**Breakdown of Gaussian elimination**: elimination without pivoting succeeds iff every
leading principal minor `det A(1:k,1:k)`, `k = 1, …, n`, is nonzero. Proof: induction on `n`
with `det A(1:k+1,1:k+1) = a₁₁ det (pivotSchur A)(1:k,1:k)` (`det_eq_mul_det_pivotSchur`,
`leadingMinor_succ_eq_mul_leadingMinor_pivotSchur`); the case `k = 1` gives `a₁₁ ≠ 0`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20 (Ex. 20.1); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.2.1.
atlas: lu-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_lu_snd_apply_self_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LUSucceeds A ↔ ∀ (i : Fin n), (NLAlib.lu A).2 i i ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_lu_snd_apply_self_ne_zero
doc:
The pivots are the diagonal of `U`: elimination succeeds iff `(lu A).2` has nonzero
diagonal. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20.

NLAlib.lyapunovADIFactor.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K] [Fintype n] [Fintype s]

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovADIFactor_mul_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K]

name: NLAlib.lyapunovADIPropagator

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovADIPropagator_const.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (p : ℝ) (j : ℕ) :

NLAlib.lyapunovADISolve.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K] [Fintype n]

NLAlib.lyapunovADIUpdateFactor.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K] [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.lyapunovADIUpdateFactor

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovADI_fst.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K] [Fintype n] [Fintype s]

name: NLAlib.lyapunovADI_fst
doc: The computed residual factor is exactly the propagated original factor.

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovADI_residual.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K] [Fintype n]
  [Fintype s] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K) (B : Matrix n s K) (p : ℕ → ℝ)
  (hP : ∀ (j : ℕ), IsUnit (A - ↑(p j) • 1).det) (j : ℕ) :

doc:
The exact residual of the actual iterate is its computed factor Gram.
Source: user derivations, equation (G8).

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovADI_snd_nonneg_le_solution.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [RCLike K]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq n] (A X : Matrix n n K) (B : Matrix n s K) (p : ℕ → ℝ) (hp : ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 < p j)

name: NLAlib.lyapunovADI_snd_nonneg_le_solution
doc: The computed iterate lies between zero and every PSD solution.

signature: NLAlib.lyapunovCayleySolution.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A Q : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ
name: NLAlib.lyapunovCayleySolution
doc: The stable Cayley construction of a continuous Lyapunov solution.

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovCayleySolution_equation.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A Q : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hA : NLAlib.IsHurwitz A) :
  A * NLAlib.lyapunovCayleySolution A Q + NLAlib.lyapunovCayleySolution A Q * A.conjTranspose + Q = 0
name: NLAlib.lyapunovCayleySolution_equation
doc:
The continuous Lyapunov equation follows from the actual convergent
Cayley Stein Gramian. No continuous exponential bound is a hypothesis.

signature: NLAlib.lyapunovGramian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A Q : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ
name: NLAlib.lyapunovGramian
doc:
The actual improper Bochner integral over positive time. Changing `Ioi 0`
to `Ici 0` has no effect for Lebesgue measure.

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovGramian_eq_of_solution.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A Q X : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hA : NLAlib.IsHurwitz A) (hX : A * X + X * A.conjTranspose + Q = 0) : NLAlib.lyapunovGramian A Q = X
name: NLAlib.lyapunovGramian_eq_of_solution
doc:
Every actual continuous Lyapunov solution equals the improper Gramian.
The derivative is integrated by improper FTC and the semigroup endpoint is
proved to vanish. Source: user derivations, continuous Gramian formula (G1).
atlas: lyapunov-stability-gramian (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lyapunovGramian_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype s]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (B : Matrix n s ℂ) (hA : NLAlib.IsHurwitz A) (v : n → ℂ) :
  (NLAlib.lyapunovGramian A (B * B.conjTranspose)).mulVec v = 0 ↔
    ∀ j < Fintype.card n, B.conjTranspose.mulVec ((A.conjTranspose ^ j).mulVec v) = 0
name: NLAlib.lyapunovGramian_mulVec_eq_zero_iff
doc:
A controllability Gramian's kernel is exactly the finite unobservable
space. The finite cutoff `j < card n` is proved sufficient by Cayley–Hamilton.
Source: user derivations, equation (G2).
atlas: lyapunov-stability-gramian (partial)

signature: NLAlib.lyapunovIntegrand.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A Q : Matrix n n ℂ) (t : ℝ) : Matrix n n ℂ
name: NLAlib.lyapunovIntegrand
doc: The semigroup Gramian integrand, using the adjoint of the actual exponential.

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_comp_perm.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x : ι → ℝ) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) :
  NLAlib.Majorized (x ∘ ⇑σ) x
name: NLAlib.majorized_comp_perm
doc:
A coordinate permutation is majorized by the original vector, including
equality of totals. Source: a permutation matrix is doubly stochastic.

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_diagonal_eigenvalues.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.Majorized (fun i => RCLike.re (A i i)) hA.eigenvalues
name: NLAlib.majorized_diagonal_eigenvalues
doc:
**Schur's theorem.** The real diagonal of a Hermitian matrix is majorized by its spectrum
(`Majorized` sorts intrinsically; arbitrary finite indices, repeated eigenvalues and empty
shapes are included). Over `ℝ` the diagonal is `Matrix.diag A` (`RCLike.re_to_real`).
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.45.
atlas: schur-horn

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_eigenvalues₀_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.Majorized ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (hA.eigenvalues₀ + hB.eigenvalues₀)
name: NLAlib.majorized_eigenvalues₀_add
doc:
The spectrum of a real symmetric sum is majorized by the coordinatewise
sum of the two decreasing spectra. Equality of totals follows from trace.
Fan (1949), Theorem 1; Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.39.
atlas: ky-fan-maximum-principle

name: NLAlib.majorized_eigenvalues₀_add_sub
doc:
Lidskii's ordinary majorization of the coordinatewise signed eigenvalue
increment. Bhatia 1997, Theorem III.4.1; no sorting of the increment is assumed.
atlas: lidskii

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_doublyStochastic.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized x y ↔ ∃ D ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ ι, D.mulVec y = x
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_doublyStochastic
doc:
Full HLP equivalence between ordinary majorization and the existence of an
doubly stochastic matrix, including empty index types and signed vectors.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_orthogonal_diagonal_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (d lam : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized d lam ↔ ∃ Q, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧ (Q * Matrix.diagonal lam * Q.transpose).diag = d
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_orthogonal_diagonal_eq
doc:
Ordinary real majorization is exactly attainment as the diagonal of a real
orthogonal conjugate of the prescribed spectrum. Horn–Johnson (2013),
Theorems 4.3.45 and 4.3.48; signed and repeated spectra and dimension zero.
atlas: schur-horn

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_mem_convexHull_permutations.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized x y ↔ x ∈ (convexHull ℝ) (Set.range fun σ => y ∘ ⇑σ)
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_mem_convexHull_permutations
doc:
Full HLP equivalence with convex-hull membership in the permutation orbit.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_sum_convex_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized x y ↔ ∀ (φ : ℝ → ℝ), ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ → ∑ i, φ (x i) ≤ ∑ i, φ (y i)
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_sum_convex_le
doc:
Full ordinary-majorization equivalence with all convex scalar sum tests.
The affine tests `u` and `-u` recover equality of totals.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Proposition 4.B.1.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_mulVec_of_doublyStochastic.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (y : ι → ℝ)
  {D : Matrix ι ι ℝ} (hD : D ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ ι) : NLAlib.Majorized (D.mulVec y) y
name: NLAlib.majorized_mulVec_of_doublyStochastic
doc:
A doubly stochastic image is majorized by its input, including equality
of totals. Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_eigenvalues_selfAdjointPart.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (z : n → ℂ) (hz : A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (z i))) :
  NLAlib.Majorized (fun i => (z i).re) (Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues ⋯)
name: NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_eigenvalues_selfAdjointPart
doc:
The complete real-part eigenvalue list of a complex matrix is majorized
by the Hermitian-part eigenvalues. Eigenvalue multiplicities are
specified by the characteristic factorization; the list may be in any order.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.3.50.
atlas: real-part-eigenvalue-majorization (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_iff_exists_charpoly_and_selfAdjointPart_charpoly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (x : n → ℝ) (z : n → ℂ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized (fun i => (z i).re) x ↔
    ∃ A,
      A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (z i)) ∧
        (↑((selfAdjointPart ℝ) A)).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C ↑(x i))
name: NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_iff_exists_charpoly_and_selfAdjointPart_charpoly
doc:
**Real-part majorization (Horn–Johnson Thm 4.3.50).** `Re z ≺ x` if and only if some complex
matrix has eigenvalues `z` (as a characteristic polynomial) and Hermitian part with eigenvalues
`x`; multiplicities, arbitrary orderings and empty dimensions are included.
atlas: real-part-eigenvalue-majorization

signature:
NLAlib.mapAbsCondition.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

The absolute condition number of `f` at `x`: the operator norm of the Fréchet derivative.

name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_eq_abs_deriv
doc:
In one dimension the absolute condition number is the absolute derivative.
Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.5.

name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_eq_norm_of_hasFDerivAt
doc:
A specified Fréchet derivative computes the absolute condition number.
Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.3.

signature:
NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_momentRecurrenceMap_eq_specNorm {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin d → Polynomial ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)

doc:
The absolute local condition number is the spectral norm of the actual
moment sensitivity matrix. Source: AQ31, Gautschi (2004), Definition 2.3.

NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_momentRecurrenceMap_polynomialBasis_eq_specNorm {d n : ℕ}
  (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ ↥(Polynomial.degreeLT ℝ d)) (L : Polynomial ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (hd : 2 * n ≤ d)
  (hL : (NLAlib.hankelMomentMatrix L n).PosDef) :

    NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polynomialBasisSensitivityMatrix b L n)
name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_momentRecurrenceMap_polynomialBasis_eq_specNorm
doc:
The absolute local condition number in the actual fixed modified moments
is the spectral norm of the original functional's sensitivity matrix.
Source: AQ31 and Gautschi (2004), Definition 2.3.
atlas: recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_toEuclideanCLM.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) : NLAlib.mapAbsCondition (⇑(Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A)) x = NLAlib.specNorm A

condition matrix. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.4; its relative reading needs every input and

real division by zero coordinatewise; a zero coordinate does not force the whole
scaled-matrix norm to vanish.

The componentwise relative condition number is the absolute condition number of the scaled
local map at `0`. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.4.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_chernoff_sampling_lower.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (hN : 0 < N) (M : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (M k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun M μ)
  (hPSD : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (M k ω).PosSemidef)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (M k ω) ≤ L) (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), M k ω ∂μ = 1)
  {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  μ.real {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin ((1 / ↑N) • ∑ k, M k ω) ≤ 1 - ε} ≤ ↑d * Real.exp (-ε ^ 2 * ↑N / (2 * L))
name: NLAlib.matrix_chernoff_sampling_lower
doc:
**Matrix Chernoff for sampling, lower tail.** Let `M₁, …, M_N` be independent random
positive semidefinite `d × d` matrices with `λmax(Mₖ) ≤ L` and `𝔼 Mₖ = I`. Then for
`0 ≤ ε < 1`, `P(λmin(N⁻¹ ∑ₖ Mₖ) ≤ 1 - ε) ≤ d e^{-ε² N/(2L)}`.
Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1 with Tropp 2012, Rem 5.3; Tropp 2011, Thm 2.2.
Atlas `matrix-chernoff-sampling`. Deviation: the atlas's unspecified constant is the explicit
`2`; the index `Fin N` is inherited from the matrix Chernoff theorem.
atlas: matrix-chernoff-sampling

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_chernoff_sampling_upper.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (hN : 0 < N) (M : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (M k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun M μ)
  (hPSD : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (M k ω).PosSemidef)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (M k ω) ≤ L) (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), M k ω ∂μ = 1)
  {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
  μ.real {ω | 1 + ε ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax ((1 / ↑N) • ∑ k, M k ω)} ≤ ↑d * Real.exp (-ε ^ 2 * ↑N / (3 * L))
name: NLAlib.matrix_chernoff_sampling_upper
doc:
**Matrix Chernoff for sampling, upper tail.** Under the hypotheses of
`matrix_chernoff_sampling_lower`, for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`,
`P(λmax(N⁻¹ ∑ₖ Mₖ) ≥ 1 + ε) ≤ d e^{-ε² N/(3L)}`.
Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1 with Tropp 2012, Rem 5.3; Tropp 2011, Thm 2.2.
Atlas `matrix-chernoff-sampling`. Deviation: the atlas's unspecified constant is the explicit
`3` (valid for `ε ≤ 1`); the index `Fin N` is inherited from the matrix Chernoff theorem.
atlas: matrix-chernoff-sampling

  {ℱ : MeasureTheory.Filtration ℕ inst✝} {X V : ℕ → Ω → Matrix n n ℂ} (hXMeas : ∀ (j : ℕ), Measurable (X j))

name: NLAlib.matrix_freedman
doc:
The arbitrary-time upper matrix Freedman inequality on an arbitrary probability
space. Increments are adapted integrable Hermitian matrices, actually conditionally
centered, and bounded only above by `L I`. Predictable finite PSD variance increments
satisfy the genuine extended local quadratic moment identities on every predictable
set and every deterministic complex vector. Neither unconditional square integrability
nor integrability of the original variance is assumed. The bound includes `t=0` and
`L=0` and has the exact Bernstein coefficient.
Source: Tropp 2011, Theorem 1.2; supplied operator rederivations `thm:freedman` and
Part VII audit `audit:local-moment`, `audit:combined`.
atlas: matrix-freedman

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_sign_newton.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℂ}
  (hA : ∀ z ∈ spectrum ℂ A, z.re ≠ 0) :
  have S := NLAlib.matrixSign A;
  have G := (A - S) * (A + S)⁻¹;
  spectralRadius ℂ G < 1 ∧
    (∀ (k : ℕ),
        IsUnit (NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A k) ∧ NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A k = NLAlib.inverseCayley (G ^ 2 ^ k) * S) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto (NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A) Filter.atTop (nhds S) ∧
        ∀ (k : ℕ),
          NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A (k + 1) - S =
              2⁻¹ • ((NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A k)⁻¹ * (NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A k - S) ^ 2) ∧
            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A (k + 1) - S) ≤
              1 / 2 * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A k)⁻¹ *
                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.signNewtonIterate A k - S) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.matrix_sign_newton
doc:
All advertised sign Newton guarantees for the canonical matrix sign:
nonsingularity, exact Cayley formula, convergence, exact quadratic error,
and its spectral-norm bound.
atlas: matrix-sign-newton

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_max_residual_div
doc:
Wedin's exact maximum-residual operator bound for the leading left and
right singular spaces of SVDs. Wedin (1972), Section 3. The denominator
is `σ_(k-1)(A+E)-σ_k(A)`; the endpoint `k=min(m,n)` uses the zero-padded
next value. Empty selected frames are included whenever the displayed gap is positive.

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_specNorm_div

Wedin's mixed-gap sine operator norms are both at most the perturbation
operator norm divided by the mixed gap. Wedin (1972), Section 3.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta (partial)

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_two_mul_specNorm_div_population_gap

The leading singular-space population-gap operator bound holds without
any smallness hypothesis on the perturbation. Wedin (1972), Section 3; Weyl
and the unit sine bound give the exact constant two. The next singular value is
zero padded at `k=min(m,n)`, including unmatched rectangular null directions.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal {N p d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
  (hrank : B.rank + d ≤ N) (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hud : u ≤ ↑d) :
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
      {g | (⨅ c, √((g - B.mulVec c) ⬝ᵥ (g - B.mulVec c))) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.exp 1 * u / ↑d) ^ (↑d / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal
doc:
**Small ball for the distance to a subspace.** Let `B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ` have
`rank B + d ≤ N` with `d ≥ 1`. For a standard Gaussian vector `g ∈ ℝᴺ` and `0 ≤ u ≤ d`,
`P(dist(g, range B)² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / d)^{d/2}`, with `dist(g, range B) = inf_c ‖g - B c‖₂`.

The squared distance dominates the sum of squares of `d` coordinates of `g` in an orthonormal
basis of `(range B)ᗮ` (Bessel), which is `χ²_d` by rotation invariance; then the chi-square lower
tail. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_dist_colspace_small_ball`.
atlas: smin-small-ball

  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n)).real {A | (⨅ x, √(A.mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec ↑x)) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    (Real.exp 1 * u / (↑N - ↑n + 1)) ^ ((↑N - ↑n + 1) / 2)
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_col_span_le_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Small ball for the distance from a column to the span of the others.** For an `N × n`
standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `n ≤ N`, any column `j` and `0 ≤ u ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(dist(A_j, span{A_l : l ≠ j})² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`, the distance
being written `inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 }`.

Condition on the other columns (resample column `j`) and apply the subspace small-ball bound
with `d = N - n + 1`. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.dist_col_span_small_ball`.
atlas: smin-small-ball

`x = ∑_{i<q} A^i Ω c_i`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3; Tropp–Webber (2023) [`tw23`], §7.

  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|X i ω| / K i)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (B : ℝ) (hKB : ∀ (i : ι), K i ≤ B)

signature:
NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (X C H : Matrix d d ℂ) (ζ ω : ℂ)
  (a b : ℕ) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion
doc:
The exact insertion sum for a mixed trace with a fixed left coefficient.
Every summand has two positive total inverse-arc lengths.

signature:
NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion_eq_sum_split.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (X H : Matrix d d ℂ)
  (ζ : ℂ) (a b : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion X H H ζ (star ζ) a b =
    ∑ j,
      NLAlib.normalizedTrace
        (H *
              (resolvent X ζ ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitLeft a b j).1 *
                resolvent X (star ζ) ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitLeft a b j).2) *
            H *
          (resolvent X ζ ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitRight a b j).1 *
            resolvent X (star ζ) ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitRight a b j).2))
name: NLAlib.mixedResolventTraceInsertion_eq_sum_split
doc:
The actual cyclic mixed-trace derivative insertion is precisely its
finite positive-arc coefficient sandwich sum; no coefficient commutation
or extra derivative identity is assumed.

signature: NLAlib.mixedResolventWord.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] (ζ : ℂ) (p : ℕ) : Fin (p + p) → ℂ × Matrix n n ℂ
name: NLAlib.mixedResolventWord

The literal `p` resolvents followed by `p` conjugate-shift resolvents,

NLAlib.mixed_pow_add_mixed_pow_le {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) {m l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ m) :

name: NLAlib.mixed_pow_add_mixed_pow_le
doc:
Paired mixed powers are bounded by the two endpoint powers for nonnegative
scalars. Source: manuscript `eq:scalarpair`; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.mixed_power_insertion_sum_eq_sum_split.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (R S H : Matrix d d ℂ)
  (a b : ℕ) :
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range a, R ^ (a - i) * H * R ^ (i + 1) * S ^ b +
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range b, R ^ a * S ^ (b - j) * H * S ^ (j + 1) =
    ∑ i,
      R ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitLeft a b i).1 * S ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitLeft a b i).2 * H *
        (R ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitRight a b i).1 * S ^ (NLAlib.mixedResolventSplitRight a b i).2)
name: NLAlib.mixed_power_insertion_sum_eq_sum_split
doc:
The two ordered derivative insertion sums are exactly the single finite
positive-arc split sum. This uses no commutativity or inverse hypothesis.

signature: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtQ.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtQ
doc:
The `Q` factor of modified Gram–Schmidt (the working columns after `n` steps).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtR.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtR
doc:
The `R` factor of modified Gram–Schmidt: `r_ij = q_iᵀ w_j^{(i)}` for `i < j` (the working
column `j` before step `i`), `r_ii = ‖w_i^{(i)}‖`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Fin n → m → ℝ
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState
doc:
The working columns of **modified Gram–Schmidt** after `k` steps (Trefethen–Bau Alg. 8.1):
start from the columns of `A`; step `k` (for `k < n`) normalises column `k` to
`q_k = w_k / ‖w_k‖` and removes its component from every later column,
`w_j ← w_j − (q_kᵀ w_j) q_k` (`j > k`); columns `< k` are left alone. After `n` steps column `j`
holds `q_j`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 5.2.6.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature:
NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState_eq.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  k ≤ n →
    ∀ (j : Fin n),
      NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState A k j =
        if ↑j < k then NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A j
        else A.col j - ∑ l with ↑l < k, (NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A l ⬝ᵥ A.col j) • NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A l
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState_eq
doc:
The MGS invariant: after `k ≤ n` steps, working column `j` is `q_j` for `j < k` and
`a_j − ∑_{i<k} (q_iᵀ a_j) q_i` otherwise. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 8.

signature:
NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidt_eq.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtQ A = NLAlib.gramSchmidtQ A ∧ NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtR A = NLAlib.gramSchmidtR A
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidt_eq
doc:
**MGS = CGS in exact arithmetic**: modified Gram–Schmidt computes the same `Q` and `R` as
classical Gram–Schmidt, for every `A` (breakdowns included). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 8
(MGS is a rearrangement of CGS); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.8. Proof: the invariant
`modifiedGramSchmidtState_eq`, with `q_kᵀ q_i = 0` for `i ≠ k`.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature:
NLAlib.modulatedFejerCircleKernel_eq_sum (K : ℕ) (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  NLAlib.modulatedFejerCircleKernel K t =

doc:
The modulated positive Fejér kernel has a finite band of cosine frequencies.
The averaged-Dirichlet representation equals the usual triangular Fourier weights.

signature:
NLAlib.momentRecurrenceMap_polynomialBasisMomentVector_eq {d n : ℕ}
  (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ ↥(Polynomial.degreeLT ℝ d)) (L : Polynomial ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (hd : 2 * n ≤ d) :

        (fun i => if ↑i = 0 then L 1 else NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L ↑i) s

doc:
At the actual fixed-basis modified moment vector, the output is precisely
the original functional's included alphas, mass, and positive-order betas.
No higher moments enter, and mass is separate from the zero beta boundary.

signature:
NLAlib.monicJacobiMatrix_christoffel_eq_reversed_factors_add_boundary.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜]
  {L : Polynomial 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜} (hL : NLAlib.QuasiDefinitePolynomialFunctional L) {z : 𝕜}
  (hz : ∀ (n : ℕ), Polynomial.eval z (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n) ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.monicJacobiMatrix n
      (NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha (NLAlib.polynomialWeightedFunctional L (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C z)))
      (NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceBeta (NLAlib.polynomialWeightedFunctional L (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C z))) =
    NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix n (NLAlib.christoffelQuotient L z) *
          NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix n (NLAlib.christoffelElimination L z) +
        z • 1 +
      NLAlib.christoffelElimination L z (n - 1) • NLAlib.terminalCoordinateMatrix n
name: NLAlib.monicJacobiMatrix_christoffel_eq_reversed_factors_add_boundary
doc:
The globally quasi-definite modified recurrence has the finite reversed
Darboux factorization with its exact terminal-coordinate correction.
Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 1.33; AQ15.
atlas: kernel-polynomials-christoffel (partial), christoffel-uvarov-modification (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.monicJacobiMatrix_christoffel_eq_reversed_factors_add_boundary_of_finite.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [Field 𝕜]
  {L : Polynomial 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜} {z : 𝕜} (n : ℕ) (hL : ∀ k ≤ n, NLAlib.hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0)
  (hz : ∀ k ≤ n, Polynomial.eval z (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial L k) ≠ 0) :
  NLAlib.monicJacobiMatrix n
      (NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha (NLAlib.polynomialWeightedFunctional L (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C z)))
      (NLAlib.orthogonalRecurrenceBeta (NLAlib.polynomialWeightedFunctional L (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C z))) =
    NLAlib.darbouxUpperMatrix n (NLAlib.christoffelQuotient L z) *
          NLAlib.darbouxLowerMatrix n (NLAlib.christoffelElimination L z) +
        z • 1 +
      NLAlib.christoffelElimination L z (n - 1) • NLAlib.terminalCoordinateMatrix n

nondegeneracy through the dimension. Empty and terminal atomic dimensions are

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber
doc:
The pseudoinverse condition number `‖A‖₂ ‖A⁺‖₂` of a matrix of any shape, with the
Moore–Penrose inverse: it equals `σ₁/σ_r` with `r = rank A`
(`moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio`) and is `0` at `A = 0` (every shape). For
an invertible square matrix it is the real value of `conditionNumber A`
(`conditionNumber_toReal_eq_moorePenroseConditionNumber`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and
§5.5.2 (the condition number of a full-rank rectangular matrix).
atlas: condition-number-def

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_conjTranspose
doc:
Conjugate transposition preserves the pseudoinverse condition number at every rank.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
Taking a column Gram matrix `AᴴA` squares the pseudoinverse condition number, including at
deficient rank. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio.{u_3} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A = ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨0, ⋯⟩ / ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨Fintype.card n - 1, ⋯⟩
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio
doc:
For a positive-definite real matrix on a nonempty index type, the pseudoinverse condition
number is the ratio of its largest and smallest eigenvalues. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_mul_specNorm_inv.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : IsUnit A) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A = NLAlib.specNorm A * NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_mul_specNorm_inv
doc:
On an invertible square matrix the pseudoinverse condition number uses the ordinary inverse:
`‖A‖₂ ‖A⁻¹‖₂`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, eq. (2.6.4); Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.13).
atlas: condition-number-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_of_qr
doc:
QR preserves the total spectral condition number built from the
Moore--Penrose inverse, including singular and zero-rank matrices.
Golub--Van Loan, Section 2.6.2; supports `qr-decomposition`.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio
doc:
At positive rank the pseudoinverse condition number is the ratio of the largest and
last positive singular values, `σ₁/σ_r` (zero-indexed: `σ 0 / σ (r-1)`), on arbitrary
finite index types. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and §5.5.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_specNorm_div_singularValues_last.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜)
  (hn : 0 < Fintype.card n) (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A = NLAlib.specNorm A / NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card n - 1)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_specNorm_div_singularValues_last
doc:
Under full column rank (`rank A = card n ≥ 1`), `κ⁺(A) = ‖A‖₂ / σ_min(A)` with
`σ_min(A) = singularValues A (card n - 1)`; this covers invertible square `A`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.2 (`κ₂(A) = σ₁/σ_n`); Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.14).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_mul_left_of_hasOrthonormalCols.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {p : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
  [DecidableEq p] (Q : Matrix p m 𝕜) (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber (Q * A) = NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_mul_left_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Left multiplication by a rectangular orthonormal frame (`QᴴQ = 1`) preserves the
pseudoinverse condition number. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and §5.3.2 (`κ(R) = κ(A)` for
`A = QR`).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_nonneg.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_nonneg
doc:
Pseudoinverse condition numbers are nonnegative.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2; supports `condition-number-def`.

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_smul
doc:
Nonzero scalar multiplication preserves the pseudoinverse condition number.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_transpose
doc:
Transposition preserves the pseudoinverse condition number at every rank.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber 0 = 0
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_zero
doc:
The zero matrix has pseudoinverse condition number zero, including empty shapes.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2; supports `condition-number-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : Matrix n m 𝕜
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse
doc:
The **Moore–Penrose inverse** `A⁺` of a rectangular matrix over `ℝ` or `ℂ`: the matrix
satisfying the four Penrose identities (`isMoorePenroseInverse`), chosen by
`exists_isMoorePenroseInverse` and well defined because the identities determine it uniquely
(`IsMoorePenroseInverse.unique`). For every SVD `A = U Σ Vᴴ` it is the textbook formula
`V Σ⁺ Uᴴ`, with `Σ⁺` the reciprocals of the nonzero singular values
(`moorePenroseInverse_eq_svd`). Defined for rank-deficient and empty matrices; the full-rank
formulas `pinvL`, `pinvR` are separate definitions (`moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvL`,
`moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvR`). Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_circulant {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (c : ZMod n → ℂ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (Matrix.circulant c) = Matrix.circulant (ZMod.dft.symm fun i => (ZMod.dft c i)⁻¹)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_circulant
doc:
Inverse Fourier transformation of reciprocal modes produces the pseudoinverse column.
Source: Meyer §5.5.
atlas: circulant-fourier-pseudoinverse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_circulant_eq_fourier {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (c : ZMod n → ℂ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (Matrix.circulant c) =
    ((NLAlib.fourierUnitary n).conjTranspose * Matrix.diagonal fun i => (ZMod.dft c i)⁻¹) * NLAlib.fourierUnitary n
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_circulant_eq_fourier
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse in Fourier coordinates is the reciprocal multiplier,
with the total field inverse assigning zero at zero modes.
Source: Meyer §5.5.
atlas: circulant-fourier-pseudoinverse (partial)

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_conjTranspose
doc: Conjugate transpose commutes with the general Moore–Penrose inverse: `(Aᴴ)⁺ = (A⁺)ᴴ`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_conjTranspose_mul_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}
  {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A.conjTranspose * A) =
    NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
The general inverse of the column Gram matrix `Aᴴ A` is `A⁺ (A⁺)ᴴ`, including singular Gram
matrices. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_inv_of_isUnit.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hA : IsUnit A) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = A⁻¹
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_inv_of_isUnit
doc:
On a nonsingular square matrix, the general inverse is the ordinary inverse.
Horn--Johnson 2013, Problem 7.3.P7; supports `condition-number-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_left_inverse_mul_projector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {L : Matrix n m ℝ} (hL : L * A = 1) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = L * (A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_left_inverse_mul_projector
doc:
Any left inverse recovers the Moore–Penrose inverse after composing with
the orthogonal range projector. Penrose identities; supports least-squares perturbation.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_of_isQR.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A Q : Matrix m n 𝕜} {R : Matrix n n 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsQR A Q R)
  (hR : ∀ (i : n), R i i ≠ 0) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = R⁻¹ * Q.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_of_isQR
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse via QR: under full column rank, `A⁺ = R⁻¹ Qᴴ`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 11; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvL.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (h : IsUnit (A.conjTranspose * A)) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = NLAlib.pinvL A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvL
doc:
The general Moore–Penrose inverse agrees with `pinvL` for full column rank.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvR.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (h : IsUnit (A * A.conjTranspose)) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = NLAlib.pinvR A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvR
doc:
The general Moore–Penrose inverse agrees with `pinvR` for full row rank.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_svd.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜}
  {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = (V * NLAlib.rectDiag fun k => (NLAlib.singularValues A k)⁻¹) * U.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_svd
doc:
**`A⁺ = V Σ⁺ Uᴴ`**: any SVD `A = U Σ Vᴴ` computes the Moore–Penrose inverse as
`V Σ⁺ Uᴴ` with `Σ⁺ = rectDiag (σ⁻¹)` (scalar `0⁻¹ = 0`), independently of the choice of singular
vectors. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_zero_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = 0 ↔ A = 0
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_zero_iff
doc:
A matrix has zero Moore–Penrose inverse exactly when the matrix is zero.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_zero_of_rank_eq_zero
doc: At rank zero the Moore–Penrose inverse is zero. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_kronecker.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} {q : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [Fintype q] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (B : Matrix p q ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) A B) =
    Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_kronecker
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse of a Kronecker product is the product of the two
Moore–Penrose inverses. Horn–Johnson 1991, Section 4.2; arbitrary finite rectangular
matrices and all zero singular values are included.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_moorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) = A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_moorePenroseInverse
doc:
Taking the Moore–Penrose inverse twice recovers the original matrix.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_complement_columnProjector_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) =
    NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B).transpose * (B - A).transpose *
      (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_complement_columnProjector_eq
doc:
The upper-right pseudoinverse block has a perturbation-adjoint
factor and a complementary column-space factor. Stewart–Sun §III.3.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_eq_one_of_rank_eq_card.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

doc:
Full column rank gives the literal Moore–Penrose left inverse.
Penrose identities and rank-nullity; supports least-squares perturbation.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_eq_pinvR_mul_pinvL.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq q] (M : Matrix m q ℝ) (R : Matrix q p ℝ)

doc:
Reverse order for a full-column-rank left factor and full-row-rank right
factor. This includes empty intermediate spaces. The proof checks the four
Penrose identities and uses uniqueness. Atlas: `pseudoinverse`, `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_isHermitian.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_isIdempotentElem.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

          (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) +

entry of the left factor. Source: block multiplication; real QZ helper.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_eq_mul_moorePenroseInverse
doc:
**Uniqueness of the orthogonal projector onto a range.** If `Q` has orthonormal columns,
`range Y ⊆ range Q` (written `Q (Qᴴ Y) = Y`) and `rank Y` is at least the number of columns of
`Q` (so the two ranges coincide), then `QQᴴ = Y Y⁺`.

Proof: `P₁ = QQᴴ` and `P₂ = YY⁺` are Hermitian idempotents with `P₁P₂ = P₂ = P₂P₁`, so
`M = P₁ − P₂` is a Hermitian idempotent and `‖M‖_F² = re tr M = card q − rank Y ≤ 0`.
Standard (Golub–Van Loan, 4th ed., §2.5.1: the orthogonal projector onto a subspace is unique).
Atlas `leverage-scores` (basis independence), `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_eq_of_range_eq
doc:
The orthogonal projector depends only on the range: if `Q`, `Q'` have orthonormal columns
and the same range, then `QQᴴ = Q'Q'ᴴ`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_eq_one_of_conjTranspose_mul_eq_one
doc:
Orthonormal columns plus a square count make a unitary matrix: if `U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜`
has `UᴴU = I` and `p = card m`, then `UUᴴ = I`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_mul_add_residual
doc: Orthogonal decomposition `A = Q(QᴴA) + projResidual Q A`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_mul_eq_of_range_le
doc:
Range inclusion as a matrix identity: if `range Q ⊆ range Q'` and `Q'` has orthonormal
columns, then `Q' Q'ᴴ Q = Q`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_mul_mul_conjTranspose
doc:
Idempotence of `P = QQᴴ` for `Q` with orthonormal columns: `P² = P`.
Atlas `projection-facts`.

simple interpolation zero, contradicting Fermat's theorem.
Helper for `jackson-lipschitz` (Jackson's theorem through the sawtooth function).

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_kronecker.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

The Kronecker product's eigenvalues are exactly all pairwise products, as a
multiset with algebraic multiplicities. Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.12.

name: NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_kronecker_sum
doc:
The Kronecker sum's eigenvalues are exactly all pairwise sums, as a multiset.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.12; signed symmetric spectra and empty types are included.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_circulant {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (c : ZMod n → ℂ) :

The singular values of a circulant are precisely the moduli of its DFT,
as a multiset; repeated modes and all rank deficiencies are included.

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_diagonal_complex.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ι → ℂ) :

doc:
The complete domain singular-value multiset of a complex diagonal matrix is
the multiset of the moduli of its diagonal entries, retaining zero multiplicities.

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_eq_sqrt_eigenvalues.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

    Multiset.map (fun i => √(⋯.eigenvalues i)) Finset.univ.val

doc:
The domain-side multiset of native singular values is the square-root Gram
spectrum, including every domain zero. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_kronecker.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}
  {q : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq q] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

  Multiset.map (fun i => NLAlib.singularValues (Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) A B) ↑i) Finset.univ.val =
    Multiset.map (fun xy => xy.1 * xy.2)

doc:
The singular values of a rectangular Kronecker product are all pairwise
products of the two native domain-side singular-value lists, with multiplicities.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.15. Domain lists have `card n`, `card q`, and
`card n * card q` entries; each includes its full domain-side zero padding.
This covers empty dimensions and the additional rectangular zeros automatically.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.natDegree_minpoly_eq_card_iff_eigenvalue_finrank_eq_one.{u_1, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_3} [Field K]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K) (hsplit : A.charpoly.Splits) :

doc:
Every actual eigenvalue has a one-dimensional eigenspace exactly when the
minimal polynomial has full degree over a splitting field. Non-eigenvalues have
zero eigenspaces, so the preceding at-most-one interface is equivalent.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 3.3.14.
atlas: companion-matrix (partial)

name: NLAlib.natDegree_minpoly_eq_card_iff_exists_krylovGrade_eq_card
doc:
Full degree of the operator minimal polynomial is equivalent to existence
of a full-grade vector over any scalar field. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Theorem 3.3.14; operator derivations, (S3).
atlas: companion-matrix (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.natDegree_minpoly_eq_card_iff_finrank_eigenspace_le_one.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2}

name: NLAlib.natDegree_minpoly_eq_card_iff_finrank_eigenspace_le_one
doc:
Over a splitting field, full degree of the minimal polynomial is equivalent
to geometric simplicity of every eigenvalue, including repeated eigenvalues.
The empty-dimensional statement is vacuous on the geometric side.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 3.3.14; operator derivations, Section 6.
atlas: companion-matrix (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.natDegree_minpoly_eq_card_of_finrank_eigenspace_le_one.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2}

  (minpoly K A).natDegree = Fintype.card n

doc:
Over a field where the characteristic polynomial splits, eigenspaces of
dimension at most one force the operator minimal polynomial to have full degree.
Repeated eigenvalues and empty matrices are included.
Source: operator derivations, geometric criterion following (S3).
atlas: companion-matrix (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.neumann_and_inverse_perturbation.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (F A E : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hF : NLAlib.specNorm F < 1) (hA : IsUnit A) (hE : NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E) < 1) :
  IsUnit (1 - F) ∧
    (1 - F)⁻¹ = ∑' (k : ℕ), F ^ k ∧
      NLAlib.specNorm (1 - F)⁻¹ ≤ (1 - NLAlib.specNorm F)⁻¹ ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm ((1 - F)⁻¹ - 1) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm F / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm F) ∧
          IsUnit (A + E) ∧
            NLAlib.specNorm (A + E)⁻¹ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E)) ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm ((A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹) ≤
                  NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E)) ∧
                NLAlib.frobNorm ((A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹) ≤
                  NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ^ 2 * NLAlib.frobNorm E / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E))
name: NLAlib.neumann_and_inverse_perturbation
doc:
Complete quantitative Neumann and inverse perturbation contract. The matrix inverses are used throughout, and both the spectral and Frobenius
difference estimates retain the product-scale denominator. Empty dimensions
are included. Golub--Van Loan, Lemma 2.3.3 and Theorem 2.3.4.
atlas: inverse-perturbation

*Chebyshev Polynomials*, §1.2.

name: NLAlib.norm_div_le_conditionNumber_mul_of_mulVec_add
doc:
**Perturbation of the right-hand side.** For invertible `A`, `A x = b ≠ 0` and
`A (x + Δx) = b + Δb`: `‖Δx‖/‖x‖ ≤ κ₂(A) ‖Δb‖/‖b‖`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 12.1 (condition
number of `b ↦ x` is at most `κ(A)`); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.6.2 with `ΔA = 0`.
atlas: linear-system-perturbation

signature:
NLAlib.norm_div_le_of_add_mulVec_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A ΔA : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : IsUnit A) {x b Δx Δb : n → ℝ} (hx : A.mulVec x = b) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hΔ : (A + ΔA).mulVec (x + Δx) = b + Δb)
  (hsmall : (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal * (NLAlib.specNorm ΔA / NLAlib.specNorm A) < 1) :
  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 Δx‖ / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖ ≤
    (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal /
        (1 - (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal * (NLAlib.specNorm ΔA / NLAlib.specNorm A)) *
      (NLAlib.specNorm ΔA / NLAlib.specNorm A + ‖WithLp.toLp 2 Δb‖ / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖)
name: NLAlib.norm_div_le_of_add_mulVec_add
doc:
**Perturbation of a linear system.** For invertible `A`, `A x = b ≠ 0`,
`(A + ΔA)(x + Δx) = b + Δb` and `κ₂(A) ‖ΔA‖/‖A‖ < 1`:
`‖Δx‖/‖x‖ ≤ κ₂(A)/(1 - κ₂(A)‖ΔA‖/‖A‖) · (‖ΔA‖/‖A‖ + ‖Δb‖/‖b‖)`.
Higham 2002, Thm 7.2 (normwise, with `ε = ‖ΔA‖/‖A‖`-type tolerances); Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Thm 2.6.2; the first-order content is Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 12.1–12.2. Proof: `A Δx = Δb -
ΔA (x + Δx)`, so `‖Δx‖ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖(‖Δb‖ + ‖ΔA‖‖x‖ + ‖ΔA‖‖Δx‖)`; absorb the last term, then use
`‖b‖ ≤ ‖A‖‖x‖`. (`A + ΔA` is then invertible by `isUnit_add_of_specNorm_inv_mul_lt_one`, so
`Δx` is determined.)
atlas: linear-system-perturbation

signature:
NLAlib.norm_sub_eq_minimaxError_iff_equioscillation {n : ℕ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (f : C(↑(Set.Icc a b), ℝ))
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑n) :
  ‖f - p.toContinuousMapOn (Set.Icc a b)‖ = NLAlib.minimaxError n f ↔
    ∃ v σ,
      (StrictMono fun i => ↑(v i)) ∧
        |σ| = 1 ∧
          ∀ (i : Fin (n + 2)),

name: NLAlib.norm_sub_eq_minimaxError_iff_equioscillation
doc:
A degree-`n` polynomial is best if and only if it equioscillates at `n+2` ordered points.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 10.1.
atlas: equioscillation

signature:

  ‖f - p.toContinuousMapOn s‖ = NLAlib.minimaxError n f
name: NLAlib.norm_sub_eq_minimaxError_of_equioscillation
doc:
Equal-magnitude alternating extrema certify a best degree-`n` polynomial.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 10.1, the sufficient direction. The sign is represented
by `|σ|=1`, equivalent to `σ∈{1,-1}`, and zero-error certificates are included.
atlas: equioscillation (partial)

signature:

infinity exponents, zero radius and empty matrix or summand dimensions.

Typed block Cauchy--Schwarz without writing the projections explicitly:
the maps `a r` and `b r` may already contain the domain, middle, and range
projections.  This is the exact row/column-operator inequality.

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

norm estimate is used. Empty dimensions and radius zero are included.

abstract `𝕜`.

`∑ d_i f_k(d_i)^{2ℓ} g_i² / ∑ f_k(d_i)^{2ℓ} g_i²` is at most `4/(2k+1)²`.

takes one eigenvector coordinate). Helper for `random-start-power`.

relation. Atlas: `ornstein-uhlenbeck`.

`tan θ_max` depends only on `range Q` among orthonormal frames with the same index type:
if `range Q = range P` then `tan θ_max(Q, X) = tan θ_max(P, X)`. Proof: `P = Q W` with `W = QᵀP`
orthogonal, so the inverse picks up a right factor `W`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_of_range_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) {X Y : Matrix n k ℝ} (h : X.mulVecLin.range = Y.mulVecLin.range)
  (hX : IsUnit (Q.transpose * X)) : NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q Y
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_of_range_eq
doc:
`tan θ_max` depends only on `range X`: if `range X = range Y` and `QᵀX` is invertible,
then `tan θ_max(Q, X) = tan θ_max(Q, Y)` (and `QᵀY` is invertible too). Source: Saad (2011)
[`saad11`], §5.2.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {r : Type u_4} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] (Q : Matrix n k ℝ)
  {Qp : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQp : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qp) (hc : Q * Q.transpose + Qp * Qp.transpose = 1)
  (X : Matrix n k ℝ) : NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = NLAlib.specNorm (Qp.transpose * X * (Q.transpose * X)⁻¹)
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul_mul
doc:
With an orthonormal complement `Q⊥`: `tan θ_max = ‖Q⊥ᵀ X (QᵀX)⁻¹‖₂`, the form of Saad and
Golub–Van Loan. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.4.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_zero_of_not_isUnit.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) (hC : ¬IsUnit (Q.transpose * X)) : NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = 0
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_zero_of_not_isUnit
doc:
Singular overlap makes the total algebraic inverse-overlap norm zero.
This is a totalization convention, not a finite tangent at a right angle.

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_le_of_range_eq_subspaceIterate
doc:
**Convergence of subspace iteration, basis form.** Under the hypotheses of
`overlapTangentNorm_pow_mul_le`, for any `Q₀` with `range Q₀ = range Ω` and any `Q_k` with
`range Q_k = S_k = subspaceIterate A Ω k` (for instance the orthonormal bases the algorithm
carries), `tan θ_max(range U, range Q_k) ≤ (β/α)^k tan θ_max(range U, range Q₀)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 5.2; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 8.2.2.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_mul_right.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) {R : Matrix k k ℝ} (hR : IsUnit R) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q (X * R) = NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_mul_right
doc:
`tan θ_max` is invariant under a change of basis of `range X`: `tan θ_max(Q, X R) =
tan θ_max(Q, X)` for invertible `R`, since `(I − QQᵀ) X R (QᵀXR)⁻¹ = (I − QQᵀ) X (QᵀX)⁻¹`. In
particular `X` need not be orthonormalised. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_nonneg
doc: `tan θ_max ≥ 0`. Atlas `principal-angles-def` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_pow_mul_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq s] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {U : Matrix n s ℝ}
  {V : Matrix n r ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (hV : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V)
  (hUV : U * U.transpose + V * V.transpose = 1) {d : s → ℝ} {e : r → ℝ} (hAU : A * U = U * Matrix.diagonal d)
  (hAV : A * V = V * Matrix.diagonal e) {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) (hd : ∀ (i : s), α ≤ |d i|)
  (he : ∀ (j : r), |e j| ≤ β) {Ω : Matrix n s ℝ} (hΩ : IsUnit (U.transpose * Ω)) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm U (A ^ k * Ω) ≤ (β / α) ^ k * NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm U Ω
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_pow_mul_le
doc:
**Convergence of subspace iteration (symmetric case).** With an invariant orthogonal
splitting `UUᵀ + VVᵀ = I`, `AU = U diag(d)`, `AV = V diag(e)`, `|dᵢ| ≥ α > 0`, `|eⱼ| ≤ β` and
`UᵀΩ` invertible:
`tan θ_max(range U, range (A^k Ω)) ≤ (β/α)^k tan θ_max(range U, range Ω)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 5.2 (symmetric case); Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
Thm 8.2.2. Deviation: invariant splitting `(U, V, d, e)` with bounds `α, β` instead of ordered
eigenvalues (`α = |λ_s|`, `β = |λ_{s+1}|`); the iterate is the block `A^k Ω` (any basis of `S_k`:
`overlapTangentNorm_le_of_range_eq_subspaceIterate`).
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence

signature: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (u x : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq
doc:
The totalized quadratic overlap ratio of `u` and `x`,
`tan² ∠(u, x) = (‖u‖² ‖x‖² − ⟨u, x⟩²)/⟨u, x⟩²`. For a unit `u` this is
`‖(I − u uᵀ) x‖²/⟨u, x⟩²`. The algebraic value is `0` when `⟨u, x⟩ = 0` (the angle is `π/2`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1 (where `tan θ(u, x)` is used with `‖u‖ = 1`).
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (the one-column case of `overlapTangentNorm`,
`sq_overlapTangentNorm_replicateCol_eq_overlapTangentSq`).

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Eigenvector angle, polynomial form.** Let `u` be a unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue
`λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀`, and `p` a polynomial with `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every other sorted
position. Then `tan² ∠(u, p(A) b) ≤ (M/p(λ_{i₀}))² tan² ∠(u, b)`. With `deg p < q`,
`p(A) b ∈ K_q(A, b)`. This algebraic quotient identity uses zero at vanishing overlap; its geometric form
`tanSqAngle_aeval_mulVec_le` requires nonzero starting overlap and nonzero `p(λ_{i₀})`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1, proof of the angle bound
(`i = 1`).
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle (partial)

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_inverseIterate_le
doc:
**Inverse iteration, angle bound.** Let `A` be real symmetric, `μ` not an eigenvalue, `u` a
unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue `λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀` (the one closest to `μ`),
and `d > 0` with `|λᵢ − μ| ≥ d` at every other sorted position (`d` the distance of the second
closest, T&B's `|μ − λ_K|`). Then the inverse-iteration iterates satisfy
`tan² ∠(u, (A − μI)^{-k} x₀) ≤ (|λ_{i₀} − μ|/d)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. Source:
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.2; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.2.
Deviations: squared tangents; unnormalised iterates (normalisation is bookkeeping,
`overlapTangentSq_smul`).
atlas: inverse-iteration

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_le_of_forall_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq
doc:
**Angle contraction under a spectral multiplier.** Let `u` be a unit eigenvector for the
eigenvalue at sorted position `i₀`, `|g| ≤ M` at every other sorted position, and
`uᵢ ⬝ w = g(λᵢ)(uᵢ ⬝ v)` for every `i` (e.g. `w = p(A) v`, `w = (A − μI)⁻¹ v`). Then
`tan² ∠(u, w) ≤ (M/g(λ_{i₀}))² tan² ∠(u, v)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of
Thm 27.1. Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`, `power-iteration`, `inverse-iteration`.

signature: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (u x : n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_nonneg
doc: `tan² ∠(u, x) ≥ 0` (Cauchy–Schwarz). Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`.

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_of_norm_eq_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {u : n → ℝ} (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1)
  (x : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x = (x ⬝ᵥ x - (u ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2) / (u ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_of_norm_eq_one
doc: For a unit vector `u`, `tan² ∠(u, x) = (‖x‖² − (u ⬝ x)²)/(u ⬝ x)²`. Helper.

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u)
  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → |hA.eigenvalues₀ i| ≤ ρ)
  (x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u (NLAlib.powerIterate A x₀ k) ≤
    (ρ / |hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀|) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerIterate_le
doc:
**Power iteration, angle bound.** Let `A` be real symmetric, `u` a unit eigenvector for the
eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀`, and `|λᵢ| ≤ ρ` at every other sorted
position. Then `tan² ∠(u, A^k x₀) ≤ (ρ/|λ₁|)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. No hypothesis on `x₀` or on
the gap is needed for the inequality (a right angle has the junk value `0` on both sides); it
is informative when `ρ < |λ₁|` and `u ⬝ x₀ ≠ 0`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`],
Thm 27.1; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 8.2.1. Deviations: squared tangents; `ρ` any
bound on the other eigenvalues (T&B: `ρ = |λ₂|`); unnormalised iterates
(`overlapTangentSq_powerStep_iterate_le` for the normalised ones).
atlas: power-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerStep_iterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u)
  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → |hA.eigenvalues₀ i| ≤ ρ)
  (x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u ((NLAlib.powerStep A)^[k] x₀) ≤
    (ρ / |hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀|) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerStep_iterate_le
doc:
**Power iteration, normalised iterates.** Under the hypotheses of
`overlapTangentSq_powerIterate_le`, the textbook iterates `x_k = (powerStep A)^[k] x₀` (normalised at
every step) satisfy `tan² ∠(u, x_k) ≤ (ρ/|λ₁|)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.1.
atlas: power-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (u x : n → ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u (c • x) = NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_smul
doc:
Scaling does not change an angle: `tan² ∠(u, c x) = tan² ∠(u, x)` for `c ≠ 0`. Helper for
`power-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.overlap_singularValues_mem_Icc.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (i : ℕ) :

    Set.Icc 0 1

doc:
Overlap singular values lie between zero and one for orthonormal
frames. Stewart–Sun §I.5, since both frame maps are contractions.

signature:
NLAlib.pairwise_commute_iff_exists_simultaneous_diagonalization.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_3} [Field K] (A : ι → Matrix n n K)
  (hdiag : ∀ (i : ι), NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable (A i)) :
  (Pairwise fun i j => Commute (A i) (A j)) ↔ ∃ V d, IsUnit V ∧ ∀ (i : ι), A i * V = V * Matrix.diagonal (d i)
name: NLAlib.pairwise_commute_iff_exists_simultaneous_diagonalization
doc:
A diagonalizable family commutes exactly when it has one common
diagonalizing similarity. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorems 1.3.12
and 1.3.21; no finiteness assumption on the family is imposed.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization

signature:
NLAlib.pairwise_commute_iff_exists_simultaneous_unitary_diagonalization.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : ι → Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hA : ∀ (a : ι), A a * (A a).conjTranspose = (A a).conjTranspose * A a) :
  (Pairwise fun a b => Commute (A a) (A b)) ↔ ∃ U d, ∀ (a : ι), A a = ↑U * Matrix.diagonal (d a) * (↑U).conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.pairwise_commute_iff_exists_simultaneous_unitary_diagonalization
doc:
A family of normal matrices commutes exactly when it shares a unitary
diagonalization. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.4.8.1; arbitrary
families and finite matrix shapes are allowed.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization

signature: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) : Matrix n (Fin k) ℝ
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor
doc:
The **partial Cholesky factor** `F ∈ ℝ^{n×k}`: column `j` is `R(:, s j) / √R(s j, s j)` with
`R` the residual after the first `j` pivots. CETW 2023, Alg. 1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_castSucc.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin (k + 1) → n) (i : n)
  (j : Fin k) : NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s i j.castSucc = NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A (Fin.init s) i j
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_castSucc
doc:
The first `k` columns of the factor for `k + 1` pivots are the factor for the first `k`
pivots.

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_last.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin (k + 1) → n) (i : n) :
  NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s i (Fin.last k) =
    NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A (Fin.init s) i (s (Fin.last k)) /
      √(NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A (Fin.init s) (s (Fin.last k)) (s (Fin.last k)))
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_last
doc: The last column of the factor is the scaled pivot column of the current residual.

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_mul_transpose_eq_nystrom.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) :
  NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s * (NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s).transpose =
    NLAlib.nystrom A (NLAlib.selectionMatrix s)
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_mul_transpose_eq_nystrom
doc:
SCAFFOLD: partial-cholesky-nystrom
**Partial Cholesky is column Nyström**: for PSD `A` and any pivot sequence `s`,
`F Fᵀ = A(:,S) A(S,S)⁺ A(S,:)`, the Nyström approximation with the selection matrix of `S`.
CETW 2023, §2 (label to verify); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
Proof sketch: write `A = GᵀG` (`exists_eq_transpose_mul_of_posSemidef`). Partial Cholesky on
`A` is Gram–Schmidt on the columns `G(:, s 0), G(:, s 1), …` in order: by induction the
residual is `Gᵀ (I − Pⱼ) G` with `Pⱼ` the orthogonal projector onto the span of the first `j`
pivot columns of `G` (a zero pivot means the column is already in the span). Hence
`F Fᵀ = Gᵀ P_k G`, and `nystrom_eq_of_eq_transpose_mul` gives `nystrom A Ω = Gᵀ P G` with
`P` the projector onto `range (G Ω) = span {G(:, s j)}`.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom

signature: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} : (Fin k → n) → Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual
doc:
The **residual of partial Cholesky** after the pivots `s 0, …, s (k−1)`, in this order.
CETW 2023, Alg. 1 (residual update); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_left.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) (j : Fin k) (i : n) : NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A s (s j) i = 0
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_left
doc:
The partial Cholesky residual of a PSD matrix vanishes on the pivot rows.
CETW 2023, §2.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_right.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) (j : Fin k) (i : n) : NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A s i (s j) = 0
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_right
doc:
The partial Cholesky residual of a PSD matrix vanishes on the pivot columns.
CETW 2023, §2.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_eq_sub_nystrom.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) :
  NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A s =
    A - A.submatrix id s * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A.submatrix s s) * A.submatrix s id
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_eq_sub_nystrom
doc:
**The partial Cholesky residual is the generalized Schur complement**:
`R = A − A(:,S) A(S,S)⁺ A(S,:)`, for PSD `A` and any pivot sequence. With
`posSemidef_partialCholeskyResidual` and `partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_left/right`, the
residual is PSD and zero on the rows and columns of `S`. CETW 2023, §2; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom

name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc:
Every positive-probability pivot history is exact once its length reaches the
input rank. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-rank`; CETW (2025), rank-zero termination.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature: NLAlib.partialPivotSwap {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ
name: NLAlib.partialPivotSwap
doc:
The row swap of partial pivoting: exchange row `0` with the row of an entry of largest
modulus in column `0`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.4.1.

signature: NLAlib.pencilPolynomial {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : Polynomial ℂ
name: NLAlib.pencilPolynomial
doc: The determinant polynomial of the square pencil `A - λB`.

signature:
NLAlib.pencilPolynomial_eq_prod_of_unitary_qz {n : ℕ} {A B S T : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
  {Q Z : ↥(Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)} (hA : A = ↑Q * S * (↑Z).conjTranspose) (hB : B = ↑Q * T * (↑Z).conjTranspose)
  (hS : S.IsUpperTriangular) (hT : T.IsUpperTriangular) :
  NLAlib.pencilPolynomial A B =
    Polynomial.C ((↑Q).det * (↑Z).conjTranspose.det) * ∏ i, (Polynomial.C (S i i) - Polynomial.X * Polynomial.C (T i i))
name: NLAlib.pencilPolynomial_eq_prod_of_unitary_qz
doc:

signature: NLAlib.pivotSchur {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.pivotSchur

The **Schur complement of the leading pivot**: for `A = [[a, rᵀ], [c, C]]` on `Fin (n + 1)`,
`pivotSchur A = C − a⁻¹ c rᵀ`. This is the trailing matrix after one step of Gaussian
elimination (Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2.10) and of the Cholesky
recursion (Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 23). Total: for `a = 0` it is the trailing block `C`.

signature:
NLAlib.pivotSchur_apply {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (i j : Fin n) :
  NLAlib.pivotSchur A i j = A i.succ j.succ - (A 0 0)⁻¹ * (A i.succ 0 * A 0 j.succ)
name: NLAlib.pivotSchur_apply
doc: Entrywise form of the pivot Schur complement: `Cᵢⱼ − cᵢ rⱼ / a`.

signature:
NLAlib.pivotSchur_leadingSubmatrix {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k + 1 ≤ n + 1) :
  NLAlib.pivotSchur (NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix A (k + 1)) = NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix (NLAlib.pivotSchur A) k
name: NLAlib.pivotSchur_leadingSubmatrix
doc:
The pivot Schur complement commutes with taking leading blocks:
`pivotSchur (A(1:k+1, 1:k+1)) = (pivotSchur A)(1:k, 1:k)`.

signature: NLAlib.planeRotation.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] (u v : n → ℝ) (c s : ℝ) : Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.planeRotation
doc:
The **plane rotation** by `(c, s)` in the plane of the orthonormal pair `u, v`:
`I + (c − 1)(u uᵀ + v vᵀ) + s (u vᵀ − v uᵀ)`. For `u = eᵢ`, `v = eⱼ` this is Golub–Van Loan's
`G(i, j, θ)` with `c = cos θ`, `s = sin θ`. For a non-orthonormal pair it is just this matrix.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.8.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (u v x : n → ℝ) (c s : ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s).mulVec x =
    x + (c - 1) • ((u ⬝ᵥ x) • u + (v ⬝ᵥ x) • v) + s • ((v ⬝ᵥ x) • u - (u ⬝ᵥ x) • v)
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_mulVec
doc:
A plane rotation acts by `x ↦ x + (c − 1)((u·x) u + (v·x) v) + s ((v·x) u − (u·x) v)`:
on the plane, `u ↦ c u − s v` and `v ↦ s u + c v`; the orthogonal complement is fixed.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.8.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_apply_diag_of_disjoint_eigenvectors.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : A.transpose = A) (u v : n → ℝ) (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1)
  (hv : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ = 1) (huv : u ⬝ᵥ v = 0) (α β : ℝ) (hAu : A.mulVec u = α • u) (hAv : A.mulVec v = β • v)
  (hdisjoint : ∀ (i : n), u i * v i = 0) (c s : ℝ) (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) (i : n) :
  (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s * A * (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s).transpose) i i =
    A i i + s ^ 2 * (β - α) * (u i ^ 2 - v i ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_apply_diag_of_disjoint_eigenvectors
doc:
The diagonal increment from rotating eigenvectors with disjoint coordinate supports is
exactly `s²(β-α)(uᵢ²-vᵢ²)`, including repeated and negative eigenvalues. Horn–Johnson 2013,
proof of Theorem 4.3.48.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_of_eigenvectors.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : A.transpose = A) (u v : n → ℝ) (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ = 1)
  (huv : u ⬝ᵥ v = 0) (α β : ℝ) (hAu : A.mulVec u = α • u) (hAv : A.mulVec v = β • v) (c s : ℝ)
  (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) :
  NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s * A * (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s).transpose =
    A + (s ^ 2 * (β - α)) • (Matrix.vecMulVec u u - Matrix.vecMulVec v v) +
      (c * s * (β - α)) • (Matrix.vecMulVec u v + Matrix.vecMulVec v u)
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_of_eigenvectors
doc:
Conjugating a symmetric matrix by a rotation of two of its eigenvectors changes only their
two-dimensional spectral block; no restriction on signed or repeated eigenvalues.
Horn–Johnson 2013, proof of Theorem 4.3.48.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_single_conjugation_diag.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hA : A.transpose = A) (i j : n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c s : ℝ) (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) (k : n) :
  have Δ := 2 * c * s * A i j + s ^ 2 * (A j j - A i i);
  (NLAlib.planeRotation (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1) c s * A *
        (NLAlib.planeRotation (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1) c s).transpose)
      k k =
    A k k + if k = i then Δ else if k = j then -Δ else 0
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_single_conjugation_diag
doc:
A coordinate plane rotation changes the two selected diagonal entries by
opposite increments and fixes every other diagonal entry. Schur–Horn variational
rederivation, equation (1).

signature:
NLAlib.polarSchulz_defect_and_error_bounds.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (hRank : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (hA : NLAlib.specNorm A < √3)
  (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1))).PosSemidef ∧
    (1 - NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1))).PosDef ∧
      NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1))) < 1 ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 2))) ≤
            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1))) ^ 2 ∧
          NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1) - NLAlib.canonicalPartialPolar A) ≤
              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1))) ∧
            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A (k + 1))) ≤
              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.polarSchulzDefect (NLAlib.polarSchulzIterate A 1)) ^ 2 ^ k

doc:
