signature:
NLAlib.posSemidef_fromBlocks_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m m 𝕜) (B : Matrix m n 𝕜) (C : Matrix n n 𝕜) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.conjTranspose C).PosSemidef ↔
    A.PosSemidef ∧ (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * B = 0 ∧ (NLAlib.generalizedSchurComplement A B C).PosSemidef
name: NLAlib.posSemidef_fromBlocks_iff
doc:
**Albert's criterion**: `[[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]] ⪰ 0` iff `A ⪰ 0`, `(I − AA⁺) B = 0` (range of `B`
inside range of `A`) and `M / A = C − Bᴴ A⁺ B ⪰ 0`. No Hermitian hypotheses are needed: each
side forces `A` and `C` Hermitian. Albert 1969, Thm 1; cf. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorems 7.7.7
and 7.7.9 for the invertible case.
Proof: (⇒) `A ⪰ 0` and `C ⪰ 0` are principal submatrices; for `z ∈ ker A`,
`(z, 0)ᴴ M (z, 0) = 0` forces `Bᴴ z = 0`, i.e. `range B ⊆ range A`, which is `(I − AA⁺)B = 0`;
then with `y = −A⁺Bx` the quadratic form is `xᴴ(M/A)x ≥ 0`. (⇐) the square completion
`dotProduct_fromBlocks_eq_generalizedSchurComplement_square`.
atlas: generalized-schur-complement-psd

          Real.cos (NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q i) =
            NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin n) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (P.transpose * Q)) ↑i) ∧
      NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * Q) ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.projResidual P Q) ∧
          NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.specNorm (P * P.transpose - Q * Q.transpose) ∧
            NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = ↑(Fintype.card n) - NLAlib.frobSq (P.transpose * Q) ∧

                NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * Q) ∧
                  NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q = NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype Q P ∧
                    (∀ (P' Q' : Matrix m n ℝ),
                        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P' →
                          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q' →
                            P.mulVecLin.range = P'.mulVecLin.range →
                              Q.mulVecLin.range = Q'.mulVecLin.range →
                                NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q = NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P' Q') ∧
                      (0 < Fintype.card n →
                          NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) =
                            √(1 -
                                NLAlib.singularValues
                                    ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin n) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (P.transpose * Q))
                                    (Fintype.card n - 1) ^
                                  2)) ∧
                        (IsUnit (P.transpose * Q) →
                            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.tangentPrincipalAngles P Q) =
                              NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * Q * (P.transpose * Q)⁻¹)) ∧
                          (∀ (hn : 0 < Fintype.card n),
                              NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q ⟨Fintype.card n - 1, ⋯⟩ < Real.pi / 2 →
                                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.tangentPrincipalAngles P Q) =
                                  NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * Q * (P.transpose * Q)⁻¹)) ∧
                            (Fintype.card n = 0 →
                              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = 0 ∧
                                NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = 0 ∧
                                  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.tangentPrincipalAngles P Q) = 0)

doc:

orthonormal frames and an orthonormal complement. Stewart–Sun §I.5,
Golub–Van Loan §2.5.3. The angle and sine/tangent matrices use the actual
singular-value list. Empty frames are explicit; a last angle is mentioned
only at positive width, and the inverse formula requires the overlap to be
invertible, derived also from the last-angle condition.

NLAlib.prod_singularValues_mul_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype p]

name: NLAlib.prod_singularValues_mul_le
doc:
Horn's product inequality `∏_{i<k} σ_i(AB) ≤ ∏_{i<k} σ_i(A) σ_i(B)` at every natural prefix
length, with zero-indexed, zero-padded singular values, on arbitrary finite real matrix indices.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 3.3.4. No positivity, rank, or nonemptiness assumptions are imposed.
atlas: horn-product-inequality (partial)

Independent products of scalar Hermite functions, indexed by their

NLAlib.productHermite_update.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a : ι → ℕ) (i : ι) (n : ℕ) (x : ι → ℝ) :

NLAlib.projResidual.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {q : Type u_4}

signature:
NLAlib.psd_trace_pairing_characterizations.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [RCLike 𝕜] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  (A.PosSemidef ↔ ∀ (B : Matrix n n 𝕜), B.PosSemidef → 0 ≤ (A * B).trace) ∧
    (∀ (B : Matrix n n 𝕜), A.PosSemidef → B.PosSemidef → ((A * B).trace = 0 ↔ A * B = 0)) ∧
      ∀ (B C : Matrix n n 𝕜), A.PosSemidef → B ≤ C → (A * B).trace ≤ (A * C).trace
name: NLAlib.psd_trace_pairing_characterizations
doc:
The PSD cone is self-dual under the trace pairing; the pairing vanishes

signature:
NLAlib.pseudoinverse_perturbation_bounds.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A =
      -NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (B - A) * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A +
          NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B).transpose * (B - A).transpose *
            (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) +
        (1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * B) * (B - A).transpose * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).transpose *
          NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A ∧
    NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ≤
        Real.goldenRatio *
            max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ^ 2)
              (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) ^ 2) *
          NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
      (A.rank = B.rank →
        NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ≤
            Real.goldenRatio * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) *
                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) *
              NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
          NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ≤
              √2 * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) *
                NLAlib.frobNorm (B - A) ∧
            NLAlib.specNorm (A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A - B * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) ≤
                min (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B)) *
                  NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * A - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * B) ≤
                  min (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A))
                      (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B)) *
                    NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
                (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) < 1 →
                  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) ≤
                    NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) /
                      (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * NLAlib.specNorm (B - A))))
name: NLAlib.pseudoinverse_perturbation_bounds
doc:
Every advertised Moore–Penrose perturbation assertion, with the exact
golden ratio and `sqrt(2)` constants. Wedin (1973), Stewart–Sun §III.3; the proof
uses the orthogonal block argument in the supplied operator derivations.
Rank equality is imposed only on the branches that require it. All ranks and
arbitrary finite row/column types, including empty ones, are covered.
atlas: pseudoinverse-perturbation

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithm {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm
doc:
The **shifted QR algorithm** driven by a QR routine `qr` and shifts `μ`: `A₀ = A`,
`A_{k+1} = R Q + μ_k I` where `(Q, R) = qr (A_k − μ_k I)`. Total for every `qr`; it computes the
QR algorithm when `QRAlgorithmSucceeds` holds. The unshifted algorithm is `μ = fun _ => 0`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 28.1 (unshifted), Alg. 29.1 (shifted);
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §7.3.1, §7.5. Alternative: hypotheses on arbitrary sequences
`Q_j, R_j`; a routine argument keeps the recursion total and lets `qr` be `givensQR` or any
choice of QR.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors
doc:
The factor pair `(Q_{k+1}, R_{k+1}) = qr (A_k − μ_k I)` of step `k`. Source: Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 28.1. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors_snd_apply_self_ne_zero
doc:
If no shift is an eigenvalue (`det (A − μ_j I) ≠ 0` for `j < k`), every `R_{j+1}` has a
nonzero diagonal (`A_j − μ_j I` is orthogonally similar to `A − μ_j I`). Source: Golub–Van Loan
(2013) [`gvl13`], §7.4.2. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmQ {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmQ
doc:
The accumulated orthogonal factor `Q^{(k)} = Q_1 ⋯ Q_k`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 28 (eq. 28.8). Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmR {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmR
doc:
The accumulated triangular factor `R^{(k)} = R_k ⋯ R_1`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 28 (eq. 28.8). Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmSucceeds_givensQR {n : ℕ} {μ : ℕ → ℝ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg A)
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.QRAlgorithmSucceeds NLAlib.givensQR μ A k
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmSucceeds_givensQR
doc:
**Realisation for the Givens routine**: on an upper Hessenberg `A`, every factor pair of the
Givens QR algorithm is a QR factorization, so all the identities above apply
(`A_k = Q^{(k)ᵀ} A Q^{(k)}`, `∏ (A − μ_j I) = Q^{(k)} R^{(k)}`). Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013)
[`gvl13`], §7.4.2.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmSucceeds_of_forall_isQR
doc:
A routine that returns a QR factorization of every matrix makes the algorithm succeed for
every `k` (such routines exist: `exists_isFullQR`, Householder). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Alg. 28.1.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_eq_transpose_mul_mul
doc:
**The QR iterates are orthogonally similar to `A`**: `A_k = Q^{(k)ᵀ} A Q^{(k)}`, for any
shifts. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 28.3 (eq. 28.10); Golub–Van Loan (2013)
[`gvl13`], §7.3.1.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_succ {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.qrAlgorithm qr μ A (k + 1) =
    (NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors qr μ A k).2 * (NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors qr μ A k).1 + μ k • 1
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_succ
doc: `A_{k+1} = R_{k+1} Q_{k+1} + μ_k I`. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_zero {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : NLAlib.qrAlgorithm qr μ A 0 = A
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_zero
doc: `A₀ = A`. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

The Euclidean columns of a matrix, with the standard matrix column order.

NLAlib.qrColumnFamily_orthogonal_mul {n k : ℕ} (O : ↥(Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))

signature: NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray {n k : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ

signature:
NLAlib.qr_decomposition.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [LinearOrder n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (hCard : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m) :
  ∃ Q R,
    NLAlib.IsQR A Q R ∧
      (∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ R i i) ∧
        R.transpose * R = A.transpose * A ∧
          (∀ (k : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues R k = NLAlib.singularValues A k) ∧
            NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber R = NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A ∧
              (∀ (e : n ↪ m),
                  ∃ W T,
                    NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W ∧
                      W * W.transpose = 1 ∧
                        W.submatrix id ⇑e = Q ∧
                          W * T = A ∧ T.submatrix (⇑e) id = R ∧ ∀ i ∉ Set.range ⇑e, ∀ (j : n), T i j = 0) ∧
                (A.rank = Fintype.card n →
                  (∀ (i : n), 0 < R i i) ∧
                    Q * Q.transpose = A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A ∧
                      ∀ (Q' : Matrix m n ℝ) (R' : Matrix n n ℝ),
                        NLAlib.IsQR A Q' R' → (∀ (i : n), 0 < R' i i) → Q' = Q ∧ R' = R)
name: NLAlib.qr_decomposition
doc:
Complete QR factorization for real matrices with at least as many rows
as columns, in the canonical form `IsQR A Q R`. The thin factor (existence alone is
`exists_isQR`) has nonnegative upper diagonal and the
Gram, native singular values and Moore--Penrose condition number of the
input. For every coordinate embedding the same frame and triangular factor
extend to a full orthogonal factorization with a zero-padded corner. At full
column rank the diagonal is positive, the range projector agrees
with the Moore--Penrose projector, and the pair is unique among positive
diagonal QR pairs (`IsQR.eq_of_diag_pos`). Arbitrary finite row indices, ordered finite column
indices, singular inputs and empty spaces are covered.
Trefethen--Bau, Theorems 7.1--7.2; Golub--Van Loan, Theorems 5.2.1 and 5.2.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition

signature: NLAlib.quadForm.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (z : n → 𝕜) : 𝕜
name: NLAlib.quadForm

The quadratic form `zᴴ A z = star z ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ z)` (𝕜-valued; Mathlib's `PosSemidef` form). Over
`ℝ` it is `zᵀ A z` (`rw [quadForm_def, star_trivial]`). Atlas: `hutchinson-unbiased`,
`hutchinson-variance`.
atlas: quadform-def

NLAlib.quadFormContinuousLinearMap.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

NLAlib.quadFormContinuousLinearMap_apply.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

NLAlib.quadFormLinearMap.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] (u : n → 𝕜) :

NLAlib.quadFormLinearMap_apply.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] (u : n → 𝕜)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_add.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (x y : n → 𝕜) :

name: NLAlib.quadForm_add
doc:
Expansion of the quadratic form of a sum:
`(x + y)ᴴ A (x + y) = xᴴAx + xᴴAy + yᴴAx + yᴴAy`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (g p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i,
      Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) g * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 *
        ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ g(λᵢ) p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A` and polynomials
`p`, `g`. Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {g p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hg : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x g) (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤
    M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, weighted form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S`, the weight polynomial `g` is nonnegative on `S` and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ g(A) v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_{g(A)} ≤ M ‖v‖_{g(A)}`. The weights
`g = X` (energy norm, CG), `g = X²` (residual norm, MINRES) and `g = 1` (error norm) are the
cases used by Krylov methods. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29 (case `g = X`). Generalises `quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le` (KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2).
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i, hA.eigenvalues i * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 * ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A`. Audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hS : S ⊆ Set.Ici 0) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤ M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, energy form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S ⊆ [0, ∞)` (so `A` is positive semidefinite) and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ A v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_A ≤ M ‖v‖_A`. This is the form used for the
CG error (Greenbaum 1997, §3.1; Saad 2003, Thm 6.29); audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`. The case `g = X` of `quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_bounds_of_sandwich.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hlo : a • 1 ≤ A) (hhi : A ≤ b • 1) (x : n → ℝ) : a * x ⬝ᵥ x ≤ NLAlib.quadForm A x ∧ NLAlib.quadForm A x ≤ b * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.quadForm_bounds_of_sandwich

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Chebyshev iteration, `A`-norm rate.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, and `A x⋆ = c`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: squared norms;
the iterate is defined by its residual polynomial (no recurrence).
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  {k : Type u_3} [Fintype k] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (W : Matrix n k 𝕜) (v : k → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (W.conjTranspose * A * W) v = NLAlib.quadForm A (W.mulVec v)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul
doc:
Congruence: `quadForm (WᴴAW) v = quadForm A (Wv)` for a rectangular `W`. Helper for
`preconditioned-cg` and `ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues` (Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.5.9).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  {m : Type u_3} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (y : n → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (A.conjTranspose * A) y = star (A.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y
name: NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
`(Aᴴ A y)ᴴ y = (Ay)ᴴ (Ay)`: the quadratic form of the normal-equations matrix. Helper for
`cgls-lsqr-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_def.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (z : n → 𝕜) :

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_diagonal_eq_sum_norm_sq_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (d x : n → ℂ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (Matrix.diagonal d) x = ∑ i, ‖x i‖ ^ 2 • d i
name: NLAlib.quadForm_diagonal_eq_sum_norm_sq_smul
doc:
The quadratic form of a diagonal complex matrix is the convex-weight sum
with weights the squared coordinate moduli.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (z : n → 𝕜) :

name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_eigenvalues

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜)
  (z : n → 𝕜) : NLAlib.quadForm A z = ∑ i, ∑ j, star (z i) * A i j * z j
name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_mul_mul
doc:
The quadratic form as the double sum `zᴴ A z = ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ (conj zᵢ) Aᵢⱼ zⱼ` (the order of factors

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_fromBlocks.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m m ℝ)
  (B : Matrix m n ℝ) (C : Matrix n n ℝ) (x : m → ℝ) (y : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C) (Sum.elim x y) =
    NLAlib.quadForm A x + 2 * x ⬝ᵥ B.mulVec y + NLAlib.quadForm C y
name: NLAlib.quadForm_fromBlocks
doc:
The quadratic form of a symmetric block matrix is the sum of both
diagonal quadratic forms and twice the cross term. Horn--Johnson (2013),
Section 7.7; helper for PSD-block quadratic tests.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_hutchinsonBlock.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]

doc:
The quadratic form of the block matrix at `vec(Z)` is the Hutchinson estimator.
Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_le_norm_sq_mul_cfc_leftRadauJacobiMatrix_of_iteratedDeriv_nonpos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]

NLAlib.quadForm_le_norm_sq_mul_cfc_lobattoJacobiMatrix_of_iteratedDeriv_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]

Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 3.7; operator derivations (AQ11).
atlas: gauss-radau-lobatto (partial)

A positive odd derivative makes the actual right Radau Schur matrix estimate

Source: Gautschi (2004), Theorem 3.7; operator derivations (AQ10).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_map_pow_vecMulVec_self.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (b x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Matrix.vecMulVec b b).map fun t => t ^ k) x = (∑ i, x i * b i ^ k) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_map_pow_vecMulVec_self
doc:
A natural entrywise power of a rank-one Gram matrix has the squared
scalar moment as quadratic form. Exponent zero gives the constant feature.
Horn--Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 7.5.9;
helper for the finite Vandermonde certificate.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_mul_quadForm_inv_le_moorePenroseConditionNumber_sqrt.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hN : 0 < Fintype.card n) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A x * NLAlib.quadForm A⁻¹ x ≤
    1 / 4 * (√(NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A) + (√(NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A))⁻¹) ^ 2 *
      ‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖ ^ 4
name: NLAlib.quadForm_mul_quadForm_inv_le_moorePenroseConditionNumber_sqrt
doc:
Kantorovich's condition-number formula uses the existing matrix condition
number and the Euclidean norm, with the square root and its reciprocal.
Positive dimension is required only to identify the condition number with
the extreme-eigenvalue ratio. Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.4.12.
atlas: kantorovich-inequality

name: NLAlib.quadForm_mul_quadForm_inv_le_of_sandwich
doc:
**Kantorovich's inequality** with spectral endpoints: if `a I ≤ A ≤ b I` with `0 < a ≤ b`,
then `(xᵀ A x)(xᵀ A⁻¹ x) ≤ ((a + b)² / 4ab) ‖x‖⁴`. Empty dimensions and `x = 0` are included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.12.
atlas: kantorovich-inequality

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_nonneg_of_eigenvalues_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hpsd : ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues i) (x : n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.quadForm A x
name: NLAlib.quadForm_nonneg_of_eigenvalues_nonneg
doc:
A symmetric matrix with nonnegative eigenvalues has `xᵀ A x ≥ 0`. Moved from
`Krylov/CG.lean` (atlas `cg-convergence`, helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_polyIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Error bound for a polynomial method, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in
`S`, a weight `g ≥ 0` on `S` and `|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`,
`‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1;
Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
atlas: polynomial-method-def

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_reindex.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {ι : Type u_3} {κ : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
  (A : Matrix ι ι 𝕜) (e : ι ≃ κ) (z : ι → 𝕜) :
  (NLAlib.quadForm ((Matrix.reindex e e) A) fun k => z (e.symm k)) = NLAlib.quadForm A z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_reindex
doc:
Relabelling the coordinates by an equivalence does not change the quadratic form.
Atlas `hanson-wright` (index transport).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Richardson contraction, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
step `ω ≥ 0`, `A x⋆ = c` and a weight `g ≥ 0` on `[a, b]`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ ρ^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}` with `ρ = max(|1 − ωa|, |1 − ωb|)`. With
`g = X` (`0 ≤ a`) this is the `A`-norm bound of the atlas, with `g = 1` the Euclidean error.
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.richardsonIterate (2 / (a + b)) A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (((b - a) / (b + a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal
doc:
**Richardson with the optimal step** `ω = 2/(a + b)`: for symmetric positive definite `A`
with spectrum in `[a, b]`, `0 < a ≤ b`, `‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ ((b − a)/(b + a))^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.1; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_rowSelector.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (i : n) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (NLAlib.rowSelector A i) z = z i * A.mulVec z i
name: NLAlib.quadForm_rowSelector
doc: `zᵀ (rowSelector A i) z = zᵢ (A z)ᵢ`. Atlas: `diagonal-estimator` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sampleCovariance.{u_2, u_3} {d : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [Fintype d] [Fintype ι] (X : ι → d → ℝ)
  (u : d → ℝ) : NLAlib.quadForm (NLAlib.sampleCovariance X) u = (↑(Fintype.card ι))⁻¹ * ∑ i, (X i ⬝ᵥ u) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sampleCovariance
doc:
A real sample covariance quadratic probe is the empirical average of
the squared linear probes. The formula also includes an empty sample family.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_selfAdjointPart.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (x : n → ℂ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (↑((selfAdjointPart ℝ) A)) x = ↑(NLAlib.quadForm A x).re
name: NLAlib.quadForm_selfAdjointPart
doc:
Taking the Hermitian part takes the real part of a quadratic form.
This relates the native self-adjoint-part map to accretivity.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_single.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (i : n) (c : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (Pi.single i c) = c ^ 2 * A i i
name: NLAlib.quadForm_single
doc:
A single-coordinate quadratic form equals its squared amplitude times the
corresponding diagonal matrix entry.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_smul.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (c : 𝕜)
  (z : n → 𝕜) : NLAlib.quadForm A (c • z) = star c * c * NLAlib.quadForm A z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_smul
doc: Homogeneity of the quadratic form: `(c z)ᴴ A (c z) = (conj c) c · zᴴ A z`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sq_eq_sum.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜)
  (z : n → 𝕜) : NLAlib.quadForm A z ^ 2 = ∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, ∑ l, A i j * A k l * (star (z i) * z j * star (z k) * z l)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sq_eq_sum
doc:
Expansion `(zᴴ A z)² = ∑ᵢⱼₖₗ A_ij A_kl (conj z_i) z_j (conj z_k) z_l`.
Atlas: `hutchinson-variance` (helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimizer
doc:
**The class theorem.** Let `A` be symmetric, `A x⋆ = c`, and `g` a weight polynomial with
`g(λᵢ) ≥ 0` at every eigenvalue. If `x` minimises `‖· − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} = quadForm (g(A)) (· − x⋆)`
over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then for every residual polynomial `p` (`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with
`|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, `‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`.
CG is `g = X` (via `cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub`), MINRES `g = X²`, the error-minimising
method `g = 1`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1 (CG) and §3.2 (MINRES);
Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Thm 6.29; KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound` (the shared step; tags are on the instances).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x - xs) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate
doc:
**CG convergence, condition-number form.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a ≤ b`, `A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`; with `κ = b/a`,
`(√b − √a)/(√b + √a) = (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1)`. When `a = b` (`A = aI`), CG is exact after one step
and the bound reads `0` for `q ≥ 1` and `4 ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` for `q = 0`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.5; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `chebyshev-minimax`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`krylov-subspace`. Deviation: squared `A`-norms (the source states the unsquared form); the
degenerate case `a = b` is included.
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_poly
doc:
**CG error bound, polynomial form.** Let `A` be symmetric positive semidefinite,
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. For every polynomial `p` with `deg p ≤ q`,
`p(0) = 1` and `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue,
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` (with `‖v‖_A² = quadForm A v`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (and the inequality (38.10)); Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29. Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `polynomial-spectral-bound`, `krylov-subspace`,
`residual-polynomial` (the case `g = X` of `quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimizer`).
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isPCGIterate
doc:
**Preconditioned CG bound under a Loewner sandwich.** Let `P` be positive definite, `A` with
`a P ≼ A ≼ b P` for `0 < a ≤ b` (so `A` is symmetric positive definite and `κ(P⁻¹A) ≤ b/a`),
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th PCG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`.
Proof: CG on `P^{-1/2} A P^{-1/2}`, whose spectrum lies in `[a, b]`
(`isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate`, `quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], Ch. 8.
Deviation: squared `A`-norms.

signature: NLAlib.quadratureBvThreshold (ν : ℕ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.quadratureBvThreshold
doc:
An explicit sufficient cutoff for the eventual corrected Clenshaw–Curtis BV
bound: `ν(ν+1)/2 + ceil((105/16)ν2^ν)`. The ceiling is written with exact natural
arithmetic. Source: focused reroutes, Theorem “An explicit eventual bound”.

signature:
NLAlib.quadrature_error_bounds_and_continuous_convergence.{u_1} {ι : ℕ → Type u_1} [(n : ℕ) → Fintype (ι n)]
  [(n : ℕ) → DecidableEq (ι n)] (hcard : ∀ (n : ℕ), Fintype.card (ι n) = n + 1) (v : (n : ℕ) → ι n → ℝ)
  (hv : ∀ (n : ℕ), Function.Injective (v n)) (hvI : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ι n), v n i ∈ Set.Ioo (-1) 1)
  (horth :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      p.degree < ↑(Fintype.card (ι n)) →
        ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ (v n)) * Polynomial.eval x p = 0)
  {A : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ) (hAd : DifferentiableOn ℂ A (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ))
  (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖A z‖ ≤ M) {ν : ℕ} {F : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ} {V : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν)
  (hAC : ∀ j < ν, AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval (F j) (-1) 1)
  (hderiv : ∀ j < ν, ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ), x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1 → deriv (F j) x = F (j + 1) x)
  (hBV : BoundedVariationOn (F ν) (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) (hV : (eVariationOn (F ν) (Set.Icc (-1) 1)).toReal ≤ V) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) :
  (∀ (n : ℕ),
      2 ≤ n →
        |(∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, (A ↑x).re) - NLAlib.clenshawCurtisRule n fun x => (A ↑x).re| ≤
          64 / 15 * M / (ρ ^ (n - 1) * (ρ ^ 2 - 1))) ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ),
        1 ≤ n →
          |(∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, (A ↑x).re) -
                ∑ i, (∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (v n) i)) * (A ↑(v n i)).re| ≤
            64 / 15 * M / (ρ ^ (2 * n) * (ρ ^ 2 - 1))) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ),
          ν < n →
            2 ≤ n →
              |(∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, F 0 x) - NLAlib.clenshawCurtisRule n (F 0)| ≤
                32 * V / (15 * Real.pi * ↑ν * (↑n - ↑ν) ^ ν)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ),
            1 ≤ n →
              ν < 2 * n + 1 →
                |(∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, F 0 x) -
                      ∑ i, (∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (v n) i)) * F 0 (v n i)| ≤
                  32 * V / (15 * Real.pi * ↑ν * (2 * ↑n + 1 - ↑ν) ^ ν)) ∧
          (∀ (n : ℕ),
              NLAlib.quadratureBvThreshold ν ≤ n →
                |(∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, F 0 x) - NLAlib.clenshawCurtisRule n (F 0)| ≤
                  32 * V / (15 * Real.pi * ↑ν * (2 * ↑n + 1 - ↑ν) ^ ν)) ∧
            Filter.Tendsto (fun n => NLAlib.clenshawCurtisRule n f) Filter.atTop (nhds (∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, f x)) ∧
              Filter.Tendsto
                (fun n => ∑ i, (∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (v n) i)) * f (v n i))
                Filter.atTop (nhds (∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, f x))
name: NLAlib.quadrature_error_bounds_and_continuous_convergence
doc:
Actual Clenshaw–Curtis and Lebesgue Gauss quadrature satisfy all sharp analytic
and BV bounds and converge for every continuous function. Gauss nodes are supplied
through the natural distinct-interior orthogonal-nodal interface; positivity,
reflection and exactness of their integrated cardinal weights are proved from it.
The eventual Clenshaw–Curtis bound uses an explicit sufficient threshold.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 19.3–19.5, official 2013-edition errata to
equations (19.10) and (19.12),
and focused polynomial-approximation reroutes, explicit eventual-bound theorem.

name: NLAlib.range_qrAlgorithmQ_castLE_eq_subspaceIterate
doc:
SCAFFOLD: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration
**The leading columns of `Q^{(k)}` span the subspace iterates of the leading columns of `I`.**
For invertible `A` and `j ≤ n`, the first `j` columns of `Q^{(k)}` span
`S_k(A, I_{:, 1:j}) = range (A^k I_{:, 1:j})`: unshifted QR is simultaneous iteration on all
leading blocks at once. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 28.3 and Lect. 28 (the
"simultaneous iteration" interpretation); Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §7.3.1.
Proof sketch: `A^k E_j = Q^{(k)} R^{(k)} E_j = Q^{(k)}_{:, 1:j} R^{(k)}_{1:j, 1:j}`
(`pow_eq_qrAlgorithmQ_mul_qrAlgorithmR`, `R^{(k)}` upper triangular), and `R^{(k)}_{1:j, 1:j}`
is invertible because `R^{(k)}` is (`det A^k = det Q^{(k)} det R^{(k)} ≠ 0` and the leading
block of an invertible upper triangular matrix is invertible); then
`subspaceIterate_mul_of_isUnit`. Without invertibility only `⊇` holds. Difficulty 2.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

  (P Q : Polynomial 𝕜) (A : Matrix m m 𝕜) (B : Matrix n n 𝕜) (C : Matrix o o 𝕜) (G : Matrix m n 𝕜) (H : Matrix n o 𝕜)

    if ↑i < u.natDegree then (P % u).coeff ↑i else T (Polynomial.X ^ (↑i - u.natDegree) * P)

signature:
NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference_mul.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (P Q R S : Polynomial 𝕜) (A B C G H : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hQA : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval A) Q))
  (hQB : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval B) Q)) (hQC : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval C) Q))
  (hSA : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval A) S)) (hSB : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval B) S))
  (hSC : IsUnit ((Polynomial.aeval C) S)) :
  NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference (P * R) (Q * S) A B C G H =
    NLAlib.rationalMatrixEval P Q A * NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference R S A B C G H +
        NLAlib.rationalBlockDifference P Q A B G * NLAlib.rationalBlockDifference R S B C H +
      NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference P Q A B C G H * NLAlib.rationalMatrixEval R S C

Ordered second block product rule, including the cross insertion in its
specified order. Source: F16.

signature:
NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference_one.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (Q : Polynomial 𝕜) (A B C G H : Matrix n n 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.rationalSecondBlockDifference 1 Q A B C G H =
    ((Polynomial.aeval A) Q)⁻¹ * NLAlib.polynomialBlockDifference Q A B G * ((Polynomial.aeval B) Q)⁻¹ *
          NLAlib.polynomialBlockDifference Q B C H *
        ((Polynomial.aeval C) Q)⁻¹ -
      ((Polynomial.aeval A) Q)⁻¹ * NLAlib.polynomialSecondBlockDifference Q A B C G H * ((Polynomial.aeval C) Q)⁻¹

doc:
Ordered second inverse rule. Source: F17.

signature:
NLAlib.rational_exactness_iff_divided_weights_exactness.{u_1} (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ) (ω : Polynomial ℝ)
  (hω : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂μ, 0 < Polynomial.eval x ω) {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (v w : ι → ℝ)
  (hv : ∀ i ∈ s, Polynomial.eval (v i) ω ≠ 0) (d : ℕ) :
  (∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      p.degree < ↑d →
        ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x p / Polynomial.eval x ω ∂μ =
          ∑ i ∈ s, w i * (Polynomial.eval (v i) p / Polynomial.eval (v i) ω)) ↔
    ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      p.degree < ↑d →
        ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x p ∂NLAlib.dividedPolynomialMeasure μ ω =
          ∑ i ∈ s, w i / Polynomial.eval (v i) ω * Polynomial.eval (v i) p
name: NLAlib.rational_exactness_iff_divided_weights_exactness
doc:
A prescribed rational rule is exact if and only if the weights divided
by the denominator are polynomial-exact for the reciprocal-density measure.
Source: the converse rational Gauss implication; operator derivations AQ36.
atlas: rational-gauss-quadrature (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.rational_gauss_rule_of_positive_denominator {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {a b : ℝ} (hs : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂μ, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) {ω : Polynomial ℝ} (hω : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, 0 < Polynomial.eval x ω)
  {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n) (hn : ↑n ≤ μ.support.encard) :
  let ν := NLAlib.dividedPolynomialMeasure μ ω;
  have hν := ⋯;
  (∀ (i : Fin n),
      NLAlib.gaussNodes ν hν n i ∈ Set.Icc a b ∧
        0 < NLAlib.gaussWeights ν hν n i * Polynomial.eval (NLAlib.gaussNodes ν hν n i) ω) ∧
    ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      p.degree < ↑(2 * n) →
        ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x p / Polynomial.eval x ω ∂μ =
          ∑ i,
            NLAlib.gaussWeights ν hν n i * Polynomial.eval (NLAlib.gaussNodes ν hν n i) ω *
              (Polynomial.eval (NLAlib.gaussNodes ν hν n i) p / Polynomial.eval (NLAlib.gaussNodes ν hν n i) ω)
name: NLAlib.rational_gauss_rule_of_positive_denominator
doc:
The actual Gauss rule of the positive divided measure supplies a rational
rule for the original measure, with real nodes in its support enclosure and
strictly positive multiplied weights. No polynomial-exact rule is assumed.
Source: Gautschi (2004), rational Gauss construction AQ36.
atlas: rational-gauss-quadrature (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.rational_rule_eq_divided_measure_gauss_of_exactness {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {a b : ℝ} (hs : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂μ, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) {ω : Polynomial ℝ}
  (hω : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, 0 < Polynomial.eval x ω) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n) (hn : ↑n ≤ μ.support.encard) (v w : Fin n → ℝ)
  (hv : Function.Injective v)
  (hexact :
    ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      p.degree < ↑(2 * n) →
        ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x p / Polynomial.eval x ω ∂μ =
          ∑ i, w i * (Polynomial.eval (v i) p / Polynomial.eval (v i) ω)) :
  let ν := NLAlib.dividedPolynomialMeasure μ ω;
  have hν := ⋯;
  ∃ e,
    (∀ (i : Fin n), v (e i) = NLAlib.gaussNodes ν hν n i) ∧
      ∀ (i : Fin n), w (e i) / Polynomial.eval (v (e i)) ω = NLAlib.gaussWeights ν hν n i

doc:
Any distinct-node rational rule of the full numerator degree range is the
actual Gauss rule of the reciprocal-density measure after dividing its weights.
Source: Gautschi (2004), rational Gauss converse AQ36.

NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom_eq_sketchedOutput.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3}

The raw generalized Nyström output agrees with the normalized-frame

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (x : n → 𝕜) :
  ℝ
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient
doc:
The Rayleigh quotient `ρ(x) = re (xᴴAx) / re (xᴴx)` (real-valued; junk value `0` at `x = 0`).
It is the quantity of the Rayleigh–Ritz theory only for Hermitian `A` (then `xᴴAx` is real and
`λ_min ≤ ρ(x) ≤ λ_max`); for other `A` it is the real part of the numerical-range value.
Over `ℝ` it is `xᵀAx / xᵀx` (`simp only [rayleighQuotient_def, quadForm_def, star_trivial,
RCLike.re_to_real]`). Source: Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 27. Helper for `power-iteration`; Mathlib's
`ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient` of `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A` agrees with it at `ℝ`
(`rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_eq`).

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_compression.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {Q : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (z : r → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.rayleighQuotient (Q.conjTranspose * A * Q) z = NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A (Q.mulVec z)
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_compression
doc: Rayleigh quotients are preserved by an orthonormal compression.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_def.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜)
  (x : n → 𝕜) : NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A x = RCLike.re (NLAlib.quadForm A x) / RCLike.re (star x ⬝ᵥ x)

A zero subdiagonal boundary of a real normal quasitriangular matrix
separates orthogonal diagonal blocks. Horn–Johnson 2013,

signature:
NLAlib.real_similarity_descent_properties.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A B : ι → Matrix n n ℝ) :
  (∀ (S : Matrix n n ℂ),
      IsUnit S →
        (∀ (i : ι), (A i).map Complex.ofReal = S * (B i).map Complex.ofReal * S⁻¹) →
          ∃ T, IsUnit T ∧ ∀ (i : ι), A i = T * B i * T⁻¹) ∧
    ∀ (U : ↥(Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ)),
      (∀ (i : ι), (A i).map Complex.ofReal = ↑U * (B i).map Complex.ofReal * (↑U).conjTranspose) →
        ∃ Q, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧ ∀ (i : ι), A i = Q * B i * Q.transpose
name: NLAlib.real_similarity_descent_properties
doc:
Both real-descent clauses with their common-family quantifiers:
nonsingular complex similarities descend to nonsingular real similarities,
and unitary complex similarities descend to real orthogonal similarities.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorems 1.3.29 and 2.5.21.

NLAlib.rectSecondMoment.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (Z : Ω → Matrix m n ℂ) : ℝ

doc:
The matrix variance statistic of a rectangular random matrix: `max ‖𝔼 Z Zᴴ‖ ‖𝔼 Zᴴ Z‖` (spectral

signature:
NLAlib.rectSecondMoment_matrixSeries_eq.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (B : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)
  (hSG : ∀ (k : Fin N), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (g k) 1 μ)
  (hVar : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), g k ω ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) :
  (NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ fun ω => ∑ k, g k ω • B k) =
    max (NLAlib.specNorm (∑ k, B k * (B k).conjTranspose)) (NLAlib.specNorm (∑ k, (B k).conjTranspose * B k))

doc:
**Variance of a rectangular series**: for independent centred unit-variance coefficients,
`rectSecondMoment μ (∑ k, g k • B k) = max ‖∑ k, B k * B kᴴ‖ ‖∑ k, B kᴴ * B k‖`. Tropp 2015,
eq. (4.1.3).
atlas: matrix-gaussian-series

signature:
NLAlib.rectSecondMoment_sum_eq.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (S : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (S k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun S μ)
  (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.specNorm (S k ω) ≤ L) :
  (NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ fun ω => ∑ k, S k ω) =
    max (NLAlib.specNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω * (S k ω).conjTranspose ∂μ))

doc:
**Variance of an independent rectangular sum**: for independent, centred, bounded summands,

NLAlib.rectangularDilation_positiveGramRow_affineCombination.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2}

      (B ≤ A ↔ ∃ X, 0 ≤ X ∧ X ≤ 1 ∧ B = CFC.sqrt A * X * CFC.sqrt A) ∧

                B.trace ≤ A.trace ∧

                    (∀ (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)), ⋯.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ k) ∧

definite real first matrix and PSD second matrix, with arbitrary interval
endpoints. Includes square comparison, trace and determinant equality,

matrix is positive definite. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.7.3 and

signature:
NLAlib.residual_eq_mul_conjTranspose_mul_residual.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}

doc:
For a completion `QQᴴ + QpQpᴴ = I` of `Q`, the residual lies in `range Qp`:
`(I − QQᴴ)A = Qp (Qpᴴ (I − QQᴴ)A)`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.4; atlas `projection-facts`.

signature:
NLAlib.residual_eq_of_range_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {k₂ : Type u_4} [Fintype k₂] [DecidableEq k₂] {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  {P : Matrix n k₂ ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hP : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P)

name: NLAlib.residual_eq_of_range_eq
doc:
The residual depends only on the range of the orthonormal frame: if `range Q = range P`
then `(I − QQᵀ) X = (I − PPᵀ) X`. Helper for `principal-angles-def` (belongs in
`NLAlib.Matrix.Subspaces.Projections`).

name: NLAlib.residual_eq_one_sub_mul
doc: `projResidual Q A = (I − QQᴴ) A`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.residual_mul
doc:
The residual commutes with right multiplication: `((I − QQᴴ)A) Ω = (I − QQᴴ)(AΩ)`.
Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.residual_mul_eq_zero_of_range
doc:
If `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, written `Q (Qᴴ (AΩ)) = AΩ`, then `(I − QQᴴ) A Ω = 0`.
This is how `Q = orth(AΩ)` enters the range-finder analysis (HMT 2011, proof of Thm 9.1).
No orthonormality is needed. Over `ℝ` the hypothesis may be given as `Q (Qᵀ (AΩ)) = AΩ`.
Atlas `projection-facts`.
atlas: projection-facts

name: NLAlib.residual_residual

Projecting the residual again changes nothing: `(I − QQᴴ)² A = (I − QQᴴ) A`.
Atlas `projection-facts`.

signature:
NLAlib.resolventCubicRemainder.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A₀ D F : Matrix n n ℂ) (a : ℝ)
  (ζ : ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ
name: NLAlib.resolventCubicRemainder
doc:
The six ordered cubic resolvent words obtained by comparing two directional
resolvent derivatives at the common third base. The three bases are `A₀`,
`A₀ - a • D` and `A₀ - a • F`, with the third direction `F - D`.
The definition is total; Hermiticity and a nonreal shift are hypotheses of
its cancellation and norm theorems.
Source: Brailovskaya--van Handel, arXiv:2201.05142v3 (2024), §6.4,
proof of Lemma 6.11.

name: NLAlib.resolventEvenMoment

The actual normalized even resolvent moment. The Gram product makes the
positivity visible without choosing eigenvectors.

signature:
NLAlib.resolventEvenMoment_eq_re_normalizedTrace_mul_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
The actual even resolvent Gram moment equals the mixed native resolvent
trace at the spectral parameter and its conjugate. The identity includes
empty dimensions and spectral parameters on the real spectrum.
Source: Brailovskaya–van Handel, arXiv:2201.05142v3, Lemma 6.9.

doc:
The native Gram trace is exactly the unnormalized even Schatten power
divided by dimension. The empty dimension has value zero on both sides.

NLAlib.resolventEvenMoment_le_inv_abs_im_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ)

Hermitian nonreal resolvents give a uniform bound for every actual
normalized even moment. The bound is independent of the matrix entries.

NLAlib.resolventEvenMoment_le_specNorm_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (ζ : ℂ)

A positive-order normalized trace moment is bounded by the corresponding
spectral-norm power.

name: NLAlib.resolventEvenMoment_nonneg
doc:
Positive-order normalized resolvent moments are nonnegative, including

exact dimension factor, including the native zero-over-zero empty convention.

Two directional resolvent derivatives differ by the common quadratic
term and six explicit cubic words. Every factor is the actual resolvent of a

matrix concentration inequalities*, arXiv:2201.05142v3 (2024), §6.4, proof
of Lemma 6.11, with the exact ordered remainder made explicit.

signature:
NLAlib.richardsonIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (ω : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.richardsonIterate
doc:
The Richardson iterate with step `ω`: `x_q = x₀ + ω ∑_{j<q} (I − ωA)^j r₀`, the polynomial
method with residual polynomial `(1 − ωX)^q`; it satisfies `x_{q+1} = x_q + ω (c − A x_q)`
(`richardsonIterate_succ`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2; Greenbaum (1997)
[`greenbaum97`], §2.1. Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`).
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.richardsonIterate_succ.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (ω : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.richardsonIterate ω A c x₀ (q + 1) =
    NLAlib.richardsonIterate ω A c x₀ q + ω • (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.richardsonIterate ω A c x₀ q))
name: NLAlib.richardsonIterate_succ
doc:
**Richardson recurrence.** `x_{q+1} = x_q + ω (c − A x_q)`, `x_0 = x₀`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.

signature:
NLAlib.richardsonIterate_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (ω : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.richardsonIterate ω A c x₀ 0 = x₀
name: NLAlib.richardsonIterate_zero
doc: `richardsonIterate` at `q = 0` is the starting point.

Changing the orthonormal basis of a trial space preserves the entire ordered Ritz
spectrum, including multiplicities and empty spaces. Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1.

name: NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix
doc:
The half-index cotangent prefix on the root sampling grid.
Source: focused reroutes, equation `polyretry:sample-C`.

NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_reflect {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hr : r ≤ 2 * N) :
  NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N (2 * N - r) = NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N r
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_reflect
doc:
A cotangent prefix reflected around a full period has the same value.
Source: focused reroutes, the finite identity `C_(N+r)=C_(N−r)`.

NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_sub_complement {N r : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hr : r ≤ N) :
  NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N N - NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N (N - r) =
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range r, Real.tan ((↑j + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (2 * ↑N))
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_sub_complement
doc:
The last `r` terms of a half-period prefix sum to its first `r` tangent terms.
Source: focused reroutes, finite cotangent-complement reflection.

signature:
NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_succ (N r : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N (r + 1) = NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N r + ((↑r + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (2 * ↑N)).cot
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_succ
doc:
Prefix values change by the next half-index cotangent.
Source: the defining finite prefix sum.

signature: NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_two_mul_eq_zero {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) : NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix N (2 * N) = 0
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentPrefix_two_mul_eq_zero
doc:
A full cotangent prefix period sums to zero.
Source: focused reroutes, finite cotangent-prefix reflection.

signature: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample (N k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample
doc:
The cotangent prefix expression for the `k`th root-grid extremum sample.
Source: focused reroutes, equation `polyretry:sample-C`.

signature:
NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_center_eq {N : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) :
  NLAlib.rootCotangentSample N (N / 2) =
    2 / ↑N * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N / 2), ((↑j + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / ↑N).cot +
      if Odd N then 1 / ↑N * Real.tan (Real.pi / (4 * ↑N)) else 0
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_center_eq
doc:
The central cotangent-prefix sample has the finite double-angle sum and the
odd tangent correction. Source: focused reroutes, equation `polyretry:central-cot`.

NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_center_le {N k : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hk0 : 1 ≤ k) (hkN : k < N) :

name: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_center_le
doc:
The central cotangent-prefix sample is smallest among all interior indices.
Source: focused reroutes, sample symmetry and midpoint convexity.

signature:
NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_reflect {N k : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hk : k ≤ N) :

name: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_reflect
doc:
Reflection of an interior sample index preserves its cotangent-prefix expression.
Source: focused reroutes, root-grid sample reflection.

signature:
NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_sub_succ {N k : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hk : k < N / 2) :
  ↑N * (NLAlib.rootCotangentSample N (k + 1) - NLAlib.rootCotangentSample N k) =
    2 * ((↑(2 * k) + 1) * Real.pi / (2 * ↑N)).cot - ((↑(2 * k) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (2 * ↑N)).cot -

name: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_sub_succ
doc:
Adjacent sample expressions have the finite midpoint-convexity difference.
Source: focused reroutes, the difference after equation `polyretry:sample-C`.

signature:
NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_succ_le {N k : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hk : k < N / 2) :
  NLAlib.rootCotangentSample N (k + 1) ≤ NLAlib.rootCotangentSample N k
name: NLAlib.rootCotangentSample_succ_le
doc:
An adjacent root sample does not increase on the first half of the grid.
Source: focused reroutes, cotangent midpoint convexity.

RSVD; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case): if `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix,

are arbitrary.

signature:
NLAlib.semidefinite_pair_congruence_normal_form.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (hB : B.PosSemidef) :
  ∃ S a b,
    IsUnit S ∧
      A = S * Matrix.diagonal a * S.transpose ∧
        B = S * Matrix.diagonal b * S.transpose ∧
          (∀ (i : n), a i = 0 ∨ a i = 1) ∧
            (∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ b i) ∧
              (∀ (i : n), a i = 0 → b i = 0 ∨ b i = 1) ∧
                A.rank = Fintype.card { i // a i = 1 } ∧
                  (A + B).rank = Fintype.card { i // a i = 1 } + Fintype.card { i // a i = 0 ∧ b i = 1 } ∧
                    Module.finrank ℝ ↥(A.mulVecLin.ker ⊓ B.mulVecLin.ker) = Fintype.card { i // a i = 0 ∧ b i = 0 }
name: NLAlib.semidefinite_pair_congruence_normal_form
doc:
Full singular PSD-pair normal form with exact three-block dimensions.
The first block is indexed by `a=1`, the second by `a=0,b=1`, and the third
by `a=b=0`; thus coordinate reordering gives `(I_r,0_s,0_t)` and
`(diag(beta),I_s,0_t)`. The identities identify `r=rank A`,
`r+s=rank(A+B)`, and `t=dim(ker A ∩ ker B)`, including all empty blocks.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.6.

  (hA₀ : A₀.IsHermitian) (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (hA : ∀ (i : ι), (A i).IsHermitian) (q : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ) (hζ : ζ.im ≠ 0) :

      ∫ (x : NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n → ℝ),
        resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x)

            NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient A q k * resolvent (NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteInterpolation A₀ A q x) ζ *
              NLAlib.gaussianFreeFiniteCoefficient A q k) *

            ζ ∂NLAlib.gaussianVector (NLAlib.GaussianFreeFiniteCoordinate ι n)

  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues k

doc: Bridge to Mathlib's `LinearMap.singularValues` (definitional). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_eq_mul_rectDiag_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜} {V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜}
  {τ : ℕ → ℝ} (hU : U.conjTranspose * U = 1) (hV : V.conjTranspose * V = 1) (hτ0 : ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 ≤ τ k) (hτ : Antitone τ)
  (hA : A = U * NLAlib.rectDiag τ * V.conjTranspose) {k : ℕ} (hk : k < min p q)
  (hq : Fintype.card n = q := by
    first
    | exact Fintype.card_fin _
    | rfl) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = τ k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_eq_mul_rectDiag_mul
doc:
**Uniqueness of singular values** (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3): if `A = U Σ_τ Vᴴ` with
`U`, `V` having orthonormal columns, `V` square (`q = card n`, discharged automatically for
`V : Matrix (Fin b) (Fin b) 𝕜` and `V : Matrix n (Fin (card n)) 𝕜`) and `τ` nonnegative and
non-increasing, then `τ k = σ_k(A)` for every `k < min p q`. Atlas `svd`.
atlas: svd

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_gram_charpoly_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}
  {n : Type u_3} {p : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜)
  (B : Matrix p n 𝕜) (h : (A.conjTranspose * A).charpoly = (B.conjTranspose * B).charpoly) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = NLAlib.singularValues B k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_gram_charpoly_eq
doc:
Matrices with the same column type whose Gram matrices `AᴴA`, `BᴴB` have equal
characteristic polynomials have equal zero-padded singular values, with possibly different
row types. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.6.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_gram_eq
doc:
Equal Gram matrices give exactly equal zero-padded singular values, on arbitrary finite
indices, with possibly different row types. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_qr.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

  (hFactor : Q * R = A) : NLAlib.singularValues R = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_qr
doc:
The zero-padded singular values of the triangular QR factor are exactly those of the
original matrix at every index, on arbitrary finite indices.
Trefethen--Bau, Theorem 7.1; Golub--Van Loan, Theorem 5.2.1.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_one_of_hasOrthonormalCols {m n : ℕ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}

name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_one_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
A real isometry has singular value one at every thin index, including
the zero-dimensional case as an empty assertion. Horn–Johnson §7.3.1.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_height_le
doc: `σ k = 0` once `k` is at least the number of rows. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_min_le
doc: `σ k = 0` once `k ≥ min (card m) (card n)`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_rank_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_width_le

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_gram_pow_mul {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (q j : ℕ) :

name: NLAlib.singularValues_gram_pow_mul
doc:
Odd rectangular Gram powers raise every singular value to the corresponding odd
power. Source: HMT (2011), §10.4.
The identity is zero-indexed and includes zero padding beyond the finite list.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_isometry_mul
doc:
Left multiplication by a matrix `H` with orthonormal columns (`HᴴH = 1`; e.g. a unitary
matrix) preserves every singular value, including the padded zeros (Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3):
the Gram matrices agree. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_last_eq_iInf.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card n - 1) = ⨅ x, ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (A.mulVec ↑x)‖
name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_eq_iInf
doc:
**Variational form of the smallest singular value.** For `A : Matrix m n 𝕜`,
`σ_{card n - 1}(A) = inf { ‖Ax‖₂ : ‖x‖₂ = 1 }` (the last singular value in the list indexed by
the number of columns; for a wide matrix both sides are `0`, and for an empty `n` both sides are
`0` by the real convention `inf ∅ = 0`). Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.3.8; proved from the Rayleigh
characterisation of the smallest eigenvalue of `AᴴA`.
atlas: svd

name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_le_norm_mulVec
doc:
`σ_min(A) ≤ ‖Ax‖₂` for every unit vector `x` (with `σ_min = singularValues A (card n - 1)`).
Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.3.8.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_mul_norm_le
doc: `σ_min(A) ‖x‖₂ ≤ ‖Ax‖₂` for every vector `x`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.3.8.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_last_pos_iff_isUnit.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (C : Matrix n n 𝕜) : 0 < NLAlib.singularValues C (Fintype.card n - 1) ↔ IsUnit C
name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_pos_iff_isUnit
doc:
A square matrix on a nonempty index type has positive smallest singular value exactly when it
is invertible. Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_last_pos_iff_rank_eq_card.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_3} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (hn : 0 < Fintype.card n) :
  0 < NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card n - 1) ↔ A.rank = Fintype.card n
name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_pos_iff_rank_eq_card
doc:
The last singular value in the list indexed by the number of columns is positive exactly
when the matrix has full column rank (`rank A = card n`, with at least one column).
Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_last_shift_le_iff_spectrum_or_resolvent.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_shift_le_iff_spectrum_or_resolvent
doc:
The closed positive-radius pseudospectrum has the usual resolvent norm
description, with eigenvalues explicitly included. The total inverse's
singular junk value never decides membership.
atlas: pseudospectrum-perturbation-equivalence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_last_shift_le_specNorm_of_mem_spectrum.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.singularValues_last_shift_le_specNorm_of_mem_spectrum
doc:
Every perturbation producing the requested eigenvalue has norm at
least the smallest singular value of the original shifted matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_le_of_forall_mem.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_3} {n : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (k : ℕ) (W : Submodule 𝕜 (n → 𝕜))
  (hW : Fintype.card n ≤ Module.finrank 𝕜 ↥W + k) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (hAW : ∀ x ∈ W, RCLike.re (star (A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x) ≤ c ^ 2 * RCLike.re (star x ⬝ᵥ x)) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k ≤ c
name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_of_forall_mem
doc:
**Courant–Fischer for singular values, min-max half.** If `‖Ax‖² ≤ c² ‖x‖²` on a subspace
`W ⊆ 𝕜ⁿ` of codimension at most `k`, then `σ_k(A) ≤ c` (zero-indexed), on arbitrary finite
index types. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3 (Thm 7.3.8). atlas
`courant-fischer`. The hypothesis `0 ≤ c` covers `k ≥ card n`, where `σ_k = 0`.
atlas: courant-fischer

name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_singularValues_add_add_specNorm
doc:
**Weyl perturbation bound, lower side.** `σ_k(A) ≤ σ_k(A + E) + ‖E‖₂`. Horn–Johnson 2013,
§7.3 (Cor 7.3.5). Atlas `weyl-mirsky`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_le_specNorm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_3} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.singularValues A k ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_specNorm
doc:
Every padded singular value is bounded by the spectral norm, on arbitrary finite index
types and over `ℝ` or `ℂ`. Horn–Johnson §5.6; atlas `norms-frob-spec`, `svd`.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_specNorm_sub_of_rank_le
doc:
**Spectral Eckart–Young, lower bound.** Every competitor of rank at most `k` has spectral
error at least `σ_k(A)` (zero-indexed): `σ_k(A) ≤ ‖A − B‖₂`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.9.1
(spectral case); HMT 2011, eq. (2.3) atlas `eckart-young`.
atlas: eckart-young

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_le_submatrix_cols.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq p] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (f : p → n)
  (hf : Function.Injective f) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A (k + (Fintype.card n - Fintype.card p)) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues (A.submatrix id f) k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_submatrix_cols
doc:
Deleting columns shifts the lower singular-value bound by the number
of omitted columns. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 7.3.6.
atlas: singular-value-interlacing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_le_submatrix_rows.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (f : p → m) (hf : Function.Injective f)
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.singularValues A (k + (Fintype.card m - Fintype.card p)) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues (A.submatrix f id) k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_submatrix_rows
doc:
Deleting rows shifts the lower singular-value bound by exactly the
number of omitted rows. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 7.3.6.
atlas: singular-value-interlacing (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_map_ofReal.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (A.map ⇑(algebraMap ℝ 𝕜)) k = NLAlib.singularValues A k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_map_ofReal
doc:
Extending a real matrix to `𝕜` (`ℝ` or `ℂ`) entrywise preserves every singular value,
including the padded zeros: no dimension doubling. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_mul_add_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype p]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq p] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m p ℝ) (B : Matrix p n ℝ) (i j : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (A * B) (i + j) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A i * NLAlib.singularValues B j
name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_add_le
doc:
Weyl's product inequality `σ_{i+j}(AB) ≤ σ_i(A) σ_j(B)`, with zero-indexed singular values
extended by zero, on arbitrary finite real matrix indices.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 3.3.16(d); empty dimensions and arbitrary indices are allowed, with no
dimension or rank side condition.
atlas: weyl-product-singular-values

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_mul_isometry_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}
  {n : Type u_3} {p : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq p]
  {H : Matrix n p 𝕜} (hH : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols H) (A : Matrix m p 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (A * H.conjTranspose) = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_isometry_conjTranspose
doc:
Right multiplication by the conjugate transpose of a matrix `H` with orthonormal columns
(`HᴴH = 1`) preserves every singular value, including the padded zeros (Horn–Johnson 2013,
§7.3). Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_le_mul_specNorm
doc:
**Right multiplication.** `σ_k(AC) ≤ σ_k(A) ‖C‖₂`. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3. Proof: the
preimage under `C` of the min-max subspace of `A` has codimension at most `k` atlas `weyl-mirsky`.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_le_specNorm_mul
doc:
**Left multiplication.** `σ_k(BA) ≤ ‖B‖₂ σ_k(A)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3; Bhatia 1997,
§III.6 (the special case `i = 0` of `σ_{i+j}(BA) ≤ σ_i(B) σ_j(A)`). Atlas `weyl-mirsky`.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_mul_pow_conjTranspose_pow.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {B : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hB : Commute B B.conjTranspose) (a b : ℕ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (B ^ a * B.conjTranspose ^ b) ↑i = NLAlib.singularValues B ↑i ^ (a + b)
name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_pow_conjTranspose_pow
doc:
Mixed normal-matrix powers raise every in-dimension singular value to
the total degree. The Fin index is essential at degree zero: singular values
outside the matrix dimension are zero, whereas scalar x^0 is one.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_mul_unitary.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) {V : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hV : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (A * V) = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_unitary
doc:
Right multiplication by a unitary matrix `V` (`VᴴV = 1`) preserves every singular value,
including the padded zeros (Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_ne_zero_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

name: NLAlib.singularValues_ne_zero_iff
doc:
The nonzero singular values are exactly the first `rank A` ones
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_neg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : NLAlib.singularValues (-A) = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_neg
doc: Negation leaves every zero-padded singular value unchanged.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_nonneg.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_nonneg
doc: Singular values are nonnegative. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_oblique_canonical {r s : ℕ} (t : ℕ → ℝ) (ht0 : ∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) (ht : Antitone t)
  (hz : ∀ (i : ℕ), min r s ≤ i → t i = 0) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (NLAlib.rectDiag t) 0 0) k = if k < r then √(1 + t k ^ 2) else 0

doc:
The actual singular values of the oblique block matrix are
`sqrt(1+t_i²)` on its range block and zero afterwards. All multiplicities,
zero coefficients and empty blocks are included. Horn–Johnson 2013,
Corollary 3.4.3.3; supports `cs-decomposition`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_one_sub_oblique_canonical {r s : ℕ} (t : ℕ → ℝ) (ht0 : ∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) (ht : Antitone t)
  (hz : ∀ (i : ℕ), min r s ≤ i → t i = 0) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (1 - Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (NLAlib.rectDiag t) 0 0) k = if k < s then √(1 + t k ^ 2) else 0
name: NLAlib.singularValues_one_sub_oblique_canonical
doc:
The complementary oblique block matrix has the same nontrivial singular
values with the range/kernel sizes exchanged. This includes either empty block.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; supports `cs-decomposition`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_pos_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (k : ℕ) : 0 < NLAlib.singularValues A k ↔ k < A.rank
name: NLAlib.singularValues_pos_iff
doc: The positive singular values are exactly the first `rank A` ones. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_reindex.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} {q : Type u_4}

  NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex em en) A) = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_reindex
doc:
Relabeling the rows and columns of a matrix (over `ℝ` or `ℂ`) by equivalences preserves
every singular value, including the padded zeros. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.6, unitary
coordinate changes (permutation matrices).

name: NLAlib.singularValues_residual_le
doc:
**Projection does not increase singular values.** For `Q` with orthonormal columns,
`σ_k((I − QQᴴ)A) ≤ σ_k(A)`. HMT 2011, §8.4 (used in Prop 8.6 and Thm 9.2)
atlas `weyl-mirsky`, `projection-facts`.
atlas: projection-facts

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_resolvent_pow_mul_resolvent_star_pow.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (ζ : 𝕜) (a b : ℕ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :

    NLAlib.singularValues (resolvent A ζ) ↑i ^ (a + b)
name: NLAlib.singularValues_resolvent_pow_mul_resolvent_star_pow
doc:
Each in-dimension singular value of a mixed native resolvent power is the
corresponding resolvent singular value raised to its total degree.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_rpow_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.singularValues_rpow_of_posSemidef
doc:
A nonnegative real functional-calculus power raises each positive-matrix
singular value to that power, with the usual scalar zero-power convention.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_smul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (c : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.singularValues (c • A) k = |c| * NLAlib.singularValues A k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_smul
doc:
Singular values are absolutely homogeneous over real scalars, including
zero scalars, zero ranks and empty dimensions. Horn–Johnson (2013), §2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.singular_subspace_perturbation_bounds {m n k : ℕ} {A E : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {U Uhat : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} {V Vhat : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V)
  (hhat : NLAlib.IsSVD (A + E) Uhat Vhat) (hk : k ≤ min m n) :
  have U₁ := NLAlib.headColumns U ⋯;
  have V₁ := NLAlib.headColumns V ⋯;
  have Uhat₁ := NLAlib.headColumns Uhat ⋯;
  have Vhat₁ := NLAlib.headColumns Vhat ⋯;
  have T := Matrix.diagonal fun i => NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) ↑i;
  have R := A * Vhat₁ - Uhat₁ * T;
  have S := A.transpose * Uhat₁ - Vhat₁ * T;
  have δ := NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) (k - 1) - NLAlib.singularValues A k;
  have g := NLAlib.singularValues A (k - 1) - NLAlib.singularValues A k;
  R = -(E * Vhat₁) ∧
    S = -(E.transpose * Uhat₁) ∧
      max (NLAlib.specNorm R) (NLAlib.specNorm S) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E ∧
        (0 < δ →
            max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁))
                  (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁)) ≤
                max (NLAlib.specNorm R) (NLAlib.specNorm S) / δ ∧
              max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁))
                    (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁)) ≤
                  NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
                √(NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁) ^ 2 +
                      NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁) ^ 2) ≤
                  √(NLAlib.frobNorm R ^ 2 + NLAlib.frobNorm S ^ 2) / δ) ∧
          (0 < g →
              max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁))
                  (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁)) ≤
                2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / g) ∧
            (k = 0 →
              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁) = 0 ∧
                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁) = 0 ∧
                  NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁) = 0 ∧
                    NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁) = 0)
name: NLAlib.singular_subspace_perturbation_bounds
doc:
Every Wedin conclusion for leading singular-vector frames, including
the exact perturbation residuals, constant-one mixed-gap operator and paired
Frobenius bounds, constant-two population-gap operator bound without a
perturbation smallness premise, and the zero-width endpoint. Wedin (1972),
Section 3; Stewart–Sun, Theorem V.4.4. Rectangular full-thin endpoints use the
zero-padded next singular value and arbitrary valid SVD choices are accepted.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta

name: NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_p
doc:
**The search directions span the Krylov space**: for `A ≻ 0` and every `k`,
`span (p_0, …, p_{k−1}) = K_k(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1,
eq. (38.2). Proof: `span_cgRecurrence_p_eq_span_r` and `span_cgRecurrence_r`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_p_eq_span_r.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ ↑i).p) =
    Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ ↑i).r)
name: NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_p_eq_span_r
doc:
**Search directions and residuals span the same spaces**: `span (p_0, …, p_{k−1}) =
span (r_0, …, r_{k−1})` for every `A` and `k` (no hypothesis). Induction on `k` with
`p_k − r_k = β_{k−1} p_{k−1}`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1, eq. (38.2).
Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_r
doc:
**The residuals span the Krylov space**: for `A ≻ 0` and every `k`,
`span (r_0, …, r_{k−1}) = K_k(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1,
eq. (38.2); Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.20. Proof: `≤` from `cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace`;
for `k ≤ ν` the residuals are nonzero (`cgRecurrence_r_ne_zero_of_lt_krylovGrade`) and
orthogonal (`dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero`), hence independent, and both sides have
dimension `k` (`finrank_krylovSpace`); for `k ≥ ν`, `K_k = K_ν`
(`krylovSpace_eq_of_krylovGrade_le`). Deviation: stated for every `k`, not only while `r_k ≠ 0`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

**Spectral norm from a net (operator form).** If `N` is an `ε`-net of the unit sphere

(deterministic half).

terms of the identity is bounded separately; `‖I - AA⁺‖, ‖I - B⁺B‖ ≤ 1`).

          (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E)) ^ 2) *
      NLAlib.specNorm E
name: NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_add_sub_le_three_mul_max

Pseudoinverse perturbation bound with the constant `3` and no rank assumption:
`‖(A + E)⁺ - A⁺‖₂ ≤ 3 max(‖A⁺‖₂², ‖(A + E)⁺‖₂²) ‖E‖₂`. Wedin 1973, Thm 4.1 with `μ = 3`;
Stewart–Sun 1990, Thm III.3.8 (the constant for a general unitarily invariant norm; the sharp
spectral constant `(1 + √5)/2` is `specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_sub_le_goldenRatio_max_sq`).
atlas: pseudoinverse-perturbation (partial)
