zero and the reciprocal of the smallest positive singular value otherwise (empty dimensions are
the rank-zero branch). Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.
atlas: pseudoinverse

doc:
For positive rank, the spectral norm of the Moore–Penrose inverse is the reciprocal of the
smallest positive singular value, at index `rank A - 1`, for rank-deficient as well as full-rank
matrices on arbitrary finite index types. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.
atlas: pseudoinverse

NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_le_div_of_rank_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

perturbation: `‖B⁺‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁺‖₂ / (1 - ‖A⁺‖₂ ‖B - A‖₂)`. Wedin 1973, §4; Stewart–Sun 1990,

arbitrary finite row/column labels are included.
atlas: pseudoinverse-perturbation (partial)

doc:
The squared spectral norm of the general inverse equals the spectral
norm of the general inverse of the row Gram matrix `A Aᴴ`, at every rank.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

matrix concentration inequalities*, arXiv:2201.05142v3 (2024), §6.4, proof
of Lemma 6.11, with the six ordered words and constants made explicit.

strength-preserving aggregate squared-sum bound. There is no independence or

arbitrary because its square is retained explicitly.

matrix concentration inequalities*, arXiv:2201.05142v3 (2024), §6.4, proof of Lemma 6.11.

signature:
NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_eq_div.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {Q Q' : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q')
  (hC : IsUnit (Q.transpose * Q')) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q Q' ^ 2 = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' ^ 2 / (1 - NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_eq_div
doc:
**`tan² = sin²/(1 − sin²)`.** For `Q`, `Q'` with orthonormal columns indexed by the same `k`
and `QᵀQ'` invertible: `tan² θ_max = sin² θ_max/(1 − sin² θ_max)`. Source: Golub–Van Loan
(2013) [`gvl13`], §2.5.3 and §8.2.4; Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`], §I.5. Proof sketch: with
`C = QᵀQ'` and `S = (I − QQᵀ)Q'`, `CᵀC + SᵀS = I`; for `v = Cw`,
`‖S C⁻¹ v‖²/‖v‖² = t/(1 − t)` with `t = ‖Sw‖²/‖w‖²`, which is increasing in `t`; the maximum
of `t` is `sin² θ_max`. (When `QᵀQ'` is singular, `tan` has the junk value `0`.)
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_replicateCol_eq_overlapTangentSq
doc:
The total one-column inverse-overlap norm squared is the vector's total

vanishes. Source: Saad (2011), §5.2 and §6.6.1; matrix-toolkit derivations, §1.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

order: `σ_k² = λ_k(AᴴA)` for `k < card n`, with Mathlib's sorted
`Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀` (Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6). For real matrices `Aᴴ = Aᵀ`
(`Matrix.conjTranspose_eq_transpose_of_trivial`). Atlas `svd`.

Atlas `sigma-tail-bound` (uses `svd`).

NLAlib.sqrt_pinv_residual_sub_div_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A E : Matrix m n ℝ) (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (b f : m → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hE : NLAlib.specNorm E ≤ ε * NLAlib.specNorm A) (hf : √(f ⬝ᵥ f) ≤ ε * √(b ⬝ᵥ b))
  (hsmall : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε < 1) :
  √((b - A.mulVec ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b) -
            (b + f - (A + E).mulVec ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E)).mulVec (b + f)))) ⬝ᵥ
          (b - A.mulVec ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b) -
            (b + f - (A + E).mulVec ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E)).mulVec (b + f))))) /
      √(b ⬝ᵥ b) ≤
    (1 + 2 * NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A) * ε
name: NLAlib.sqrt_pinv_residual_sub_div_le
doc:
**Wedin's least-squares bound (residual).** Higham's finite residual bound in ordinary
coordinates, including zero data: under the hypotheses of `sqrt_pinv_solution_sub_div_le`,
`‖r - s‖/‖b‖ ≤ (1 + 2κ(A)) ε`. Higham 2002, Theorem 20.1; Wedin 1973, §5. Transports the
stronger Euclidean coefficient `1+κ`.
atlas: least-squares-perturbation (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.sqrt_pinv_solution_sub_div_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A E : Matrix m n ℝ) (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (b f : m → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hE : NLAlib.specNorm E ≤ ε * NLAlib.specNorm A) (hf : √(f ⬝ᵥ f) ≤ ε * √(b ⬝ᵥ b))
  (hsmall : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε < 1) :
  √(((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b - (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E)).mulVec (b + f)) ⬝ᵥ
          ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b - (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E)).mulVec (b + f))) /
      √((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b) ≤
    NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε / (1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε) *
      (2 +
        (NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A + 1) *
            √((b - A.mulVec ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b)) ⬝ᵥ
                (b - A.mulVec ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b))) /
          (NLAlib.specNorm A * √((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b)))
name: NLAlib.sqrt_pinv_solution_sub_div_le
doc:
**Wedin's least-squares bound (solution).** Higham's finite relative least-squares solution
bound in ordinary coordinates, with total division covering a zero old solution: for full column
rank `A`, `x = A⁺ b`, `r = b - A x`, `‖E‖₂ ≤ ε‖A‖₂`, `‖f‖ ≤ ε‖b‖` and `κ(A) ε < 1`,
`‖x - y‖/‖x‖ ≤ κε/(1 - κε) · (2 + (κ + 1) ‖r‖/(‖A‖₂‖x‖))` for `y = (A + E)⁺(b + f)`.
Higham 2002, Theorem 20.1 (from Wedin 1973, §5); first-order form Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Thm 5.3.1. Transports `norm_least_squares_sub_div_le`.
atlas: least-squares-perturbation (partial)

the left side is `≤ 0` and the bound is trivial. Source: Vershynin 2012, Thm 5.32 (lower half);

`GaussianMatrix.gordon_lower`.

signature:
NLAlib.stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_eq_integral {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  (hμ : NLAlib.HasPolynomialMoments μ) {a b : ℝ} (hs : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂μ, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n)
  (hn : ↑n ≤ μ.support.encard) {z : ℂ} (hz : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, z ≠ ↑x) :
  NLAlib.stieltjesTransform μ z -
      Polynomial.eval z
          (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.secondKindPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) /
        Polynomial.eval z
          (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) =
    (∫ (x : ℝ),
        Polynomial.eval (↑x)
            (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) /
          (z - ↑x) ∂μ) /
      Polynomial.eval z
        (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n))
name: NLAlib.stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_eq_integral
doc:
Subtracting the finite second-kind ratio from the native transform is the
native Cauchy transform of the monic polynomial divided by its value at `z`.
Source: Gautschi (2004), Chapter 1, first equality in AQ19.
atlas: jacobi-fraction-second-kind (partial), gauss-remainder-contour-kernel (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_eq_integral_sq {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  (hμ : NLAlib.HasPolynomialMoments μ) {a b : ℝ} (hs : ∀ᵐ (x : ℝ) ∂μ, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n)
  (hn : ↑n ≤ μ.support.encard) {z : ℂ} (hz : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, z ≠ ↑x) :
  NLAlib.stieltjesTransform μ z -
      Polynomial.eval z
          (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.secondKindPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) /
        Polynomial.eval z
          (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) =
    (∫ (x : ℝ),
        Polynomial.eval (↑x)
              (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) ^
            2 /
          (z - ↑x) ∂μ) /
      Polynomial.eval z
          (Polynomial.map Complex.ofRealHom (NLAlib.monicOrthogonalPolynomial (NLAlib.polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n)) ^
        2
name: NLAlib.stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_eq_integral_sq
doc:
Polynomial orthogonality turns the native Stieltjes error into the exact
positive-norm numerator integral. Source: Gautschi (2004), Chapter 1, AQ19.
atlas: jacobi-fraction-second-kind (partial), gauss-remainder-contour-kernel (partial)

      (S.mulVec ((1 / 2) • (u - v)) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec ((1 / 2) • (u - v)) - (1 / 2) • (u - v) ⬝ᵥ (1 / 2) • (u - v)) =

signature:
NLAlib.sub_eval_interpolate_eq_circleIntegral.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → ℂ)
  (hv : Set.InjOn v ↑s) {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c x : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (Metric.ball c R))
  (hvR : ∀ i ∈ s, v i ∈ Metric.ball c R) (hx : x ∈ Metric.ball c R) :
  f x - Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate s v) (f ∘ v)) =

injectively, hence onto, itself, and `r₀ = A (x⋆ − x₀)` lies in it.

eigenvector for the eigenvalue at sorted position `i₀`, let `|g| ≤ M` at every other sorted

orthogonal to `u` is at most `M` times that of `v`: `‖w‖² − (u ⬝ w)² ≤ M² (‖v‖² − (u ⬝ v)²)`.

NLAlib.submatrix_eq_fromBlocks_of_isolated_coordinate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]

Splitting an isolated coordinate from its complement gives a scalar/direct-sum block matrix. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Lemma 6.3.10;
the two subtype blocks are the distinguished coordinate and all others.

signature:

doc:
Any perturbation matrix decomposes into its leading scalar, row,
column and trailing block in the isolated-coordinate split.
Horn–Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 6.3.12.

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] (A : Matrix n n K) (Ω : Matrix n s K) (k : ℕ) : Submodule K (n → K)
name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate
doc:
The `k`-th subspace iterate `S_k = range (A^k Ω)` of subspace (orthogonal, simultaneous)
iteration started from the block `Ω`, over any field `K`. Orthonormalisation is bookkeeping: any
`Q` with `range Q = S_k` is a basis the algorithm may carry (`range_mul_eq_subspaceIterate_succ`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.1; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.4.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate_eq_range_graph.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ}
  {U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ} {L₁ Linv : Matrix k k ℝ} {L₂ : Matrix r r ℝ} (hA₁ : A * U₁ = U₁ * L₁) (hA₂ : A * U₂ = U₂ * L₂)
  {Ω : Matrix n k ℝ} {Ω₁ R : Matrix k k ℝ} {Ω₂ : Matrix r k ℝ} (hΩ : Ω = U₁ * Ω₁ + U₂ * Ω₂) (hR : Ω₁ * R = 1)
  (hL : L₁ * Linv = 1) (t : ℕ) : NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω t = (U₁ + U₂ * (L₂ ^ t * Ω₂ * R * Linv ^ t)).mulVecLin.range
name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_eq_range_graph
doc:
Right normalization gives the exact graph of every subspace iterate.
Source: manuscript `sa:graph`; Saad (2011), §5.1. Right inverses are explicit data.

name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_le_blockKrylovSpace
doc:
Subspace iteration is block Krylov with the fixed polynomial `x^k`:
`S_k = range (A^k Ω) ⊆ K_{k+1}(A, Ω)`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.1 and §6.3;
Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], §4.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate_mul_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] {s' : Type u_4} [Fintype s'] (A : Matrix n n K) (Ω : Matrix n s K) (R : Matrix s s' K)
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.subspaceIterate A (Ω * R) k ≤ NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω k
name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_mul_le
doc:
Right multiplication of the starting block can only shrink the iterates:
`range (A^k Ω R) ⊆ range (A^k Ω)`. Helper for `subspace-iteration-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate_mul_of_isUnit.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq s] (A : Matrix n n K) (Ω : Matrix n s K) {R : Matrix s s K} (hR : IsUnit R)
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.subspaceIterate A (Ω * R) k = NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω k
name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_mul_of_isUnit
doc:
Subspace iteration depends only on `range Ω`: `S_k(A, Ω R) = S_k(A, Ω)` for invertible `R`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.1.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate_succ.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] (A : Matrix n n K) (Ω : Matrix n s K) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω (k + 1) = Submodule.map A.mulVecLin (NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω k)
name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_succ
doc:
One step of subspace iteration: `S_{k+1} = A S_k`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.1.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_zero
doc: `S_0 = range Ω`. Helper for `subspace-iteration-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceTangent.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype k] [Fintype r]
  (U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ) (U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent
doc:
The largest tangent from a subspace to the leading orthonormal block is the
largest tail-coordinate norm among vectors whose head-coordinate norm is at most one.
Source: Saad (2011), §5.1; manuscript `sa:subspace`. For transverse subspaces this is
the usual supremum of the tail/head norm ratio. This real-valued supremum
is an algebraic helper: if its defining set is unbounded above, Mathlib returns
zero. Use it under a transverse-graph or explicit boundedness hypothesis.

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceTangent_eq_zero_of_not_bddAbove.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] (U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ) (U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ)
  (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ))
  (h :
    ¬BddAbove
        ((fun x => ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (U₂.transpose.mulVec x)‖) ''
          {x | x ∈ S ∧ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (U₁.transpose.mulVec x)‖ ≤ 1})) :
  NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ S = 0
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_eq_zero_of_not_bddAbove
doc:
An unbounded defining set makes the real supremum helper zero. A finite
geometric interpretation therefore requires an explicit boundedness domain.

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceTangent_nonneg_of_bddAbove.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] (U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ) (U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ))
  (h :
    BddAbove
      ((fun x => ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (U₂.transpose.mulVec x)‖) ''
        {x | x ∈ S ∧ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (U₁.transpose.mulVec x)‖ ≤ 1})) :
  0 ≤ NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ S
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_nonneg_of_bddAbove
doc:
On its bounded domain the real subspace-tangent supremum is nonnegative,
since its feasible set contains the zero vector.

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceTangent_range_graph_eq_specNorm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ} {U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ}
  (hU₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₁) (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂) (hU : U₁.transpose * U₂ = 0)
  (F : Matrix r k ℝ) : NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ (U₁ + U₂ * F).mulVecLin.range = NLAlib.specNorm F
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_range_graph_eq_specNorm

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceTangent_subspaceIterate_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ}
  {U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ} (hU₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₁) (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂)
  (hU : U₁.transpose * U₂ = 0) {L₁ Linv : Matrix k k ℝ} {L₂ : Matrix r r ℝ} (hA₁ : A * U₁ = U₁ * L₁)
  (hA₂ : A * U₂ = U₂ * L₂) {Ω : Matrix n k ℝ} {Ω₁ R : Matrix k k ℝ} {Ω₂ : Matrix r k ℝ} (hΩ : Ω = U₁ * Ω₁ + U₂ * Ω₂)
  (hR : Ω₁ * R = 1) (hL : L₁ * Linv = 1) (t : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ (NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω t) ≤
    (NLAlib.specNorm L₂ * NLAlib.specNorm Linv) ^ t * NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ Ω.mulVecLin.range
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_subspaceIterate_le
doc:
Largest principal-angle tangents of subspace iteration contract by the magnitude
gap factor. Source: manuscript `sa:subspace-theorem`; Saad (2011), §5.1.
For diagonal eigenvalue blocks, `specNorm L₂ * specNorm Linv` is
`max |λ_tail| / min |λ_head|`. This form allows indefinite matrices and empty tails.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence (partial)

name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_subspaceIterate_le_of_diagonal
doc:
The explicit magnitude-gap bound uses any positive lower bound on the absolute
leading eigenvalues. Taking their minimum gives the manuscript's `γ = ‖Λ₂‖ / α`;
for a sorted PSD spectrum this is the usual tail/head eigenvalue ratio.
Source: manuscript `sa:subspace-theorem`; Saad (2011), §5.1.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.sudakov_fernique_inequality.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} {Ω' : Type u_3} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'} (X : ι → Ω → ℝ)
  (Y : ι → Ω' → ℝ) (hX : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => X t ω) P)
  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => Y t ω) Q) (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ∂Q = 0)
  (hinc : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X s ω - X t ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y s ω - Y t ω) ^ 2 ∂Q) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), ⨆ t, X t ω ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), ⨆ t, Y t ω ∂Q

`𝔼 (Xₛ - Xₜ)² ≤ 𝔼 (Yₛ - Yₜ)²`. Then `𝔼 maxₜ Xₜ ≤ 𝔼 maxₜ Yₜ`.

atlas: sudakov-fernique

and both prefix endpoints. Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Chapter 1.

  [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {G U V : Matrix ι ι R} {d : ι → R} (hVU : V * U = 1) (hG : G = U * Matrix.diagonal d * V)

  ∑ S ∈ Finset.powersetCard k Finset.univ, (G.submatrix Subtype.val Subtype.val).det =
    ∑ S ∈ Finset.powersetCard k Finset.univ, ∏ i ∈ S, d i

doc:
The sum of order-`k` principal minors of a diagonalizable matrix `G = U diag(d) V`
(`VU = 1`, any commutative ring) equals the elementary symmetric sum of the diagonal spectrum.
Orthogonal (`V = Uᵀ`) and unitary (`V = Uᴴ`) diagonalizations are instances.
Deshpande--Rademacher--Vempala--Wang (2006), volume-sampling proof.

name: NLAlib.sum_det_principal_minors_eq_sum_prod_of_isHermitian
doc:
The sum of fixed-order complex Hermitian principal determinants equals
the elementary sum of the actual eigenvalues. Source: the Hermitian spectral
theorem and determinant coefficient proof of manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`.

signature:

  {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d] {ι : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] (A : ι → Matrix d d ℂ) (Q : Matrix d d ℂ) :
  ∑ i,
        ∑ a,
          Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) (Matrix.single a a 1) *
              Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) Q 1 *
            Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) (Matrix.single a a 1) -
      ∑ i,
        ∑ k,
          Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) (NLAlib.gueCoefficientMatrix k) *
              Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) Q 1 *
            Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (A i) (NLAlib.gueCoefficientMatrix k) =
    0
name: NLAlib.sum_diagonal_sub_gue_covariance_sandwich_identity
doc:
Exact cancellation between the two genuine finite-N covariance
families on an actual tensor matrix with identity ensemble coordinate.
Source: arXiv:2108.06312v2, Corollary 5.3 and Lemma 6.2.

signature:

  ∑ i,
      ∑ j,
        ∑ k,
          ∑ l,
            A i j * A k l *
              (((((if i = j then 1 else 0) * if k = l then 1 else 0) +
                    (if i = k then 1 else 0) * if j = l then 1 else 0) +
                  (if i = l then 1 else 0) * if j = k then 1 else 0) +
                (m₄ - 3) * (((if i = j then 1 else 0) * if i = k then 1 else 0) * if i = l then 1 else 0)) =
    A.trace ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2

The index sum behind the Hutchinson variance:
`∑ᵢⱼₖₗ A_ij A_kl (δ_ij δ_kl + δ_ik δ_jl + δ_il δ_jk + (m₄ − 3) δ_ijkl)
  = (tr A)² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`.
Atlas: `hutchinson-variance` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.sum_sq_singularValues_add_sub_le_frobSq.{u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A E : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min (Fintype.card m) (Fintype.card n)),
      (NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) k - NLAlib.singularValues A k) ^ 2 ≤
    NLAlib.frobSq E
name: NLAlib.sum_sq_singularValues_add_sub_le_frobSq
doc:
**Mirsky's inequality** (Frobenius half of Weyl–Mirsky):
`∑_{k < min m n} (σ_k(A + E) − σ_k(A))² ≤ ‖E‖_F²`, on arbitrary finite index types. Proof:
expand `‖E‖_F² = ‖A + E‖_F² − 2⟨A + E, A⟩_F + ‖A‖_F²` and bound the inner product by the von
Neumann trace inequality (`abs_frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul`). Mirsky 1960 (Q. J. Math.
11); Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.9; Bhatia 1997, §IV.3 (unitarily invariant
form) atlas `weyl-mirsky`. Real only: the von Neumann trace inequality in the
library is real.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.sylvester_separation_bounds.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] {L : Matrix m m ℝ} {M : Matrix n n ℝ} (hL : L.IsHermitian) (hM : M.IsHermitian) (X : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  (∀ (δ : ℝ),
      0 < δ →
        (∀ (i : m) (j : n), δ ≤ |hL.eigenvalues i - hM.eigenvalues j|) →
          δ * NLAlib.frobNorm X ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (L * X - X * M)) ∧
    (∀ (a b δ : ℝ),
        0 < δ →
          (∀ (j : n), a ≤ hM.eigenvalues j ∧ hM.eigenvalues j ≤ b) →
            (∀ (i : m), hL.eigenvalues i ≤ a - δ ∨ b + δ ≤ hL.eigenvalues i) →
              δ * NLAlib.specNorm X ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (L * X - X * M) ∧
                δ * NLAlib.frobNorm X ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (L * X - X * M)) ∧
      ∀ (α δ : ℝ),
        0 < δ →
          (∀ (i : m), hL.eigenvalues i ≤ α - δ) →
            (∀ (j : n), α ≤ hM.eigenvalues j) → δ * NLAlib.specNorm X ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (L * X - X * M)
name: NLAlib.sylvester_separation_bounds
doc:
All Sylvester separation conclusions: arbitrary pairwise gaps in
Frobenius norm and interval/complement gaps in both norms. Bhatia §VII.2,
Davis–Kahan §5–6. Indices are arbitrary finite types and may be empty.
atlas: sylvester-separation-bound

signature:
NLAlib.tan_principalAngles_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

For convex `φ` on `[0, ∞)` with `φ 0 = 0` and PSD `A`, `tr φ(A) ≤ intdim A · φ ‖A‖`.

Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 7*.

doc:
The literal alternating matrix trace word as a continuous complex
multilinear map in its deterministic factors. Products are in ascending Fin
order, so this definition applies to noncommutative matrix multiplication.
Source: the multilinear functional in Brailovskaya–van Handel,
arXiv:2201.05142v3, Proposition 5.1.

name: NLAlib.traceWordMultilinearCoefficients
doc:
The ordered trace-word functional is itself continuous multilinear in its
matrix coefficients. This supplies native measurability and Bochner
integrability of the actual random multilinear functional.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_alternating_two_pairs_eq_cyclic_cut.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.trace_alternating_two_pairs_eq_cyclic_cut
doc:
At the two-pair boundary, the exact middle is simply the other Y factor.
There is no scalar division or positive-radius assumption in the cut.

signature:

doc:
The exact cyclic cut of the literal ordered alternating trace word. The
actual middle matrix is deterministic algebra and needs no norm, support,
Hermitian, or dimension assumption.

name: NLAlib.trace_cfc_abs_pow_le_sqrt_trace_even_pow
doc:
An absolute spectral trace power is bounded by the geometric mean of its two neighboring
even trace powers. Source: spectral Cauchy–Schwarz, used in Appendix `closed:thm:moment` of
the Khatri–Rao embedding manuscript.

signature:

name: NLAlib.trace_cfc_eq_sum_eigenvalues
doc:
`tr f(A) = ∑ᵢ f(λᵢ(A))` for Hermitian `A` (empty index type included).
Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.5.6; supports `slq-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_cgf_subadditivity.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)

Subadditivity of matrix cgfs: `𝔼 traceExp (∑ k, θ • X k) ≤ traceExp (cumulantSum μ X θ)` for

Tropp 2015, Lemma 3.5.1. Atlas: `matrix-laplace`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 3*.
atlas: matrix-laplace

signature:
NLAlib.trace_compression_eq_sum_mul_overlap_row_sq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} (U : Matrix m n ℝ) (Q : Matrix m r ℝ)
  (a : n → ℝ) (hA : A = U * Matrix.diagonal a * U.transpose) :
  (Q.transpose * A * Q).trace = ∑ i, a i * ∑ j, (U.transpose * Q) i j ^ 2
name: NLAlib.trace_compression_eq_sum_mul_overlap_row_sq
doc:
A spectral diagonalization turns a compression trace into
its eigenvalue-weighted overlap row squares. Yu–Wang–Samworth trace proof.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_compression_le_eigenvaluePrefix.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {r : Type u_3} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n r 𝕜}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) :
  RCLike.re (Q.conjTranspose * A * Q).trace ≤ NLAlib.eigenvaluePrefix hA (Fintype.card r)
name: NLAlib.trace_compression_le_eigenvaluePrefix
doc:
**Ky Fan maximum principle, upper bound.** Every orthonormal compression trace
`Re tr(Qᴴ A Q)` is at most the sum of the `card r` largest eigenvalues, including zero columns.
Fan (1949), Theorem 1; Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor. 4.3.39.
atlas: ky-fan-maximum-principle

name: NLAlib.trace_compression_le_trace_topEigenframe
doc:
Every competing width-`k` frame has no larger compression trace than
the named top frame. Yu–Wang–Samworth, Theorem 2, Ky Fan optimality.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_congruence_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (S : Matrix n n ℝ) (d : n → ℝ) :
  (S * Matrix.diagonal d * S.transpose).trace = ∑ i, d i * (S.transpose * S) i i
name: NLAlib.trace_congruence_diagonal
doc:
Trace of a diagonal congruence is a weighted sum of the diagonal
entries, with column-Gram diagonal weights. Horn--Johnson (2013),
Section 7.6; helper for strict inverse-trace convexity.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_conjStarAlgAut.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {R : Type u_2} [CommRing R]

doc:
Trace is invariant under unitary conjugation, over any commutative star ring (in particular
`ℝ` and `ℂ`), including empty matrices.TracePowerConvexity.trace_conjStarAlgAut`).

signature:

Relabeling rows and columns preserves the full sesquilinear trace
pairing, including its imaginary part over `ℂ`.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_conjTranspose_rectDiag_mul_rectDiag.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} (a b : ℕ → ℝ) :

The full trace pairing of rectangular diagonals is their real
coefficient dot product, including empty diagonals.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.trace_eq_ofReal_re_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

doc: The trace of a PSD matrix is the embedding of its real part. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.1.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_eq_rank_of_isIdempotentElem.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Field K]
  (P : Matrix ι ι K) (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) : P.trace = ↑P.rank

The trace of an idempotent matrix over a field is its rank. Empty index types
are included. This is Mathlib's projection trace theorem in matrix coordinates; over `ℂ`, take
`Complex.re` of both sides for the real-trace form. Atlas `eckart-young` (foundation);
`sa:volume-theorem`.

name: NLAlib.trace_eq_sum_eigenvalues₀
doc: The trace is the full sum of the decreasing eigenvalue list.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_eq_sum_of_charpoly_eq_prod.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m]

  A.trace = ∑ i, b i
name: NLAlib.trace_eq_sum_of_charpoly_eq_prod
doc:
Any complete real characteristic-root list sums to the matrix trace.
Source: the next coefficient of the characteristic polynomial; this form
allows a separately indexed complete list and includes empty matrices.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_eq_trace_mul_mul_add_trace_sub_mul_mul_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {P : Matrix n n ℝ} (hP : P * P = P) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : A.trace = (P * A * P).trace + ((1 - P) * A * (1 - P)).trace

**Trace split by an idempotent.** If `P² = P` then
`tr A = tr(P A P) + tr((I − P) A (I − P))`. Source: Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021)
[`mmmw21`], eq. (3) (with `P = QQᵀ`). Atlas: `hutchpp-unbiased` (helper; belongs in
`NLAlib.Matrix.Subspaces.Projections`).

name: NLAlib.trace_eq_trace_transpose_mul_mul_add
doc:
**Trace split by an orthonormal basis.** If `QᵀQ = I` then
`tr A = tr(QᵀAQ) + tr((I − QQᵀ) A (I − QQᵀ))`. Source: Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021)
[`mmmw21`], eq. (3); Epperly–Tropp–Webber (2024) [`etw24`], eq. (1.4). Atlas: `hutchpp-unbiased`
(helper).
atlas: hutchpp-unbiased (partial)

A word with one insertion has the cyclic trace of that insertion
times the full ordinary power.

The resolvent gradient weight has trace at most one, the key bound
for the Gram-chain Laplacian estimate. Source: operator tail proof; atlas

name: NLAlib.trace_le_of_le

The trace is monotone in the Loewner order. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 7.7.4.

signature:
NLAlib.trace_matrixExp_eq_sum_exp_of_eigenbasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (M : Matrix n n ℂ)

  (NLAlib.matrixExp M).trace = ∑ i, Complex.exp (ev i)
name: NLAlib.trace_matrixExp_eq_sum_exp_of_eigenbasis
doc:
A complete eigenvector basis computes the trace of the matrix exponential
as the sum of the scalar exponentials of its eigenvalues.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).

signature:
NLAlib.trace_matrixExp_eq_sum_exp_of_injective_mem_spectrum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (M : Matrix n n ℂ) (ev : n → ℂ) (hev : Function.Injective ev) (hmem : ∀ (i : n), ev i ∈ spectrum ℂ M) :

A list of distinct spectral points with the same index type as the matrix

branches rather than taking that identity as a separate assumption.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

            (U.transpose.mulVec (NLAlib.khatriRaoProbe (g i))) -

doc:

rank-one covariance matrices of the projected probes.

doc:
**The characteristic residual has zero coordinates in `Q`**: `Qᵀ χ(A) b = 0` for
`χ = charpoly (QᵀAQ)` when `K_{card k}(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (polynomial exactness and
Cayley–Hamilton). Any real `A`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6; Saad (1992) [`saad92`],
Lemma 3.1.

signature:
NLAlib.transpose_mulVec_aeval_mulVec_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]

and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, then `Qᵀ p(A) b = p(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b` for every `p` with `deg p ≤ q`, for
any square `A`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Lemma 3.1.
atlas: krylov-polynomial-exactness (partial)

Thm 11.1.

name: NLAlib.transpose_mul_mul_eq_of_range_le
doc:
Basis independence of the Rayleigh–Ritz compression: if `Q` and `Q'` have orthonormal
columns and `range Q' ⊆ range Q`, then `U = Qᵀ Q'` has orthonormal columns and

depend on the orthonormal basis chosen. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §4.3 and §5.1.

signature:
NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_div_sub_eq_of_tendsto {f : ℂ → ℂ} {a t : ℂ} {R r : ℝ}
  (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f {z | R < ‖z‖}) (hr : 0 < r) (hRr : R < r) (htr : ‖t‖ < r)
  (hlim : Filter.Tendsto f (Bornology.cobounded ℂ) (nhds a)) :
  (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∮ (z : ℂ) in C(0, r), f z / (z - t) = a
name: NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_div_sub_eq_of_tendsto
doc:
The exterior Cauchy formula evaluates the circle kernel at every point
inside the circle, even if the holomorphic function is not defined there. Its
value is the function's limit at infinity, not its value at the enclosed point.
This is the atomic Cauchy term in Stahl's representation (Stahl 2013, Theorem 2).
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_exp_add_mul_div_sub_eq {branch : ℂ → ℂ} {a b t : ℂ} {R r : ℝ}
  (hbranch : DifferentiableOn ℂ branch {z | R < ‖z‖}) (hr : 0 < r) (hRr : R < r) (htr : ‖t‖ < r)
  (hlim : Filter.Tendsto (fun z => branch z + b * z) (Bornology.cobounded ℂ) (nhds a)) :
  (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∮ (z : ℂ) in C(0, r), Complex.exp (branch z + b * z) / (z - t) = Complex.exp a
name: NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_exp_add_mul_div_sub_eq
doc:
An exterior eigenvalue branch with asymptotic `branch(z) + bz → a` gives the
atomic Cauchy term `exp a` in Stahl's trace-exponential formula. The branch is
only required outside a disk, and the evaluation point lies inside the circle.
Source: Stahl 2013, Theorem 2, exterior Cauchy step.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_inv_mul_eq_of_tendsto {f : ℂ → ℂ} {a : ℂ} {R r : ℝ}
  (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f {z | R < ‖z‖}) (hr : 0 < r) (hRr : R < r)
  (hlim : Filter.Tendsto f (Bornology.cobounded ℂ) (nhds a)) :
  (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∮ (z : ℂ) in C(0, r), z⁻¹ * f z = a
name: NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_inv_mul_eq_of_tendsto
doc:
The counterclockwise exterior Cauchy integral of a function holomorphic near
infinity equals its finite limit at infinity.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_inv_mul_eq_zero_of_tendsto {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R r : ℝ}
  (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f {z | R < ‖z‖}) (hr : 0 < r) (hRr : R < r)
  (hlim : Filter.Tendsto f (Bornology.cobounded ℂ) (nhds 0)) :
  (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∮ (z : ℂ) in C(0, r), z⁻¹ * f z = 0
name: NLAlib.two_pi_i_inv_mul_circleIntegral_inv_mul_eq_zero_of_tendsto
doc:
A function holomorphic near infinity and vanishing there has zero exterior
circle integral against `1 / z`. This is proved by enlarging the circle and a
uniform norm estimate, rather than by assuming a residue at infinity.
Source: Stahl (2013), Theorem 2 (supporting analysis).
Atlas: `trace-exponential-stahl` (helper).

signature:

  (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (_hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hL2 : ∀ (k : Fin N), MeasureTheory.MemLp (X k) 2 μ) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), (∑ k, X k ω - ∫ (ω' : Ω), ∑ k, X k ω' ∂μ) ^ 2 ∂μ = ∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), (X k ω - ∫ (ω' : Ω), X k ω' ∂μ) ^ 2 ∂μ

doc:

Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

The Hermitian hypothesis is not used by the proof; it is kept to match the source's setting.

signature:
NLAlib.variance_mul_mulVec_apply.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {Ω : Type u_2}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ (i : n), AEMeasurable (fun ω => z ω i) μ)
  (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0)
  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) (i : n) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => z ω i * A.mulVec (z ω) i) μ = ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + (m₄ - 2) * A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_mul_mulVec_apply
doc:
**Variance of the diagonal estimator.** If the coordinates of `z` are independent,
centred, of unit variance and common fourth moment `m₄`, then
`Var[zᵢ (A z)ᵢ] = ∑ⱼ A_ij² + (m₄ − 2) A_ii²`.
Source: Bekas–Kokiopoulou–Saad (2007) [`bks07`], §2; derived from the Hutchinson variance
identity (Avron–Toledo 2011 [`at11`], Lem. 5–6) for the row selector. Atlas:
`diagonal-estimator`; uses `hutchinson-variance`.
atlas: diagonal-estimator

signature:
NLAlib.variance_mul_mulVec_apply_of_hasLaw_gaussianVector.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.variance_mul_mulVec_apply_of_hasLaw_gaussianVector
doc:
**Variance of the diagonal estimator for a standard Gaussian vector**:
`Var[zᵢ (A z)ᵢ] = ∑ⱼ A_ij² + A_ii²` (`m₄ = 3`). Source: Bekas–Kokiopoulou–Saad (2007) [`bks07`], §2.
atlas: diagonal-estimator

signature:
NLAlib.variance_mul_mulVec_apply_of_hasLaw_rademacherVector.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

atlas: diagonal-estimator

signature:
NLAlib.variance_quadForm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ (i : n), AEMeasurable (fun ω => z ω i) μ)
  (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0)
  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => NLAlib.quadForm A (z ω)) μ =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_quadForm
doc:
**Variance of Hutchinson's estimator** (general form). If the coordinates of `z` are
independent, centred, of unit variance and common fourth moment `m₄ = 𝔼[z_i⁴]`, then
`Var[zᵀ A z] = ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²` (mathematically the same as
`∑_{i≠j} (A_ij² + A_ij A_ji) + (m₄ − 1) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`; that form is not stated separately).
Source: Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`] (Rademacher case); Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`],
Lem 5 (Gaussian), Lem 6 (Rademacher). Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`.
Deviation: no symmetry of `A` assumed; general fourth moment `m₄` (`m₄ = 1` Rademacher,
`m₄ = 3` Gaussian).
atlas: hutchinson-variance

moment of the matrix law. Hermitian support and centeredness are unnecessary.

NLAlib.variance_re_quadForm_le_quadraticWeakVariance.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc: The defined supremum bounds each actual unit quadratic-form variance.

signature:
NLAlib.variance_re_quadForm_le_sq_sqrt_quadraticWeakVariance_gaussian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (Matrix n n ℂ)) [ProbabilityTheory.IsGaussian μ] {u : n → ℂ} (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) :

name: NLAlib.variance_re_quadForm_le_sq_sqrt_quadraticWeakVariance_gaussian
doc:
The square root of the actual weak variance supplies the variance parameter
required by Gaussian maximum-eigenvalue concentration, including zero variance.

signature:
NLAlib.variance_sq_dotProduct_le_of_isotropic.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype d]
  [DecidableEq d] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X : Ω → d → ℝ} {β : ℝ} (hX : MeasureTheory.MemLp X 2 μ)

  (a : d → ℝ) (ha : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 a‖ = 1) : ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => (X ω ⬝ᵥ a) ^ 2) μ ≤ β ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_sq_dotProduct_le_of_isotropic
doc:
For an isotropic law, directional fourth-moment variance control gives
the dimension-free weak variance bound on every unit rank-one probe.

signature:
NLAlib.variance_sq_dotProduct_mulVec_le.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype d]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X : Ω → d → ℝ} {β : ℝ}

doc:
Directional fourth-moment variance control is preserved under every
deterministic linear map, hence under invertible whitening.

signature:
NLAlib.variationOn_comp_cos_le (h : ℝ → ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.variationOn_comp_cos_le
doc:
Cosine substitution does not increase variation on the standard half period.
Source: monotone reparametrization of variation; helper for `chebyshev-coeff-bv-decay`.

name: NLAlib.vecMulVec_eq_zero_of_columnRowWeight_eq_zero
doc:
A zero column/row weight means that its literal outer product is zero.
Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm-theorem`.

signature:
NLAlib.vecMulVec_mul_mul_vecMulVec.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (y : ι → ℝ) (B : Matrix ι ι ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.vecMulVec_mul_mul_vecMulVec
doc:
Sandwiching a matrix by one real rank-one matrix gives its quadratic
form times that same rank-one matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.vecMulVec_mul_prod_map_mul_vecMulVec.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (y : ι → ℝ)

name: NLAlib.vecMulVec_mul_prod_map_mul_vecMulVec
doc:
Multiplying rank-one-separated factors after an initial rank-one
matrix contracts each factor to a scalar quadratic form.

signature:
NLAlib.vecMulVec_ne_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3} [Field K] {x : m → K} {y : n → K}

name: NLAlib.vecMulVec_ne_zero
doc:
A nonzero right column and nonzero left row give a nonzero outer product.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §1.4; the assertion includes rectangular shapes.

signature:
NLAlib.vecMulVec_pow_succ.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (y : ι → ℝ) (p : ℕ) :
  Matrix.vecMulVec y y ^ (p + 1) = (y ⬝ᵥ y) ^ p • Matrix.vecMulVec y y
name: NLAlib.vecMulVec_pow_succ
doc:
A positive natural power of a real rank-one matrix is the same
rank-one matrix times a power of its trace.

signature:
NLAlib.vecMul_eigenvector_of_intertwines.{u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] {K : Type u_3} [Field K]
  {A B S : Matrix n n K} {y : n → K} {μ : K} (hS : S * A = B * S) (hy : Matrix.vecMul y B = μ • y) :

doc:
Similarity transports a left row eigenvector by right multiplication
with the inverse similarity matrix. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Theorem 2.4.11.1; for complex columns this is inverse conjugate transpose.
atlas: left-right-eigenvectors

signature:
NLAlib.vectorMinpoly.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K)
  (b : n → K) : Polynomial K

The monic polynomial of least degree annihilating `b` through `A`.
It is one when `b=0`, including empty matrices.
Source: Saad (2003), Props. 6.1–6.3.
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.vectorMinpoly_dvd_minpoly.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

The vector-relative minimal polynomial divides the operator minimal polynomial.
Source: Saad (2003), Proposition 6.1.
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.vectorMinpoly_monic.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n K) (b : n → K) : (NLAlib.vectorMinpoly A b).Monic

doc:
The vector-relative minimal polynomial is monic.
Source: Saad (2003), Props. 6.1–6.3.
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame.{u_1, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l] (Q : Matrix n l ℝ)
  (u : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame
doc:
The tangent of the angle from a vector to an orthonormal frame's range is its
orthogonal-residual norm divided by its projection norm. Source: Saad (2011), §5.1;
manuscript `sa:subspace`, per-vector angle clause. This real quotient returns
zero when the projection is zero, including nonzero orthogonal vectors.
`vectorTangentToFrameENNReal` is the geometric diagnostic including right angles.

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal.{u_1, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l] (Q : Matrix n l ℝ)
  (u : n → ℝ) : ENNReal
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal
doc:
The extended nonnegative vector-to-frame tangent: residual norm divided by
projection norm. A nonzero vector orthogonal to the frame has tangent `⊤`,
while the zero vector has tangent zero. For an orthonormal frame and nonzero
projection this agrees with the finite real quotient. Source: Saad (2011), §5.1.

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal_eq_ofReal.{u_1, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l]
  (Q : Matrix n l ℝ) {u : n → ℝ} (hp : Q.transpose.mulVec u ≠ 0) :
  NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal Q u = ENNReal.ofReal (NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame Q u)
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal_eq_ofReal
doc:
With nonzero projection, the extended tangent is the embedding of the
finite real quotient. The hypothesis explicitly excludes a right angle.

name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal_eq_top_of_projection_eq_zero
doc:
A nonzero orthogonal vector has infinite tangent, rather than the zero
produced by total real division. No orthonormality is needed for this degeneracy.

name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal_le_of_orthogonal_competitor
doc:
An orthogonal graph competitor bounds the geometric extended tangent.
The competitor forces a nonzero projection, so the result excludes the
infinite right-angle case through its mathematical hypotheses. Source: Saad (2011), §5.1.

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal_zero.{u_1, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l]
  (Q : Matrix n l ℝ) : NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal Q 0 = 0
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrameENNReal_zero
doc: The zero vector has extended tangent zero.

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_eq_zero_of_projection_eq_zero.{u_1, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l] (Q : Matrix n l ℝ) {u : n → ℝ} (hp : Q.transpose.mulVec u = 0) :
  NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame Q u = 0
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_eq_zero_of_projection_eq_zero
doc:
Zero projection makes the total real quotient zero. This lemma exposes its
invalid-angle convention; use the extended tangent for geometric diagnostics.

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_graph_col_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l] [DecidableEq l] {Q : Matrix n l ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) {U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ} {U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ} (hU₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₁)
  (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂) (hU : U₁.transpose * U₂ = 0) (F : Matrix r k ℝ)
  (hRange : (U₁ + U₂ * F).mulVecLin.range ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) (i : k) :
  NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame Q (U₁.col i) ≤ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (F.col i)‖
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_graph_col_le
doc:
Each leading graph column has angle to any containing orthonormal frame at most
its tail-column norm. Source: manuscript `sa:subspace`, the per-vector competitor.

signature:
NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_le_of_orthogonal_competitor.{u_1, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {l : Type u_4} [Fintype l]
  [DecidableEq l] {Q : Matrix n l ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) {u w : n → ℝ} (huNorm : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1)
  (huw : u ⬝ᵥ w = 0) (hw : u + w ∈ Q.mulVecLin.range) : NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame Q u ≤ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 w‖
name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_le_of_orthogonal_competitor
doc:
Comparing a unit vector with any orthogonal graph competitor bounds its angle
to the containing frame. Source: manuscript `sa:subspace`, per-vector comparison.
This is an actual vector-to-subspace tangent, not the initial graph-column norm.

name: NLAlib.vectorTangentToFrame_subspaceIterate_le_of_diagonal
doc:
Every leading eigenvector has the corrected individual magnitude-gap angle rate
to a frame containing the iterate. Source: manuscript `sa:subspace`, final per-vector
clause; Saad (2011), §5.1. The initial constant is `‖F₀ e_i‖`, not its initial angle
to the whole starting subspace. A frame for exactly the iterate is a special case.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence (partial)

signature: NLAlib.volumeSampleColumns {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Matrix (Fin m) ↥S ℝ
name: NLAlib.volumeSampleColumns
doc:
The columns indexed by a finite subset, retaining their original labels.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume`, its column submatrix `A_S`.

signature: NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq
doc:
The finite determinant-weighted expected squared projection residual.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`; the normalized distribution is used when
`k ≤ rank A`, where its normalizer is proved positive. If the normalizer is
zero, this total weighted formula is zero; `volumeSamplingLaw` requires feasibility.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_eq_mul_normalizer_succ_div {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq A k =
    (↑k + 1) * NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer A (k + 1) / NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer A k
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_eq_mul_normalizer_succ_div
doc:
The finite volume-sampling expected projection error is exactly `(k+1)Z_(k+1)/Z_k`.
For `k ≤ rank A`, the proved positive normalizer makes this the actual expectation.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`; Deshpande et al. (2006), exact error formula.
The empty-set and exact-rank endpoints are included by the same finite identity.
atlas: volume-sampling (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_le_mul_bestRankFrobSq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ A.rank) : NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq A k ≤ (↑k + 1) * NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq A k
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_le_mul_bestRankFrobSq

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_nonneg {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank) :
  0 ≤ NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq A k
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_nonneg
doc:
The finite expected squared volume-sampling residual is nonnegative.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`, nonnegative finite expectation.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_rank_eq_zero {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq A A.rank = 0
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingExpectedFrobSq_rank_eq_zero
doc:
Sampling exactly the input rank has zero expected projResidual, hence zero residual
on every positive-probability outcome of the finite volume law.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`, exact-rank endpoint.
atlas: volume-sampling (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure (Finset (Fin n))
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw
doc:
The real volume-sampling measure, defined at feasible subset sizes.
Source: Deshpande–Rademacher–Vempala–Wang (2006), volume sampling.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw_isProbabilityMeasure {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank) :
  MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw A hk)
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw_isProbabilityMeasure
doc: The feasible volume-sampling law is a probability measure.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw_singleton {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank)
  (S : Finset (Fin n)) : (NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw A hk).real {S} = NLAlib.volumeSamplingProbability A k S
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingLaw_singleton
doc: Every subset has its normalized determinant as mass at the prescribed size.

signature: NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer
doc:
The finite sum of all prescribed-size volume weights.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume`, its normalizer `Z_k`.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer_eq_sum_prod_singularValues_sq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer A k = ∑ S ∈ Finset.powersetCard k Finset.univ, ∏ i ∈ S, NLAlib.singularValues A ↑i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer_eq_sum_prod_singularValues_sq
doc:
The volume normalizer is the elementary spectral sum of squared singular values.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume`, determinant coefficient identity.
The singular values are zero-indexed and padded beyond the matrix rank.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer_pos {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank) :
  0 < NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer A k
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingNormalizer_pos
doc:
Volume sampling is a normalized finite distribution at every prescribed size up
to the input rank. Source: manuscript `sa:volume`, positivity of `Z_k`.
The empty-set and rank-zero endpoints are included.

signature: NLAlib.volumeSamplingPMF {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank) : PMF (Finset (Fin n))
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingPMF
doc:
The probability mass function of real volume sampling at a feasible size.
Source: Deshpande–Rademacher–Vempala–Wang (2006), volume sampling.

signature: NLAlib.volumeSamplingProbability {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingProbability
doc:
Prescribed-size determinant probabilities, with zero mass at other sizes.
Source: Deshpande–Rademacher–Vempala–Wang (2006), volume sampling.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingProbability_nonneg {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ A.rank)
  (S : Finset (Fin n)) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.volumeSamplingProbability A k S
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingProbability_nonneg
doc: Feasible determinant probabilities are nonnegative.

signature: NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight
doc:
The Gram determinant weight of a sampled column set; the empty determinant is one.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume`, its weight `w(S)`.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight_mul_frobSq_col_eq_insert {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n))
  {j : Fin n} (hj : j ∉ S) :
  NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight A S *
      NLAlib.frobSq
        ((A.submatrix id fun x => j) -
          NLAlib.volumeSampleColumns A S * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (NLAlib.volumeSampleColumns A S) *
            A.submatrix id fun x => j) =
    NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight A (insert j S)
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight_mul_frobSq_col_eq_insert
doc:
Adding an outside column multiplies the volume weight by its squared projection
residual. Source: manuscript `sa:volume-column`; Deshpande et al. (2006).
The determinant identity includes a dependent starting column set.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight_mul_frobSq_eq_sum_insert {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
  NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight A S *
      NLAlib.frobSq
        (A - NLAlib.volumeSampleColumns A S * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (NLAlib.volumeSampleColumns A S) * A) =
    ∑ j, if j ∉ S then NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight A (insert j S) else 0
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight_mul_frobSq_eq_sum_insert
doc:
A determinant-weighted projection error is the sum of the weights after adding
one outside column. Source: manuscript `sa:volume-theorem`, first summation step.

signature:
NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight_nonneg {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
  0 ≤ NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight A S
name: NLAlib.volumeSamplingWeight_nonneg
doc:
Every volume-sampling Gram weight is nonnegative, at every rank.
Source: manuscript `sa:volume`, positivity of `w(S)`.

signature: NLAlib.walshBitSign (a : ZMod 2) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.walshBitSign
doc:
The real sign associated to one binary bit.
Source: Walsh character construction; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshBitSign_add (a b : ZMod 2) : NLAlib.walshBitSign (a + b) = NLAlib.walshBitSign a * NLAlib.walshBitSign b
name: NLAlib.walshBitSign_add
doc:
Addition of bits multiplies their real signs.
Source: Walsh character construction; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshBitSign_sq (a : ZMod 2) : NLAlib.walshBitSign a ^ 2 = 1
name: NLAlib.walshBitSign_sq
doc:
Every bit sign has squared value one.
Source: Walsh character construction; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshCharacter {b : ℕ} (a c : NLAlib.WalshIndex b) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.walshCharacter
doc: The unnormalized real Walsh character.

signature:
NLAlib.walshCharacter_add_left {b : ℕ} (a c z : NLAlib.WalshIndex b) :
  NLAlib.walshCharacter (a + c) z = NLAlib.walshCharacter a z * NLAlib.walshCharacter c z
name: NLAlib.walshCharacter_add_left

Addition of row labels multiplies Walsh characters.
Source: Walsh construction; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshCharacter_comm {b : ℕ} (a c : NLAlib.WalshIndex b) : NLAlib.walshCharacter a c = NLAlib.walshCharacter c a
name: NLAlib.walshCharacter_comm
doc:
Walsh characters are symmetric in the row and column labels.
Source: Walsh construction; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshCharacter_sq {b : ℕ} (a c : NLAlib.WalshIndex b) : NLAlib.walshCharacter a c ^ 2 = 1
name: NLAlib.walshCharacter_sq
doc:
Every Walsh character has squared value one.
Source: Walsh construction; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshIndexEquivFin (b : ℕ) : NLAlib.WalshIndex b ≃ Fin (2 ^ b)
name: NLAlib.walshIndexEquivFin
doc: A fixed relabeling of the binary Walsh group by ordinary row labels.

signature: NLAlib.walshIndex_add_eq_zero_iff {b : ℕ} (a c : NLAlib.WalshIndex b) : a + c = 0 ↔ a = c
name: NLAlib.walshIndex_add_eq_zero_iff
doc:
Binary-vector addition is zero precisely when its two inputs agree.
Source: Walsh character orthogonality; supports `srht-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.walshMatrix (b : ℕ) : Matrix (NLAlib.WalshIndex b) (NLAlib.WalshIndex b) ℝ

An almost-everywhere displacement bound on a Markov smoothing bounds the

A coupling on a measurable common support pushes to a coupling of the
ambient measures with the same metric cost.

The composition-product measure is an explicit coupling of a law and its

The compact Kantorovich bound for ambient measures supported on a compact
set, with observables required to be Lipschitz only on that set. Atoms and
endpoint masses are allowed.

A proved dual Lipschitz bound controls the genuine infimum over

signature:
NLAlib.wassersteinEDistOne_le_tensorChebyshevMomentError {d : ℕ}

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (hμ : ∀ᵐ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) ∂μ, x ∈ NLAlib.chebyshevCube (Fin d))

    ENNReal.ofReal (12 * ↑d / ↑k + √(↑d * Real.pi ^ d / 2) * NLAlib.tensorChebyshevMomentError μ ν k)

doc:
The complete tensor moment comparison for genuine coupling-based
one-Wasserstein distance with Euclidean transport cost. The explicit positive
kernel improves the approximation term from `36d/k` to `12d/k`.
Source: MMRS Appendix A.1, Theorem 32.
atlas: chebyshev-moment-wasserstein (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.wassersteinEDistOne_le_thirtySix_div_add_chebyshevMomentError (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)

doc:
The univariate moment comparison with the displayed source constant `36`.
Source: MMRS Theorem 1. The stronger `12/k` estimate is available above.
atlas: chebyshev-moment-wasserstein (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.wassersteinEDistOne_le_twelve_div_add_chebyshevMomentError (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)

doc:
Weighted Chebyshev moment comparison for genuine coupling-based
one-Wasserstein distance, including arbitrary atomic laws on the interval.
The tensor clause is supplied separately.
Source: MMRS Theorem 1, with a stronger `12/k` approximation term.
atlas: chebyshev-moment-wasserstein (partial)

signature:

NLAlib.wassersteinEDistOne_self.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace X] [PseudoEMetricSpace X]

signature:
NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_abs_singularValues_add_sub.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A E : Matrix m n ℝ) :

    NLAlib.singularValues E ↑i
name: NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_abs_singularValues_add_sub
doc:
Rectangular Mirsky: the entire absolute singular-value difference vector is
weakly majorized by the perturbation singular list, on arbitrary finite real matrix row and
column indices. Bhatia 1997, Theorem IV.3.4. The vector has the thin rectangular
dimension `min (card m) (card n)`, with rank-deficient zeros; its coordinatewise differences are
not assumed already sorted. Empty dimensions are included.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_abs_singularValues_add_sub_padded.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]

    NLAlib.singularValues E ↑i
name: NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_abs_singularValues_add_sub_padded
doc:
Mirsky weak majorization on any finite zero-padded length, without a dimension
bound on that length. Bhatia 1997, Theorem IV.3.4; arbitrary finite indices.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_iff_sum_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_iff_sum_le
doc:
Weak majorization is equivalently the family of all subset-sum comparisons
against the corresponding top-coordinate sum.

signature:
NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_iff_sum_max_sub_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_iff_sum_max_sub_le
doc:
Weak majorization is exactly comparison of all translated positive-part
sums, including the degenerate empty coordinate space.

signature:
NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_iff_sum_monotone_convex_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :

Full weak-majorization equivalence with all increasing convex scalar sum
tests. Includes signed vectors, ties, zero prefixes and empty index types.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Proposition 4.B.2.

NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_mulVec_of_doublyStochastic.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (y : ι → ℝ)

doc:
A doubly stochastic map weakly majorizes its image, without a sign
restriction on the input vector. Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_of_sum_max_sub_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {x y : ι → ℝ}

Hinge inequalities imply all weak-majorization prefix inequalities.

NLAlib.weaklyMajorized_singularValues_add.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

Singular values of a sum are weakly majorized by the coordinatewise sum
of its two decreasing singular-value lists, for arbitrary finite matrix indices.

signature:
NLAlib.weighted_deriv_mul_rpow_exp_eq (m x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) (η : ℝ → ℝ) (hη : DifferentiableAt ℝ η x) :
  4 * x * deriv (fun y => η y * (y ^ (-m / 2) * Real.exp (y / 2))) x +
      2 * (m - x) * (η x * (x ^ (-m / 2) * Real.exp (x / 2))) =
    4 * (x ^ (1 - m / 2) * Real.exp (x / 2)) * deriv η x
name: NLAlib.weighted_deriv_mul_rpow_exp_eq
doc:
Multiplication by the Gamma integrating factor cancels the zeroth-order
coefficient of the scalar Wishart weak inequality. Source: Edelman 1988, the weighted-density substitution; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail
(helper).

signature: NLAlib.wilkinsonMatrix (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ

Wilkinson's matrix, with a variable final column. The standard example
uses `t=1`; the parameter records the successive doubling during elimination.

signature:
NLAlib.withDensity_restrict_regular_of_continuousOn_Ioi (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)
  [MeasureTheory.IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (g : ℝ → ℝ) (ℓ a : ℝ) (ha : ℓ < a) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Ioi ℓ)) :
  ((μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (g x)).restrict (Set.Ioi a)).Regular

A density continuous on a half-line gives a Radon reweighted measure after
restriction to every smaller half-line. Clamping the weight at the smaller endpoint
reduces the statement to Mathlib's continuous-density local finiteness theorem.

The native annihilation/creation composition is identity at equal

signature:

Kronecker coefficient times the genuine rank-one vacuum projection.

doc:
The mixed left-annihilation/right-field commutator is its actual
Kronecker coefficient times the vacuum rank-one projection.

signature: NLAlib.wordAnnihilation_wordVacuum.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} (i : ι) : (NLAlib.wordAnnihilation i) (NLAlib.wordVacuum ι) = 0

The coefficient representation is injective, proved from the actual

states on the native `PiLp 2` block representation, using one vacuum in each

recursion, derived from the mixed vacuum defect and not assumed as a law.

signature:

    Polynomial.C (Lagrange.nodalWeight s v i * Lagrange.nodalWeight s v j * (v i - v j)) *

    ∑ i ∈ u,
      ∑ j ∈ v,
        Polynomial.C (a i * b j * Lagrange.nodalWeight s t i * Lagrange.nodalWeight s t j * (t i - t j)) *
          (∏ k ∈ (s.erase i).erase j, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (t k))) ^ 2

doc:

(a Mathlib-level fact, not itself an atlas result).
